SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – A Springfield, Mo. man was sentenced in federal court yesterday for being an unlawful user of a controlled substance while in possession of firearms.

Jayden Lamar Wright, 21, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Megan Blair Benton to 84 months in federal prison without parole and three years of supervised release. Wright pleaded guilty to two counts of unlawfully possessing firearms as a user of a controlled substance on April 9, 2026.

On Feb. 22, 2024, an agent with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) conducted a search of Wright’s vehicle after it was present at the scene of a double homicide and seized four semi-automatic pistols belonging to Wright. Wright admitted that he was an active user of marijuana.

On March 8, 2024, ATF agents observed Wright carrying a 9mm pistol with an extended magazine as he entered a gun show in Springfield. An undercover ATF agent approached Wright and negotiated the purchase of the 9mm pistol and a magazine. Investigators later observed Wright purchasing a new semi-automatic pistol and extended magazine at the gun show. That firearm was seized during a traffic stop along with a third firearm that Wright had purchased at the gun show.

A year later, police approached Wright in connection with another investigation. Wright fled but was detained shortly thereafter and was found to be carrying another firearm.

This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Alfredo De La Rosa and Jessica Eatmon. It was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, the Greene County, Missouri Sheriff’s Office, and the Springfield, Missouri Police Department.

Project Safe Neighborhoods

This case is part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), a program bringing together all levels of law enforcement and the communities they serve to reduce violent crime and gun violence, and to make our neighborhoods safer for everyone. On May 26, 2021, the Department launched a violent crime reduction strategy strengthening PSN based on these core principles: fostering trust and legitimacy in our communities, supporting community-based organizations that help prevent violence from occurring in the first place, setting focused and strategic enforcement priorities, and measuring the results.

text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) joined her Pennsylvania Democratic House colleagues in pressing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), the GEO Group, Inc.(GEO), and Clearfield County, Pennsylvania for transparency on their intentionally opaque financial relationship with Moshannon Valley Processing Center (MVPC), the largest immigration center in the Northeast. The letter is also signed by U.S. Representatives Mary Gay Scalon (PA-05), Brendan Boyle (PA-02), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Summer Lee (PA-12), and Chris Deluzio (PA-17).

“As Members of Congress, it is our responsibility to conduct oversight of government spending and executive action. GEO has reported record profits driven by this administration’s mass deportation and immigrant surveillance campaigns. As part of these efforts, ICE and Clearfield County have both funneled Pennsylvanians’ taxpayer dollars to GEO. More importantly, our constituents have been detained at Moshannon. It is incumbent on us, as their elected representatives, to investigate the contract terms that peg their detention to GEO’s profit,” the lawmakers wrote.

ICE recently issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) to solicit contract bids that would extend immigration detention at Moshannon for another 10 years. The current five year contract is due to expire this month. The RFP sets an expedited timeline — just two weeks of visibility for the public from the time it was posted online (August 28, 2026) to when the Phase 1 Proposal(s) were due (September 11, 2026). This timing is in line with other attempts by the administration to rush government contracts and obscure how taxpayer funds are being spent.

Currently, an Intergovernmental Service Agreement (IGSA) between ICE and Clearfield County provides for the operation of the Moshannon facility and services related to the detention of persons in ICE custody, with GEO as the approved private contractor delivering those services. This contracting structure thwarts oversight because it delays the availability of crucial financial details. The IGSA agreement requires that the County submit an itemized operating fee to ICE on a monthly basis, which ICE then reviews and approves for payout.

“We request that you provide us with any and all monthly invoices for services provided pursuant to the IGSA and all communications regarding such invoices and payments made for such services at Moshannon from January 1, 2025, to present, by and among ICE, GEO, and Clearfield County,” the lawmakers continued. “We also request all invoices, payments, and communications by and among the parties and detainees regarding payments for and operation of the “detainee work program,” from January 1, 2025, to the present.”

According to recent reports, the monthly fixed rate includes a monthly operating fee, which began as $2.95 million per month and may have adjusted over time, a per diem fee of $10 per day for 1 through 800 detainees and $40 per day for 801 to 1876 detainees, reimbursement of one dollar per day for the detainee work program, transportation fees, and fees for guards.

“Finally, to the extent that additional agreements exist directly between GEO and Clearfield County, we request such agreements, corresponding contracts, any amendments or modifications, payment receipts, invoices, and supplemental documentation,” the members concluded.

In the letter, the members have requested a number of materials by September 25, 2026 — prior to the expiration of the current IGSA between ICE and Clearfield County, which is set to expire on September 28, 2026.

Following an alarming visit to MVPC, Congresswoman Dean lead her Pennsylvania colleagues in letters to ICE and the GEO Group to demand answers on GEO’s failure to comply with federal standards of adequate staffing and medical care to detainees, as well as obstruction of congressional oversight. Congresswoman Dean also recently introduced theOversight Access Act to expand congressional oversight at ICE facilities without prior notice and the No Shock Act to ban the use of electric shock gloves by ICE agents.

Find the full text of the letter here.

Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.

Surface Transportation Board Chairman Patrick Fuchs today announced that, with the approval of the Board, Marty Schlenker has been appointed to serve as Director of the STB’s Office of Economics. Chairman Fuchs also announced that Terrence McDermott has been appointed as a senior advisor to the Chairman. These appointments strengthen the Board’s expert staff, supporting ongoing reform efforts and ensuring the continued efficient and effective advancement of the agency’s mission. Immediately prior to their new roles, Mr. Schlenker and Mr. McDermott held temporary transition appointments at the Board.
As Director of the Office of Economics, Mr. Schlenker will oversee critical agency analytical functions, including data gathering and reporting and economic and industry analysis related to Board decisions. Mr. Schlenker brings extensive experience and deep expertise in data analysis, supply chain and rail technology, and rail operations planning. He previously served as Head of Strategy for autonomous rail startup Parallel Systems, operated a supply chain and technology consulting practice, served in a finance role at CSX Transportation, and held senior leadership roles in service planning and technology at BNSF Railway. Mr. Schlenker also has held leadership roles in the Railway Applications Section of the Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS) and the American Railway Engineering & Maintenance Association (AREMA). Mr. Schlenker holds an MS in Transportation from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s Center for Transportation Studies, and a BA in Economics from the University of Chicago.
Mr. McDermott, the former Director of Supply Chain—North American Rail with global agribusiness company Bunge, brings significant transportation experience and extensive supply chain knowledge from both shipper and railroad perspectives. He previously held senior roles at Ferromex, a Mexican railroad owned by Grupo México and Union Pacific, including service as Chief Marketing Officer and Vice President of Sales for Agricultural Products, Intermodal, and Automotive. Mr. McDermott has served on the Board’s Rail-Shipper Transportation Advisory Council and National Grain Car Council, as well as in leadership positions with the Transportation, Elevator, and Grain Merchants Association (TEGMA) and North American Freight Car Association (NAFCA). He also served on the Transportation Committees of the National Oilseed Processors Association and the Rail Shippers/Receivers Committee of the National Grain and Feed Association. He holds an MBA and BBA in International Business from New Mexico State University, and certificates in Supply Chain, Finance, and Leadership from Washington University in St. Louis.
“Marty’s leadership and deep knowledge of data analytics, rail operations, and finance will be essential to the agency’s advancement of an efficient and effective regulatory environment,” said Chairman Fuchs. “Terry’s extensive expertise and experience from both shipper and railroad perspectives will be critical to the Board’s efforts to assess complex supply chain dynamics and implement sound, thoughtful solutions. Both Marty and Terry strengthen the Board’s analysis of the applied effects of its actions, and I am grateful for their continued commitment to serving the public.”
title: STB Appoints Director of Office of Economics and Senior Advisor

WASHINGTON — Today, Rep. Shomari C. Figures (AL-02), Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ), Rep. Jahana Hayes (CT-05), and Rep. Mike Ezell (MS-04) will introduce the bipartisan Public Service Educational Assistance Act, a bill to support the families of critical public service employees by covering the full cost of higher education and training opportunities for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers.

"Educators, first responders, and social workers show up for us in our classrooms, our emergencies, and our hardest moments, year after year," said Booker. "Their families carry that sacrifice too, often quietly, through long hours and stretched budgets. After 20 years of service, the least we can do is make sure their kids can go to college without drowning in debt."

“Teachers, social workers, and first responders dedicate their lives in service to our communities, oftentimes unable to provide opportunities they fight so hard for others to enjoy, to their own children,” said Hayes. “I am pleased to introduce the Public Service Educational Assistance Act alongside Congressman Figures to honor the work of public servants and make it easier for their own families to pursue higher education."

“As someone who spent more than four decades in law enforcement, I know the sacrifices that come with a career dedicated to serving your community—not just for the individual wearing the badge, but for their entire family,” said Ezell. “The Public Service Educational Assistance Act recognizes that commitment by helping provide educational opportunities for the children of those who have devoted decades of their lives to public service. I’m proud to help introduce this legislation to support the families of our law enforcement officers, first responders, educators, and others who dedicate their careers to serving their neighbors.”

This legislation establishes a federal education assistance program covering the full cost of postsecondary education and training opportunities – including those enrolled in trade schools and vocational programs – for the dependents of educators, first responders, and social workers who have completed at least 20 years of qualifying service.

This bill is endorsed by the Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, the National Association of Social Workers, the International Association of Fire Fighters, and the Major Cities Chiefs Association.
title: Figures, Booker, Hayes, Ezell to Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Cover College and Trade School Costs for Families of America’s First Responders, Teachers, and Social Workers

SHREVEPORT – On September 17, 2026, a federal criminal complaint was filed charging Tre'veon Jackson , 24, of Shreveport, with Carjacking with Serious Bodily Injury. Jackson was arrested by the United States Marshals Service in Marshall, Texas, and now faces federal charges in Shreveport. Jackson faces up to 25 years in federal prison for the charge.

“When dangerous offenders like Mr. Jackson escape from custody, it’s an all-hands-on-deck situation that requires federal, state, and local law enforcement working together to eliminate the threat. Our Office is proud to have sprung into action alongside our partners to bring federal charges against Mr. Jackson and coordinate with the United States Marshals Service, the FBI, and state and local partners to bring this offender back into custody,” said United States Attorney Zachary A. Keller. “This Office is grateful to all of our law enforcement partners, particularly the United States Marshals Service, for their exceptional diligence locating and apprehending Mr. Jackson. We look forward to seeing justice done in this case.”

“We don’t want to get into the specifics of the capture, but I will say that the United States Marshals Service has the most talented men and women in law enforcement today,” said United States Marshal Brian H. Barber. “This is what we train for, and this is what we do. When we got the call that there was a fugitive, our investigators and deputies were in pursuit within minutes. There was no way Mr. Jackson was getting away with the United States Marshals Service looking for him.” According to court documents, on September 14, 2026, Jackson escaped from custody during a medical transport. Shortly after his escape, Jackson allegedly approached a man outside a hotel in Bossier City, violently assaulted him, and stole his vehicle. It is further alleged that Jackson then led law enforcement officers on a high-speed chase reaching speeds of over 110 miles per hour before crashing the vehicle and fleeing on foot. A multi-agency manhunt ensued, and Jackson remained at large for several days until he was finally located and arrested in Marshall. He is now in federal custody.

U.S. Attorney Zachary A. Keller for the Western District of Louisiana made the announcement.

The FBI, U.S. Marshals Service, the Bossier City Police Department, Marshall Police Department, Harrison County Sheriff’s Office, the Texas State Technical College Police Department, and the Texas Rangers investigated this case. It is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Allison Foster and Samuel Crichton, with assistance from Legal Assistant Emily Favrot.

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

This case was prosecuted as part of Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN), the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities. Learn more at www.justice.gov/psn.

You find a copy of this press release (and any updates) on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Western District of Louisiana at www.justice.gov/usao-wdla.

Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Western District of Louisiana at www.lawd.uscourts.gov or at https://www.lawd.uscourts.gov/cmecf-pacer. The case number for this matter is 5:26-mj-00233-01.

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) led 7 Members of the Virginia delegation — including U.S. Senators Mark Warner (D-VA) and Tim Kaine (D-VA), and Representatives Bobby Scott (VA-03), Don Beyer (VA-08), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) and James Walkinshaw (VA-11) — in sending a letter to Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins in strong opposition to the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Area Conservation Rule (the “Roadless Rule”).

Since its implementation in 2001, the Roadless Rule has protected 45 million acres of forest lands across the country, including nearly 394,000 acres in the Commonwealth of Virginia. Under the Trump Administration, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and Forest Service filed a proposal in August of this year to repeal the Roadless Rule, which could have devastating impacts on water quality, biodiversity, economic development and more for these regions.

“This proposal would strip protections from approximately 84% of Virginia’s roadless areas, opening these lands to road construction, logging, and other industrial activities. The consequences for Virginia’s environment, economy, and public health would be severe, falling squarely on the families and communities we represent,” wrote the lawmakers. “With more roadless acres than any other state east of the Mississippi River, Virginia has an outsized stake in decisions regarding the Roadless Rule. Once lost, these ecosystems and the countless benefits they provide to clean air, clean water, and climate resilience cannot be easily restored, if at all.”

The letter outlines the risks this rescission would pose to Virginia by jeopardizing Virginia’s drinking water and ecosystems, threatening economic activity driven by recreation and tourism activities, increasing wildfire risk and straining public resources.

“For 25 years, the Roadless Rule has demonstrated that protecting America’s national forest lands is both effective and widely supported. Rescinding the Roadless Rule would ignore this overwhelming public consensus while undermining Virginia’s drinking water, biodiversity, local economies, and public safety,” the lawmakers concluded. “We urge the Department to withdraw this dangerous proposal and maintain the Roadless Area Conservation Rule of 2001 in its entirety.”
title: McClellan Leads Virginia Democratic Delegation to Oppose Trump’s Efforts to Rescind the Roadless Rule

Vasquez delivers major wins for water security, wildfire recovery, flood protection and the Rio Grande

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) helped pass the Water Resources Development Act of 2026, securing up to $50 million in new water infrastructure authorizations for communities in New Mexico focused on drought and wildfire recovery, flood protection and the long-term health of the Rio Grande.

“I fought to put New Mexico front and center in this bill, and I’m proud to have delivered,” said Vasquez. “This bill provides up to $50 million for local water infrastructure to protect the Rio Grande and help communities recover from wildfires – critical wins for New Mexicans as we face a dire water shortage.”

The Water Resources Development Act, known as WRDA, authorizes water infrastructure projects, studies and policies carried out by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. This year, Vasquez pushed to make sure New Mexico’s unique water challenges were reflected in a bill that shapes water policy across the country.

Rep. Vasquez secured the following wins for New Mexico:

$25 million for Doña Ana County water infrastructure: Vasquez secured a $25 million authorization for water infrastructure in Doña Ana County, including water supply and desalination projects. This creates a major new federal opportunity to strengthen the region’s water supply and put brackish groundwater to productive use.

$25 million for Valencia County water infrastructure: Vasquez secured a $25 million authorization for water and wastewater infrastructure in Valencia County, including stormwater management. The provision will help communities tackle flooding, improve water systems and build more resilient infrastructure.

Major modernization of the Rio Grande Environmental Management Program: Vasquez secured an expansion of the program to support projects addressing drought, wildfire and flood resilience, fish and wildlife habitat, sedimentation and salinity, water infrastructure, and invasive species. WRDA authorizes $20 million annually from fiscal years 2026 through 2030 and strengthens reporting and long-term planning for the Rio Grande.

Post-fire watershed assessments across New Mexico: Vasquez secured post-disaster watershed assessments covering areas impacted by the Buck, Trout, Cotton, South Fork and Salt Fires in Catron, Grant and Valencia Counties and near Ruidoso. These assessments can help identify long-term watershed restoration and flood-risk reduction projects needed to protect communities recovering from devastating wildfires.

Greater scrutiny of large new water users: Vasquez pushed for greater federal scrutiny of the enormous water demands that can come with new data centers, and WRDA requires the Army Corps to examine how new commercial and industrial water users affect federal water supply and water conservation projects. The provision provides a new tool for understanding how major new developments could put additional pressure on limited water resources.

New Rio Grande Basin water supply study: Vasquez secured a new Army Corps feasibility study focused on water supply and ecosystem restoration across the Rio Grande Basin in New Mexico. WRDA also adds the Middle Rio Grande to federal watershed assessments that examine future municipal, domestic, industrial, and agricultural water needs. This is especially important as New Mexico tries to meet its water compact obligations to Texas.

New tools to protect the Rio Grande: Vasquez secured the addition of the Middle Rio Grande to the Army Corps’ watershed assessment program, advancing efforts to improve the health and long-term resilience of the river. WRDA also expands drought-resiliency tools to address harmful nonnative riparian species such as salt cedar and restore native vegetation.

Federal action along the Rio Chama: Vasquez, along with the New Mexico delegation, secured language directing the Army Corps to expedite environmental and drought-resiliency project modifications along the Rio Chama and Rio Grande between Abiquiu and Cochiti Reservoirs. The provision advances his push for stronger federal management of this critical stretch of New Mexico’s river system.

This bill is supported by the American Farm Bureau Federation, American Iron and Steel Institute, American Public Works Association, American Rivers, American Road & Transportation Builders Association, American Society of Civil Engineers, American Society of Landscape Architects, Association of Equipment Manufacturers, National Association of Counties, National Association of Flood & Stormwater Management Agencies, National Association of Manufacturers, National League of Cities, National Parks Conservation Association, National Stone, Sand & Gravel Association, National Utility Contractors Association, National Water Resources Association, National Water Supply Alliance, U.S. Chamber of Commerce, and many others.

###

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Secures Critical Resources for New Mexico Water Infrastructure in House-Passed Bill

Jackson, MS – A Neshoba County man was sentenced to 108 months in prison for possessing with intent to distribute methamphetamine, announced U.S. Attorney Baxter Kruger of the Southern District of Mississippi, Special Agent in Charge Robert A. Eikhoff of the Federal Bureau of Investigation made the announcement.

According to court documents, Jerithan Willis, 43, possessed with intent to distribute methamphetamine in the Pearl River Community of Mississippi Band of Choctaw Indians Reservation.

In August of 2025, a federal grand jury indicted Willis for his role in the distribution of methamphetamine. On March 3, 2026, Willis entered a plea of guilty to the charge.

On September 23, 2026, Willis was sentenced to 108 months in federal prison, followed by five years of supervised release upon his release from prison. He was also fined $1,500.

The conviction was a result of an investigation by the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Safe Trails Task Force which is comprised of officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Choctaw Police Department, Neshoba County Sheriff’s Department, and various state and local law enforcement agencies.

U.S. Attorney Kruger commended the work of the Safe Trails Task Force, the Neshoba County Sheriff’s Department, and the Choctaw Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Kevin J. Payne, Brian K. Burns, and Special Assistant United States Attorney Kalleigh McCoy.
title: Neshoba County Man Sentenced for Possession with the Intent to Distribute Methamphetamine

Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, announced that the United States Department of Energy is making several awards through its SPARK Program that will help modernize the electric grid for Ohio.

Key among these awards is Federal funding of $136 Million for the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio (PUCO) that is part of a $1.9 Billion project. The Federal funds will cover half of the costs for an upcoming Ohio SPARK program project that seeks to improve electric grid infrastructure in the State. This funding is made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act passed by Congress in 2021. The release of these Federal funds follows an Op-Ed published last week in The Toledo Blade by Congresswoman Kaptur calling for the modernization of Northwest Ohio’s electrical grid.

"I am excited to see the fruits of a once-in-a-generation Federal infrastructure investment take root in our Northwest Ohio communities,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water. “Modernizing our region’s electrical grid is imperative to lower energy costs for hardworking families, small businesses, and manufacturers alike, and this funding award is a step forward in meeting the ever-growing demand that our economy needs to flourish.”

Signed into law in 2021, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act is a five-year bipartisan infrastructure law that marks the largest Federal investment made in American infrastructure in the last century. Systems across transportation, energy, and water have all received increased resources to further bolster improvements and repairs to our Nation’s infrastructure.

SPARK, or the “Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades,” is a United States Department of Energy program that supports States, Tribes, and electric utilities in their efforts to strengthen grid resilience and innovation. Ohio’s SPARK program specifically has several subprojects planned to improve electric grid infrastructure by implementing new technologies. Today’s announcement of a $136 Million award through this program will cover half of the $273 Million total cost of the planned Ohio SPARK projects, greatly lowering the costs that otherwise would have been passed on to ratepayers.

As a senior member of House Appropriations Committee, Congresswoman Kaptur is committed to securing Federal investments for our Northwest Ohio communities. She was a strong supporter of the legislation that made this Public Utilities Commission of Ohio award possible, and is encouraged that the Bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act continues to result in valuable Federal investments in our region’s highways, bridges, energy systems, drinking water infrastructure, and more.

Other SPARK awards announced today by the United States Department of Energy that are relevant for improved transmission and reliability in the overall Great Lakes Region and that will have indirect benefit for ratepayers in Northwest Ohio include:

$174 Million in Federal funds for the State of Indiana’s Office of Energy Development in support of a total $349 Million project called, “Expanding Cross-Regional Transfer Capability Across the PJM–MISO Seam Through Accelerated Reconductoring and Advanced Transmission.” With these funds, four sets of advanced and transmission technologies will be deployed across neighboring Indiana’s grid improving capacity monitoring, line rating, and advanced power flow control on the grid operated by PJM Interconnection and the Midcontinent Independent System Operation (MISO).

$50 Million in Federal funds for American Electric Power Service Corporation (AEPSC) to support a total $152 Million project called, “Next-Generation Optical Transport Network for Smart Grid Modernization.” AEPSC will uses these Federal funds to develop a unified, system-wide approach to expanding advanced communications across 527 AEP transmission network locations to improve the delivery of power, enhance operational visibility, and enable next-generation grid capabilities. The project includes the installation of 265 miles of underground fiber, and installation of new line rating technology deployment at 14 sites enhancing the ability to monitor and analyze electric capacity. While AEP Ohio primarily provides power in Central and Southern Ohio, the transmission network that will be improved with this Federal investment directly interfaces with the Regional PJM Interconnection grid servicing Northwest Ohio.

$21 Million in Federal funds for Electric Power Research Institute, Inc. (EPRI) to support a total $42 Million project called, “ATREES: Advanced Transmission Technologies for Reliable and Efficient Energy Supply.” This project proposes to deploy two advanced transmission technologies (ATTs)—advanced power flow controllers (APFCs) and dynamic line ratings (DLRs)—within the FirstEnergy (FE) and Salt River Project (SRP) transmission systems to maximize existing transmission capacity, accelerate load connections, and enhance reliability and energy deliverability.

A full copy of Congresswoman Kaptur’s Op-Ed published last week in The Toledo Blade calling for the modernization of Northwest Ohio’s electrical grid can be found online by clicking here.
title: Kaptur Announces $381 Million in US Department of Energy Awards to Improve Ohio’s Electric Grid

FEMA Delivers More Than $68 Million to Help Fire Departments and Other First Responder Organizations in the Midwest
FEMA will continue making awards over the next week
CHICAGO – This week, FEMA awarded more than $68 million in grant funding for fire departments and other first responder organizations in Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio and Wisconsin. FEMA disburses this money to support firefighters and other emergency personnel because they are often the first ones on the scene when disaster strikes. They play an essential role in keeping American communities safe. By empowering these emergency responders to strengthen and expand their capacity, FEMA is contributing to the nation’s overall resilience.
FEMA is administering these funds through its three Fiscal Year 2025 fire grant programs: the Assistance to Firefighters Grants, Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program, and Fire Prevention and Safety grant program. FEMA published the funding opportunities in May 2026, making $648 million available across all three programs. Over the next week, FEMA will continue awarding these funds directly to fire departments, first responder agencies, and other organizations focused on fire prevention and firefighter safety.
The funding announced this week in FEMA Region 5 includes more than $58 million under FEMA’s Assistance to Firefighters Grants. Recipients can use this money to outfit responders with compliant personal protective equipment, acquire emergency response vehicles, and develop health, wellness, and resiliency initiatives to prepare responders for incidents. Examples of awards include:
- More than $880,000 to the Grand Rapids Township Fire Department in Grand Rapids, Ohio
- More than $860,000 to the North Shore Fire Department in Milwaukee, Wisconsin
- More than $850,000 to the Village of Alsip Fire Department in Alsip, Illinois
FEMA also awarded more than $9.6 million under its Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response grant program. Recipients can use the money to cover personnel costs for firefighters, as well as recruitment efforts and retention programs. Examples of awards include:
- Nearly $940,000 to City of Brooklyn Center City Hall in Minneapolis, Minnesota
- More than $850,000 to the Michigan Association of Fire Chiefs in Ann Arbor, Michigan
- More than $830,000 to the Indiana Fire Chiefs Association Inc. in Indianapolis, Indiana
FEMA also awarded more than $700,000 under its Fire Prevention and Safety grant program. Recipients can use the money to fund scientific research and technology development that will strengthen community fire prevention programs and/or improve firefighter safety, health and well-being. Examples of awards include:
- Nearly $300,000 to Monroe Fire Protection District in Bloomington, Indiana
- More than $160,000 to Delta Charter Township in Lansing, Michigan
- More than $130,000 to Bloomfield Charter Township in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan
FEMA will continue awarding funding for its Fiscal Year 2025 fire grant programs over the next week. For information on all the awards issued thus far, visit the fire grants programs webpages: Assistance to Firefighters Grants, Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response, and Fire Prevention and Safety
title: FEMA Delivers More Than $68 Million to Help Fire Departments and Other First Responder Organizations in the Midwest

Congressman Glenn Ivey (MD-04) joined Governor Wes Moore today for the ribbon-cutting ceremony for Microsoft’s Discovery Center at the Capital of Quantum at the University of Maryland. The new quantum research center, in the heart of the University of Maryland’s Discovery District, will serve as a development hub for next-generation quantum technologies, marking a critical milestone in Maryland’s momentum to become a global leader for quantum information science and technology innovation.

“Quantum has the potential to transform every part of our economy and society and the opening of this new discovery center is another step in Maryland leading the nation in this emerging sector,” said Gov. Moore. “Our partnership with Microsoft and our continued investment in the Quantum ecosystem, creates jobs, stimulates our economy, and drives innovation. Together, we will solve some of the world’s most pressing challenges right here in Maryland.”

Launched by Governor Moore at IonQ's College Park headquarters in January 2025, the Capital of Quantum Initiative is a public-private partnership with the state, the University of Maryland, College Park and private partners to catalyze more than $1 billion in investments in Maryland’s quantum industry. Since the Capital of Quantum Initiative was announced, the State of Maryland and the University of Maryland have reached over $500 million in pledged investments to strengthen the state’s quantum ecosystem through academics, workforce development, and technical support.

“Maryland is positioning itself at the forefront of the quantum revolution, and the launch of the Discovery Center marks another major step forward,” said Congressman Glenn Ivey. “Here in Prince George’s County, we have the talent, research institutions, and entrepreneurial ecosystem to turn groundbreaking discoveries into new companies, good-paying jobs, and economic opportunity. I’m proud to join Governor Moore, the University of Maryland, Microsoft, and our partners in building the Capital of Quantum right here in Maryland and ensuring our region helps lead the next generation of American innovation.”

“This moment fulfills the commitment that UMD made a year ago when we joined the State of Maryland in announcing Microsoft as a member of our growing quantum community," said University of Maryland President Darryll J. Pines. "We are excited for the progress of this partnership and welcome the quantum companies investing in Maryland, as we continue to grow the Capital of Quantum.”

"One year ago, Governor Moore, the State of Maryland, the University of Maryland, and Microsoft came together around a shared ambition to advance Maryland's Capital of Quantum initiative," said Executive Vice President of Microsoft Discovery & Quantum Jason Zander. "Today, we are delivering on that commitment and creating an ecosystem to translate quantum innovation into lasting scientific and economic impact."

Since launching the Capital of Quantum Initiative, Maryland has welcomed nearly a dozen quantum startups to the Discovery District’s diverse network of quantum innovators, and IonQ has announced three significant mergers with quantum and aerospace firms.

Today’s ribbon-cutting ceremony coincided with QuEra, a Boston-based company that develops quantum computers using neutral atoms based on research conducted at both Harvard University and MIT, announcing that it would establish office space in the Discovery District. Last week, British-based Riverlane, a global leader in quantum error correction, announced that Maryland would become the site of its new U.S. headquarters. These expansions follow the University of Maryland welcoming additional commercial tenants to the Capital of Quantum like IQM and Quantum Motion, in addition to Microsoft’s cutting-edge quantum research lab.

Additional deals reached within the past year include an agreement between the State of Maryland and the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) providing up to $100 million in matching grants for state and private quantum investments, a major expansion of IonQ’s global headquarters, and the development of a new, 110,000 square-foot headquarters for Applied Research Laboratory for Intelligence and Security (ARLIS) at the University of Maryland—$65 million capital project that will advance national defense technology and solidify the state’s status as a global leader in quantum.

###
title: Team Maryland Welcomes New Microsoft Discovery Center at Ribbon Cutting Ceremony in University of Maryland’s Discovery District

Coast Guard urges Northeast mariners to seek safe harbor ahead of severe gales and seas
BOSTON – The Coast Guard Northeast District is urging the maritime community throughout the Northeast to secure vessels and remain in port ahead of a major offshore storm system forecast to impact the region from Sept. 24 through Sept. 28, 2026.
All mariners and coastal residents should prepare for gale-force winds, offshore 15-25-foot seas, heavy coastal rainfall, and significant tidal surge. These conditions present extreme danger to vessel navigation, stability, and shoreline infrastructure.
Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid hazardous conditions. Remain in port, seek safe harbor and/or secure your vessel for heavy winds and seas. Ensure you have the most up to date Marine Safety Information Broadcasts for your local area.
Marinas, yacht clubs and private residents should ensure all paddle craft and small boats are secured to prevent unintentional drifting out to sea. Unsecured gear that washes adrift triggers false-alarm search-and-rescue operations, diverting emergency crews from real life-threatening emergencies.
In case of a maritime emergency, contact your local Coast Guard Sector via VHF Channel 16 or at their respective phone number:
Sector Northern New England: (833) 449-2407
Sector Boston: (833) 449-0539
Sector Southeastern New England: (866) 819-9128

Ranking Member Scott Urges Education Department to Withdraw Proposed Grant Rule
WASHINGTON –House Committee on Education and Workforce Ranking Member Robert C. "Bobby" Scott (D-VA-03) urged Secretary of Education Linda McMahon to withdraw in its entirety the Department of Education's proposal to revise the Education Department General Administrative Regulations (EDGAR). EDGAR governs the Department's management of education grant programs. The proposed rule would give the Department broader power to steer grant awards, pull back continued funding for multiyear projects, and end grants at its own discretion, even when a recipient has done nothing wrong.
Ranking Member Scott warned that the proposal would expand the Department's authority over grants even as the Trump Administration is dismantling the Department. He also noted that the rule overlaps with the Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) government-wide grant proposal, which Congress recently blocked on a temporary basis.
“The Department’s Proposed Rule would inject dysfunction and chaos into the grant-making process, increase politicization, require the application of undefined standards, and further this Administration’s misuse of power in the distribution of federal funds,” wrote Ranking Member Scott. “[It] represents bad policy for the administration of our federal education programs and will ultimately harm students, schools, communities, researchers, universities, localities, states, and other organizations, institutions, and individuals that rely on these grant programs to improve educational programming, teaching, learning, and ultimately student outcomes.”
Ranking Member Scott also argued that the Department should not pursue new rulemaking while it fails to meet its current statutory obligations and works to hand off its congressionally mandated functions to other agencies.

SCRANTON - The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania announced that Jason Lozada, age 51, of Philadelphia, PA; Michael Rinaldi, age 49, of Philadelphia, PA; Ryan Kehoe, age 49, of Wilkes-Barre, PA; Michelle Hall, age 46, of Wilkes-Barre, PA; William Miller, age 43, of Forty-Fort, PA; Dylan Mohr, age 29, of Benton, PA; Keith Sassaman, age 48, of Shavertown, PA; and Melissa Butler, age 49, of Wilkes-Barre, PA, were indicted by a federal grand jury on drug trafficking and firearms charges.

According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, the indictment alleges that the eight defendants conspired to distribute and possess with intent to distribute controlled substances, including methamphetamine, from in or around August 2025 through in or around September 2026. The 21-count indictment also alleges that the defendants distributed and possessed with intent to distribute methamphetamine and fentanyl on numerous occasions, in addition to multiple firearms charges.

According to public records, Michael Rinaldi was sentenced on July 26, 2021, by Senior United States District Judge Robert D. Mariani to serve 235 months of imprisonment following a conviction on federal drug trafficking charges. On January 17, 2025, Rinaldi received an Executive Grant of Clemency from former President Joseph R. Biden Jr., commuting Rinaldi’s remaining term of imprisonment.

The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) led the investigation with assistance from the Luzerne County Drug Task Force, Hazelton Police Department, Wilkes-Barre Police Department, Philadelphia Police Department, Kingston Police Department, and Pittston Police Department. Assistant United States Attorney Kyle A. Moreno is prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities.

If convicted, the maximum penalty under federal law for the drug offenses charged is 20 years’ imprisonment per count. The maximum penalty for the firearm offenses charged ranges from 15 years to life imprisonment. Each charge comes with a term of supervised release following imprisonment, and a fine. A sentence following the finding of guilt is imposed by the Judge after consideration of the applicable federal sentencing statutes and the Federal Sentencing Guidelines.

Indictments are only allegations. All persons charged are presumed to be innocent unless and until found guilty in court.

17 charged in California fentanyl trafficking network following HSTF investigation
SAN DIEGO — During the first week of September, 17 alleged members of a San Diego-based fentanyl trafficking organization were charged in federal court with distributing large quantities of fentanyl throughout the city.
On Sept. 3, more than 200 federal, state and local law enforcement officials completed a coordinated takedown, arrested 13 defendants, and executed a search warrant in San Diego. Two defendants had prior arrests within the same week, and two are fugitives.
During this 10-month Homeland Security Task Force investigation, authorities seized more than 27 kilograms of fentanyl, preventing more than 13 million potentially lethal doses from being distributed in San Diego. Furthermore, agents seized more than 14.5 kilograms of cocaine, 0.6 kilograms of heroin, 0.8 kilograms of methamphetamine, and $49,000 in cash.
“This investigation has been a massive, life-saving success, but we are not satisfied yet,” said Homeland Security Investigations acting Executive Associate Director John Condon. “The combined effort of the HSTF, HSI San Diego, along with state and local partners has prevented more deadly fentanyl from reaching our neighborhoods, but this work continues. We will carry on using the full strength of this partnership to disrupt and dismantle every drug trafficking organization within our borders.”
Court documents state in November 2025, HSI San Diego and the San Diego County Sheriff’s Department, as part of the Fentanyl Abatement and Suppression Team, began an investigation into a drug trafficking organization supplying fentanyl to multiple street-level dealers in San Diego. On Nov. 25 that year, agents seized 4.8 kilograms of fentanyl, 0.8 kilograms of methamphetamine, $10,042 in cash and arrested Fabian Iniguez Ontiveros. A search of Iniguez’s cell phone revealed dozens of different fentanyl sub-distributors working for this drug trafficking organization.
Through various investigative methods, agents identified the organization’s leader and seized drug ledgers showing the organization routinely sold an ounce of fentanyl for $600 to $700, even making up to $20,000 in one night of deliveries. After Iniguez’s arrest, agents identified the new principal fentanyl distributor in the United States as Maricielo Ibarra Barrera.
During April and May 2026, investigators infiltrated the organization, participating in multiple fentanyl purchases coordinated by the organization and delivered by Ibarra. Investigators used months of surveillance operations to observe hundreds of instances when Ibarra drove from her residence to various locations around San Diego making multiple brief stops consistent with drug distribution.
From June through August 2026, investigators obtained federal wiretaps targeting cellphones the organization used. During that time, investigators intercepted dozens of calls and texts between members of the organization in the U.S. and Mexico, leading directly to several fentanyl seizures.
On Aug. 17, agents arrested Ibarra and executed a search warrant at her residence, where investigators discovered approximately 1.7 kilograms of fentanyl, 0.6 kilograms of heroin and $15,568 in cash. On Sept. 1, agents arrested two more members of the organization — Richard Alexander Arias Cruz and Juan Manuel Godinez — and seized 14.52 kilograms of cocaine and 20.28 kilograms of fentanyl.
Special agents and task force officers with HSI San Diego’s Fentanyl Abatement and Suppression Team led this investigation. HSI San Diego’s FAST is a multiagency task force comprising state, local and federal partners. First established in August 2022, FAST focuses on the disruption and dismantlement of criminal organizations that smuggle and distribute fentanyl within San Diego County. FAST targets fentanyl smuggling and distribution networks to counter the rising overdose rate and decrease the availability and accessibility of fentanyl.
title: 17 charged in California fentanyl trafficking network following HSTF investigation

LITTLE ROCK—Candelario Gameros-Ante, who is in the United States illegally, will spend the next 144 months in federal prison after being convicted of being an illegal alien in possession of firearms, being a felon in possession of firearms, and illegal reentry into the United States after he was previously deported. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, announced the sentence, which was handed down on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, by United States District Judge Brian S. Miller.

On June 3, 2025, Gameros-Ante, 47, of Mexico, was indicted by a federal grand jury in a three-count Indictment charging him with being a felon in possession of firearms, being an illegal alien in possession of firearms, and illegal reentry of a previously deported alien. On May 6, 2026, Gameros-Ante pleaded guilty to all three counts in the Indictment. In addition to the 12-year sentence, Judge Miller also sentenced Gameros-Ante to two years’ supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system.

On May 10, 2025, Searcy Police Department officers responded to a vehicle accident to discover that the driver, who was a minor, was shot in the neck and paralyzed. During a search of the area, officers discovered three shell casings in a yard in the proximity of the shooting and ultimately arrested someone who identified himself as Edgar Gameros. After obtaining a search warrant and searching his address, Searcy officers discovered three firearms, including the firearm used to shoot the minor driver. An investigation conducted by the Drug Enforcement Administration revealed that Gameros-Ante was in fact the person who previously self-identified as Edgar Gameros at arrest.

Gameros-Ante currently has Arkansas state charges of Terroristic Act and Battery-First Degree pending against him that are related to the shooting of the minor.

Gameros-Ante was previously removed from the United States to Mexico after a January 7, 2004, felony conviction for conspiracy to possess methamphetamine with intent to deliver. Gameros-Ante then illegally reentered the United States and assumed the identity of his brother, Edgar Gameros.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America , a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime.

The investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives with assistance from the Searcy Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Jordan Crews.

The milestone was reached after the U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Tampa seized more than 25,000 pounds of cocaine in three interdictions over the course of six days
WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement announcing that the U.S. Coast Guard has successfully seized more than 25,000 pounds of cocaine across three interdictions in less than a week, surpassing more than 260,000 pounds of cocaine seized overall in Operation Pacific Viper.
On September 11, a maritime patrol aircraft spotted a go-fast vessel in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, south of Costa Rica. U.S. Coast Guard Cutter (USCGC) Tampa launched its cutter boat and embarked helicopter to intercept it. The helicopter crew employed effective warning shots before Coast Guard law enforcement personnel conducted a boarding.
U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Tampa
During the boarding, Coast Guard personnel discovered suspected contraband that tested presumptively positive for cocaine. The crew of USCGC Tampa seized approximately 3,100 kilograms, or more than 6,800 pounds, of cocaine, embarked three suspected smugglers, and sank the vessel as a hazard to navigation.
Five days later, on September 15, USCGC Tampa’s embarked helicopter detected a suspected drug-smuggling vessel south of Panama. As the cutter responded, crews spotted a second suspected drug-smuggling vessel. Coast Guard personnel interdicted both vessels, seizing approximately 6,827 kilograms, or more than 15,000 pounds, of cocaine and embarked six suspected smugglers.
The following day, USCGC Tampa was diverted by a maritime patrol aircraft to a go-fast vessel south of Panama. Tampa launched its cutter boat and embarked helicopter, and the helicopter crew employed warning shots and disabling fire to stop the vessel. The cutter boat crew interdicted four suspected narco-terrorists and seized approximately 1,568 kilograms, or 3,456 pounds, of cocaine after the helicopter crew located a bale field.
Over the course of these three interdictions, the total amount of cocaine seized was 11,456 kilograms, or more than 25,256 pounds.
The seized drugs aboard the USCGC Tampa
With 1.2 grams of cocaine considered a potentially deadly dose, these three interdictions represent approximately 9.5 million potentially deadly doses kept from reaching communities. Since surpassing the 225,000-pound cocaine seizure milestone, the Coast Guard has continued Operation Pacific Viper’s aggressive counter-drug operations and has seized approximately 119,165 kilograms, or over 262,000 pounds, of cocaine in the Eastern Pacific.
“In just six days, the Coast Guard Cutter Tampa has seized more than 25,000 pounds of cocaine in three interdictions, bringing the total amount of cocaine seized in Operation Pacific Viper to more than 260,000 pounds,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “Thanks to the hard work of the brave men and women of the U.S. Coast Guard, more than 9 million lethal doses of cocaine will never reach our shores. President Trump promised to make America safe again, and stopping these drugs from infecting our communities is exactly how we do it. DHS is committed to keeping our borders secure, on land and at sea.”
“We own the sea, and Operation Pacific Viper is proving that every day,” said Admiral Kevin Lunday, Commandant of the Coast Guard. “Coast Guard crews are taking the fight to narco-terrorists in the maritime domain, denying them the routes they rely on to move drugs, money and violence, while protecting the homeland and disrupting transnational criminal organizations far from U.S. shores.”
Operation Pacific Viper has accelerated counter-drug operations in the Eastern Pacific, a primary corridor for narcotics smuggling from Central and South America. The Coast Guard has surged cutters, aircraft, and tactical teams to interdict, seize, and disrupt the flow of cocaine and other illicit drugs. These efforts are a critical component of the broader U.S. strategy to combat narco-terrorism and dismantle transnational criminal organizations.
Detecting and interdicting narco-terrorism on the high seas involves significant interagency and international coordination. U.S. Southern Command’s Joint Interagency Task Force-South, based in Key West, Florida, detects and monitors aerial and maritime transit of illegal drugs. Once interdiction becomes imminent, the law enforcement phase of the operation begins, and control of the operation shifts to the U.S. Coast Guard throughout the interdiction and apprehension.
Interdictions in the Eastern Pacific Ocean are performed by members of the U.S. Coast Guard under the authority and control of the Coast Guard’s Southwest District, headquartered in Alameda, California.
# # #
title: U.S. Coast Guard Surpasses 260,000 Total Pounds of Cocaine Seized in Operation Pacific Viper

WASHINGTON - Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21), a senior member of the House Agriculture Committee, joined Representatives Dan Newhouse (WA-04), David Rouzer (NC-07), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), and Monica De La Cruz (TX-15) in leading a bipartisan push urging the Trump Administration to secure stronger payment protections for American fresh produce growers and shippers doing business in Mexico through the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) process.

In a letter to U.S. Trade Representative Chief Agricultural Negotiator Julie Callahan and U.S. Department of Agriculture Under Secretary for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs Luke Lindberg, the lawmakers called on the Administration to secure protections in Mexico equivalent to those provided under the U.S. Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA). While American produce sellers have payment protections at home and Canada has established comparable protections, U.S. growers and shippers selling into Mexico remain exposed when buyers fail to pay or become insolvent.

In their letter, the lawmakers wrote:

“As the Administration works to reduce the agricultural trade deficit and expand export opportunities for U.S. specialty crops, American growers and shippers should have confidence that they will be paid for the products they sell abroad. Accordingly, we respectfully request that the Administration prioritize securing a commitment from Mexico through the USMCA process to establish protections for sellers of perishable agricultural commodities equivalent to those provided under the U.S. PACA Trust and Canada's Bill C-280. Establishing such a mechanism would create reciprocal protections across all three USMCA countries and provide greater certainty for American growers and shippers doing business across North America.”

The full letter can be found HERE.

BACKGROUND:

The Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA) has long provided U.S. growers and produce sellers with important protections when buyers fail to pay or become insolvent. In 2024, Canada enacted similar protections for fresh fruit and vegetable sellers, providing greater financial certainty for produce transactions in both countries.

Mexico does not currently provide U.S. growers and shippers with equivalent protections, leaving American sellers exposed when buyers fail to pay. As the United States and Mexico continue negotiations related to the 2026 review of the USMCA, including discussions on agriculture, Costa and his bipartisan colleagues are urging the Administration to close that gap and establish consistent payment protections for produce sellers across North America.
title: Costa Leads Bipartisan Push to Protect American Produce Growers in U.S.-Mexico Trade

EPA Lowers Costs, Helps Bring Leaking Underground Storage Tank Sites Back to Productive Use in the Midwest
Permitting reform championed by EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin leads to highest underground storage tank site closure rate on Midwest Tribal territories in more than a decade
Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced monitoring and remediation partnerships with Tribal communities brought a record number of underground storage tank sites back to productive use. In 2026, EPA addressed 10 leaking underground storage tank sites in Michigan and Minnesota, removed a leaking tank in Wisconsin while improving cleanup standards, and saved taxpayers more than $550,000.
“EPA’s permitting reforms are cutting unnecessary testing, saving time and taxpayer dollars, and putting those resources back to work where they matter most,” said EPA Regional Administrator Anne Vogel. “That means faster site investigations, quicker tank removals when needed, and stronger protection for nearby properties through close coordination with Tribes.”
Addressing UST sites has typically required years of monitoring, small-scale remediation and testing for contamination that may have migrated offsite. In September 2025, EPA issued streamlined guidance, Reassessing Exposure Threats from Petroleum Underground Storage Tank Releases, to create a faster process to evaluate and remove leaking underground tanks and reduce costs by hundreds of thousands of dollars. The guidance focuses on testing along exposure pathways, such as private drinking water wells and other places people come into direct contact contaminants, instead of full site assessments.
The 10 sites closed in 2026 include:
- Nine releases at four different sites in Saginaw Chippewa territory near Mount Pleasant, Michigan: 
  - Five at Next Door Store #5010, an operating gas station, located at 629 South Mission Street.
  - Two at Next Door Store #5039, an operating gas station, located at 5025 East Pickard Road.
  - One at Sagamok Shell, an operating gas station, located at 2428 South Leaton Road.
  - One at Krapohl Ford Lincoln Mercury, an operating car dealership, oil change facility and body shop, located at 1415 E Pickard Street.
- One release in Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux territory near Prior Lake, Minnesota:
  - Shakopee Dakota Convenience Store #2, an operating gas station, located at 14160 Wilds Path NW.
EPA also used Brownfields assessment funding to remove one tank from Mole Lake Smoke Shop, a former gas station, located at 3081 State Hwy 55 on Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa territory near Crandon, Wisconsin.
In L’Anse, Michigan, EPA worked extensively with Keweenaw Bay Indian Community to test whether contamination had spread offsite from Lute’s Corner Store, a former gas station across the street from Keweenaw Bay Ojibwa Community College. Ensuring the college was free from contamination opened the door for Keweenaw Bay Indian Community to put the property into a protected trust. The college can now expand its programs and offer additional outdoor learning opportunities to students.
Last year, EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin reaffirmed the EPA Policy for the Administration of Environmental Programs on Indian Reservations (EPA Indian Policy), which contains fundamental principles to guide EPA’s work with Tribes. EPA has made significant progress partnering with Tribes to remove leaking storage tanks, prioritize timely action and empower local expertise.
Underground storage tanks are found in nearly every community across the United States, with an estimated 542,000 tanks nationwide. They are used to store a variety of regulated products, mostly gasoline and diesel fuel at sites such as gas stations. Leaking or inadequately maintained tanks can pose serious threats to human health and the environment by contaminating soil and groundwater, risking fire, explosion or the release of dangerous vapors. EPA is responsible for monitoring and remediating UST sites in Tribal territories and has identified more than 60 potentially leaking tanks in EPA’s Great Lakes region.
To learn more about EPA’s work on underground storage tanks in Tribal communities, visit EPA’s website.

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), a Navy Reserve veteran and member of the House Armed Services Committee, joined Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18) and 12 fellow Democratic veterans in a letter urging President Trump to confront China over its support to Iran. The lawmakers sent the letter ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House this week.

On July 17, an Iranian ballistic missile struck sleeping quarters at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, killing three U.S. soldiers and wounding four others. The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran obtained high-resolution satellite imagery of the base from Chinese entities before and after the strike, and that U.S. officials connected that intelligence to the attack.

The lawmakers demanded Trump hold Xi accountable for Beijing’s role in U.S. troop deaths, and that he publicly condemn China’s support for IRGC operations.

“As veterans, we know what it means to send Americans into harm’s way, and we know what is owed to them in return: the truth, and a Commander-in-Chief willing to hold accountable anyone and everyone who might do harm to our troops,” the veterans wrote.

The lawmakers wrote: “We implore you to use your meeting to strongly condemn China’s sharing of satellite information that resulted in the deaths of three U.S. servicemembers in Jordan on July 17th, and demand that President Xi cease any support, cooperation, and information sharing with Iran and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).”

The letter also cited May State Department sanctions on three China-based firms for supplying satellite imagery of U.S. and allied military facilities to Iran.

They continued, “In May, the State Department sanctioned three China-based firms for supplying Iran with satellite imagery of American and allied military facilities. Senior officials in your administration reportedly spent months warning their Chinese counterparts that companies in their country were arming Iran with the targeting data. […] Your meeting with President Xi presents an important opportunity to condemn China’s role in arming and enabling Iran, and to demand an end to their support.”

Goodlander joined the letter alongside Democratic Veterans Caucus Chair Rep. Pat Ryan and Reps. Salud Carbajal, Gilbert Cisneros, Herbert Conaway, Jason Crow, Chris Deluzio, Chrissy Houlahan, Ted Lieu, Seth Moulton, Mike Thompson, Derek Tran, and Eugene Vindman.

Read the full letter here.

title: Goodlander Joins Democratic Veterans in Demanding Trump Hold China Accountable for Support to Iran

Fort Myers, Florida – Christiane Vinette Young (75), a Canadian national illegally present in the United States, has been charged by information with three counts of voting by an alien. If convicted on all counts, she faces a maximum penalty of three years in federal prison. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to the information, Young voted in three federal elections—the 2024 general election, 2022 general election, and 2022 primary—despite knowing that she was not a citizen of the United States.

An information is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty.

This case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and the Lee County Supervisor of Elections. It will be prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Benjamin S. Winter.
title: Illegal Alien Charged with Illegally Voting in Three Federal Elections

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Ahead of President Trump’s meeting with President Xi Jinping of the People’s Republic of China (PRC), U.S. Representative Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, is urging President Trump to maintain longstanding U.S. commitments in the Indo-Pacific while using direct diplomacy with Beijing to address the emerging national security risks posed by artificial intelligence and reduce the risk of dangerous miscalculation.

Ranking Member Bera joined East Asia and Pacific Subcommittee Chair Young Kim (CA-40) in a bipartisan letter outlining priorities for the Trump-Xi summit, including upholding America’s longstanding policy toward Taiwan and supporting Taiwan’s self-defense, securing the release of wrongfully detained Americans, disrupting the fentanyl trade, and reducing Beijing’s leverage over critical mineral supply chains.

In a separate letter, Bera, House Foreign Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gregory Meeks (NY-05), and House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa Ranking Member Sara Jacobs (CA-51) led 26 other House Democrats in calling for sustained dialogue between the United States and the PRC focused on artificial intelligence safety and risk.

“President Trump must make clear that the United States will not compromise its commitments to peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific for the sake of reaching a broader deal with Beijing. That means standing firm on Taiwan, pressing for the release of wrongfully detained Americans, combating the networks fueling the fentanyl crisis, and reducing dangerous supply-chain dependencies,” said Representative Bera.

“At the same time, the President should seek agreement on implementing AI guardrails and establishing reliable channels of communication that reduce the risk of miscalculation and provide mechanisms to deconflict during a crisis. During the Cold War, the United States and the Soviet Union developed similar mechanisms to communicate during moments of heightened tension. Washington and Beijing need those channels in place to address current and emerging threats,” Bera continued.

Standing Firm on Taiwan and Advancing U.S. Security Priorities

In the Bera-Kim letter, the lawmakers urge President Trump to maintain America’s longstanding One-China policy, guided by the Taiwan Relations Act, the three U.S.-China Joint Communiqués, and the Six Assurances. They specifically call for continued efforts to strengthen Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities and for the President to make clear that the United States will not consult with Beijing over arms sales to Taiwan.

“Maintaining America’s decades-long policy on Taiwan – guided by the Taiwan Relations Act, the three U.S.-China Joint Communiqués, and the Six Assurances – by increasing Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities, including through additional arms sales, is essential to U.S. security,” Bera and Kim wrote. “We urge you to make clear that the U.S. will not consult with the PRC on arms sales to Taiwan consistent with the U.S. One-China policy.”

The Kim-Bera letter also urges President Trump to press for the release of wrongfully detained U.S. citizens Min Zin and Youlin Chen, expand law-enforcement cooperation to target fentanyl precursor chemicals and the networks supporting the fentanyl trade, and reduce U.S. dependence on the PRC for critical minerals and key pharmaceutical inputs.

Read the full Bera-Kim letter here.

Establishing AI Guardrails and Crisis Communications

In the Bera-Meeks-Jacobs letter, the lawmakers led more than two dozen U.S. House Democrats in calling for a sustained dialogue between the United States and the PRC focused on AI safety and national security risks. The letter calls for shared standards and red lines around dangerous uses of AI, a standing crisis communications channel, mechanisms to report consequential AI incidents, and discussions on maintaining human control over nuclear weapons decisions and preventing advanced AI capabilities from reaching dangerous non-state actors.

“The purpose of a U.S.-China dialogue on AI should be focused and practical: reduce risks of miscalculation and address the dangers that neither country can manage alone,” the lawmakers wrote.

The Bera-Meeks-Jacobs letter also calls for a standing channel that both countries could use to report anomalous AI events and prevent misunderstandings, work on technologies that could help verify claims about AI activities, and narrowly scoped engagement between American and Chinese AI researchers focused on safety and risk while protecting U.S. technology and intellectual property.

“The promise and risks of AI are too great for the United States and China to not talk,” the lawmakers added.

Read the full Bera-Meeks-Jacobs letter here.

###
title: Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit, Bera Urges Trump to Stand Firm on Taiwan and Establish AI Crisis Guardrails
