Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Delivers State-of-the Art Air Traffic Control Management Tool to Transform The Flying Experience, Reduce Delays & Cancellations For the Traveling Public
Cutting-edge platform – called SMART – centralizes 200 data streams to produce recommendations that will improve how the airspace is managed and flights are scheduled
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator (FAA) Bryan Bedford today unveiled the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) – a cutting-edge tool that centralizes 200 data streams – including weather patterns, flight paths, traffic flow, and controller staffing metrics – into one platform. SMART’s AI-supported engine then synthesizes all this data to provide a comprehensive visualization of where planes are going, how much traffic the system can handle, and where congestion or weather could cause challenges.
Aviation specialists can use the platform to see what conditions will be in the future and make recommendations to fix the problems before they arise.
Key benefits of SMART include:
- Fewer delays & cancellations: Flyers will spend less time waiting on the tarmac, circling above their arrival airport, or dealing with diversions.
- Optimized airspace: Unlocks more capacity with more efficient routing around bad weather and congestion.
- More predictable operations: Preventing disruptions before they happen will reduce stress on controllers, let them focus on their more mission – safety.
- Lower ticket prices: When airlines waste less fuel, reduce staff overtime, and have more planes arrive on time, operating costs fall. That means cost savings for consumers.
“Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we are already making remarkable progress on building a brand new air traffic control system. But to really improve the flying experience for the American people, we needed to build a 21st century scheduling tool like SMART,” said U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy. “By fundamentally reshaping how we manage our airspace and preventing problems before they happen, SMART will slash those frustrating delays, reduce stress on air traffic controllers, and lower travel prices. The Trump Administration is committed to making flying hassle-free and affordable again.”
How it works:
At the beginning of each day, thousands of scheduled flights face built-in delays because demand for airspace can exceed an airport’s capacity. When too many flights are scheduled to use the same airspace at the same time, congestion builds and delays follow. Weather can further reduce available airspace capacity, forcing the FAA to reroute flights or shutdown large portions of the airspace. The result is a system that too often has to react to disruptions as they happen and unnecessary delays for passengers.
SMART fixes this by moving the FAA from a reactive approach to a predictive one. Instead of waiting for congestion to build, SMART uses data to help the FAA anticipate demand, weather and airspace constraints and plan hours, days and even weeks ahead.
The FAA began using SMART in a limited mode today in the airspace around Washington, D.C. and plans to gradually expand it to other parts of the country. SMART cannot be used to replace the critical role air traffic controllers play or take over control of an aircraft. All of SMART’s recommendations are reviewed by FAA staff, and local leadership at air traffic control facilities can choose to accept or pass on these scheduling suggestions.
Learn more about SMART and its specific capabilities here.
“Thanks to the leadership of President Trump and Secretary Duffy, we are moving at record speed to build the modern air traffic control system America needs,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford. “Combining SMART with our ongoing hardware upgrades gives us the tools to cut flight delays, optimize traffic, and keep airspace capacity across the country open–all while maintaining our gold standard of safety.”
“United believes that using SMART to open airspace intelligently has the potential to significantly reduce delays and cancellations during weather events. If it works as we think it can, it will do more to reduce delays and cancellations than anything that’s happened in decades,” said United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby. “We are excited to partner with the FAA to realize the potential benefits for our customers and employees.”
“Delta fully supports the FAA's efforts to modernize the National Airspace System through investments in technologies that can enhance operational efficiency, improve situational awareness, and help reduce congestion, including the SMART initiative,” said Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian. “We appreciate the FAA's collaborative approach and are actively engaged in the development process. As implementation begins, we look forward to continuing to work closely with the FAA and industry partners to ensure these tools deliver meaningful benefits for our people, our customers, and the broader aviation system.”
“We applaud Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford for their efforts to leverage technology to make the airspace more efficient and safer,” said American Airlines CEO Robert Isom. “We are working closely with the FAA on their ATC modernization efforts and programs like SMART - which when done thoughtfully and methodically will offer enhanced benefit to the traveling public.”
“I’m encouraged by the early work we have seen on the FAA’s new SMART system. It has the real potential to more efficiently manage the nation’s airspace and reduce flight delays and cancellations for our customers,” said Southwest Airlines CEO Bob Jordan. “We look forward to continuing our collaboration with Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford to move the new technology forward.”
“The United States has the largest and safest airspace in the world. The FAA SMART initiative is finally making sure we will have the best flight management tools as well,” said Airlines for America CEO & President Chris Sununu. “Its potential to strengthen safety, increase capacity and improve efficiency will have a direct positive effect on American travelers and the shipping public, reducing delays and cancellations across the country. We’re just in the initial stages, but it’s one of the most exciting and bold initiatives taken on by the FAA in decades.”
Additional Information:
President Trump & Secretary Duffy have already made incredible progress in transforming the national air space for the better.
Thanks to the Working Families Tax Cut, the Department is deploying $12.5B at breakneck speed – upgrading telecommunications lines, installing new radios and radars, and transitioning to electronic flight strips. This deployment is set to be completed by the end of 2028, with all 13 modernization workstreams on track.
Track the progress at Modern Skies.
Secretary Duffy has also worked around the clock to supercharge our air traffic control pipeline and recruit the next generation of air traffic controllers. We have:
- Recruited a record-breaking 4,000 controllers in the pipeline in the first 18 months of President Trump’s Administration
- Had the fastest application pace in American history for controllers
- Reached our highest staffing levels in a decade, with approximately 11,000 controllers currently in our towers
- Shaved more than five months off the time-to-hire process
- Incentivized the best and brightest with significant bonuses to older controllers to delay retirement AND cash awards to new hires
title: Trump’s Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy Delivers State-of-the Art Air Traffic Control Management Tool to Transform The Flying Experience, Reduce Delays & Cancellations For the Traveling Public

SYRACUSE, NY - Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today announced that he is cosponsoring H.R. 5487, the Keep the Lights Local Act, legislation to prohibit foreign ownership of American public utilities.

The bill would help protect ratepayers, strengthen accountability, and keep more of the money families pay through their monthly utility bills invested in American communities instead of supporting profits overseas.

Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) said, “Families in Central New York and the Mohawk Valley are paying too much to power their homes and businesses, and they shouldn’t be forced to subsidize the profits of foreign corporations. The Keep the Lights Local Act will help lower costs and keep more ratepayer dollars here at home - supporting grid reliability, infrastructure improvements, and local workers. Keeping control of energy production and transmission is essential to American energy and national security. I’ll keep fighting for affordable, reliable energy and real accountability for ratepayers.”

Under current federal law, foreign corporations and foreign governments are not prohibited from owning public utility holding companies in the United States. The Keep the Lights Local Act would close that gap by barring foreign corporations and governments from owning American public utility holding companies. The legislation was introduced by Representative Josh Riley (NY-19).

Mannion has made energy affordability and ratepayer protection a priority in Congress. He recently voted for the Ratepayer Protection Act to prevent data centers from shifting their electricity costs to families and small businesses, cosponsored legislation to end special federal tax breaks for data centers, and has called for data centers to mitigate impacts on local air quality, drinking water and water supplies.
title: Representative John Mannion Cosponsors the ‘Keep the Lights Local Act’ to Prohibit Foreign Ownership of American Utilities and Keep Ratepayer Dollars Invested at Home

Yesterday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries spoke to reporters following a roundtable in Providence with Representatives Seth Magaziner (RI-02) and Gabe Amo (RI-01) and local healthcare union leaders about how House Democrats are committed to ending the Republican healthcare crisis and building a healthcare system that works for everyday Americans.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good afternoon, everyone. It’s an honor and a privilege to be here in the great state of Rhode Island. Thank you, Congressman Magaziner for convening us and for your incredible leadership in the healthcare area and in many other areas on behalf of the people of the Ocean State. And I want to thank, of course, Congressman Magaziner and Congressman Amo, just for their partnership, their tremendous commitment to improving the lives of the people of Rhode Island and the American people and for the work that they have done and will continue to do to address the healthcare crisis that exists in the United States of America right now. Certainly want to thank Jesse and Lynn and Pat, of course, SEIU 1199, United Nurses, the AFL-CIO—all of the wonderful practitioners and healthcare providers who joined us at a very robust, comprehensive, thoughtful roundtable discussion where I learned a lot about the challenges that the people of Rhode Island are confronting in the midst of a Republican healthcare crisis that is worsening their ability to provide comprehensive and compassionate care to the people that they so ably serve.

And unfortunately, it’s a familiar conversation that I’ve had—as I’ve traveled the country—with people all throughout America. The Republican healthcare crisis is devastating the ability of healthcare providers to serve our families, our loved ones, our friends and our neighbors in the way that they are committed to doing, particularly in an environment now where you have so many healthcare providers who are overworked and underpaid, as well as, of course, far too often underappreciated. House Democrats appreciate the work of our healthcare heroes and are committed to making sure that we provide them with the support necessary to enable them to provide the best possible care to people here in Rhode Island and all throughout America.

As House Democrats, our core principle is that when you work hard and play by the rules, you should be able to live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. And that includes access to high-quality, affordable healthcare. It cannot be the situation where, in this country—the wealthiest country in the history of the world—accessing high-quality, affordable healthcare is simply a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. No, it has to be a right available to every single person here in Rhode Island, every single American. That is our commitment. A lot of work that needs to be done because of the Republican healthcare crisis. So we’re committed, as a top priority as House Democrats, to reversing these Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits. And then getting to work together with providers, like those we had an opportunity to talk with today, to construct the best possible healthcare ecosystem, a system that the American people deserve so they can go see a nurse and go see a doctor and get high-quality healthcare whenever and wherever they need it.

Republicans have made a lot of promises to the American people, and they’ve broken them all. Donald Trump promised to lower costs on day one, but costs haven’t gone down in the United States of America. Costs have gone up as a direct result of policies, including the Trump Tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans and the people of Rhode Island by thousands of dollars per year. Donald Trump promised not to start endless wars in the Middle East, but to stop them, and then turned around and has gotten us involved in a reckless and costly war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices on the people here in Rhode Island and beyond.

It was Donald Trump who promised to love and cherish Medicaid and then turned around, along with House Republicans and Senate Republicans, and enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, putting a target on hospitals here in Rhode Island, putting a target on nursing homes here in Rhode Island, putting a target on home care workers here in Rhode Island and putting a target on community-based health centers. Enough with this Republican assault on healthcare. We’re committed, as House Democrats, to turning it around.

Full press availability can be watched here.

###
title: LEADER JEFFRIES IN PROVIDENCE: “AFFORDABLE HEALTHCARE HAS TO BE A RIGHT AVAILABLE TO EVERY SINGLE AMERICAN”

BOSTON – A Lynn man has been arrested and charged for allegedly transporting a minor to engage in prostitution.

Emmanuel Devallon, 32, was indicted by a federal grand jury on one count of transporting a minor to engage in prostitution. The defendant was arrested on Sept. 17, 2026 and appeared in federal court in Worcester on Sept. 18, 2026. He remains detained in federal custody.

According to the indictment, in June 2026, Devallon knowingly transported a minor in interstate commerce with the intent that she engage in prostitution or any criminal sexual activity.

The charge of transporting a minor to engage in prostitution provides for a minimum mandatory sentence of ten years and up to life in prison, five years and up to life on supervised release, and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement. Valuable assistance in the investigation was provided by the Peabody Police Department, Lynn Police Department and Boston Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Craig E. Estes, of the Human Trafficking & Civil Rights Unit is prosecuting the case.

If you or someone you know may be impacted or experiencing commercial sex trafficking, please contact USAMA.VictimAssistance@usdoj.gov .

This case was brought in collaboration with Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .

The details contained in the indictment are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law.
title: Lynn Man Indicted for Transporting Minor to Engage in Prostitution

(Towson, MD) – Maryland Congressman Johnny Olszewski today issued the following statement after President Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and POLITICO from the White House and confiscated the press credentials of their journalists. The three outlets announced today they are suing the Trump Administration over the ban.

“A free and independent press is fundamental to our democracy. President Trump’s attack on news organizations he doesn’t like is outrageous and unconstitutional.

This issue is bigger than any one news outlet. It’s about whether the President of the United States gets to decide which journalists are allowed access to him based on favorable coverage. He doesn’t.

Unfortunately, this is part of a broader pattern from the Trump Administration — using the power of the federal government to punish journalists and restrict the ability of the press to hold those in power accountable. That is the kind of overreach we associate with authoritarian regimes, not a healthy democracy. I commend other, competing news organizations for standing in solidarity to defend the First Amendment.

The White House belongs to the American people. They have a right to an independent press that asks tough questions, reports the facts, and holds their government accountable.”
title: Olszewski on Trump’s Attack on the Press: “Outrageous and Unconstitutional”

GLEN COVE, NY — Congressman Tom Suozzi (NY-03) was recognized today by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce with its “Advocate for American Business” Award during a stop of the Chamber’s national Free Enterprise Express Opportunity Tour at Standard Bots in Glen Cove.

U.S. Chamber Executive Vice President and Chief Policy Officer Neil Bradley presented Suozzi with the award, recognizing his bipartisan, commonsense approach to governing, his leadership as Democratic Co-Chair of the Problem Solvers Caucus, and his work on affordability, immigration reform, and other issues affecting American families and businesses.

Suozzi is the first Democratic Member of Congress to receive the award during the Chamber’s national Opportunity Tour.

“The U.S. Chamber is proud to recognize Rep. Tom Suozzi as the first Democratic Member of Congress to receive this award on the Free Enterprise Bus Tour. Rep. Suozzi has been a steadfast defender of free market capitalism and his approach to policy prioritizes real solutions for American families and businesses. We look forward to continuing to work with him to advance free enterprise policies that allow businesses, workers, and communities to grow and thrive,” said Bradley.

“I want to thank the U.S. Chamber of Commerce for this recognition and for bringing the Free Enterprise Express here to Glen Cove,” said Suozzi. I’ve always believed that the best way to grow our economy is to give people the opportunity to work hard, build something, create jobs, and succeed. Companies like Standard Bots are doing exactly that right here on Long Island. We need to work together — Democrats and Republicans — to bring down costs, support our small and growing businesses, and create an environment where American innovation can thrive. That’s how we grow our economy, create opportunity, and keep the American Dream alive for the next generation.”

The event was held at Standard Bots, a growing Glen Cove company that designs and assembles industrial robotic arms in the United States. The company provided a local example of the entrepreneurship, innovation, and job creation the Chamber’s nationwide tour is seeking to highlight.

“We’re proud to welcome Congressman Suozzi and the U.S. Chamber’s Free Enterprise Express to Standard Bots here in Glen Cove,” said Evan Beard, Co-Founder and CEO of Standard Bots. “We believe America can and should lead the world in advanced manufacturing and robotics. By encouraging innovation, investment, and entrepreneurship, we can build many more things in America, create good jobs, and compete globally.”

The Chamber also cited Suozzi’s leadership of the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus, his five-point affordability plan, his leadership on the Promise to America, and his efforts to advance bipartisan immigration reform.

The Free Enterprise Express Opportunity Tour is traveling across the country for six weeks, visiting 20 states and holding more than 50 events highlighting local businesses, employers, workers, and community leaders. The tour is designed to showcase the role of entrepreneurship, innovation, competition, and economic growth in creating jobs and opportunity.

The tour is part of the U.S. Chamber’s New Fight for Free Enterprise, a multi-year initiative to promote free enterprise and highlight businesses and entrepreneurs in communities across the country.

###
title: Suozzi Recognized as First Democratic Member of Congress To Be Awarded U.S. Chamber’s “Advocate for American Business” Award

Mexican National Sentenced in Scheme to Bribe Ecuadorian and Mexican Government Officials
Javier Aguilar, 52, a Mexican national living in Houston, Texas, and a former oil trader, was sentenced in Brooklyn, New York, to four years in prison for his role in two separate schemes to bribe foreign officials in Ecuador and Mexico. He was also ordered to pay $7.13 million in forfeiture and a $100,000 fine.
“This sentence makes clear that corrupt actors, like Javier Aguilar, who facilitated and led two major international bribery and money laundering schemes will be brought to justice and punished accordingly,” said Assistant Attorney General Andrew A. Tysen Duva of the Justice Department’s Criminal Division. “We will root out those who brazenly undermine the rule of law and use our financial system to launder their corrupt funds, and we will prosecute them to the fullest extent of the law.”
“This sentence sends a powerful message of deterrence to those who might be tempted to engage in similar bribery schemes,” said U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York. “This sentencing is further demonstration of our office’s long-standing commitment to rooting out corruption in the commodities markets. We will be indefatigable in protecting American interests from corruption that unfairly tilts the playing field and threatens American businesses.”
“Aguilar bribed, falsified, manipulated the system, and engaged in several corrupt financial practices, all while using U.S. financial institutions to carry out his criminal actions,” said Assistant Director Heith Janke of the FBI Criminal Division. “This case demonstrates the broad reach of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the FBI’s ability to investigate and bring criminals to justice who seek to engage in this type of crime.”
According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Aguilar paid more than $1 million in bribes to officials of Ecuador’s state-owned oil company Petroecuador, and of PEMEX Procurement International (PPI), a subsidiary of Mexico’s state-owned oil company PEMEX, in order to obtain and retain business for his then-employer, Vitol Inc. The trial evidence showed that between 2015 and 2020, Aguilar was a trader at Vitol Inc. (Vitol), the U.S. affiliate of one of the largest energy trading companies in the world. As part of the scheme, Aguilar and his co-conspirators agreed to bribe senior Ecuadorian officials to obtain a $300 million contract to purchase fuel oil for Vitol. Aguilar and his co-conspirators used another Middle Eastern state-owned entity to circumvent Petroecuador’s restrictions on contracts with private companies. In return for the promise and payments of bribes, the Ecuadorian officials then ensured that the Middle Eastern state-owned entity and Vitol were awarded the contract.
To conceal the scheme, Aguilar and his co-conspirators used a series of fake contracts, sham invoices, and shell entities incorporated in Curaçao, Panama, and the Cayman Islands. Aguilar also used alias email accounts to communicate with his co-conspirators.
The evidence at trial also demonstrated that Aguilar used the same system of shell entities and sham invoices to launder bribe payments to two officials at PPI. In total, Aguilar paid approximately $600,000 in bribes to PPI officials to obtain contracts for Vitol to supply hundreds of millions of dollars of ethane gas to PEMEX.
The jury convicted Aguilar of conspiracy to violate the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) and violating the FCPA in connection with the Ecuador bribery scheme, and conspiracy to commit money laundering in connection with the Ecuador and Mexico bribery schemes. He separately pleaded guilty to conspiracy to violate the FCPA and to violate the Travel Act in connection with the Mexico bribery scheme.
Seven of Aguilar’s co-conspirators, including three foreign government officials, have pleaded guilty for their roles in the schemes. These individuals have collectively agreed to forfeit more than $63 million in proceeds from the schemes.
In December 2020, Vitol admitted to bribing officials in Ecuador, Mexico, and Brazil in violation of the anti-bribery provisions of the FCPA. Vitol entered into a deferred prosecution agreement with the Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of New York. As a part of the resolution, Vitol agreed to pay a combined $135 million in penalties as part of a coordinated resolution with the Justice Department, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, and authorities in Brazil.
FBI Miami’s International Corruption Squad investigated the case.
Assistant Chief Derek J. Ettinger of the White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section, Trial Attorney D. Hunter Smith of the Money Laundering, Narcotics and Forfeiture Section (MNF), and Assistant U.S. Attorney Nick M. Axelrod for the Eastern District of New York are prosecuting the case, with assistance from Deputy Chief Suzanne Elmilady and Assistant U.S. Attorney Sherin Daniel for the Southern District of Texas. Assistant U.S. Attorney Jonathan P. Lax for the Eastern District of New York was also responsible for the case. The MNF Special Financial Investigations Unit and the Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs also provided substantial assistance.
The Criminal Division’s White Collar and Corporate Enforcement Section is responsible for investigating and prosecuting FCPA and Foreign Extortion Prevention Act (FEPA) matters. Information about the Justice Department’s FCPA and FEPA enforcement efforts can be found at www.justice.gov/criminal/fraud/fcpa.
MNF’s mission is to take the profit out of crime, eliminate drug cartels, and protect the U.S. financial system. MNF pursues criminal prosecutions and criminal and civil asset recovery actions involving: financial facilitators who launder profits for criminals; financial institutions and their officers and employees whose actions threaten the U.S. financial system and financial institutions; international money launderers who support transnational organized crime; and the top command and control of international drug trafficking organizations.
MNF’s International Unit investigates and prosecutes cross-border money laundering schemes involving transnational criminal organizations, cartels, foreign official corruption and related money laundering affecting the U.S. financial system and prosecutes criminal cases and civil forfeiture matters to recover the proceeds of those crimes.
title: Mexican National Sentenced in Scheme to Bribe Ecuadorian and Mexican Government Officials

Projects will test next-generation geothermal technologies and explore promising resources to support affordable, reliable, secure American energy
September 21, 2026
WASHINGTON—The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced more than $99 million for 21 projects selected to advance geothermal energy development across the United States. The projects will conduct field-scale tests of next-generation geothermal technologies and exploration drilling to characterize and potentially confirm promising geothermal resources.
Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, the Energy Department is advancing American geothermal innovation to unlock the nation’s abundant domestic energy resources. Geothermal can provide reliable, around-the-clock power to help meet growing demand while strengthening U.S. energy security.
“These projects will empower American innovators to unlock the tremendous geothermal resources beneath our feet,” said DOE Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we’re advancing next-generation geothermal technologies that can lower costs, strengthen American energy dominance, and turn more of our vast domestic geothermal resources into reliable and affordable power.”
The 21 projects will advance geothermal development in two key areas. Five projects will conduct field-scale enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) tests to validate technologies under real-world conditions, while 16 additional projects will conduct exploration drilling to identify and characterize promising next-generation geothermal resources. Together, these efforts will help reduce technical and development risk and provide the information needed to support future commercial projects and investment.
Data generated by these projects will be publicly available through DOE’s Geothermal Data Repository (GDR), giving industry, researchers, and other stakeholders access to information from the field tests and geothermal exploration activities. Making these data available can extend the value of the projects beyond individual sites by helping inform future technology development and geothermal exploration across the industry.
Selection for award negotiations is not a commitment by DOE to issue an award or provide funding. Before funding is issued, DOE and the applicants will undergo a negotiation process, and DOE may cancel negotiations and rescind the selection for any reason during that time.
title: Energy Department Announces $99 Million for 21 Projects to Advance U.S. Geothermal Energy Development

WICHITA, KAN. – A Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) led operation yielded the dismantling of a drug trafficking ring in Kansas operated on behalf of a Mexican drug cartel. Ringleader, Euriel Talavera, 32, of Wichita and 14 other defendants pleaded guilty to criminal charges following a multi-agency investigation which included federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies.

According to court documents, in December 2022, the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), and Wichita Police Department began investigating a drug trafficking ring in Wichita. Investigators learned that the Sinaloa Cartel and cartel associates controlled the operation that distributed fentanyl, cocaine, and methamphetamine. Every few weeks, the traffickers traveled from Wichita to Phoenix, Arizona, or other locations to pick up large quantities of drugs and then returned to Wichita for distribution. Talavera stayed in regular contact with cartel members in Mexico.

Talavera pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl and was sentenced 228 months in prison.

“HSTF’s mission is to save lives by arresting transnational drug dealers and confiscating the poison they peddle before it reaches our communities. When investigators learned about an arrangement to bring 160,000 counterfeit Percocet pills laced with fentanyl to Wichita for distribution, law enforcement set up surveillance, observed the exchange, and after a traffic stop, intercepted the drugs,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser.

“This is another example of how the HSTF model is improving the safety of our communities by detecting, disrupting, and dismantling drug trafficking organizations. We will continue to work tirelessly with our partners to identify and hold accountable any organization or individual looking to perpetuate the flow of drugs into Kansas,” said FBI Kansas City Special Agent in Charge Chris Ormerod.

“Cartels like Sinaloa are not just trafficking drugs, they are trafficking death into our communities,” said HSI Kansas City acting Special Agent in Charge Rick Sabatini. “This operation proves what happens when HSI and our HSTF partners bring relentless pressure to bear: we dismantle the networks pushing fentanyl and methamphetamine into Kansas, seize their profits, and put their people in prison. If you work for a cartel, we will find you, we will build the case, and we will bring the full weight of federal law enforcement to your doorstep.”

Fourteen other defendants have pleaded guilty to crimes related to the case:

• Jonathan Gutierrez-Diaz, 30, an illegal alien from Mexico, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl and was sentenced 136 months in prison. • Joe Louis Washington, 33, of Wichita, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and was sentenced to 120 months in prison. • Aron Garcia-Campa, 36, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute methamphetamine and was sentenced to 96 months in prison. • Alexis Ortega-Ramos, 29, an illegal alien from Mexico, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl and was sentenced to 72 months in prison. • Shelan D. Peters, 24, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and was sentenced to 60 months in prison. • Jermel L. Goines, 44, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and was sentenced to 60 months in prison. • Breili Osmani Sermeno-Hernandez, 42, an illegal alien from Guatemala, pleaded guilty to one count of use of a communication facility to facilitate a drug trafficking crime and was sentenced to 48 months in prison. • Heiu Kevin Nguyen, 33, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of use of a communication facility to facilitate a drug trafficking crime and was sentenced to 24 months in prison. • Katia Nevarez, 29, of Wichita pleaded guilty to one count of money laundering and was sentenced to12 months and one day in prison. • Richard Oral Mathie, 60, of Elmendorf, Texas, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to distribute fentanyl but absconded before sentencing.

Santiago Rodriguez, 25, Angel Garcia, 26, Dominitrix M. Jones, 33, Alonso Pacheco-Tabullo, 23, all of Wichita pleaded guilty to crimes related to this case and were sentenced to probation.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Kansas Highway Patrol (KHP), and the Wichita Police Department investigated the case.

This operation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Kansas City comprises agents and officers from FBI; Homeland Security Investigations; Drug Enforcement Administration; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; and the Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation Division, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Kansas.

###
title: HSTF Operation leads to more than a dozen defendants in Kansas sentenced for working for Mexican drug cartel

HARRISBURG - The United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Pennsylvania announced that Sean Stark, age 38, of Carlisle, Pennsylvania, was charged by criminal information with involuntary manslaughter.

According to United States Attorney Brian D. Miller, the information alleges that on March 12, 2026, Stark killed Private First Class Krystofer Lopez at Letterkenny Army Depot while conducting firearms training in a grossly negligent manner.

Along with the information, the U.S. Attorney’s Office also filed a plea agreement in which Stark agreed to waive indictment and plead guilty to the information. Stark will enter a plea of guilty in accordance with the plea agreement at a hearing to be scheduled by the court.

“The circumstances surrounding Mr. Lopez’s death are heartbreaking for his family and loved ones,” said U.S. Attorney Miller. “I hope this prosecution brings some relief for the family while ensuring that justice is delivered.”

The U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Division investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorneys Scott Ford and Alisan Martin are prosecuting the case.

If convicted, Stark faces a maximum penalty for this offense of eight years of imprisonment, a term of supervised release following imprisonment, and a fine. A sentence following the finding of guilt is imposed by the Judge after consideration of the applicable federal sentencing statutes and the Federal Sentencing Guidelines.

Criminal informations are only allegations. All persons charged are presumed to be innocent unless and until found guilty in court.

Two Granddaughters, Two Tattoos

Today, Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) announced she received another tattoo to mark her granddaughter Sadie’s 18th birthday:

“One tattoo was a story – two is now tradition, and one I am so happy to carry on to show my love for my grandchildren. After my first tattoo for my granddaughter Rigby’s 18th birthday, my granddaughter Sadie asked that I get another for hers. I said absolutely. When Sadie was a baby, she'd lift her head like a little bird coming out of a nest, my le petit oiseau, French for little bird. That is why my new tattoo is a swallow.”

Joe Capobianco, owner of Hope Tattoo Gallery in New Haven, gave DeLauro the new ink. DeLauro received her first tattoo in 2023 with her granddaughter Rigby. “I am thankful to Joe and Hope Tattoo Gallery for a beautiful new piece of body art,” DeLauro said.

“People keep asking me if there will be more tattoos to come. I have more grandchildren, so the answer is probably yes. And every one of them will be worth it.”
title: DeLauro Gets Another Tattoo

WASHINGTON (Sept. 21, 2026) — The National Transportation Safety Board today issued safety recommendations urging the rail industry to end the practice of requiring workers to ride rail equipment to provide point protection during shoving movements.
The recommendations call on railroads and the Federal Railroad Administration to prohibit the practice, require safer alternatives, and identify hazards before operations begin.
"Railroad workers deserve a safe workplace and should never have to risk their lives to do their jobs," said NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy. "Our investigations have repeatedly shown that riding moving rail equipment can have deadly consequences. Railroads have safer alternatives, and they should use them."
During a shoving movement, a locomotive pushes railcars while a worker ensures the track ahead is clear. Some railroads allow workers to perform this task while riding on the lead railcar.
Workers riding railcars face numerous hazards, including falls from moving equipment, being struck by vehicles at highway-railroad grade crossings, and being pinned or crushed during collisions or derailments. Employees can also be thrown from equipment or trapped between railcars and nearby structures.
Since October 2020, the NTSB has investigated 16 accidents involving workers riding rail equipment during shoving movements. Fourteen workers were killed and two were seriously injured. Since August, NTSB has opened two additional investigations.
The NTSB found that federal regulations do not adequately address these risks and do not consistently require crews to identify hazards before work begins. Important risk factors can include limited visibility, close clearances, track and walkway conditions, grade crossings, switches, and derails.
Safer alternatives are available, including providing point protection from the ground, using vehicles, cameras, and other technologies that allow crews to monitor the track ahead without riding rail equipment.
"Repeated accidents that seriously injure or kill railroad workers are unacceptable," said NTSB Vice Chairman Michael Graham. "These recommendations provide a safer path forward by reducing unnecessary exposure to hazards and strengthening pre-job hazard assessments."
The NTSB recommends that railroads conduct and document site-specific hazard assessments before work begins. The assessments should evaluate environmental and operational hazards, available alternatives to riding equipment, and the safest method of providing point protection. Findings should be discussed with employees during pre-job safety briefings.
“Railroads can better protect workers during shoving movements by requiring pre-job hazard assessments, safety briefings and alternatives to riding equipment,” said NTSB Board Member Tom Chapman. “These measures will help ensure every rail worker goes home safely.”
“This report shows that the same safety issues continue to cause rail worker deaths and injuries,” said NTSB Board Member John DeLeeuw. “Moving rail equipment safely should not expose employees to unacceptable risk.”

A Chicago felon who perpetrated a sophisticated and extensive fraud scheme involving stolen and altered U.S. Treasury checks presented at Eastern Iowa financial institutions in 2023 and 2024 was sentenced on September 9, 2026, to more than 13 years in federal prison.

Tyrone Terrell Harris, age 34, from Chicago, Illinois, received the prison term after he pled guilty on March 24, 2026, to five counts of theft of government property, five counts of aggravated identity theft, one count of money laundering, and one count of money laundering conspiracy.

Evidence presented in Harris’s case, as well as at other hearings in related cases, showed that Harris provided nearly $1.5 million in stolen and altered U.S. Treasury checks to co-conspirators for presentation to Eastern Iowa financial institutions. Harris recruited his co-conspirators, including felons and a sex offender, from across the United States. Once in Eastern Iowa, Harris armed the co-conspirators with fake driver’s licenses in the names of the persons to whom the U.S. Treasury had issued the checks and these victims’ true social security numbers and dates of birth. In some cases, Harris also supplied the co-conspirators with incorporation documents fraudulently obtained from the Iowa Secretary of State. The co-conspirators then opened individual and corporate bank accounts in the victims’ names and quickly withdrew the fraud proceeds in cash to evade detection by law enforcement.

At his sentencing hearing, Harris admitted his involvement with 15 stolen or altered U.S. Treasury checks, between March 2023 and February 2024, with a combined face value of $1,437,833.36. Harris perpetrated his fraud, identity theft, and money laundering crimes against 11 victims. Harris and his co-conspirators successfully obtained $462,696.56 in taxpayer money.

Harris has prior criminal convictions in Illinois, Georgia, and Oklahoma. He has prior felony convictions for attempting to elude a police officer, driving a motor vehicle under the influence, and running a roadblock in Oklahoma. He has battery and reckless conduct convictions in Illinois. The reckless conduct conviction stemmed from a drive-by shooting in which Harris was the driver.

Harris was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by Chief United States District Judge C.J. Williams. Harris was sentenced to 160 months’ imprisonment. He was ordered to make $760,575.43 in restitution to the victims. He must also serve a three-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in federal system. In sentencing Harris to his 160-month prison term, Chief Judge Williams stated that Harris’s crime was sophisticated and constituted a “massive fraud.”

Harris is the latest defendant to plead guilty in the Northern District of Iowa as part of the fraudulent U.S. Treasury check scheme. Other individuals convicted include:

Edgar Stacey Delgado , age 32, from East Los Angeles, California, was convicted of one count of Forged Endorsement on a U.S. Treasury Check and one count of Aggravated Identity Theft. On February 26, 2025, Delgado was sentenced to 18 months’ imprisonment and three years of supervised release, and he was also ordered to pay $201,510.69 in restitution.

Irvin Lantern , age 68, from Chicago, Illinois, was convicted of one count of Forged Endorsement on a U.S. Treasury Check and one count of Aggravated Identity Theft. On February 4, 2025, Lantern was sentenced to 24 months’ imprisonment and three years of supervised release, and he was also ordered to pay $33,000 in restitution. Lantern has an extensive criminal history in Illinois.

Dale Ford , age 60, from Cedar Rapids, Iowa, was convicted of one count of Forged Endorsement on a U.S. Treasury Check and one count of Aggravated Identity Theft. On March 14, 2025, Ford was sentenced to 36 months’ imprisonment and three years of supervised release, and he was also ordered to pay $91,916 in restitution. Ford had over 30 prior criminal convictions by the time of his federal sentencing hearing.

Tim Dale Howe , age 62, from Cedar Rapids, Iowa, was convicted of one count of Forged Endorsement on a U.S. Treasury Check and one count of Money Laundering Conspiracy. On July 28, 2025, Howe was sentenced to 6 months of imprisonment, 6 months of home confinement, and three years of supervised release, and he was ordered to pay $87,851.37 in restitution. Howe previously was convicted in Florida in 2005 for committing a sex offense against a child.

Cornelius Devon Hicks , age 50, from Cedar Rapids, Iowa, was convicted of one count of Forged Endorsement on a U.S. Treasury Check and one count of Money Laundering. On July 7, 2025, Hicks was sentenced to 41 months’ imprisonment and three years of supervised release, and he was ordered to pay $47,175.65 in restitution. Hicks has an extensive criminal history in Iowa and Tennessee.

Harris is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Timothy L. Vavricek and was investigated by the Internal Revenue Service - Criminal Investigation and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. The Cedar Rapids Police Department assisted in the investigation.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division. The core mission of the Fraud Division is to zealously investigate and prosecute those who steal or fraudulently misuse taxpayer dollars. Department of Justice efforts to combat fraud support President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file numbers are 25-CR-97 (Harris), 23-CR-90 (Delgado), 23-CR-49 (Ford), 23-CR-2077 (Lantern), 24-CR-63 (Howe), and 24-CR-80 (Hicks).

Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.
title: Chicago Felon Sentenced to More Than Decade in Federal Prison in “Massive” U.S. Treasury Check Scheme

On behalf of the United States of America, I extend warm congratulations to the people of Armenia on your Independence Day.

CLEVELAND – A 30-year-old man with a history of drug trafficking offenses has been sentenced to prison after he was once again found in violation of federal drug and firearms laws.

Jermaine S. Cottrell, of Cleveland, was sentenced to 155 months (12.91 years) in prison by U.S. District Judge Donald C. Nugent after pleading guilty in June to:

Felon in Possession of a Firearm and Ammunition; prior convictions include Drug Trafficking in 2018, 2020, and 2021

Possession with Intent to Distribute Controlled Substances (3 counts).

Judge Nugent also ordered Cottrell to serve three years of supervised release and to forfeit a pistol, magazine, and ammunition.

According to court documents and evidence presented before the court, in September 2025, Cottrell was located in the parking lot of a CVS pharmacy. As officers attempted to box in the car to prevent flight, Cottrell, used his vehicle to ram into police cars and then fled on foot.

While officers attempted to secure him in handcuffs, Cottrell shoved several small plastic bags of narcotics into his mouth which he later spit out while EMS transported him to a hospital. A forensic analysis of the drugs in Cottrell’s possession were determined to include cocaine, methamphetamine, heroin, fluorofentanyl, and fentanyl. A firearm with an extended magazine was in the driver’s side door of the vehicle Cottrell was operating.

The investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) and the Lakewood Police Department.

Assistant United States Attorney Jennifer J. King led the prosecution for the Northern District of Ohio.
title: Career Offender Sentenced to Nearly 13 Years in Prison for Drug Trafficking and Firearms Offenses

LAS VEGAS – A Las Vegas man was sentenced today by United States District Judge Gloria M. Navarro to 97 months in prison to be followed by 35 years of supervised release for maintaining two large collections of child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and distributing CSAM utilizing a peer-to-peer network. The government requested a sentence of 97 months in prison.

“This defendant deliberately engaged in the sick, destructive trade of child exploitation, capitalizing on the unimaginable suffering of innocent children,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Today’s lengthy sentence ensures that a dangerous, unrepentant predator is stripped of his freedom and permanently cut off from fueling this vile digital marketplace. We will never stop hunting down and aggressively prosecuting those who profit from the abuse of the most vulnerable among us.”

“Randall William Rushton’s sentence underscores the FBI’s unwavering commitment to protecting our most vulnerable citizens - our children,” said Special Agent in Charge Christopher S. Delzotto for the FBI Las Vegas Field Office. “Furthermore, it serves as a definitive reminder of our relentless pursuit of perpetrators who exploit youth. Our communities are undeniably safer with this individual incarcerated. Expelling those who prey on others, especially children, is paramount to public safety and reinforces our steadfast dedication to shielding the innocent from these insidious crimes.”

According to court documents, Randall William Rushton made available on two separate occasions over 600 total images and videos of CSAM for download by other users of a peer-to-peer network. He also possessed over 11,000 images and videos depicting sadistic or masochistic conduct, including infants and toddlers and children under the age of 12.

Rushton pleaded guilty to two counts of distribution of child pornography and one count of possession of child pornography. In addition to his sentence of imprisonment, Rushton will be required to pay restitution to his victims and to register as a sex offender in the place where he resides, where he is an employee, and where he is a student, under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act (SORNA).

The FBI investigated the case. Assistant United States Attorney Afroza Yeasmin prosecuted the case.

These cases are a part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc .

title: Las Vegas Man Sentenced to Over Eight Years in Prison for Distribution and Possession of Massive Collections of Child Sexual Abuse Material

Nebraska Fugitive Arrested in Mexico After Five Years on the Run
For immediate release
Chris Cicha, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Omaha, NE – A Wood River man wanted by the U.S. Marshals Service District of Nebraska Metro Fugitive Task Force (MFTF) since 2021 was arrested by law enforcement in Tijuana, Mexico, Sept. 17.
Ernesto Guerrero-Zarraga, 25, was wanted on a bench warrant by the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) for conspiracy to distribute and possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and conspiracy to distribute and possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of methamphetamine actual.
In August 2020, Guerrero-Zarraga was arrested by the MFTF on state warrants for first-degree assault, use of a firearm to commit a felony, and attempt of a class 2 felony. On June 12, 2021, Guerrero-Zarraga posted a $5,000 bond and was released from custody. On June 14, 2021, authorities learned that Guerrero-Zarraga posted the wrong bond amount and was released from custody in error. An arrest warrant was issued in U.S. District Court for the District of Nebraska for Guerrero-Zarraga.
After the MFTF developed information that Guerrero-Zarraga was in Tijuana, they coordinated with the USMS Office of International Operations, the Mexico Foreign Field Office and local authorities in Mexico to locate and arrest Guerrero-Zarraga.
Law enforcement in Tijuana located Guerrero-Zarraga and took him into custody without incident. Guerrero-Zarraga is a U.S. citizen and was deported from Mexico on Sept. 18 and taken into custody by the USMS Southern District of California.
Guerrero-Zarraga is awaiting extradition back to Nebraska.
U.S. Marshals Service task forces combine the efforts of federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies to locate and arrest our nation’s most dangerous fugitives. These task forces are dedicated to reducing violent crime by locating and apprehending wanted criminals. They also serve as the central point for agencies to share information on fugitive matters. In 2025, the U.S. Marshals arrested 73,323 fugitives, cleared 87,984 warrants, which averaged out to around 293 fugitives arrested per day in 2025 alone.
title: Nebraska Fugitive Arrested in Mexico After Five Years on the Run | U.S. Marshals Service

LOS ANGELES – An Orange County woman who is the former girlfriend of a cryptocurrency fraudster who called himself “The Godfather” was sentenced today to 18 months in federal prison for failing to report more than $2.6 million in ill-gotten gains she obtained via her then-boyfriend’s criminal activities.

Iris Rabaya Au, 37, of Irvine, was sentenced by United States District Judge Percy Anderson, who also ordered her to pay $1,484,343 in restitution and to forfeit a fleet of luxury and high-performance cars, designer handbags, and three “Godfather” sculptures, among other assets.

Au pleaded guilty in March 2025 to one count of subscribing to a false tax return.

According to Au’s plea agreement, from 2020 to 2024, once dated Adam Iza, 26, who resided in Beverly Hills and Newport Beach, and was a self-styled cryptocurrency businessman who has been in federal custody since September 2024.

Iza committed a series of crimes, including fraudulently obtaining access to advertising accounts and lines of credit provided by Facebook Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc. and selling access to those accounts. Iza obtained millions of dollars of unreported income because of these schemes.

Separately, Iza engaged active Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) deputies to provide private security for him and caused the deputies, among other things, to obtain court-authorized search warrants and confidential law enforcement information targeting people with whom Iza had financial and personal disputes.

At Iza’s direction, Au created shell corporations and opened bank accounts in the names of those entities. She then used the illicit funds placed into those accounts to pay approximately $1 million to the deputies, mostly in cash, purchase or lease luxury real estate, cars, jewelry, and clothing, pay for recreational activity for Iza and herself valued at nearly $10 million, and acquire approximately $16 million in cryptocurrency for Iza.

Au transferred more than $2.6 million from these various accounts to her personal bank accounts during the period 2020 through 2023, income that she willfully failed to report to the IRS on her federal tax returns.

“[Au] set up the financial infrastructure that enabled Adam Iza to move, spend, and conceal millions of dollars in fraud proceeds while she personally benefited from the wealth,” prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum. “Au concealed entities and income from her tax preparer and filed returns reporting only a small fraction of what she had actually received. Those were affirmative acts designed to prevent the IRS from learning the true extent of her income.”

Iza pleaded guilty in January 2025 in Los Angeles federal court to one count of conspiracy against rights, one count of wire fraud, and one count of tax evasion. His sentencing hearing is scheduled for October 5 before Judge Anderson.

Iza is serving a 15-year federal prison sentence for his involvement in an attempted robbery of Bitcoin and a kidnapping in Connecticut in August 2024.

IRS Criminal Investigation and the FBI investigated this matter.

Assistant United States Attorney Maxwell K. Coll of the National Security Division prosecuted this case.
title: Irvine Woman Sentenced to 18 Months in Federal Prison for Not Reporting $2.6 Million in Income She Obtained via Crypto Criminal

text:
Transcript of Ranking Member Ro Khanna’s Remarks at Asia Society on U.S.-China AI Agreement Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
NEW YORK – Today, Rep. Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ranking Member of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, delivered remarks outlining his vision for the future of U.S. strategy toward China, including U.S.-China safeguards to prevent the loss of human control of AI, American economic competitiveness, effective deterrence, and the role of diplomacy in managing strategic competition.
Khanna delivered the remarks at Asia Society in New York on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, as leaders from around the world gather to address shared global challenges and the future of international cooperation. His remarks also addressed the need for economic rebalancing and moral leadership in diplomacy and development around the world.
Following his remarks, Ranking Member Khanna joined the Hon. Dr. Kevin Rudd AC, Global President and CEO of Asia Society and the 26th Prime Minister of Australia, for a fireside conversation on how the United States and China can manage sustained strategic competition, reduce the risks of conflict, identify areas of practical cooperation, and navigate their respective roles in an increasingly competitive and multipolar international environment.
A full transcript of Ranking Member Khanna’s remarks is below.
Over the last few months, we’ve seen shocking polls from some of our closest allies and partners around the world in terms of the trust they have in the United States versus China.
In Canada, our closest ally in the Western Hemisphere, 44 percent of Canadians view China favorably, up from just 14 percent three years ago. In contrast, only 33 percent have a favorable view of the United States, down from 57 percent in 2023.
Germany is hemorrhaging ten thousand manufacturing jobs per month in large part because its industry is getting crushed by heavily subsidized Chinese imports. And yet, 33 percent of Germans view China favorably, compared to just 27 percent who have a positive view of America.
In Italy, Prime Minister Meloni once fancied herself a friend of President Trump, but today 51 percent of Italians view China favorably, compared to 31 percent for the U.S.
In the UK, with whom America has had a “special relationship” since at least the days of Winston Churchill, 46 percent of Brits have a favorable view of China versus only 41 percent who are favorable toward the United States.
These numbers are even worse across much of the Global South, including in many countries in South and Southeast Asia that are frequent targets of China’s bullying, but are now being bullied even more by our own country.
Because of this bullying, the president of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, recently suggested making Canada the EU’s first “associate member.” Leaders across Europe are planning for a post-American world because they don’t trust the American electorate to not vote for another Trump-like leader in the future.
During Donald Trump’s first term, around 2017, Xi Jinping started describing the world order as going through what he called “great changes unseen in a century.”
He was referring to the political turmoil in the United States and many other democracies that led to “Brexit” in 2015 and to Donald Trump’s first election in 2016. He was also referring to China’s own extraordinary rise in economic and military power.
The world is experiencing changes unlike any we have seen in a very long time, perhaps in the lifetimes of any of us here in this room.
So, what has changed?
Americans have made clear that we reject the unfettered globalization that deindustrialized our country and hollowed out once-thriving communities like Johnstown, PA and Middletown, OH. I saw Fairless Works shut down where I grew up in Bucks County.
Deindustrialization and economic dislocation have rippled across much of the world. Populist anger contributed to Brexit and the electoral success of far-right parties across Europe from France and Germany to Austria and Croatia.
Almost one in four Europeans now vote for far-right parties, almost five times more than the proportion in the mid-1990s.
In the United States, we are trying to do something historically unprecedented in becoming the first cohesive multiracial democracy in the world. We have the highest foreign-born percentage of our population in America since 1924, and no nation comes close to our diversity with our African-American, Latino, Asian, and Native American populations.
China is the polar opposite in its campaign of forced and often brutal assimilation of its Tibetan, Uyghur, Southern Mongolian, and other non-Han communities, including through its so-called “Ethnic Unity Law.”
And finally, the AI revolution is transforming our economy, creating unprecedented wealth but also creating real risks for society in the loss of control, misalignment, the loss of jobs and staggering wealth inequality.
The safety risks are so severe that the founders of three major American AI companies recently called for “pacing the frontier” to make sure that the rate of advancement in AI doesn’t outpace humanity’s ability to control it. I’ve called on the major Chinese labs to make the same pledge.
So, the question now is, what comes next?
Will China lead the world, or will America lead it?
We live in a time devoid of statesmanship.
Ironically, the only American providing global leadership these days is Pope Leo, who I went to see this summer and who has written a marvelous treaty on AI, Magnifica Humanitas. Last month, I wrote letters to American AI companies asking them to commit to its principles.
I want America to be a moral leader in the world again.
But to do this, we need a new generation offering a new doctrine for American foreign policy.
First, a new generation must make clear that we renounce and categorically reject the doctrine of “might makes right,” which President Trump has recklessly applied to his Iran war and in the Caribbean.
Instead, America must lead and be a friend to the world, standing up for freedom and human rights.
We should remember President Kennedy’s famous words from his address to the nation during the Cuban Missile Crisis, where he reminded Americans that:
“Our goal is not the victory of might, but the vindication of right […] here in this Hemisphere, and, we hope, around the world.”
A generation earlier, FDR announced his “good neighbor” policy in his first inaugural address, where he pledged America to “the policy of the good neighbor—the neighbor who resolutely respects himself and, because he does so, respects the rights of others.”
We can even go back to the Founding Fathers themselves, like Thomas Jefferson, who called for “peace, commerce, and honest friendship with all nations” to be one of the essential principles of American governance.
These principles must be cornerstones of our foreign policy once again. We must restore our alliances with nations working to become pluralistic democracies and work with them in good faith to advance human and economic rights and democracy around the world.
This includes ending our hypocrisy and supporting self-determination for the Palestinians living side-by-side with a secure Israel as the Arab Peace Plan has long called for.
We must not take a hectoring tone. Instead, we must work diplomatically, including with NGOs, to stand up for the universal truths that are enshrined in the UN Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
And like President Kennedy, we should not mistake rejecting the principle of “might makes right” for neglecting the importance of might itself.
We must ensure that America retains naval and air superiority in the Pacific to counterbalance China’s rapid build-up of military power.
We must invest in attritable drones and autonomous vehicles to make sure that our military can prevail on the battlefield of the future, and does not just keep fighting yesterday’s wars.
This brings me to the second principle for a new foreign policy doctrine, which is that we need an America that uses its power to help solve the world’s problems, not to militarily threaten and bully other countries.
When the world thinks of us, they shouldn’t think of the size of our military or the destructive power of our bombs. Instead, they should think of America as a peacemaker and leader who can convene others to resolve humanity’s biggest issues.
We should lead in addressing the climate crisis, global poverty, ending war, and illiteracy.
But today, let’s start with AI.
We can begin by showing American leadership on the issue of AI safety.
Winning an AI war is like winning a nuclear war. It is catastrophic for civilization.
America’s AI labs might be winning today, but nobody wins if humans lose control of AI or if bad actors use AI to unleash a chemical or biological attack.
We must lead the way by showing the world what responsible AI regulation looks like. This starts by establishing a federal AI Safety Agency and imposing strict liability on labs that fail to follow the rules or unleash catastrophic harm.
Rule Number One must be a ban on recursive self-improvement. This is when AI develops AI— and it is the clearest path to humans losing control of this technology.
Rule Number Two is mandatory certifications and inspections to prevent misuse and misalignment.
Once we’ve led the way at home, we need the world to follow. Our President should pursue a binding agreement with China to keep humans in control, which must be enforceable and verifiable.
The third principle for a new foreign policy is to build a fresh economic vision for the world that replaces corporate-dominated globalization. We must build the economy of the future for every American in every place, not just for a few billionaires.
This starts with what I call a New Economic Patriotism.
After World War II, European industry lay devastated by half a decade of total war. Public discontent was rising, which American leaders feared would lead to radical and destabilizing ideologies.
In response, the Marshall Plan helped rebuild Europe’s economy and shore up public support for capitalism and democracy.
Today, American industry lies devastated by five decades of offshoring and financial engineering by private equity. Populist anger is rising at the elites who chased low wages overseas and shut down factories to maximize shareholder value.
We need a Marshall Plan for America to achieve economic renewal across our nation, with high-paying industrial and service jobs in every community.
Rebuilding our economy at home is not isolationism. It promotes economic and national security and helps overcome the anger so many Americans feel about deindustrialization.
We can combine this strategy with policies that help other nations, especially in Latin America and the Global South, to develop their own economies in ways that don’t compete with our jobs.
The Development Finance Corporation and USAID can and should support this effort in developing nations.These countries in turn will be better markets for American exports. Our assistance can also help rebuild trust in places that have been courted by Chinese gifts and attention.
We would not do this in China’s way of seeking dominance and control. We would do it because we want to see the spread of free enterprise and democracy.
If we focus on rebuilding American factory towns and rural communities, and if we deliver on shared prosperity within our country, Americans will see that economic engagement with the world need not be zero sum.
Americans will support the economic development of other nations so long as we trust that it won’t lead to foreign goods being dumped back into our market or happen at the expense of our working class.
My final principle for a new American foreign policy is that at home, America must strive to become a cohesive multiracial nation, and in doing so, become a model for the world.
I have often spoken of my deep admiration for Frederick Douglass, whose 1867 speech “Composite Nation” ranks as one of the greatest in American history. In it, he calls on America to celebrate immigrants and become what he called a “composite nation”: taking the best from the ways of life of different people, from different parts of the world, and melding it into something beautiful here.
After fifteen years in bondage, he still believed that in the free air of America the best ideas of different traditions would emerge, and that we could become a shining pluralistic democracy with shared prosperity for all.
That is the America I see emerging after Donald Trump. It will be born if we build economic security and dignity for every American in every community.
To be Douglass’s composite nation, we must guarantee economic dignity in Johnstown and Middletown, in Downriver Detroit, in Milwaukee Orangeburg, Las Vegas; and Lordstown for Black, Latino, and white Americans alike.
Building a multiracial democracy will require the greatest economic mission in generations. An America that is economically resilient across geographies will be more likely to be an outward-facing, confident nation that once again leads the free world.
I want an America that rejects Donald Trump’s philosophy, which preys on our worst fears to divide us, and emulates dictators who build a world of domination and dependence.
I want an America that rediscovers the decency, the positive outlook, and the can-do pragmatism our Founders brought into the world 250 years ago.
Those capacities are still in us. We simply have to make sure this nation is not enriching a few, but working for the people I grew up with in Pennsylvania and working for all Americans.
If we provide economic opportunity everywhere, we can become the world’s first cohesive multiracial democracy, a nation that carries the freedom struggles of every corner of the earth, and is a moral light to the aspirations of free people.
This is our duty and our calling.
Thank you.
###
title: Transcript of Ranking Member Ro Khanna’s Remarks at Asia Society on U.S.-China AI Agreement Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting

EPA Advances Cosmo Specialty Fibers Cleanup Work, Continues Treatment Operations
SEATTLE— U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s time-critical removal action at the Cosmo Specialty Fibers site in Cosmopolis, Washington, has reached multiple milestones over the past two weeks, including the completion and commissioning of a chemical treatment plant designed to neutralize corrosive waste before it is shipped for disposal. To date, over 222,000 gallons of acidic waste have been treated, and over 180,000 gallons have been shipped off-site. EPA anticipates removing over 1 million gallons of waste from the site.
“The Trump EPA remains firmly committed to advancing this removal action safely while keeping the local community informed as work continues at the Cosmo Specialty Fibers site,” said EPA Regional Administrator Emma Pokon. “This effort shows our commitment to clean air, land, and water, and to a safe, transparent cleanup process for all Americans.”
EPA began site mobilization in early August, coordinating with local fire, law enforcement, emergency management, and environmental health officials. The removal action is a proactive measure intended to safely eliminate potential environmental hazards and reduce future risk to the surrounding community. EPA’s work at the site is expected to be completed this calendar year.
“We are making steady progress at the Cosmo Specialty Fibers site, and the treatment system is now fully operational,” said EPA On-Scene Coordinator Thomas Vroman. “By treating waste on site before shipment, we are improving safety and lowering disposal costs.”
For the past two years, EPA and Washington State Department of Ecology have worked closely to assess conditions at the non-operational facility and identify actions needed to reduce potential risks to the community and the environment. In April 2026, the Department of Ecology, the long-term lead agency for the site, requested EPA assistance with the removal of the remaining chemicals in tanks and containers.
