- For Immediate Release:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued a direct final rule that updates its regulations to clarify that non-animal methods can be used where appropriate for testing the safety of drugs and biological products intended for human use before they’re tried in humans.
The update reflects advances in science and technology that have expanded the range of testing options available in human drug development, including methods using human cells, organs-on-chips, computer models and other advanced technologies.
“This new rule supports the Trump Administration’s push to explore ways to complement, or where appropriate, replace animal studies with methods that may better predict how medicines will actually affect people,” said Acting FDA Commissioner of Food and Drugs, Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “It gives scientists and drug developers greater flexibility to use the testing approach that best addresses their scientific question. Our goal is not to replace one rigid approach with another. It is to support rigorous, modern science — including animal studies when they remain appropriate and validated alternatives when they can provide the evidence needed to protect patients.”
The rule replaces terms like “animal tests” and “animal studies” with the terms “nonclinical tests” and “nonclinical studies.” Related terms, including “preclinical” and “in vitro,” are also replaced. The rule defines “nonclinical test” and “nonclinical study” in line with the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2022 (FDORA). The law recognizes newer methods that do not use animals and traditional animal studies as possible ways to provide the evidence needed to begin studies in people.
The rule removes language that could suggest that animal testing is the only acceptable way to generate safety information for regulatory decisions in products intended for human use. It does not eliminate or prohibit animal studies, change evidentiary standards or impose new costs or requirements on drug developers.
To demonstrate their practical application, the FDA also launched a database featuring specific uses of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs). The initial release includes 25 examples drawn from publicly available FDA review materials.
The new rule and database are among several actions that the Department of Health and Human Services, including the FDA, is taking to advance drug development using NAMs, which are innovative testing methods that may better reflect human biology. Developers may use NAMs to generate safety information when the methods are adequately validated and appropriate for the product and regulatory question.
These actions are in line with Pillar 1 — Innovation and Global Leadership — of the FDA’s Public Health Pillars. By formally recognizing a broader range of scientific approaches, the FDA is keeping pace with emerging technologies and strengthening the agency’s leadership in regulatory science. Encouraging the use of NAMs also complements Operation TrialBlazer, the Department of Health and Human Services initiative to modernize clinical research and accelerate the development of life-saving treatments. Clearer terminology and regulatory expectations can reduce avoidable uncertainty as sponsors develop nonclinical evidence and prepare applications to begin clinical trials.
The agency is inviting the public, including clinicians, parents, caregivers, the scientific community, industry, and others, to comment on the rule.
For additional information, see the Federal Register notices announcing the direct final rule, the companion proposed rule, and the comment period. If the FDA receives significant adverse comments on the direct final rule, the agency will withdraw it and continue rulemaking through the standard notice-and-comment process using the companion proposed rule. Publishing both simultaneously ensures the rulemaking can proceed efficiently under either scenario.
Additional Information
- Nonclinical Testing Terminology Direct Final Rule
- Nonclinical Testing Terminology Proposed Rule
- FDA Direct Final Rule Procedures
- Reducing Animal Testing in Nonclinical Studies: Year One Progress and the Path Forward
The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products.

title: FDA Updates Regulations to Advance Innovative Alternatives to Animal Testing

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Mike Lawler (NY-17) held a press conference to amplify the importance of their bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act, legislation that would establish clear, practical guardrails for the powerful new AI “agents” now operating inside America’s networks. This commonsense legislation ensures that businesses and agencies have the ability to see and stop rogue agents before they cause real damage. The Representatives also highlighted several other bipartisan actions they’ve led this Congress on AI — including legislation to protect consumers, develop America’s workforce, and boost innovation.

Watch Gottheimer and Lawler’s remarks here.

“You can’t drive a car in this country without a license plate, without insurance, without some way for a cop — or the person you just rear-ended — to know who’s behind the wheel and who’s responsible,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Co-Chair of the House Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy. “AI agents right now don’t have any of that. Our bill puts a driver’s license on every AI agent operating in this country — so organizations can find every agent on their network, verify who built it, watch it in real time, and cut off its access the second something looks wrong. That means putting humans back in the driver’s seat. It’s time for Congress to get back to work and get this done.”

“This isn’t about stopping AI or stifling innovation. It is about making sure we can safely deploy AI. A pause is not a safeguard. Some states have put a moratorium on the infrastructure that powers this technology. That does not invent a kill switch. It does not inventory the agents already on a hospital network or a utility system,” said Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17.) “If the United States taps the brakes while others floor it, we do not get safer AI. We get someone else’s AI. We are not going to regulate ourselves into second place.”

Right now, most organizations have no reliable way to know how many unauthorized AI agents are running in their systems, who built them, or what they have access to. AI agents can be activated by employees, embedded in third-party software, or deployed by vendors — often with little to no visibility for the organization whose networks they’re operating on to know that they are there. That blind spot is becoming more dangerous by the day. The recent Hugging Face incident and other autonomous cyberattacks have shown AI systems are being used to hack organizations at scale, without a person ever watching or stepping in.

Drafted and introduced by Gottheimer and Lawler, the Stop Rogue AI Act would direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) to develop national standards, guidelines, and best practices for discovering, verifying, monitoring, and controlling AI agents.

Other Bipartisan AI Initiatives from Gottheimer and Lawler include:

AI Workforce Training Act (H.R. 7576) — Helps workers upgrade their AI skills without leaving their jobs. More than 60% of small businesses now use AI — double the share from 2023 — and the challenge isn’t that AI is replacing workers, it’s that workers need help keeping up with the tools their employers are already using. The bill provides a 30% tax credit, capped at $2,500 per employee, for training in practical AI skills. The goal: help workers adapt to AI, not get replaced by it.

Advancing American Quantum Leadership Act of 2026 (H.R. 9585) — Expands the definition of “quantum” under the Export-Import Bank’s China and Transformational Exports Program, broadening “quantum computing” to “quantum information science and technology.”

No Rigged Grocery Prices Act (H.R. 8895) — Bans grocery stores and delivery apps from using AI-driven personal data to charge different customers different prices for the exact same item.

The two members have also pressed the administration and industry on AI accountability — urging the Federal Trade Commission to protect anti-discrimination measures for AI systems; calling on the CEOs of leading AI companies to ensure voters get accurate, unbiased information ahead of the 2026 midterms; and urging DHS, DOJ, CISA, and the FEC to coordinate against AI-related threats to the 2026 elections.

Below: Gottheimer and Lawler discuss their AI legislation.
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer, Lawler Push Bipartisan Plan on AI Safety

LYNCHBURG, Va. – Law enforcement leaders from more than 20 agencies across the greater Lynchburg area announced the results of Operation United Resolve today. Between August 1, 2026, and August 31, 2026, law enforcement officers from 21 partner agencies arrested 140 fugitives and executed 316 warrants. The operation resulted in the seizure of more than 600 grams of cocaine, 25 grams of fentanyl, 212 grams of MDMA, and 30 grams of methamphetamine. The quantity of fentanyl seized during the operation was enough to result in over 10,000 fatal overdoses.

In addition to the drug seizures, 29 firearms, including 15 handguns, 14 long guns, and one machine gun were taken off the streets, along with $80,159 in cash. Officers also recovered 1,036 images of Child Sexual Abuse Material.

“This Office is dedicated to strengthening federal, state, and local partnerships to promote safe neighborhoods throughout the Western District of Virginia. I commend our federal, state and local partners, Chief Edwards of the Lynchburg Police Department, Acting U.S. Marshal Davis, Lynchburg area sheriffs, and the men and women who made this combined mission a success. This operation follows prior highly successful multiagency Project Safe Neighborhood operations in Danville and Roanoke -- and more are on the way,” First Assistant United States Attorney Robert N. Tracci said today.

“In accordance with the directives of the President, Attorney General, and our Director, the U.S. Marshals Service, Western District of Virginia, is committed to being engaged, at the highest level, with each of our partner Federal, State, and Local agencies to ensure success in making our communities safe. The citizens of Western Virginia deserve safe streets and to not be exposed to violent offenders and predators. I commend Central Virginia law enforcement, and their leadership, for their exceptionally proactive approach to partner as a “United” team to serve the citizens who pay our salaries to keep them safe. The combined efforts of these types of operations, led by the Marshals Service, is frankly impressive, and we are humbled to be a part of the Virginia law enforcement team, and to play a leading role in the same. The officers who participated in these operations spent countless hours and risked their lives to protect our citizens. We stand with them and are incredibly grateful to First Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert Tracci for leading the federal agencies in these partnerships to make our streets safer.”

“The success of this operation highlights the undeniable power of strong, collaborative partnerships,” said Lynchburg Police Chief Kennith R. Edwards, Jr. “Protecting our neighborhoods and community often requires an all-hands approach. Working diligently with our federal, state, and local partners allows us to pool our strength, hold violent offenders accountable, and deliver the peace of mind and security that every resident in Lynchburg deserves.”

“This remarkable enforcement operation demonstrates the collective efforts of federal, state, and local law enforcement working together to protect communities in Western Virginia from violent crime and illegal narcotics,” said DEA Special Agent in Charge Cindy Marx of the Washington Division. “The DEA remains committed to defending our country from deadly drugs and dangerous drug trafficking organizations harming, damaging, and destroying our communities.”

“Operation United Resolve demonstrates the impact we can achieve when local, state and federal law enforcement agencies unite behind a shared mission,” said ATF Washington Field Division Special Agent in Charge Anthony Spotswood. “The arrests made, firearms recovered and warrants executed represent more than statistics—they represent violent offenders taken off our streets and dangerous weapons and drugs removed from our communities. ATF is proud to support this operation and remains committed to working alongside our partners to protect the communities we serve.”

“This past month, the dedication of our combined efforts has led to real, measurable results: dangerous drugs have been taken off our streets, violent criminals are behind bars, and criminal networks that threatened our neighborhoods have been dismantled. Every arrest, every investigation, every act of service makes our communities safer,” said FBI Assistant Special Agent in Charge Michael Smith.

“HSI is proud to stand with so many law enforcement partners united in one goal: making the Commonwealth of Virginia a safer place to live. We know that our local partners and communities are the key to making our neighborhoods safer and HSI is committed to leveraging federal resources to get the best results and see justice served,” said Homeland Security Investigations Washington, D.C. Acting Special Agent in Charge Kai Wah Chan.

“The US Postal Inspection Service sees firsthand through our investigations how devastating narcotics can be to our communities,” says Inspector in Charge Damon E. Wood. “Postal Inspectors remain committed to working with our law enforcement partners to disrupt the flow of these deadly drugs and holding those criminals involved in narcotics distribution accountable.”

This operation was part of the revamped Project Safe Neighborhoods, a combined law enforcement initiative that aims to provide a rapid response to violent crime, conduct strategic federal, state, local, and tribal partnerships, and increase accountability and deterrence to promote public safety.

United Resolve Lynchburg is the third PSN operation in the Western District of Virginia in recent months initiated by First Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert Tracci in coordination with the United States Marshals Service and law enforcement partners from federal and state agencies, police departments, and sheriffs offices. Operation Washout “No Limits” Danville (November 2025) resulted in the apprehension of 96 violent fugitives, took 15 firearms out of the hands of criminals, and resulted in the seizure of enough fentanyl to kill nearly 30,000 Virginians. https://www.justice.gov/usao-wdva/pr/officials-announce-results-project-safe-neighborhoods-operation-combined-resolve . Operation Combined Resolve Roanoke Valley (June 2026) resulted in 150 arrests and resulted in the seizure of enough fentanyl to kill the entire Roanoke Valley. https://www.justice.gov/usao-wdva/pr/officials-announce-results-project-safe-neighborhoods-operation-combined-resolve These operations reflect the commitment of the U.S. Attorney’s for the Western District of Virginia to work with law enforcement partners at all levels to eliminate violent crime, street gangs, illegal firearms, and other threats to our citizens and communities.

These operations were carried out by the United States Marshals Service, Roanoke City Police Department, Lynchburg Police Department, Danville Police Department, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Department of Homeland Security-Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), United States Postal Inspection Service, Virginia State Police, Virginia Attorney General’s Office, Virginia National Guard-Counter Drug Unit, Virginia Department of Probation and Parole, Bedford County Sheriff’s Office, Lynchburg City Sheriff’s Office, Amherst County Sheriff’s Office, Montgomery County Sheriff’s Office, Bedford Police Department, Bedford County Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office, Amherst County Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office, Campbell County Sheriff’s Office, Appomattox County Sheriff’s Office, Lynchburg Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office, Campbell County Commonwealth’s Attorney’s Office, Salem Police Department, Star City Task Force, Roanoke County Police Department, Vinton Police Department and Commonwealth’s Attorney, Pittsylvania County Sheriff’s Office, Blue Ridge Regional Jail Authority, and the Danville Department of Probation and Parole.

EPA Begins Lead Cleanup at Former Friction Materials Site in Huntington, Indiana
CHICAGO (September 21, 2026) – Today, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) began a cleanup of lead-contaminated soil from the former Friction Materials site at 1849 East Sabine St. in Huntington, Indiana. The cleanup is expected to take approximately 60 days.
During the cleanup, EPA will secure the site and excavate lead-contaminated soil before backfilling with clean soil. Crews will transport lead-contaminated soil offsite for disposal at an EPA-approved facility. EPA will conduct air monitoring throughout the cleanup to ensure dust does not leave the site.
The 11.7-acre former Friction Materials site contains the remnants of a large automotive parts manufacturing facility. Operations at the site began in the early 1900s and continued for nearly a century. The site’s ownership changed hands several times before Friction Materials acquired the property in the late 1960s. The company used the site to manufacture automotive brake parts until ceasing all operations and declaring bankruptcy in 2000. The site sat vacant for more than a decade before the City of Huntington acquired the property via tax lien in 2014.
EPA has previously conducted two cleanups at the site:
- In 2017 and 2018, EPA removed and disposed of approximately 2,000 gallons of hazardous liquid waste and approximately 3,000 pounds of hazardous solid waste from the site, including asbestos-containing material.
- In 2022 and 2023, EPA removed more than 2,350 tons of lead-contaminated soil from 11 residential properties surrounding the site and some of the most highly contaminated areas onsite.
In 2025, an assessment by the Indiana Brownfields Program discovered additional lead contamination present in deeper soil throughout the site. The state referred the site to EPA for further assessment and removal. Earlier this year, EPA sampling confirmed the program’s findings.
For more information about the response, visit the Friction Materials removal website.

Washington, D.C.—Congressmen Vicente Gonzalez (D-TX-34) and Dan Crenshaw (R-TX-02) announced the introduction of the bipartisan H.R. 10434, the Empower Energy Exporting Communities Act. This legislation would establish an Oil & Gas Community Trust Fund to support infrastructure and public services in communities near major oil and gas export ports, without creating a new tax. South Texas is home to several major energy export hubs, including the Port of Corpus Christi and the Port of Brownsville.

“South Texas serves as a crucial gateway for the distribution of oil and gas exports to international markets,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “It is only right that our region directly benefits from the operations it supports. The establishment of a trust fund would not burden taxpaying Americans but instead reinvest already existing revenue from oil and gas companies to advance South Texas’s infrastructure of opportunity from our roads, bridges, and clean drinking water to public education and much more.”

"This bill ensures that a portion of the federal revenue already generated by the oil and gas industry is reinvested in the roads, ports, water systems, and other critical infrastructure these communities rely on, all without raising taxes," said Congressman Crenshaw. "I’m proud to join Congressman Gonzalez in supporting the Texas communities that help make America an energy superpower."

Specifically, Congressman Gonzalez’s bill would direct the Oil & Gas Community Trust Fund to be financed by 3% of corporate income tax revenues received from oil & gas companies. These funds would be used to make payments to eligible communities, including counties, parishes, municipalities, or Tribal communities located within 50 miles of a major port of export. The funds can only be used for infrastructure and public service investments, and payments cannot exceed the proportion of total trust fund dollars that matches its share of national exports.
title: Congressmen Gonzalez, Crenshaw Introduce Bipartisan Empower Energy Exporting Communities Act

Memphis, TN – Kokou Sanoumegah, 29 , of Memphis, has pled guilty to being a felon in possession of firearms and illegal possession of a machinegun. United States Attorney D. Michael Dunavant, for the Western District of Tennessee, announced the guilty plea today.

On April 16, 2025, a private fugitive recovery unit located Sanoumegah, a fugitive with active arrest warrants, in Memphis, Tennessee. According to the evidence, while taking him into custody, they discovered a Glock 17 9mm pistol in Sanoumegah’s waistband and a Diamondback DB-15 AR-style pistol located next to where Sanoumegah had been sitting.

The Glock contained a machinegun conversion device (MCD) known as a “switch”, as well as an extended magazine with 39 rounds and 1 round in the chamber. The Diamondback AR-style pistol was found with a drop-in auto sear, designed to convert it to a fully automatic weapon, with 59 rounds in the magazine and 1 round in the chamber. The AR pistol had been reported stolen, and neither firearm contained a proper serial number.

Sanoumegah is a convicted felon after previously pleading guilty to a 2016 armed robbery offense in Desoto County (MS). While in custody for these firearms offenses, Sanoumegah was charged with aggravated assault and possession of contraband in a penal institution for an incident on August 6, 2025, in which it is alleged that he stabbed another inmate in the Shelby County Jail 17 times with a homemade weapon, causing paralysis to the victim.

In June 2024, Sanoumegah was charged with possession of a firearm, theft of a firearm, possession of a controlled substance, and aggravated criminal trespassing; that case was dismissed about a year later due to lack of prosecution, State court records show.

On September 16, 2026, Sanoumegah pled guilty to being a convicted felon in possession of firearms and possession of a machinegun. Sanoumegah is scheduled to be sentenced before U.S. District Court Judge Brian C. Lea on December 16, 2026 and faces a sentence of 144 months in federal prison. There is no parole in the federal system.

U.S. Attorney D. Michael Dunavant said, “Sanoumegah has a demonstrated history of violence, and has no hesitation about repeatedly committing multiple crimes when the risk to human life is high. Now the federal system will accomplish justice by doing what should have been done a long time ago – imposing a real consequence that will justly punish and incapacitate him for at least 12 years.”

This case was investigated by the Memphis Police Department (MPD) as part of the Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) initiative.

Special Assistant United States Attorney Benjamin N. Frizzell, a United States Marine Corps Judge Advocate, and Assistant United States Attorney Gregory Wagner prosecuted the case on behalf of the government.

Special Assistant United States Attorney Benjamin N. Frizzell, a United States Marine Corps Judge Advocate, and Assistant United States Attorney Gregory Wagner prosecuted the case on behalf of the government.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

LEXINGTON, Ky. – A Lexington man, Kevin Sanders, 48, was sentenced on Friday to 330 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Robert Wier for several drug trafficking and firearms charges.

Sanders was convicted in May 2026 of four counts of distributing fentanyl, three counts of distributing methamphetamine, three counts of possessing with intent to distribute 600 grams or more of fentanyl, 500 grams or more of cocaine, and 50 grams or more of methamphetamine (actual). He was also convicted of possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime and of possession of a firearm by a convicted felon

According to testimony at trial, beginning in February 2025, law enforcement officers with the HIDTA Task Force, began an investigation into the drug trafficking activities of Kevin D. Sanders. During the investigation, law enforcement officers purchased 49 grams of fentanyl and 83 grams of methamphetamine from Sanders. In April 2025, a search warrant was obtained for his residence, and law enforcement seized 3,705 grams of pure methamphetamine, 608 grams of fentanyl, and 500 grams of cocaine. Additionally, officers located and seized five firearms. Sanders has a prior conviction for Attempt First Degree Murder from Cook County, Illinois.

Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky; John Nokes, Special Agent in Charge, ATF, Louisville Field Division; Phillip J. Burnett, Jr., Commissioner of the Kentucky State Police; and Chief Rodney Richardson, Richmond Police Department, jointly announced the sentence.

The investigation was conducted by the ATF, KSP, and Richmond Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Cynthia Rieker prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States.

Trump’s America First Resilience Strategy, which calls for a new, risk-informed approach that treats resilience as an investment opportunity. It also delivers on the Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mullin’s commitment to empowering state and local officials to manage their own disaster preparedness—with FEMA supporting only if needed.

Most projects focus on improving infrastructure to reduce flood risk, while others address hazards such as earthquakes and wildfires. A list of these Congressional Directed Spending projects is available on FEMA.gov.

This competitive grant program is designed to empower states and territories to support local jurisdictions with flood reduction efforts. WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) announced that two of his bipartisan bills with Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) and Congresswoman Erin Houchin (IN-09) passed out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee. The bills are as follows:

H.R. 7294, AI for Secure Networks Act (Menendez and Pfluger)

The AI For Secure Networks Act strengthens the cybersecurity of America’s communications networks by promoting the responsible use of artificial intelligence while addressing the risks posed by its misuse.

“As our communications networks face growing threats, we must advance forward thinking solutions to protect the communications, emergency services, critical infrastructure, and financial systems Americans depend on,” said Congressman Menendez. “Our legislation promotes the responsible use of AI while confronting the growing risks posed by its exploitation, including the potential for more sophisticated cyberattacks on the communications systems Americans rely on every day. I look forward to working to pass this legislation and strengthen protections for our networks and the people who depend on them.”

Click here to view Congressman Menendez’s remarks.

H.R. 5967, Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act (Menendez and Houchin)

The Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act establishes a federal task force to develop a national scam prevention strategy that strengthens support for victims, provides local law enforcement stronger tools to stop scams, and lowers the risk of financial losses from fraudulent activity.

“As scams become increasingly more sophisticated, we need a national strategy to protect American families and consumers,” said Congressman Menendez. “The Strategic Task Force on Scam Prevention Act brings together the federal government, law enforcement, and corporations to protect our families and seniors from being targeted by bad actors online and over the phone. I am proud that our legislation has passed the full Committee and is one step closer to becoming law and look forward to its passage through the House.”

Click here to view Congressman Menendez’s remarks.

ANNISTON, AL – On September 21, 2026, FEMA’s Center for Domestic Preparedness (CDP) officially opened its new student training and in-processing center at its Advanced Responder Training Complex.
Department of Homeland Security Under Secretary for Management Brian Cavanaugh participated in the ribbon-cutting ceremony. He was joined by FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton, DHS Deputy Under Secretary for Management Erin Hoffman, Center for Domestic Preparedness Acting Superintendent Chris Chesney, FEMA’s National Preparedness Directorate Deputy Assistant Administrator Dr. Thom Layou and other distinguished guests.
“The men and women who respond first when disaster strikes deserve the very best training and resources we can provide,” said DHS Under Secretary for Management Brian Cavanaugh. “This new facility represents an investment by President Trump in America’s first responders, in the communities they serve, and in our nation’s ability to respond when it matters most. By strengthening the Center for Domestic Preparedness, we are ensuring responders across the country are better equipped, better trained, and ready to protect the American people.”
The new facility provides a place to equip state, local, tribal and territorial emergency responders with the information, skills and abilities required to react and respond to mass casualty incidents, including those involving chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear or explosive (CBRNE) materials. The building includes classroom space and a large area where students can be in-processed before training and gather with fellow responders. It will also house CDP Training and Education staff as well as staff associated with training support and delivery functions.
“The Center for Domestic Preparedness is committed to training the best for the worst. Facilities like these reflect the importance of empowering and enabling local responders to protect their communities,” said FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton. “By investing in these facilities, state, local, tribal and territorial governments can ensure they have the skills needed to reduce risk and build their capacity to respond to emergencies and disasters.”
Before, during and after a disaster, emergency management is best when it is locally led, state managed and federally supported. By providing training on preparedness, protection and all-hazards response, CDP strengthens the local capacity of communities across the country. Each year, approximately 60,000 emergency responders from state, local, tribal and territorial governments participate in this training to hone the skills they need to keep people safe. Since it opened its doors in 1998, CDP has trained more than 1.5 million responders.
For more information about CDP training or to register for upcoming classes, visit https://cdp.dhs.gov.
title: FEMA’s Center for Domestic Preparedness Opens New Student Training and Intake Center

FRESNO, Calif. — Five Fresno residents have pleaded guilty to participating in a year-long bank fraud scheme that sought to defraud banks out of $1 million, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

Zorian Temple, 25, pleaded guilty today to bank fraud. On Aug. 17, 2026, Davonntae Barfield, 31; Zion Brewer, 40; and Nyric Hinton, 28, also pleaded guilty. On Aug. 31, 2026, Harry Cooper Neal, 30, pleaded guilty.

According to court records, from 2022 to 2023, Brewer, a U.S. Postal Service employee, stole checks from the mail and gave them to the other defendants. The others then recruited bank account holders, or used their own bank accounts, to deposit the stolen checks and withdraw the proceeds. The defendants met each other and coordinated the scheme primarily through Facebook and Facebook Messenger.

In total, the stolen checks had a face value of more than $1 million. The actual loss to the banks, however, was a few hundred thousand dollars because the banks detected most of the stolen checks and stopped payment before the defendants could withdraw the funds.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation, the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, the U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, and the Fresno Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Joseph Barton is prosecuting the case.

U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Thurston is scheduled to sentence Neal on Nov. 30, 2026, Barfield, Brewer, and Hinton on Dec. 7, 2026, and Temple on Jan. 11, 2027. The defendants face a maximum statutory penalty of 30 years in prison and a fine of up to $1 million. The actual sentences, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables.
title: Five Fresno residents plead guilty to a bank fraud scheme organized on Facebook

U.S. Marshals in TX Arrest MO Homicide Fugitive on the Run for 10 Years
For immediate release
Sean Mallon, Supervisory Deputy U.S. Marshal
St. Louis, MO – The U.S. Marshals (USMS) in north Texas, in conjunction with the USMS in eastern Missouri, today arrested a St. Louis man wanted for an April 2016 murder in St. Louis.
Jonathan Harris, 58, wanted for the murder of Jose Orona, who was killed in the 500 block of Antelope Street, was arrested without incident at 12:38 p.m. at a homeless shelter in the 1800 block of Corsicana Street in Dallas.
The USMS Eastern Missouri Fugitive Task force adopted the fugitive case in October 2016. Investigators learned shortly after the incident that Harris fled the area and was possibly living in various homeless shelters in Texas.
After developing information that Harris was living in Dallas under a false name and frequenting the Corsicana Street homeless shelter, investigators sent a collateral lead to the USMS North Star Fugitive Task Force, who located and arrested Harris. He was transported to a local holding facility awaiting extradition back to St. Louis.
“The tireless work of the men and women of the US Marshals service is bringing justice to our streets every day. I applaud these deputies for their dedication to duty and commitment to our community”. said Steven Lewis, U.S. Marshal for the Eastern District of Missouri. “I commend the diligence and tenacity of the men and women who worked this investigation. The message that we wish to convey to fugitives and their associates is that we are coming for you!”
The U.S. Marshals have a long history of aiding and providing expertise to other law enforcement agencies in support of fugitive investigations. The success of U.S. Marshals task force initiatives, combined with the outstanding relationships forged with other law enforcement agencies, has led to the formation of permanent fugitive task forces, as well as ad-hoc task forces in response to unique cases that pose immediate threat to the public. In 2025, U.S. Marshals Service-led fugitive task forces arrested over 73,000 federal, state and local fugitives and cleared nearly 88,000 warrants.
title: U.S. Marshals in TX Arrest MO Homicide Fugitive on the Run for 10 Years | U.S. Marshals Service

Coast Guard offloads over $57 million in illicit drugs interdicted in the Caribbean Sea
Coast Guard Southeast District- southeastpublicaffairs@uscg.mil
MIAMI — U.S. Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba’s crew offloaded approximately 7,250 pounds of cocaine and 2,082 pounds of marijuana, worth an estimated $57 million, Monday, in Port Everglades.
The seized contraband was the result of two interdictions in the Caribbean Sea by the crews of USCGC Escanaba and USCGC Richard Dixon with an embarked Coast Guard law enforcement detachment.
“The excellent watchstanding and quick, crucial decisions enabled success in this interdiction,” said Petty Officer 1st Class Douglas Strong, a boatswain’s mate assigned to Escanaba. “A complete ship-wide evolution must go flawlessly for an interdiction like this to happen. It was a textbook team effort that ensured over 2,000 pounds of illicit narcotics never made it into our communities. Thanks to the crews of Coast Guard Cutter Richard Dixon and Homeland Security Cutter-Ocean for their partnership - one team one fight.”
The following assets and crews were involved in the interdiction operations:
- U.S. Coast Guard Tactical Law Enforcement Team - Pacific, LEDET 101
Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba’s offload continues the Coast Guard’s mission to interdict, seize, and disrupt transshipment of cocaine and other bulk illicit drugs by sea. The Coast Guard’s persistent operations and rapid response have denied criminal organizations billions in illicit revenue and prevented the flow of dangerous drugs into American communities.
The Coast Guard is the United States’ lead federal agency for maritime drug interdiction. We are part of the Department of Homeland Security team protecting our nation and are at all times a military service and part of the joint force defending it. Interdictions in the Caribbean Sea are performed by members of the U.S. Coast Guard under the authority and control of the Coast Guard Southeast District, headquartered in Miami.
Coast Guard Cutter Escanaba is a 270-foot medium endurance cutter homeported in Portsmouth, Virginia, under U.S. Coast Guard Atlantic Area Command.
Visit our Newsroom for Coast Guard Southeast District press releases. Visit our DVIDS account for Coast Guard Southeast District imagery.
For breaking news, follow us on X (formerly Twitter). For additional information, find us on Facebook and follow us on Instagram.
-USCG-
title: Coast Guard offloads over $57 million in illicit drugs interdicted in the Caribbean Sea

Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA), who serves as co-Chair of the bipartisan Congressional Artificial Intelligence (AI) Caucus and represents a Northern Virginia district that includes Ronald Reagan National Airport (DCA) in the U.S. House, issued the following statement today on the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) deployment of an AI Strategic Management of Airspace Routing Trajectories (“SMART”) system to manage flights at Washington area airports including DCA:

“The FAA should not use my constituents as guinea pigs for an unproven AI air traffic control system. The safety of the 24 million people traveling through DCA each year must be the top priority. Residents of this region are still uncertain about air safety after last year’s fatal accident, and the Administration did shockingly little to educate the traveling public about this development before implementing it in one of the most complex airspaces in the world.

“Unfortunately, I was informed today that air traffic controllers were not consulted on the ‘SMART’ system’s design and development, and were not trained on using it prior to the system’s adoption at local airports. I was further informed that the air traffic controllers have been told the ‘SMART’ system can adjust schedules and potentially even routes. Despite outward appearances, the airlines reportedly were privately ‘panicking’ about the hasty implementation of this system. I do not know why the Administration felt the need to race it into use, but it is unacceptable to use AI as a substitute for rebuilding the human-directed air traffic controller workforce.

“Dangerously rushing a system that holds Americans’ lives in its hands is not a good use case for artificial intelligence. I call on the FAA to immediately suspend its operation, at the very least until it is clearly established beyond doubt via air traffic controller feedback and independently verified stress testing that the technology is safe.”
title: Beyer Calls For Suspension Of AI System Deployed By FAA At Washington Area Airports

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that on September 18, 2026, a federal jury in New Haven found RYAN FIELDS, 52, of Port Neches, Texas, guilty of federal offenses related to illegally selling misbranded and unapproved prescription drugs.

According to the evidence introduced during the trial and other court proceedings, from September 2021 to June 2023, Fields and Lisa Mahan, who formerly resided in Glastonbury, Connecticut, operated two websites, pinnedaminos.com and projectaminos.com, as well as a private Facebook group called Pinned Aminos, through which they illegally sold and distributed to customers throughout the U.S. misbranded prescription drugs. They did not require customers to provide a valid prescription, and some of the drugs they sold and distributed were unapproved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for human consumption. The drugs they sold also included drugs they illegally imported from foreign manufacturers.

To avoid detection and mislead the FDA, the pinnedaminos.com website had a disclaimer that falsely stated that the products for sale were “intended for laboratory and research use only,” and “not intended for human ingestion.” In addition, the labeling on the drugs sold and delivered to customers falsely stated that the drugs were “research compounds” and/or “not for human consumption.” Contrary to these representations, Fields and Mahan knew and intended that the drugs they sold were for human use, and through emails and posts on the Pinned Aminos Facebook group, they provided customers with information on the health benefits of the drugs they sold and directions on dosage.

Fields unlawfully shipped over 10,000 parcels to customers throughout the country and collected more than $1.4 million from customers. Fields and Mahan used the proceeds to pay themselves, purchase cars, and purchase a residence in Texas.

Fields and Mahan were arrested on August 23, 2023.

The jury found Fields guilty of one count of conspiracy to introduce misbranded or unapproved drugs into interstate commerce and to smuggle goods into the United States, which carries a maximum term of imprisonment of five years, and one count of conspiracy to commit money laundering, which carries a maximum term of imprisonment of 20 years.

The jury also ordered the forfeiture of Fields’ Texas residence and a vehicle he purchased with proceeds from the conspiracy.

Fields is released on bond pending sentencing, which is not scheduled.

On April 6, 2026, Mahan, 56, pleaded guilty to the conspiracy charge. On August 13, 2026, she was sentenced to three years of probation.

This matter has been investigated by the Food and Drug Administration, Office of Criminal Investigations; the Drug Enforcement Administration; and Homeland Security Investigations. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Neeraj N. Patel and Justyn P. Stokely.

U.S. Attorney Sullivan thanked the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Texas for their assistance in this matter.
title: Former Connecticut Resident Guilty of Operating Websites to Illegally Sell Misbranded and Unapproved Drugs

text:
As the Department of the Air Force works to build a more connected and resilient Battle Network, military and industry leaders focused on one central challenge: how to move capability to the warfighter faster during a panel at the Air and Space Forces Association’s Air, Space & Cyber Conference, Sept. 15.
The “Next-Generation Battle Management” panel brought together Elaine Bitonti of Collins Aerospace; retired Maj. Gen. Scott Jobe with Boeing; retired Col. Sean Lowe with SAIC; and retired Maj. Luke Savoie with Elbit America. Brig. Gen. Joshua Williams, the Department of the Air Force portfolio acquisition executive for Command, Control, Communications and Battle Management, moderated the panel.
Williams opened by emphasizing the need to move beyond systems that operate independently of one another.
“The Department of the Air Force will not accept business models built on closed software stacks, black box hardware or restricted data interfaces,” Williams said. “The government must own and govern the technical baseline to ensure rapid iterative upgrades.”
For Savoie, that openness must extend from architecture to technology operating at the edge of the fight.
“How do you solve the compute portion on the edge, so that these tools and the connected network is working further and further forward and faster and faster within the loop of the folks that are on the front edge?” Savoie asked.
Bitonti connected that challenge directly to the movement of data across the force.
“I think first, you know, we understand from a battle management perspective, it’s all about how we’re moving the data,” Bitonti said, explaining that separating software from hardware and creating flexible communications architectures can allow systems to adapt as new requirements emerge.
That flexibility, the panelists agreed, is only useful if the DAF can test and field new capabilities quickly.
“One of the keys I think for the government is rapid prototyping, demonstrations and ensuring that we have industry partnerships,” Jobe said. “In order to really prove it to the DAF Battle Network or to the Joint Force, you got to go out there and demonstrate it, show that it’s real.”
Jobe pointed to a recent example in which an AMRAAM was launched from an MQ-28 Ghost Bat and integrated with an E-7 Wedgetail and F/A-18 Hornet within nine months.
“So that’s one example of the many things we’re doing and the rapid prototyping and getting to the field to demonstrate capabilities,” Jobe said.
The panel then turned to one of the biggest barriers between development and operational use: testing, security and accreditation.
Lowe described a process where software can move through development, security compliance, developmental testing and operational testing in sequence, with each transition potentially adding weeks or months.
“This is how you get months and years of delay,” Lowe said. He pointed to an approach where developmental and operational testers work alongside developers, allowing changes to be identified and addressed much earlier. “By putting the DTOT folks in the right places, particularly with the developmental teams, we can accelerate this.”
“The ATO process is … one, it’s out of control of most of the people in program office, and when you get to it, it does bring everything to a screeching halt,” Savoie said, calling for a broader examination of cybersecurity, information technology security and accreditation processes.
Jobe similarly pointed to the security environment as an area where policy and decision-making could move faster.
“I think we could probably move a lot faster,” Jobe said. “Maybe some communication and education to the personnel that are inside the acquisition system might be beneficial.”
For Bitonti, data sharing between services and coalition partners presents another policy challenge.
“We talk about really wanting to operate as a joint force and also with our coalition partners, but there are multiple restrictions, policy restrictions on rule sets of what data we can and can’t share,” she said.
“At this point, it’s not actually a technological impediment that is causing some of our struggles sharing data. It’s policy impediments.”
As the panel closed, Williams brought the discussion back to the DAF’s responsibility to deliver capability at the pace required by an evolving fight.
“Acquisition is a warfighting function,” Williams said. “We must deliver open, resilient, software-driven capability at the speed of operational relevance.”
title: Connecting the fight: AFA 2026 panel explores next-generation DAF battle management

Legislation would establish ambitious energy standard to rapidly reduce emissions and achieve up to 100% renewable energy generation by 2046

WASHINGTON, DC – Congresswoman Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09) joined U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-VT) and U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) in reintroducing the bicameral American Renewable Energy Act (AREA), legislation to establish an ambitious 70% renewable energy resource standard by 2036 to drastically reduce emissions, decrease pollution, and promote community resilience. To achieve this goal, AREA prioritizes the development and implementation of solar, wind, and geothermal energy, as well as marine energy, limited hydropower, and methane digesters for smaller farms and wastewater plants.

The bill also seeks to ensure the equitable distribution of economic, health, and resiliency benefits of renewable energy deployment by establishing an enforcement mechanism that requires at least 50% of collected funds be spent on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and storage projects in impacted communities.

“As we witness the devastating impacts of climate change on communities across our nation, we can no longer afford the luxury of inaction. The choices we make today will determine the world we leave to our children and grandchildren. We have the tools, the technology, and the knowledge to build a cleaner future; we need Congress to act,” said Rep. Clarke. “Investing in renewable energy also means confronting the environmental injustices that have left our nation’s most underserved communities bearing the greatest burden. My legislation puts clean energy technology and innovation to work, reducing emissions, improving air quality and health outcomes, and creating millions of good-paying renewable energy jobs. We cannot leave future generations to pay the price for problems we have the power to solve today.”

“Taking immediate, ambitious action to reduce emissions and build a clean energy future is essential to combating the climate crisis. Now is the time to enact a national renewable energy standard. Vermont has long led the nation in the clean energy transition, passing historic legislation just this summer that puts us on the path to achieve 100% renewable electricity by 2046,” said Senator Welch. “This bill will help the country follow in Vermont’s footsteps to speed the transition to renewables and build energy independence.”

“As Americans face skyrocketing electricity bills and the increasingly harmful impacts of the climate crisis, unleashing the power of clean energy has never been more important. This legislation will help us accelerate bringing cleaner options for consumers online while reducing emissions, lowering our dependence on fossil fuels and volatile global markets, creating new jobs, and cutting costs for working Americans. This is a key step in our fight towards a cleaner, healthier, and more affordable energy future,” said Senator Van Hollen.

AREA would require retail electricity suppliers to achieve at least 20% renewable energy generation in 2027, with an increase to 70% by 2036, and up to 100% by 2046. The bill would also require retail electricity suppliers to strengthen energy resilience by contributing an increasing share of their generation through distributed renewable energy, such as rooftop solar, starting with 15% in 2027, with an increase to 20% deployment requirement after five years.

Additionally, AREA also stipulates that electricity suppliers must meet their requirements by submitting renewable energy credits or paying an alternative compliance payment that begins at $50/megawatts per hour (MWh) and increases with inflation. Compliance with the bill would be facilitated by the creation of six regional credit trading markets to track retail electricity suppliers’ transition to renewable energy and ensure the benefits of renewable energy development are spread across the country.

Further, AREA seeks to ensure the equitable distribution of economic, health, and resiliency benefits and investments created by renewable energy deployment by establishing an enforcement mechanism that requires at least 50% of collected funds to be spent on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and storage projects in impacted communities. The legislation would also require utilities to produce 20% of their energy generation from renewables in impacted communities, reducing the need for polluting fossil fuel power plants in historically marginalized areas.

The American Renewable Energy Act is endorsed by the Chesapeake Climate Action Network; Evergreen Action; Sierra Club; Indivisible; and Vote Solar.

“The American Renewable Energy Act (AREA) is a major step toward building an electric grid that is cleaner, more affordable, and more just. By setting a strong national renewable electricity standard while ensuring that the benefits of the clean energy transition reach frontline and impacted communities, AREA will help reduce harmful pollution, create good-paying jobs, and protect families from the rising costs of fossil fuels. Chesapeake Climate Action Network (CCAN) Action Fund proudly supports AREA and urges Congress to move this bill forward to deliver the clean energy future that American families across the country deserve,” said Quentin Scott, Federal Policy Director, CCAN Action Fund.

“Shifting to renewable energy is no longer just an option, it is the necessary next step for the United States to meet the urgency of the climate crisis. The American Renewable Energy Act is the bold legislation we need to meet rising electricity demand, while improving public health, reducing American reliance on fossil fuels, and creating new jobs to supercharge our clean energy economy,” said Lena Moffitt, Executive Director, Evergreen Action. “The transition to clean energy is well underway and the federal government must be a leader in ensuring Americans benefit from the lower energy costs and cleaner air that renewable energy can deliver.”

“In the last year, electricity cost increases rapidly outpaced the rate of inflation while toxic and deadly emissions from coal plants spiked significantly,” said Patrick Drupp, ClimatePolicy Director, Sierra Club. “It is more urgent than ever that we invest in affordable, reliable, and clean energy to relieve families from soaring bills and protect our communities from more deadly pollution. Despite Donald Trump’s persistent attacks on clean energy, it is evident that Americans want more clean energy because of how much cleaner, cheaper, and faster it is. We applaud Senator Peter Welch for his work as a steadfast champion of the American Renewable Energy Act and look forward to working together more in the future.”

“A strong federal renewable energy standard establishes a clear national floor for clean energy while preserving states’ ability to pursue even more ambitious policies,” said Nathan Phelps, Managing Director, Vote Solar. “This legislation provides the certainty needed to accelerate investment in affordable, reliable clean energy, expanding access to solar and the benefits of the clean energy transition. By complementing state renewable energy standards, a federal RPS ensures that communities across the country can benefit from lower energy costs, cleaner air, and a stronger economy.”

Learn more about the American Renewable Energy Act of 2026.

Read the full bill text here.

title: CLARKE, WELCH, VAN HOLLEN REINTRODUCE BICAMERAL BILL TO CREATE 70% RENEWABLE ENERGY RESOURCE STANDARD BY 2036, SPEED U.S. CLEAN ENERGY TRANSITION

Criminal illegal alien in ICE custody passes away at Winnfield Correctional Center in Louisiana
NEW ORLEANS — Carlos Josue Marchena-Marchena, a 36-year-old criminal illegal alien from Costa Rica, passed away in ICE custody Sept 18, 2026. His criminal history includes convictions for retail fraud and malicious destruction of personal property with a separate arrest for retail fraud second degree, and an arrest for assault.
On Sept. 18, Marchena was found unresponsive and staff at Winnfield Correctional Center immediately called a medical emergency and began life-saving measures. Emergency Medical Services (EMS) responded to prepare transportation of Marchena to Winn Parish Medical Center (WPMC) for advanced medical treatment. Upon arrival at WPMC, medical staff and EMS continued resuscitative efforts. Despite life-saving efforts, at approximately 8:00 am, an onsite physician at WPMC pronounced Marchena deceased. The official cause of death remains pending further medical examination.
U.S Border Patrol arrested Marchena for illegally entering the United States without inspection on or about Feb. 9, 2021. He was convicted of retail fraud April 4, 2024, and malicious destruction of personal property Aug. 12, 2025, in the 58th District Court in Holland, Michigan. He was arrested by ICE Jan. 14, 2026, after his arrest by the Ottawa County Sheriff’s Department (Michigan) for assault. On July 29, 2026, a DOJ immigration judge ordered him removed.
While in custody, Marchena received proper medical care and was seen by medical professionals.
Consistent with ICE policy, Enforcement and Removal Operations notified the Department of Homeland Security, the ICE Office of Inspector General and the ICE Office of Professional Responsibility via the Joint Intake Operation Center. The Consulate of Costa Rica was notified.
ICE makes official notifications to Congress, nongovernmental organization stakeholders and the media upon reports of in-custody deaths and posts news releases with relevant details on its public website. Information is available in the ICE Newsroom and on the Detainee Death Reporting page.
ICE is committed to ensuring that all those in custody reside in safe, secure and humane environments. Comprehensive medical care is provided from the moment individuals arrive and throughout their stay. All people in ICE custody receive medical, dental and mental health intake screenings within 12 hours of arriving at each detention facility, a full health assessment within 14 days of entering ICE custody or arriving at a facility, access to medical appointments and 24-hour emergency care. At no time during detention is a detained noncitizen denied emergency care.

IR-2026-113, Sept. 21, 2026
WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service last week wrapped up the fifth and final 2026 Tax Forum in San Diego with nearly 13,000 attending the five forums where tax professionals participated in workshops and seminars and received one-on-one assistance with taxpayer cases.
“The tax forums provide a great opportunity for the IRS to hear feedback from tax professionals and for the IRS to provide presentations on emerging tax policies,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano. “The two-way communications at the tax forums give all stakeholders a professional space to share critical insights about how tax law operates in practical, real-world situations. Year after year, the tax forums prove their value as a tool to enhance tax administration.”
Other forums this year were held in Chicago, New Orleans, New York and Orlando.
Each forum included a Case Resolution Room that allowed the Taxpayer Advocate Service, along with the IRS, to focus on some of the toughest cases through one-on-one assistance. This year 1,165 cases were resolved during the five events.
Also at the Digital Account Services Room, 1,635 tax professionals were able to get assistance with e-services, Preparer Identification Numbers (PTIN) and identity authentication support.
Topics covered in seminars and workshops included Artificial Intelligence, Digital Assets Information Reporting, managing IRS collection cases and navigating IRS audits. There were multiple sessions covering provisions in the Working Families Tax Cuts including no tax on tips and no tax on overtime, and what to expect during the upcoming 2027 filing season.
Commenting on the meeting, Felicia Jester, a tax professional from Atlanta, Georgia and owner of Mastermind Taxes, said “the IRS and tax professional speakers and presenters were extremely knowledgeable and engaging. You can genuinely tell that the presenters care about getting accurate and useful information out to tax professionals. I also really appreciated the Q&A portions of the sessions and the Stakeholder Liaison and Case Resolution tables.”
“I personally visited the Stakeholder Liaison table for assistance with an actual client case, and they were extremely helpful in pointing me in the right direction. Being able to take what I learned at the Forum and immediately apply it to help a client made the experience even more valuable. I’m already looking forward to attending again in 2027,” she added.
The event also featured an Expo Hall that had IRS engagement tables and an IRS Zone for tax pros to connect directly with IRS subject matter experts who were able to answer questions and provide IRS resources and services. The Forum also included participation from associate partners, including: the American Bar Association, the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, Low Income Taxpayer Clinics, the National Association of Enrolled Agents, the National Association of Tax Professionals, the National Society of Accountants, the National Society of Tax Professionals and the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance Program.
title: IRS wraps up successful Nationwide Tax Forums with nearly 13,000 attendees

SACRAMENTO, Calif. — Christopher William Edward Abplanalp, 38, of Roseville, pleaded guilty today to one count of wire fraud, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced.

According to court documents, between February 2023 and July 2025, working as an executive manager at a Placer County business, Abplanalp stole more than $2.3 million, most of which he then spent gambling. In executing this scheme, he diverted money from the business’s account with an online payment processing system to his own personal account, or to various other friends or acquaintances. Abplanalp also repeatedly charged a client’s credit card for items the client had not ordered and for invoices that did not exist, and then transferred the proceeds to himself. He also instructed clients to tender payments directly to him, and told vendors to issue rebates and refunds to his personal account, rather than the business. To conceal his theft, Abplanalp altered, deleted or made false entries to the business’s accounting software.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation conducted the investigation with assistance from IRS Criminal Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Dhruv M. Sharma is prosecuting the case.

Abplanalp is scheduled to be sentenced by U.S. District Judge Dale A. Drozd on Feb. 8, 2027. Abplanalp faces a maximum statutory penalty of 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. The actual sentence, however, will be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables.
title: Roseville man pleads guilty to defrauding employer of more than $2.3 million

Washington, D.C.–Today, Congresswomen Deborah Ross (NC-02) and Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Tropospheric Ozone Research Act of 2026 to fund multi-year scientific research on the warming effects of tropospheric ozone. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Brian Schatz (D-HI) introduced companion legislation in the Senate earlier this year.

Unlike the ozone layer that protects the Earth from UV radiation, tropospheric ozone is a major air pollutant and potent greenhouse gas found near the surface of the Earth. It causes an estimated 500,000 premature deaths and up to 26 percent losses in crop yields globally each year. Tropospheric ozone is also the third-largest driver of climate change after carbon dioxide and methane.

Because tropospheric ozone lasts only weeks in the atmosphere, cutting tropospheric ozone could significantly reduce temperatures in the near term, alleviating the severity of climate change effects and reducing the risk of crossing climate tipping points.

The bill would fund a three-year, $10M per year scientific research program on the warming effects of tropospheric ozone. It would also direct EPA to publish a summary report identifying key findings, assessing the costs and benefits of mitigating tropospheric ozone precursors, and providing policy recommendations and future research needs.

The legislation is endorsed by the Clean Air Task Force and the Natural Resources Defense Council.

“For years, we have known that tropospheric ozone pollution is costing lives and driving climate change, but there is still so much we need to understand to effectively address it,” said Congresswoman Deborah Ross. “This bill will empower our scientific community to find solutions to reduce tropospheric ozone’s harmful effects and its contributions to global warming. We need research and information in order to act against super pollutants like tropospheric ozone so we can confront the growing climate crisis.”

"In the wake of continued cuts to climate research funding by the Trump administration, it is now more important than ever to support the efforts at scientific research institutions and universities to better understand the ozone so that municipalities, farmers, and legislatures alike can be better prepared for future events caused by climate change,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04). “I’m proud to co-lead the Tropospheric Ozone Research Act with Congresswoman Ross to improve scientific understanding of the tropospheric ozone’s warming impacts and inform future strategies to reduce global temperatures.”

“The Tropospheric Ozone Research Act of 2026 and its House companion bill would advance our understanding of ground-level ozone as a climate super pollutant, said Dr. Richie Kaur, Senior Superpollutant Reduction Advocate at NRDC. “Tropospheric ozone is an air pollutant and a fast-acting driver of warming that damages human health, food systems, and ecosystems, with disproportionate impacts on vulnerable communities. At the same time, it represents a great opportunity for near-term progress—where stronger science can inform practical policies that deliver rapid public health, ecosystem, and climate benefits. As the world overshoots 1.5 degrees of warming above pre-industrial levels, we need to examine every tool in the climate toolkit to bend the warming curve.”

“Tropospheric ozone pollution has been neglected by policymakers despite its contribution to roughly half a million premature deaths a year, billions of dollars in economic damages, and about a quarter degree of present-day warming," said Darin Schroeder, Methane Legal and Regulatory Director at Clean Air Task Force. "The research funded by this bill and its companion in the Senate would create the knowledge base to change that inaction. This scientific investment would improve our understanding of how tropospheric ozone moves through and affects our atmosphere, providing a firm foundation for the US to better develop and target the solutions to drive this harmful pollutant down.”

Bill text is available here.

###
title: Ross + Foushee Introduce Bill Advancing Science to Reduce Warming from Tropospheric Ozone, a Potent Air Pollutant and Greenhouse Gas

U.S. Representative Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) introduced a resolution to recognize the importance of protecting continuous Medicaid coverage for individuals who are undergoing cancer treatment. Interruption to health coverage during cancer treatment can create unnecessary risk and hardship for patients. More than 75% of individuals undergoing cancer care have delayed or skipped vital treatment due to administrative issues with third-party systems. In many states, cancer patients are required to repeatedly verify their medical circumstances, even when state Medicaid programs already hold the necessary information. Streamlining Medicaid processes and reducing these hurdles is essential to ensuring support for those receiving cancer treatment.

"No one fighting cancer should ever have to pause or skip lifesaving treatment because of bureaucratic red tape. Forcing patients to jump through redundant administrative hoops creates unnecessary hardship and puts lives at risk. This resolution recognizes the importance of continuous coverage so that patients on Medicaid can focus on what matters most: their health and recovery."

The resolution is endorsed by Less Cancer.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE.
title: Dingell Introduces Resolution Recognizing the Importance of Continuous Care for Patients Undergoing Cancer Treatment on Medicaid

DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a man who fired multiple rounds from an AR‑style rifle off the Margaret McDermott Bridge amid New Year’s Eve celebrations was sentenced to 35 months in federal prison for unlawfully possessing a firearm as an illegal alien.

Jose Raul Alarcon Sanchez, an illegal alien from Mexico, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge David C. Godbey. In imposing the 35‑month sentence, Judge Godbey noted that although Alarcon Sanchez is young, his conduct was “incredibly dangerous” and warranted a significant term of imprisonment.

“Spraying rifle fire off a downtown bridge is a lawless act that puts our Dallas residents at risk. This sentence makes clear that anyone who turns a celebration into a crime scene will face swift and serious federal consequences,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “We will not tolerate violent, brazen conduct that endangers the public, and we will continue to use every federal tool available to protect North Texans.”

“Spraying rifle fire off a downtown bridge is a lawless act that puts our Dallas residents at risk. This sentence makes clear that anyone who turns a celebration into a crime scene will face swift and serious federal consequences,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “We will not tolerate violent, brazen conduct that endangers the public, and we will continue to use every federal tool available to protect North Texans.”

“This case is a clear example of why we never stop working the evidence,” said ATF Dallas Field Division Special Agent in Charge Brian Garner. “What happened on that bridge could have ended in tragedy, but our agents and our law enforcement partners methodically followed the evidence—from the shell casings recovered at the scene to the firearm and ultimately to the individual who pulled the trigger. When someone recklessly uses a firearm in a way that puts innocent people in danger, ATF will use every investigative resource available to identify that firearm, identify the shooter, and build the case necessary to hold them accountable.”

According to court records, just after midnight on Jan. 1, Alarcon Sanchez and another man stood among stopped vehicles and crowds gathered to watch celebratory fireworks from the Margaret McDermott Bridge. The two men took turns filming each other firing black rifles over the side of the bridge.

On Jan. 5, Dallas Police Department officers recovered significant ballistic evidence at the scene, including seventy‑nine 5.56/.223 caliber fired cartridge casings and multiple 9mm and .40 caliber casings both on and beneath the bridge. Additional matching cartridge casings and ammunition were recovered from Alarcon Sanchez’s pockets and his van when he was arrested by Grand Prairie Police later that night in response to a separate “shots fired” call.

A subsequent search warrant executed at Alarcon Sanchez’s residence on Jan. 28, resulted in the recovery of multiple firearms, including an AR‑15‑style pistol later linked to the fired cartridge casings found on the bridge. Agents also recovered his Mexican passport and confirmed that he had overstayed a temporary visitor visa issued in May 2025.

Investigators additionally located social media photographs and videos posted by Alarcon Sanchez days before and immediately after the New Year’s Eve shooting, depicting him holding and firing the same AR‑style rifles believed to have been used on the bridge.

The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Dallas Field Division and the Dallas Police Department conducted the investigation, with assistance from the Grand Prairie Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Marissa Aulbaugh from the Violent Crimes section prosecuted the case.

###
title: Illegal alien who fired AR style rifle from crowded Dallas bridge on New Year’s Eve sentenced to 35 months in prison

MEDIA AVAILABILITY: Coast Guard opens new recruiting office on Long Island
Editor’s Note: Media interested in attending should contact Chief Petty Officer Cory Green at Cory.J.Green@uscg.mil no later than Thursday, Oct. 2, 2026, to RSVP.
WHO: Capt. Jay W. Guyer, commander, Coast Guard Accessions Service Center; Chief Petty Officer Cory Green, recruiter-in-charge, Coast Guard Recruiting Office Long Island; local government and community leaders; Coast Guard recruiters; and participating Coast Guard units.
WHAT: Coast Guard Recruiting Office Long Island Grand Opening and community outreach event. The event will include an official ribbon-cutting ceremony, remarks from Coast Guard and local leadership, recruiting engagement opportunities, and displays highlighting Coast Guard missions and capabilities.
WHEN: Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. Event from noon to 3 p.m. Setup begins at 11 a.m.
WHERE: Coast Guard Recruiting Office Long Island, 235 Sunrise Highway, Lynbrook, NY.
LYNBROOK, N.Y. — The Coast Guard is scheduled to hold a grand opening ceremony for the new Coast Guard Recruiting Office Long Island in Lynbrook, Saturday formally establishing a dedicated recruiting presence serving communities across Long Island.
The grand opening will bring together Coast Guard leadership, local officials, community members and Coast Guard operational units for a public event highlighting the service’s missions, capabilities and career opportunities.
Long Island’s geography and maritime heritage provide a natural connection to the Coast Guard’s missions. Communities across the island are surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean, Long Island Sound and an extensive network of bays, harbors and waterways where Coast Guard members perform missions including search and rescue, maritime safety and security, law enforcement, environmental protection and homeland security.
The establishment of Recruiting Office Long Island provides residents with a dedicated local resource to learn about opportunities to serve in both the active-duty and reserve components of the Coast Guard and connects the service more directly with Long Island’s schools, colleges, community organizations and prospective applicants.
Capt. Jay W. Guyer, commander, Coast Guard Accessions Service Center, is scheduled to participate in the ceremony and provide remarks commemorating the opening of the new recruiting office.
“Long Island has a proud maritime heritage and a natural connection to the missions of the United States Coast Guard. Establishing a dedicated recruiting presence here allows us to build stronger relationships with these communities and introduce more young Americans to the opportunities that come with Coast Guard service. As our service continues to grow to meet the nation’s evolving maritime challenges, offices like this will help us find and develop the next generation of Coast Guard men and women.”
The event is designed to be more than a traditional ribbon cutting. Members of the public will have an opportunity to meet Coast Guard members, speak directly with recruiters and experience displays representing Coast Guard operational missions and capabilities.
Planned displays and activities include Coast Guard operational and recruiting assets, with opportunities for attendees and media to learn more about the people, equipment and missions of the Coast Guard. Specific participating assets will be announced as availability is finalized.
For local students, young adults and families, the event will also provide an opportunity to learn about Coast Guard career paths, training, education benefits and opportunities to serve the nation while performing missions that have a direct connection to the maritime communities surrounding Long Island.
“This office gives us an opportunity to become part of the Long Island community rather than simply recruit from it,” said Chief Petty Officer Cory Green, recruiter-in-charge of Coast Guard Recruiting Office Long Island. “Long Island is surrounded by the waterways where Coast Guard men and women serve every day. We want students, families and community members to know who we are, understand what we do, and know that there is now a Coast Guard recruiting office right here in their community where they can learn how they can be part of that mission.”
The mission of Recruiting Office Long Island is to connect individuals throughout Long Island with opportunities to serve in the Coast Guard and guide prospective applicants toward meaningful careers in the service.
Learn more about Coast Guard Recruiting Office Long Island here.
For information about joining the Coast Guard, visit GoCoastGuard.com.
