KANSAS CITY, KAN. – A federal jury convicted a Missouri man of forcing and coercing minors to commit sexual acts with adults in exchange for money.

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, Calvin Johnson, 31, of Kansas City, Missouri, was found guilty on:

• two counts of sex trafficking accomplished by force, fraud, or coercion; • two counts of sex trafficking of a child; and • two counts of transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity.

Between February 2022 and January 2023, Johnson transported two minors within Kansas as well as other states including Missouri and Nebraska, while using force and coercion to compel the vulnerable victims to engage in commercial sex acts.

On April 20, 2022, the Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) spoke to a minor after a traffic stop. Law enforcement learned the victim was a runaway from the juvenile care system and performing commercial sex acts at the behest of Johnson. The victim indicated Johnson booked motel rooms, posted solicitations for clients on websites, rented cars, and transported the victim to hotels for commercial sex acts.

On January 17, 2023, law enforcement encountered the second minor inside a motel room. The second victim was also a runaway.

A forensic search of the victims’ cellphones and social media accounts showed communications with Johnson clearly indicating he was selling the victims for sexual services. Johnson directed the victims to have clients send him money on digital payment apps then he kept all payments. Investigators obtained booking information from various hotels across multiple states in the region and found evidence of rooms booked and paid for by Johnson.

“Human traffickers are known to prey on underage runaways because these minors have multiple vulnerabilities that increase the likelihood they will become targets of exploitation and abuse,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan A. Kriegshauser. “We at the Department of Justice are relentless in advocating for the rights of human trafficking victims and seeking justice on their behalf.”

The Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) are investigating the case.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Faiza Alhambra and Audrey McCormick are prosecuting the case.

Project Safe Childhood

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc.

title: Jury convicts Missouri man of sex trafficking minors

Five Defendants Charged with Defrauding and Exploiting H-2A Visa Program to Smuggle Aliens into the United States
ATLANTA — U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) supported a federal investigation that resulted in the indictment of five people for their roles in a scheme to exploit a nonimmigrant visa worker program. The defendants fraudulently obtained worker visas and smuggled aliens into the United States. The U.S. Attorney for Southern District of Georgia made the announcement.
According to court documents, Martha Aquino, also known as “Martha Patricia Resendez Sanchez” or “Marta,” 61; Evangelina Aquino De Galvan, 49; and Julio Cervantes, 38, all of Alma, Georgia; as well as Marco Cervantes, also known as “Chiquilin,” 41, of Rowlett, Georgia; and Juan Felipe Romero-Lopez, 31, an illegal alien from Mexico, conspired to exploit the H-2A visa program by fraudulently obtaining temporary visas to bring workers into the United States.
The defendants lied about where the workers would work and reside and did not comply with the laws and rules governing the visa program. Specifically, they demanded and received improper payments from the workers before the workers could seek H-2A visas or begin working in the United States. They confiscated and withheld the workers’ identification documents, including passports, and at times threatened or used violence against the workers to deter them from leaving or failing to work. After the workers’ visas expired, the conspirators enabled them to remain in the United States and even offered to transport them elsewhere in the United States in exchange for additional improper payments.
Aquino, Julio Cervantes, and Marco Cervantes were arrested. Aquino De Galvan remains at large. Romero-Lopez has been detained after being originally charged in May 2026 for unlawful possession of a firearm by an illegal alien. Aquino, Aquino De Galvan, and Julio Cervantes are charged with conspiring to commit visa fraud, visa fraud, and encouraging and inducing aliens to enter the United States illegally for commercial advantage and private gain. Marco Cervantes is charged with conspiring to commit visa fraud and visa fraud. Romero-Lopez is charged with conspiring to commit visa fraud and being an illegal alien in possession of a firearm.
If convicted, all five defendants face a maximum penalty of five years in prison for visa fraud conspiracy. Aquino, Aquino De Galvan, Julio Cervantes, and Marco Cervantes also each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for visa fraud. Aquino, Aquino De Galvan, and Julio Cervantes each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison for encouraging and inducing illegal entry, and Romero-Lopez faces a maximum penalty of 15 years in prison for being an illegal alien in possession of a firearm.
This case is being investigated by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations in Savannah, the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service, the Department of Labor’s Office of Inspector General, and the Georgia Bureau of Investigation. HSI’s Human Smuggling Unit in Washington, D.C.; U.S. Custom and Border Protection’s National Targeting Center International Interdiction Task Force; and USCIS assisted with the investigation.
An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

title: Five Defendants Charged with Defrauding and Exploiting H-2A Visa Program to Smuggle Aliens into the United States

Gainesville, Florida – DeShawn Russ, 36, of Jacksonville, Florida, was sentenced to nine years in federal prison for possession of ammunition by a convicted felon. The sentence was announced by John P. Heekin, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Florida.

U.S. Attorney Heekin said: “Keeping this violent, serial felon off our streets and locked away behind bars is necessary to protect our communities from his continued criminality. I am grateful for the excellent investigative work by the Gainesville Police Department, with support from our federal law enforcement partners, that facilitated this successful prosecution by my office.”

Court documents reflect that the Gainesville Police Department responded to a shooting within a vehicle where officers found a bullet hole in the driver’s window. Russ, who was known to the driver, was located nearby. Although no firearm was recovered, a .380 bullet was located in his pocket. Russ is multi-time convicted felon and is therefore prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. At sentencing, the Court found that the defendant shot the firearm and then engaged in obstruction by encouraging witnesses to change their statements.

“Time and again, convicted felons who are prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition continue to place our community at risk,” said Gainesville Police Chief Nelson Moya. “We are grateful for the thorough work of our investigators and our federal partners in holding him accountable for his actions.”

The case involved an investigation by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives and the Gainesville Police Department. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Christie S. Utt.

Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN) is the Department of Justice’s nationwide initiative that brings federal, state, local, and tribal law enforcement, prosecutors, and other public safety partners together to coordinate efforts to combat violent crime and make communities safe. Coordinated by U.S. Attorneys’ offices in each of the 94 federal districts, PSN is tailored to particular communities to strategically address specific violent crime and public safety challenges. As a key component of Operation Take Back America, PSN serves a central role in the Department’s commitment to make our country safe. PSN emphasizes three core principles: rapid federal response to violent crime and criminal offenders; strong, strategic partnerships among law enforcement at all levels; and accountability and deterrence through the prosecution of the most serious, readily provable offenses and other strategies. These efforts complement and strengthen President Trump’s Homeland Security Task Forces, ensuring a comprehensive federal response to the most pressing public safety issues facing communities .

The United States Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Florida is one of 94 offices that serve as the nation’s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. To access public court documents online, please visit the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Florida website. For more information about the United States Attorney’s Office, Northern District of Florida, visit https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndfl .
title: Convicted Felon Sentenced to Nine Years in Federal Prison for Possession of Ammunition

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives April McClain Delaney, Sarah Elfreth, and Johnny Olszewski and U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (all D-Md.) announced $33,931,039 in federal funding to support infrastructure and equipment upgrades at Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI), Carroll County Regional Airport, and Hagerstown Regional Airport. The investments will fund important safety improvements at all three airports, as well as upgraded equipment and an evaluation of the noise exposure at BWI, including its impact on surrounding communities, which members of Maryland’s Congressional Delegation urged the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to address in April.

"Maryland’s airports and aviation industry are crucial for trade and business. Thanks to the hard work of Team Maryland, our congressional offices secured more than $30 million to make our airports safer, more accessible, and more efficient. These investments will provide Hagerstown Regional Airport with the funds necessary to make improvements to its 2/20 runway and adjacent building infrastructure—critical safety upgrades needed to fully comply with FAA guidance,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney.

“Maryland’s airports are economic engines, serving travelers and businesses across the region and around the world. That’s why we worked to deliver these investments in important updates to BWI, Carroll County Regional, and Hagerstown Regional airports. These federal funds will help ensure these airports meet important safety standards, and, at BWI, will support efforts to address local communities’ noise concerns,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“Our airports here in Maryland fuel our economy, connect us to the rest of the world, and support our businesses. I am proud to partner with my colleagues to announce over $33 million in federal funding to upgrade the infrastructure at three of our airports. Modernizing our infrastructure is an investment in our future and in our safety – I’m glad we are getting this done,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

“Airports are not simply places where flights arrive and depart – they are engines of opportunity, connecting people to jobs, businesses to customers, communities to global markets, and regions to long-term economic growth,” said Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth. “Each of Maryland’s airports, including the Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport here in the Third Congressional District, has played a critical role in the growth of our communities, our state, and our nation. I was grateful to work with Team Maryland to secure this much-needed $21 million investment for BWI that will evaluate noise exposure for our neighbors and ensure the safety of worldwide travelers,” said Congresswoman Elfreth.

“As Maryland continues to grow, we must ensure our airports have the infrastructure and equipment they need to operate safely, efficiently, and effectively,” said Congressman Olszewski. “This funding will strengthen our aviation infrastructure and help ensure these facilities can continue serving our communities and the rest of the nation. I was proud to work with Team Maryland to help deliver these critical investments.”

The federal funding has been announced as follows:

$21,091,172 to Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI) to support an evaluation of noise exposure at the airport and surrounding areas as well as the reconstruction of 110,000 square yards of the existing North Cargo Apron pavement and installation of low-emission equipment, including five gate electrification systems and remote ground power units.

$7,609,500 to Carroll County Regional Airport to shift Runway 16/34 by 250 feet to bring the airport into conformity with current standards.

$5,230,367 to Hagerstown Regional Airport to remove a building and relocate fencing identified as obstructive by the Federal Aviation Administration. The funding will also help the airport rehabilitate lighting and 3000 feet of pavement on Runway 2/20 to maintain the structural integrity and minimize foreign object debris.

These investments are provided through the FAA’s Airport Improvement Program (AIP). Senator Van Hollen worked to fund the AIP through the passage of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, which authorized $4 billion a year for Fiscal Years 2025 through 2028.
title: Maryland Congressional Delegation Members Announce Over $30 Million for Infrastructure Upgrades at Maryland Airports

NORWICH, CT – This week, House Speaker Mike Johnson canceled another day of scheduled House votes. Earlier this month, Speaker Jonhson also canceled the last two weeks of previously scheduled voting days in September, meaning that the House of Representatives will not return to session for over seven weeks until November 9th. In total, Speaker Johnson has canceled 23 House voting days so far in 2026.

“It’s beyond irresponsible that Speaker Johnson is choosing to shut down the House of Representatives while AI executives are sending urgent warnings on the need for AI safeguards,” Courtney said. “Congress would not be starting from scratch on this issue. There are commonsense, bipartisan AI safeguard bills ready to be voted on. For example, I strongly support the AI Kill Switch Act to put emergency third-party protections in place to protect against the threat of rogue AI programs acting outside of human control. The CEO of Anthropic has endorsed this approach. I am also a cosponsor of the Preventing Deepfakes of Intimate Images Act, a bill to criminalize creating and posting non-consensual deepfakes on social media. This bill is especially needed to address the disturbing surge of instances of generative AI use related to child sexual exploitation reported to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. The House could vote on these two bills today and take real action to protect the public. Speaker Johnson instead chose to cancel votes – a dereliction of duty.”

This week, Rep. Courtney joined over 100 colleagues in calling on Speaker Johnson to cancel his premature recess in order to pass bipartisan AI safeguard bills.

title: Courtney Statement on Speaker Johnson Shutting Down of the House of Representatives

text:
WASHINGTON, DC — A días de cumplirse nueve años del huracán María, el comisionado residente Pablo José Hernández, junto al demócrata de mayor rango del Comité de Seguridad Nacional de la Cámara de Representantes, Bennie Thompson (MS-02), y la representante Nellie Pou (NJ-09), presentó al H.R. 10441 - Puerto Rico Disaster Recovery Completion Act of 2026, para dar a Puerto Rico hasta 2035 para completar proyectos elegibles de recuperación financiados por FEMA y evitar que las fechas límite federales se conviertan en otro obstáculo para terminar la reconstrucción.

“Agilizar la reconstrucción es parte de nuestra agenda para priorizar lo básico. Tenemos un problema: los fondos para ciertos proyectos tienen fecha de expiración y hay que pedir extensiones para cada uno. Eso toma tiempo y aumenta la carga burocrática. Por eso proponemos una extensión para todos los proyectos hasta 2035”.

“Sin lugar a dudas, Puerto Rico debe contar con todas las herramientas que necesita para poder reconstruirse tras el huracán María, un desastre devastador que la administración Trump manejó mal desde el principio. La recuperación de Puerto Rico no debe verse obstaculizada por plazos ni trabas burocráticas que dificulten completar la recuperación de la isla”, añadió el miembro de mayor rango Thompson. “Puerto Rico debe contar con el tiempo que necesita para reconstruirse por completo, y agradezco al comisionado residente Hernández por presentar esta legislación.”

“Como una de los pocos miembros puertorriqueños del Congreso, asumo con gran seriedad nuestra responsabilidad con la isla y su gente. Esta legislación dará a nuestros conciudadanos estadounidenses el tiempo y la flexibilidad que necesitan para recuperarse plenamente”, dijo la congresista Pou (Traducción del inglés). “Ahora mismo, en 2026, hay familias que dependen de cargar agua de pozos para beber y lavar su ropa. La red eléctrica continúa en condiciones críticas. Nuestro gobierno federal debe dar a los puertorriqueños todas las herramientas y el tiempo que necesitan para recuperarse plenamente. Este proyecto de ley es un primer paso clave.”

“En Mayagüez hemos vivido de primera mano lo complejo que ha sido llevar adelante los proyectos de reconstrucción. Hay procesos de permisos, revisiones, contrataciones y otras gestiones que requieren coordinación con distintas agencias y que no siempre están bajo el control de los municipios. Darle a Puerto Rico hasta 2035 nos permitiría completar proyectos que ya tienen fondos asignados, sin perder la fiscalización ni los requisitos federales. Por eso respaldo esta medida y la gestión del Comisionado Residente para que podamos terminar la reconstrucción que nuestro pueblo todavía necesita.” dijo Jorge Luis Ramos Ruiz, Alcalde de Mayagüez.

A días del noveno aniversario del huracán María, la reconstrucción de Puerto Rico sigue inconclusa. Al 30 de septiembre de 2025, COR3 reportó 19,202 proyectos activos de recuperación relacionados con María que ya tenían fondos obligados, pero que todavía no habían llegado a su cierre, una muestra de la magnitud del trabajo que queda pendiente casi una década después del huracán.

COR3 ha identificado entre los cuellos de botella los complejos requisitos federales, los procesos de permisos y revisión ambiental, las limitaciones de mano de obra y de la cadena de suministros, y los retos de coordinación entre las entidades locales y federales, factores que continúan retrasando el paso de fondos obligados a proyectos completados.

Esos atrasos fueron precisamente lo que el Comisionado Residente junto a los Congresistas Thompson y Pou examinaron este verano durante una delegación del Comité de Seguridad Nacional (Homeland Security) de la Cámara de Representantes a Puerto Rico. Los miembros se reunieron con funcionarios de FEMA, alcaldes y líderes locales para escuchar directamente los obstáculos que enfrenta la reconstrucción y visitaron proyectos como la Escuela Superior Francisco Morales en Naranjito, donde la reconstrucción permanente no comenzó hasta años después de María.

Puerto Rico todavía tiene proyectos de reconstrucción de FEMA sin completar, pero esos proyectos no tienen una sola fecha límite común. Cada obra tiene su propio plazo de ejecución y, cuando no puede terminarse a tiempo, el Gobierno tiene que solicitar una extensión a FEMA proyecto por proyecto.

El Puerto Rico Disaster Recovery Completion Act of 2026 responde directamente a ese problema al extender hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2035 el periodo de ejecución y la fecha límite para completar los proyectos de recuperación de FEMA cubiertos por la medida. Esto daría más tiempo para terminar proyectos elegibles, mientras obliga a FEMA a informar qué obras continúan pendientes, qué obstáculos están provocando atrasos y cuándo se espera que sean completadas.

La legislación:

Extendería hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2035 el plazo para completar proyectos elegibles de obras permanentes de FEMA que todavía no hayan llegado a su cierre;

Permitiría solicitar extensiones adicionales después de 2035 mediante el proceso existente de FEMA cuando sea necesario;

Cubriría proyectos elegibles relacionados con los huracanes Irma y María, los terremotos de 2019-2020 y el huracán Fiona; y

Requeriría que FEMA, en consulta con COR3, presente informes anuales al Congreso y al Comisionado Residente detallando cuántos proyectos se han completado, cuándo se espera completar los que siguen en curso y qué obstáculos están retrasando las obras.

Este requisito de informes permanecería vigente hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2035, dando al Congreso una evaluación anual del progreso de los proyectos de recuperación cubiertos por la medida en Puerto Rico.

###

Nine Years After María, Hernández, Thompson and Pou Introduce Bill to Give Puerto Rico More Time to Finish Reconstruction

Hernandez’s legislation would provide Puerto Rico until 2035 to complete eligible disaster recovery projects and require FEMA to report on obstacles and timelines.

WASHINGTON, DC — As Puerto Rico approaches the ninth anniversary of Hurricane María, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández of Puerto Rico alongside House Homeland Security Committee Ranking Member Bennie Thompson (MS-02) and Representative Nellie Pou (NJ-09) introduced H.R. 10441 - Puerto Rico Disaster Recovery Completion Act of 2026 to give Puerto Rico until 2035 to complete eligible FEMA-funded recovery projects and prevent federal deadlines from standing in the way of finishing the reconstruction.

“Nine years after María, Puerto Rico should be talking about a reconstruction completed, not deadlines that could get in the way of finishing it,” said Resident Commissioner Hernández. “Our communities have waited long enough. This bill gives Puerto Rico the time to finish the work while making sure FEMA remains accountable for getting these projects across the finish line.”

“Without question, Puerto Rico should be given all the tools it needs to be able to rebuild after Hurricane María, a devastating disaster that the Trump administration mismanaged from the very beginning. Puerto Rico’s recovery should not be hindered by deadlines and red tape that get in the way of finishing the island’s recovery,” added Ranking Member Thompson. “Puerto Rico should have the time it needs to fully rebuild, and I thank Resident Commissioner Hernández for introducing this legislation.”

“As one of the few Puerto Rican members of Congress, I take our responsibility to the island and its people very seriously. This legislation will give our fellow Americans the time and flexibility they need to make themselves whole,” said Congresswoman Pou. “Right now, in 2026, families are relying on carrying water from wells to drink and wash their clothes. The power grid remains in dire shape. Our federal government must give Puerto Ricans all of the tools and time they need to become whole again. This bill is a key start.”

“In Mayagüez, we have experienced firsthand how complex it has been to move reconstruction projects forward. There are permitting processes, reviews, contracting requirements, and other steps that require coordination with different agencies and are not always within the municipalities’ control. Giving Puerto Rico until 2035 would allow us to complete projects that already have funding allocated, without sacrificing oversight or federal requirements. That is why I support this measure and the Resident Commissioner’s efforts to ensure that we can finish the reconstruction our people still need,” said Jorge Luis Ramos Ruiz, Mayor of Mayagüez.

BACKGROUND

Ahead of the ninth anniversary of Hurricane María, Puerto Rico’s reconstruction remains unfinished. As of September 30, 2025, COR3 reported 19,202 active María recovery projects that had been obligated but had not yet reached closeout, underscoring the scale of work still underway nearly a decade after the storm. COR3 has pointed to complex federal requirements, permitting and environmental reviews, workforce and supply-chain limitations, and coordination challenges as continuing bottlenecks slowing projects from obligation to completion.

Those challenges were front and center this summer when Hernández, Thompson and Pou traveled to Puerto Rico as part of a House Homeland Security Committee delegation, where they met with FEMA officials, mayors and local leaders and visited projects such as Francisco Morales High School in Naranjito, where permanent reconstruction did not begin until years after María.

Puerto Rico still has FEMA-funded reconstruction projects that remain unfinished, but those projects do not share a single common deadline. Each project has its own completion timeline, and when it cannot be finished on time, the government must request an extension from FEMA on a project-by-project basis.

The Puerto Rico Disaster Recovery Completion Act of 2026 responds directly to those concerns by extending the period of performance and project completion deadline for covered FEMA disaster recovery projects in Puerto Rico through December 31, 2035, giving eligible projects more time to be completed while requiring FEMA to account for what remains unfinished, what is causing delays and when those projects are expected to be finished.

The legislation would:

Extend the completion deadline to December 31, 2035 for eligible FEMA permanent-work projects that have not yet been closed out;

Allow additional extensions after 2035 through FEMA’s existing extension process when more time is necessary;

Cover eligible projects stemming from Hurricanes Irma and María, the 2019-2020 earthquakes and Hurricane Fiona; and

Require FEMA, in consultation with COR3, to report annually to Congress and the Resident Commissioner on the number of projects completed, expected completion dates for projects still underway and obstacles delaying their completion.

The reporting requirement would remain in place through December 31, 2035, providing Congress with an annual accounting of the progress of covered recovery projects in Puerto Rico.

###
title: A días del noveno aniversario de María, Hernández, Thompson y Pou presentan proyecto para dar más tiempo a Puerto Rico para terminar la reconstrucción

Today, FEMA announced more than $5.6 million in grant funding will be awarded to states in FEMA Region 7. This funding will empower community leaders to take decisive steps to protect infrastructure and people from future disasters. This funding aligns with President Donald J. Trump’s America First Resilience Strategy, which calls for a new, risk-informed approach that treats resilience as an investment opportunity. It also delivers on the Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mullin’s commitment to empowering state and local officials to manage their own disaster preparedness—with FEMA supporting only if needed.
The funding announced today includes:
- More than $4.3 million through FEMA’s Pre-Disaster Mitigation Grant Program to fund disaster mitigation projects in Iowa and Kansas. Congress directed these funds be distributed in the Fiscal Year 2026 Homeland Security and Further Additional Continuing Appropriations Act. Most projects focus on improving infrastructure to reduce flood risk, while others address hazards such as earthquakes and wildfires. To view the list of Congressional Directed Spending projects, visit this link on FEMA.gov.
- Nearly $1.3 million through FEMA’s Community Assistance Program – State Support Services Element to fund floodplain management practices. This competitive grant program is designed to empower states and territories to support local jurisdictions with flood reduction efforts. When done correctly, this can save lives and reduce the cost of future disasters. A list of these floodplain management awards by state and territory is available on FEMA.gov.
- More than $66 thousand through FEMA’s National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program grants to reduce the risk of earthquakes. The State of Missouri will receive federal funds to train officials, conduct exercises, and carry out other activities to prepare for potential earthquakes.
For more information about these grant obligations and awards, visit the following FEMA webpages: Community Assistance Program – State Support Services Element, National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program, and Pre-Disaster Mitigation Grant Program.

David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of IRS Criminal Investigation in New England, announced that WILLIAM LAVIMONIERE, 66, of Plainfield, waived his right to be indicted and pleaded guilty today in Hartford federal court to tax evasion.

According to court documents and statements made in court, on October 10, 2012, Lavimoniere was sentenced in Hartford federal court to 33 months of imprisonment for fraud and tax offenses stemming from his embezzlement of more than $348,000 from a non-profit corporation that served Connecticut adults and students who have disabilities. In November 2012, Lavimoniere divorced his wife to transfer assets, including their residence, to her to avoid collection by the IRS. Lavimoniere was released from federal prison in April 2015.

For the 2008 through 2011 tax years, Lavimoniere had an outstanding tax assessment balance of $213,267, not including penalties and interest. Lavimoniere only paid approximately $7,007 toward the assessment. In December 2023, the IRS ceased civil collection of the outstanding assessment because the collection statute expired.

After Lavimoniere was released from prison, he operated a trucking and furniture installation business named WJL Handling LLC (“WJL”). For the 2016, 2017, 2018, 2023, and 2024 tax years, Lavimoniere earned substantial income from WJL but willfully failed to file federal tax returns. For the 2019 through 2022 tax years, Lavimoniere filed tax returns that underreported income from WJL. Lavimoniere made significant structured cash withdrawals to avoid financial reporting thresholds, paid his employees “under the table,” and used his business bank account to pay personal expenses. He also continued to live in his former residence with his ex-wife and deposited cash into her bank account, which she then used to pay the mortgage and other household expenses.

The government has calculated that Lavimoniere owes $246,417 in restitution to the IRS, and Lavimoniere has agreed to cooperate with the IRS to pay all outstanding taxes, interest, and penalties.

Tax evasion carries a maximum term of imprisonment of five years.

Lavimoniere is released on a $75,000 bond pending sentencing, which is scheduled for December 9.

This matter is being investigated by the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Heather L. Cherry.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Plainfield Man with Prior Federal Conviction Pleads Guilty to Tax Evasion

Washington, D.C. – This week, Representatives Maggie Goodlander (NH-2) and Veronica Escobar (TX-16) led a group of ten Democratic Members of Congress in a letter to Secretary of Veterans Affairs (VA) Doug Collins expressing their concern for the apparent lack of support for the VA Advisory Committee on Women Veterans (ACWV).

The full letter can be found here and below:

Secretary Collins:

We write to express our concern regarding the apparent lack of support for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Advisory Committee on Women Veterans (ACWV). According to the ACWV Charter, which you signed October 6, 2025, this Federal Advisory Committee (FAC) must meet twice annually and submit a report to the Secretary of Veterans Affairs annually on July 1st. However, according to the files assembled and maintained by VA’s Advisory Committee Management Office in accordance with the law, the committee has not met since December 2024. No report has been published for either 2025 or 2026.

Additionally, we understand that the most recent Chair of the ACWV, Colonel (Ret.) Wanda A. Wright, resigned from that position in April 2026 in protest of VA having “effectively rendered the Committee inactive” and affirming the digital record of inactivity referenced above by noting the ACWV has not met since December 2024.

Under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA), it is a requirement that advisory committees meet regularly, conduct business transparently, and actively fulfill their statutory purpose. Specifically, the ACWV is mandated by statute, 38 U.S.C. § 542, which requires that the Secretary of Veterans Affairs establish an advisory committee consisting of members from the general public who represent women veterans, veterans with service-connected disabilities, and those recently separated from the military and/or are recognized authorities in fields including gender-specific health-care needs of women. The law also requires you to consult with and seek advice from the ACWV with respect to VA health care, benefits, outreach, and other programs administered by VA. The committee, by statute, is to submit a report to you which you are required to submit to Congress within 60 days of receipt. We did not receive a report in 2025 and have seen no evidence that we should expect one in 2026.

The lapse in the ACWV’s required activities raises concerns about whether the Department is fulfilling its statutory obligation to consult with and seek the committee’s advice on matters affecting women veterans. The limited information available regarding the committee’s status further raises questions about whether VA is meeting its obligations under law and providing Congress and the public with adequate transparency regarding the operation of a Congressionally mandated advisory body.

To better understand the Department’s practices related to this FAC, we request responses to the following questions no later than October 2, 2026:

How many times did the VA Advisory Committee on Women Veterans meet in 2025?

As of the date of your response, how many times has the ACWV met in 2026?

What is informing your decisions about how to optimally provide care, benefits, and

services to women veterans in the absence of regular meetings of the ACWV?

Each FAC has an associated budget and employees. Given that ACWV has not met as

required in 2025 and 2026, have the budget and employees been redirected and if so how are they being used? Please provide funding levels used to support FAC activities in

FY2025 and FY2026 and descriptions of how the funding was used.

What is your plan to ensure that meetings of the ACWV occur according to its statue and charter?

We appreciate your prompt attention to these questions and expect a timely and complete response. Congress created these advisory committees to ensure that the voices, expertise, and experiences of veterans inform the Department charged with serving them. Veterans and their families, caregivers, and survivors deserve nothing less than a clear accounting of why the Advisory Committee on Women Veterans has been allowed to fall silent and what the Department will do to restore these critical perspectives to the table.

In addition to Representatives Goodlander and Escobar, the signers of this letter include Representatives Terri Sewell (AL-7), Ed Case (HI-1), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-6), George Latimer (NY-16), Nikki Budzinski (IL-13), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Madeleine Dean (PA-4), and Deborah Ross (NC-2).

###
title: Goodlander, Escobar Express Concern for Apparent Lack of Support for VA Advisory Committee on Women Veterans

Earlier today, an indictment was unsealed in federal court in Brooklyn, charging Michael Brown, also known as “Mack Bills,” with sex trafficking by force, fraud, and coercion; interstate prostitution; and promotion of prostitution. The charges relate to Brown’s trafficking of women to work as prostitutes in New York, including along an open‑air sex trafficking market on a stretch of Pennsylvania Avenue in Brooklyn known as the “Penn Track,” and his transportation of women from New York to at least one other state with the intent that they engage in commercial sex for his financial benefit. Brown was arrested today and is scheduled to be arraigned this afternoon before United States Magistrate Judge Lara K. Eshkenazi.

Joseph Nocella, Jr., United States Attorney for the Eastern District of New York, and James C. Barnacle, Jr., Assistant Director in Charge, Federal Bureau of Investigation, New York Field Office (FBI) announced the arrest and charges.

“As alleged, the defendant trafficked women to serve as commercial sex workers for him on the notorious Penn Track in Brooklyn and in at least one other state,” stated United States Attorney Nocella. “Today’s arrest demonstrates our commitment to protecting victims of exploitation. Our Office will continue to prioritize the investigation and prosecution of sex trafficking crimes that threaten the safety and dignity of our communities, and to eradicate this blight in our district.”

Mr. Nocella expressed his appreciation to the FBI and the New York City Police Department Child Exploitation and Human Trafficking Task Force for their work on the case.

“Michael Brown allegedly trafficked multiple women to engage in prostitution, benefitted financially from their involuntary arrangement, and even threatened violence when challenged. The FBI and its law enforcement partners will continue to work tirelessly to get these criminals off of the streets to face justice for their heinous acts,” stated FBI Assistant Director in Charge Barnacle.

According to court filings, between March 2026 and August 2026, Brown had numerous women working in prostitution for him on the Penn Track and other locations, and trafficked at least two of those women using force, fraud, and coercion. Specifically, evidence obtained pursuant to the investigation reflects that Brown regularly required his female victims to solicit customers on the Penn Track and other locations, including in at least one other state, and to engage in commercial sex acts with those customers. Brown collected the proceeds earned by these women after they engaged in commercial sex acts with customers, and he used threats, emotional manipulation, and violence to discipline and control them.

For example, in several communications, women working for Brown call him “daddy,” discuss giving money from “dates,” i.e. , paid sexual encounters, to the defendant, and discuss posting advertisements for prostitution and tips on how to increase making money in prostitution. Brown also has messages discussing methods to discipline the women working in prostitution for him. In a message sent in or about September 2025, he talks about insubordination from a woman working for him and stated in substance and in part that he “need[s] something more creative than the gut punch for this one…” and decides he “[m]ight put that Hoe on her knees on rice.”

If convicted of sex trafficking, Brown faces a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years’ imprisonment and a maximum of life imprisonment. The interstate prostitution and promotion of prostitution charges each carry a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison

The charges in the indictment are allegations and the defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

The government’s case is being handled by the Office’s Human Trafficking and Civil Rights Section. Assistant United States Attorney Erin Reid is in charge of the prosecution.

The Defendant :

MICHAEL BROWN (also known as “Mack Bills”) Age: 35 Brooklyn, New York

E.D.N.Y. Docket No. 26-CR-267 (NRM)
title: Brooklyn Man Charged with Sex Trafficking, Interstate Prostitution, and Promotion of Prostitution at “Penn Track” in East New York, Brooklyn and Elsewhere

Baltimore, Maryland – The U.S. Attorney’s Office announced, today, that after a four-day trial, a federal jury convicted a Maryland man of several child sex-abuse crimes.

The jury found James Edward Howeth, 43, of East New Market, guilty of two counts of sexually exploiting a minor, one count of distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM), and three counts of possessing CSAM. Howeth faces a mandatory minimum 15 years, and a maximum of 140 years, in federal prison.

Kelly O. Hayes, U.S. Attorney for the District of Maryland, announced the guilty verdict with Special Agent in Charge Jimmy Paul, FBI Baltimore Field Office, and Colonel Michael A. Jackson, Superintendent, Maryland State Police (MSP).

During the trial, evidence showed that Howeth enticed and coerced a minor female to engage in sexually explicit conduct for the purpose of producing CSAM. The government also proved that Howeth used a cell phone to distribute CSAM.

According to court documents, between April 2021 and April 2022, Howeth produced sexually explicit depictions of the minor victim who was 4 and 5 years old at the time. Law enforcement discovered that Howeth possessed more than CSAM files and that in September 2023, Howeth sent a text message to another person with a CSAM file attached.

Then as part of the investigation, on March 14, 2024, law-enforcement officers executed a search warrant on Howeth’s East New Market home. During the search, law enforcement seized several of Howeth’s electronic devices including two cellphones, a laptop, and a desktop. A search of the cellphones revealed a text conversation in which Howeth discussed his sexual attraction to the minor victim and other children in addition to CSAM images of the minor victim that Howeth produced on two separate occasions.

Law enforcement also located more than 200 CSAM files on the cellphones and more than 100 CSAM files on the laptop.

Howeth is facing a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years and a maximum sentence of 30 years in federal prison for each count of sexually exploiting a minor. He also faces a minimum of five years and a maximum of 20 years for distributing CSAM, along with a maximum of 20 years for each count of possessing CSAM.

This case is part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit justice.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, visit justice.gov/psc and click on the “Resources” tab on the left of the page.

Actual sentences for federal crimes are typically less than the maximum penalties. A federal district court judge determines sentencing after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.

U.S. Attorney Hayes commended the FBI and MSP for their work in the investigation. Ms. Hayes also thanked Assistant U.S. Attorneys Colleen Elizabeth McGuinn and Reema Sood who are prosecuting the federal case.

For more information about the Maryland U.S. Attorney’s Office, its priorities, and resources available to help the community, please visit justice.gov/usao-md .

# # #
title: Maryland Man Convicted of Child Sex-Exploitation Crimes

Today, Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) released a letter to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting ICE Director David Venturella demanding answers on the investigation into the death of Edwin Jovanny Lopez Cornejo and the status of detainee Amro Sehaim.

The letter comes after the Department failed to respond to an inquiry sent by the Congresswoman and several members of the New Jersey Delegation on August 7th calling for answers surrounding the death of Lopez Cornejo and demanding the immediate humanitarian release of Amro Sehaim, an Egyptian national and small business owner in the 12th District who, before his detention, was undergoing treatment for cancer.

The letter reads in part:

Individuals in your custody are your responsibility. The shocking number of deaths within ICE custody, including Mr. Lopez Cornejo’s, is appalling and unforgivable. The conditions in ICE detention facilities across the country are atrocious and bring shame to your Department, this Administration, and our nation.

The September 17th letter demands detailed explanations as to the conditions that led to the death of Mr. Lopez Cornejo and of the actions being taken to provide Mr. Sehaim with adequate, independent medical care.

For decades, Presidents have promised to cut prescription drug prices, but only President Donald J. Trump has delivered. Prescription drug prices have now recorded their sharpest annual drop in more than 60 years — and those lower prices now reach every Medicaid program in America.
President Trump is the first President to actually lower prescription drug prices.
Official data confirms the largest annual decline in more than 60 years — the steepest drop since 1963 — with prices falling every month of 2026.
President Trump ended the era of Americans paying the highest drug prices on Earth.
Through Most Favored Nation pricing, 26 of the world’s largest drugmakers — covering 90% of the branded U.S. market — have agreed to bring U.S. prices in line with the lowest paid by comparable developed nations. These agreements are projected to save Americans more than $600 billion.
Every state Medicaid program in the nation now gets Most Favored Nation drug prices.
All 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico are in, unlocking nearly $65 billion in Medicaid drug savings over the next decade — real relief for low-income families, children, seniors, and the disabled, and another big win for taxpayers.
TrumpRx is already putting hundreds of millions back in patients’ pockets.
The platform has delivered more than $700 million in savings and now covers more than 1,000 branded and generic medicines. GLP-1 drugs that once cost over $1,000 a month start as low as $149; eligible Medicare seniors pay just $50 a month, with more than 500,000 seniors already saving $216 million. Fertility drugs, inhalers, insulin, cholesterol treatments, and dozens of other high-cost drugs have been slashed 50–90% or more.
President Trump is bringing drug manufacturing home and securing our supply chain.
The same 26 companies have committed about $170 billion to U.S. manufacturing and R&D and are stocking the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve — cutting America’s dependence on foreign supply chains for essential medicines.
title: President Trump Extends Most Favored Nation Drug Pricing to Every Medicaid Program in America

BROWNSVILLE, Texas – A 40-year-old Baytown man has been sentenced for possession with intent to deliver cocaine.

Pablo Luis Fuentes-Rivas pleaded guilty July 2, 2025.

At a Sept. 17 hearing, U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. ordered Fuentes-Rivas to serve 70 months in federal prison. His prison term will be immediately followed by three years of supervised release.

The investigation revealed that on March 29, 2025, authorities conducted an undercover operation involving the delivery of a tractor-trailer loaded with cocaine to the Houston and Baytown areas.

Three vehicles traveled in tandem with the drug load and conducted counter-surveillance during the trip. Efren Pinales-Hernandez drove one of the vehicles.

Law enforcement later observed Fuentes-Rivas, Pinales-Hernandez, and Daniel Teniente-Marfileno at a Baytown truck lot offloading bundles of cocaine from the tractor-trailer into a Ford F-150 driven by Teniente-Marfileno.

After Teniente-Marfileno left with the cocaine, law enforcement conducted a traffic stop, took him into custody, and seized approximately 182.25 kilograms of cocaine with an estimated street value of nearly $2.3 million. Authorities then arrested Fuentes-Rivas and Pinales-Hernandez at the truck lot as they attempted to leave.

Teniente-Marfileno, 39, a Mexican citizen residing in Baytown, also pleaded guilty and is set for sentencing Sept. 29.

Pinales-Hernandez, 51, Weslaco, is set for further criminal proceedings.

Fuentes-Rivas has been and will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Oscar Ponce prosecuted the case.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of U.S. law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF South Texas comprises agents and officers from Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations; FBI; Drug Enforcement Administration; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; Department of Transportation; IRS Criminal Investigation; Interpol/Department of State; and the Naval Criminal Investigative Service with the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Texas leading the prosecution.
title: Baytown man sent to prison following Homeland Security Task Force cocaine investigation

President Donald J. Trump is delivering on his promises to America’s outdoorsmen by cutting red tape, removing burdensome and unnecessary restrictions levied by previous Administrations and expanding America’s great outdoor recreation sector that generates over $1.2 trillion annually and supports over 5 million jobs.
Last night, the President signed two Executive Orders to bolster American hunting and revive American saltwater angling. Industry leaders and stakeholders nationwide hailed the President’s  leadership and commitment to restoring Americans’ access to Federal lands, revitalizing our Nation’s outdoor recreation economy, while conserving and protecting America’s abundant natural resources. 
Here’s what they are saying: 
Secretary Doug Burgum: “Sportsmen are among our greatest conservationists, and this administration is committed to supporting the men and women who help protect our public lands and wildlife.  At @POTUS’ direction, @Interior will: 
- Expand hunting access
- Promote habitat management
- Improve migratory bird hunting authorizations
- Encourage Sunday hunting
- Support hunter education and youth and veteran programs
Putting American hunters, fishermen and outdoorsmen FIRST.”
Senator Tom Cotton: “Hunting is an important part of Arkansas’s culture and economy. Thankful President Trump is prioritizing America’s hunting heritage for future generations.”
Rep. Bruce Westerman: “Today’s executive orders signed by President Trump are generational victories for America’s sportsmen and women. The actions taken by President Trump expand access to public lands and waters, eliminate burdensome regulation, reinvigorate our outdoor economy and invest in the next generation of hunters and anglers. I’m proud to have advanced legislation on many of these policies through the Natural Resources Committee, including the reauthorization of the Great American Outdoors Act. I look forward to working with the Trump administration to codify these executive orders and support our nation’s hunters and anglers.”
Rep. August Pfluger: “For years, Washington made it harder to access the public lands and waters that belong to the American people. Today’s executive order by @POTUS expands wildlife access to hunters and anglers, rolls back overreaching Biden-era restrictions like the lead ammunition mandates, and opens up more opportunities for the next generation of sportsmen. I’m proud to support this action and applaud President Trump for rolling back the overreach of the previous administration.”
Rep. Addison McDowell: “Proud to join hundreds of anglers and hunters tonight as President Trump just signed an executive order reversing Biden-era restrictions on America’s outdoorsmen. By cutting burdensome red tape on fishermen and bringing outdoor recreation into the 21st century, President Trump is putting the American Outdoorsman First!”
The National Rifle Association: “The NRA is proud to stand beside @POTUS to protect the Second Amendment nationwide. We applaud President Trump’s newest executive orders protecting the storied tradition of American outdoorsmanship. 🤝”
Center for Sportfish Policy President and CEO Jeff Angers: “This Executive Order is a historic recognition of what millions of American anglers and coastal communities have known for decades: marine recreational fishing deserves a management system built for the way Americans fish. By prioritizing better data, stronger state partnerships and modern management approaches, President Trump’s order builds on our conservation gains creating a path to more reliable access and opportunity in America’s oceans.”
National Shooting Sports Foundation President and CEO Joe Bartozzi: “Today’s Executive Order by President Trump demonstrates that this administration stands with America’s sportsmen and women. This is a tremendous victory to ensure that America’s hunting heritage is protected for today’s hunters and the coming generations of outdoorsmen and women. NSSF has long championed several of these key policy issues, including protecting the right to use traditional ammunition, accessing public lands and increasing opportunities for Sunday hunting. We are proud to have led this fight and prouder still that the Trump administration is embracing commonsense policies to promote, protect and preserve hunting and the shooting sports across America.”
Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation President and CEO Jeff Crane: “The Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation commends President Trump for bringing together leaders from across the sportsmen’s community and recognizing the tremendous contributions hunters, anglers, trappers, and recreational shooters make to our nation. America’s outdoor heritage is one of our nation’s greatest traditions, and today’s event demonstrates the President’s continued commitment to ensuring these traditions remain strong for generations to come.”
Ducks Unlimited CEO Adam Putnam: “Hunters have been our nation’s most ardent conservationists for generations, and it’s terrific to see President Trump publicly recognize that in the White House Rose Garden. This Executive Order is an acknowledgment of hunters’ longstanding contributions to conservation, hunting access, sound waterfowl science, and hunter education. Our proud hunting heritage has been woven into the fabric of our great nation’s identity for 250 years, and this sort of commitment will help ensure it remains that way for future generations.”
Delta Waterfowl CEO Jason Tharpe: “We sincerely appreciate the President’s Executive Order as it highlights a number of Delta’s priorities for both ducks and duck hunters. Having the President affirm the need for access, addressing infrastructure on public lands, enhancing habitat through agreements with willing landowners and ensuring waterfowl hunting regulations are based on the best available data are all core needs and we appreciate the President’s leadership. Delta Waterfowl is deeply appreciative of President Trump’s historic announcement in furtherance of America’s hunting and conservation heritage. Simply put, this executive order will serve to benefit ducks and duck hunters for years to come and we look forward to working closely with the administration toward its implementation.”
National Marine Manufacturers Association President and CEO Frank Hugelmeyer: “Recreational boating and fishing are the foundation of America’s outdoor heritage and an important driver of our nation’s recreation economy. [Yesterday’s] actions further reaffirm the importance of ensuring Americans can access and enjoy our nation’s waters. Access supports American manufacturing, jobs, and small businesses across the country. Thank you to President Trump and his administration for recognizing the value of outdoor recreation and the American industries and communities it supports.”
Coastal Conservation Association President and CEO Pat Murray: “We’re grateful the Administration has taken this opportunity to emphasize the social and economic importance of recreational fishing. State-based management has never been more important for our federal fisheries and we applaud this critical need being highlighted in this Executive Order.”
American Sportfishing Association President and CEO Glenn Hughes: “The American Sportfishing Association thanks President Trump for this decisive action to improve management and data collection for America’s saltwater fisheries. This Executive Order will have long-term benefits for the sportfishing industry and America’s 15.5 million saltwater recreational anglers.”
Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation President and CEO Kyle Weaver: “On behalf of the Rocky Mountain Elk Foundation (RMEF), we thank President Trump and his administration for recognizing the vital role hunters play in sustaining wildlife and for issuing the Reinvigorating America’s Hunting Heritage Executive Order that strongly aligns with RMEF’s mission to ensure the future of elk, other wildlife, their habitat and our hunting heritage. We are honored by the president’s invitation to attend the White House ceremony where the policy was announced.
The order’s focus on expanding public access, actively managing habitat, facilitating wildlife movement and habitat connectivity, strengthening cooperation with state wildlife agencies, supporting science-based management of game populations, addressing predators and other population-limiting factors, and combatting invasive species closely reflects RMEF’s work for more than four decades. These priorities are central to our mission, and we look forward to working with the administration, federal agencies and state partners as the order is implemented.”
Sportsman Boats CEO Tommy Hancock: “Healthy fisheries and access to them go hand in hand. For American boat builders, this is about more than the boats we build. It’s about the families who spend time together on the water, the men and women whose livelihoods depend on the marine industry and our shared responsibility to conserve these resources. We appreciate President Trump and his Administration recognizing the importance of recreational fishing and taking action to strengthen conservation, improve fisheries management and preserve meaningful access.”
Rivers of Recovery Chairman Mitch Butler: “Rivers of Recovery commends the Trump Administration for recognizing the importance of America’s hunting and fishing traditions and expanding access to these opportunities for our nation’s veterans. Our years of research have proven that intentionally designed outdoor experiences can produce measurable improvements in the well being of combat veterans, including reductions in symptoms of post traumatic stress, depression and anxiety. By strengthening access to hunting, fishing and the outdoors, this action supports both the healing of our nation’s veterans and the conservation heritage that makes these experiences possible.”
Pheasants Forever and Quail Forever Vice President of Government Affairs Ariel Wiegard: “America’s hunting heritage is worth protecting—and that starts with putting more wildlife on the landscape and more opportunity within reach of hunters. From expanding access to public lands to investing in the habitat, wildlife management, and community spirit needed to sustain the legacy of iconic game species like bobwhite quail, this Executive Order recognizes that conservation and hunting go hand in hand. Pheasants Forever and Quail Forever are proud to work alongside the Trump Administration, states, landowners, and hunters to ensure America’s hunting traditions remain strong for generations to come.”
Mule Deer Foundation President and CEO Greg Sheehan: “Growing mule deer and other game populations requires healthy habitat and strong partnerships. We appreciate President Trump and his Administration’s focus on working with states, landowners, and conservation partners to address the factors limiting these herds. The Mule Deer Foundation stands ready to help deliver measurable conservation results.”
American Association of Meat Processors Executive Director Chris Young: “The American Association of Meat Processors is proud to support the President’s Hunter’s Bill of Rights. We are particularly excited about the effort to expand wild game donation programs across the United States and our members, the small meat processors of the country who butcher the vast majority of the wild game meat, stand ready to help keep this promise to the American people.”
National Deer Association President and CEO Nick Pinizzotto: “The National Deer Association is proud to celebrate the announcement of a Hunter’s Bill of Rights, especially the President’s keen attention to the issue of venison donation. There are so many places in this country that are experiencing hyperabundant deer populations. Venison donation programs are good for hunters, good for agricultural producers, and good for our small business partners in the meat processing community. We are excited to continue our work on this issue as hunting seasons start to open across the country”
Wild Sheep Foundation CEO Gray Thornton: “The Wild Sheep Foundation applauds the administration’s continued emphasis on hunting access, voluntary work with landowners, and care for public lands as vital parts of wildlife conservation. The Castle Mountains National Monument was wrongly closed to hunters and now we can look forward to correcting that error.”
Boone and Crockett Club CEO Tony Schoonen: “As fall hunting seasons begin across the country, the Boone and Crockett Club appreciates the administration’s timely attention to the important issues facing wildlife today. We look forward to working with the now mobilized agencies to address today’s challenges with quail, bighorn sheep, mule deer, and other species not yet fully recovered.”
American Conservation Coalition President Chris Barnard: “Hunting and fishing are ingrained in the DNA of our nation and serve as crucial tools for the conservation of our natural heritage. The American Conservation Coalition and our 150,000 grassroots members are glad to see the administration’s efforts to expand access and continue this American tradition in balance with our conservation needs.”
Contender Boats CEO Joe Neber: “The future of recreational fishing depends on healthy oceans and healthy fisheries. Anglers have long understood that good conservation and good access are connected. By putting better science, modern technology and more effective management at the center of federal fisheries policy, this Executive Order provides a stronger foundation for both.”
title: WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: President Trump Delivers Historic Victories for America’s Hunters, Anglers, and Outdoorsmen

Trump EPA and U.S. Rep. Clay Fuller Highlight Significant Brownfield Investments in North Georgia
CHICKAMAUGA, Georgia (September 18, 2026) – On September 18, 2026, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 4 Administrator Kevin McOmber and U.S. Representative Clay Fuller (GA-14) joined state and local officials at the Chickamauga Civic Center to highlight $6 million in Brownfields funding.
This investment includes $4 million to City of Chickamauga to clean up the former Crystal Springs Print Works site, $1.5 million to Northwest Georgia Regional Commission to assess properties for potential redevelopment, and $500,000 to Rome-Floyd County Development Authority to expand the inventory of brownfield sites and assess prospective properties.
“Brownfields work is about more than cleanup. It is about restoring confidence in a property, supporting local economic development, creating jobs, and improving quality of life,” said EPA Regional Administrator Kevin McOmber. “These grants will help Northwest Georgia turn challenged properties into community assets.”
“Since taking office, I've worked closely with municipalities across Georgia's 14th District to support efforts to revitalize our communities and promote economic growth,” said U.S. Representative (GA-14) Clay Fuller. “I am thrilled to join EPA and our local leaders in announcing $6 million in federal brownfields funding that will help clean up contaminated properties, prepare for redevelopment, and return them to productive use for the communities they serve. I will fight to bring federal cleanup, infrastructure funding home each and every day.”
“The most successful brownfield redevelopments can best be accomplished through partnerships and pooling resources together at the federal, state, and local levels,” said Jeff Cown, Georgia Environmental Protection Division Director. “The redevelopment of a single brownfield can be a catalyst, and the engine needed to spur economic growth.”
“We appreciate EPA’s continued partnership and investment in Rome and Floyd County,” said Evie McNiece, Rome County Development Authority board member. “This support is helping us not only address challenges of the past but also create new opportunities for the future.”
Background: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has announced $13.5 million in Brownfields Multipurpose, Assessment and Cleanup (MAC) grants to accelerate the cleanup of polluted sites across Georgia. With these funds, EPA is investing directly in American communities to clean up and redevelop blighted properties, delivering on the Trump Administration’s commitment to ensure that clean air, land, and water go hand-in-hand with economic growth and opportunity.
EPA’s Brownfields Program began in 1995 and has provided over $3 billion in grant funding to assess and clean up contaminated properties and return blighted properties to productive reuse.
To date, Brownfields investments leveraged more than $45 billion in cleanup and redevelopment. Over the years, the relatively small investment of federal funding was able to leverage, from both public and private sources, more than 228,900 jobs. Through fiscal year 2025, on average, $19.47 was leveraged for each EPA Brownfields Grant dollar awarded through multipurpose, assessment, revolving loan fund and cleanup cooperative agreements.
###
title: Trump EPA and U.S. Rep. Clay Fuller Highlight Significant Brownfield Investments in North Georgia

ATLANTA – Three aliens from Mexico, Venezuela, and Antigua and Barbuda face federal charges for allegedly voting illegally in recent federal elections.

“Voting in federal elections is a sacred right reserved to U.S. citizens, and every vote illegally cast by an alien cancels out a legal vote,” said U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg. “Maintaining the integrity of our elections and protecting the voting rights of citizens are among the highest priorities of my office. We will work with federal law enforcement and our state partners to vigorously safeguard those rights through the prosecutions brought to date and more that may soon follow.”

“Protecting the integrity of U.S. elections requires enforcing the laws that govern who may lawfully participate,” said Ryan McSeveney, Special Agent in Charge of the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service Miami Field Office, which oversees the Southeastern United States. “DSS is committed to working closely with our law enforcement partners to investigate allegations of unlawful voting and related document and identity fraud.”

“When a foreign national votes in U.S. elections, it violates federal law and undermines public trust in our election system,” said Ellen Johnson, Acting Special Agent in Charge of HSI in Georgia and Alabama. “HSI will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to investigate illegal voting and protect the integrity of America’s immigration and election systems.”

According to U.S. Attorney Hertzberg, the charges, and other information presented in court: Since September 1, 2026, three foreign nationals have been charged with voting in federal elections in the Northern District of Georgia.

Pauline Lewis, 65, an alien residing in Dawsonville, Georgia, is alleged to have voted by absentee ballot in the November 5, 2024, January 5, 2021, and November 3, 2020 federal elections. Lewis is allegedly a citizen of Antigua and Barbuda who entered the United States on a student visa in 1979 and remained in the country but never applied to become a U.S. citizen. Today, she appeared in federal court following her arrest on a criminal complaint charging her with voting as a non-citizen in a federal election.

Gabriel Covarrubias, 44, an alien residing in Lawrenceville, Georgia, is alleged to have voted in person using a false name in the November 5, 2024 federal election. Covarrubias is allegedly a citizen of Mexico who falsely claimed in a U.S. passport application submitted in March 2023 that he had a different name and was born in Puerto Rico. On September 1, 2026, he waived indictment and was charged by criminal information with making a false statement in a U.S. passport application and voting as a non-citizen in a federal election.

Analiea Milliscent Eccles, 43, an alien residing in Morrow, Georgia, is alleged to have voted nine times between 2008 and 2024. Eccles is allegedly a citizen of Venezuela who entered the United States on a temporary visitor visa in 1991 and remained in the country, applying for and receiving Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) status in 2013. Although she allegedly sought to renew that status earlier this year, she has never applied to become a U.S. citizen. On September 14, 2026, she appeared in federal court following her arrest on a criminal complaint charging her with voting as a non-citizen in a federal election and making a false claim of U.S. citizenship to vote in an election.

Members of the public are reminded that the complaints and information only contain charges. The defendants are presumed innocent of the charges, and it will be the government’s burden to prove the defendants’ guilt beyond a reasonable doubt at trial.

The cases are being investigated by the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Homeland Security Investigations, with valuable assistance from the Office of the Georgia Secretary of State.

These prosecutions are part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. The Atlanta Wilhelm HSTF comprises agents and officers from ATF, CGIS, DEA, FBI, ICE-HSI, IRS-CI, DOL-OIG, DSS, USMS, USPIS, and USSS, as well as numerous state and local agencies, with the prosecution being led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia.

For further information please contact the U.S. Attorney’s Public Affairs Office at USAGAN.PressEmails@usdoj.gov or (404) 581-6185. The Internet address for the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Georgia is http://www.justice.gov/usao-ndga .
title: Three Aliens Charged with Voting in Federal Elections

HHS Awards More Than $42 Million to States and Territories to Advance ‘Treatment First’ Model in Support of President Trump’s Executive Order
WASHINGTON, D.C. — September 18, 2026 — The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), a division of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced that it has awarded $42.3 million in new supplemental funding to states and territories through two federal block grants to advance President Trump’s Executive Order on Ending Crime and Disorder on America’s Streets and accelerate adoption and implementation of the Best Practices Toolkit: Addressing Homelessness and Addiction through Treatment First. An additional $2 million was also awarded to the national office and all 10 regional centers of the Addiction Technology Transfer Center (ATTC) Network to support implementation.
“President Trump has directed us to break the cycle of homelessness and addiction by putting treatment, recovery, and self-sufficiency first,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “These investments will help states move people from crisis into treatment and from treatment into lasting recovery, stable housing, and work. We are funding results that help people reclaim their health and independence.”
With the Treatment First approach, the objective is lasting stability — not another temporary stop in the cycle between the street, shelter, emergency room, and criminal justice system. Helping people engage in effective treatment, supporting lasting recovery, and promoting self-sufficiency can improve individual lives while strengthening communities.
“Treatment First means building a system that does not leave people cycling between homelessness, emergency rooms, and the criminal justice system,” said SAMHSA Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary Christopher D. Carroll. “These investments will help states strengthen the infrastructure — partnerships, data, workforce, and recovery supports — needed to connect people with serious mental illness and addiction to effective treatment and support them on a path toward lasting recovery, stable housing, employment, and self-sufficiency.”
Of the $42.3 million, $17.3 million was awarded to Community Mental Health Services Block Grant (MHBG) recipients. The supplemental funding will help states and territories build the systems, partnerships, workforce capacity, policies, and technical infrastructure needed to put Treatment First principles into practice. The funding is focused on technical assistance, training, policy development, and cross-system coordination rather than the direct provision of treatment services.
Another $25 million was awarded to Substance Use Prevention, Treatment, and Recovery Services Block Grant (SUPTRS BG) recipients to expand capacity for safe, licensed, certified or chartered sober and recovery housing nationwide. The supplement provides funding for training and technical assistance to enhance efforts to increase the supply of recovery residences and strengthen quality and accountability standards that give individuals in recovery greater choice in selecting housing that supports long-term sobriety and self-sufficiency.
The SUPTRS BG funding supplement is designed to work in tandem with an additional $2 million in supplemental funding awarded to all 10 regional ATTCs and the ATTC National Coordinating Office, ensuring that best practices for workforce training, licensure, certification, charter support, and outcome measurement tools needed for successful implementation are shared nationwide. This supplement will equip states, recovery community organizations, and sober/recovery housing operators with evidence-based tools to expand safe, certified housing that supports self-sufficiency and long-term sobriety.
Consistent with the Treatment First model, states and territories may use the funding to strengthen coordination across behavioral health, healthcare, housing, courts, law enforcement, homelessness services, community organizations, and other partners — so individuals can move more effectively from crisis and stabilization into treatment, recovery, and long-term self-sufficiency.
Through these investments, SAMHSA is helping states build coordinated, accountable systems focused not simply on service delivery, but on measurable progress toward treatment engagement, recovery, improved mental health, stable housing, employment, self-sufficiency, and reduced repeated homelessness and crisis-system involvement.
If you or someone you know is struggling or in crisis, help is available. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. To locate a treatment facility or provider, visit FindTreatment.gov.
Like HHS on Facebook, follow HHS on X @HHSgov, @SecKennedy, and sign up for HHS Email Updates.
