Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07) today voted in favor of H.R. 9497, the Water Resources Development Act of 2026, legislation that would advance critical water infrastructure projects and studies across the country.

“Safe, reliable water infrastructure is essential to the health, safety, and prosperity of our communities,” said Vindman. “After seeing firsthand the devastating impact of Orange County’s water crisis, I was proud to secure the $50 million investment to help strengthen and modernize the county’s water system. We’re also taking action to restore the Rappahannock River by removing the Ficklen Island Dam and improving habitat for wildlife. These investments will help ensure our water infrastructure is prepared for the future and it’s why I voted for this legislation today.”

The bill would authorize the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers to begin 14 water infrastructure projects and 133 feasibility studies and modifications for future construction. It would also update Corps policies to strengthen coordination with state and local governments on water infrastructure needs.

Vindman secured authorization for two projects in Virginia’s Seventh Congressional District: $50 million for water infrastructure improvements in Orange County and the removal of Ficklen Island Dam in Fredericksburg.

In August 2024, Orange County experienced a major drinking water crisis after catastrophic pump failures at the Wilderness Water Treatment Plant led to hydrocarbons entering the county’s water supply. The failure prompted “Do Not Use” and “Do Not Drink” advisories, severely disrupting daily life for residents and businesses.

Under this bill, Orange County will be able to access $50 million in federal funding to strengthen and modernize its water infrastructure, helping ensure the county has a more reliable and resilient water system for years to come.

The removal of the Ficklen Island Dam, located on the Rappahannock River in Fredericksburg, would restore the shoreline and improve the well-being of wildlife living in and the around river.

Ambassador Mike Waltz
U.S. Representative to the United Nations
New York, New York
AS DELIVERED
Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you to the briefers.
I’ll start my remarks with something that should not surprise anyone: that the United States will not tolerate the Taliban taking American citizens hostage. Period. Nor will we be intimidated or coerced by a Taliban that cruelly uses American citizens as bargaining chips or some kind of leverage in its ill-fated pursuit of international legitimacy.
In March, in fact, Secretary of State Rubio designated Afghanistan under the Taliban as a State Sponsor of Wrongful Detention, as it kidnaps citizens of not just Americans, but of dozens of nationalities everyday for ransom and political concessions.
And this should surprise no one who has had to personally deal with the Taliban as I have.
I’ve seen them hang children, terrorize families, pillage whole villages, and prey on the very people they claim to represent.
In fact, after the fall of Kabul, I met with an Afghan interpreter who had finally escaped after he had been beaten night after night trying to get through Taliban checkpoints before getting on a flight out.
When this interpreter, who was a former teacher, finally arrived here, the Taliban called him on his phone. He actually called him from his 10-year-old nephew’s phone. And their message was disgusting. It was sadistic. Sadly predictable. They essentially told him, come back and submit himself to Taliban justice, or the 10-year-old boy would pay the price.
And colleagues, this is how the Taliban operates. We should be clear-eyed as a Council on who we’re dealing with. And when it wants leverage, it reaches for innocent people.
So today, we call on the members of the Council to condemn the Taliban for their unjust detention of U.S. citizens and other citizens. Demand their release. We should also condemn the Taliban’s sheltering, as many of you have said today, of terrorist groups, and the utter destruction of their once great country under their cruelty.
And don’t take my word for it. The Secretary-General reported this year that human rights violations remain widespread—extrajudicial killings, arbitrary arrests, torture, ill treatment. And as many of us have referenced, the ban on girls’ education beyond sixth grade has now entered its fifth year.
In fact, before this body two years ago, the actress Meryl Streep now infamously remarked that a female cat in Kabul has more rights than an Afghan woman. A female cat can sit on the front porch, can see the sunlight, can walk to a public park, where Afghan girls and women are now banned.
UNESCO estimates that 2.2 million Afghan girls are now shut out of education. Afghanistan is the only country in the world where girls and women are barred from secondary and higher education.
And it is so heartbreaking. After 20 years, an entire generation of Afghan women got a taste of freedom and a better life. That door is now closed on them.
UNAMA itself has documented in report after report thousands of cases of arbitrary arrest and detention, torture, ill-treatment, enforced disappearance, extrajudicial killings under Taliban rule.
And three months ago, UNAMA documented thirty women arrested in Herat. Why? Because of dress code violations.
When Afghans stood up bravely and protested those arrests, UNAMA also reported that Taliban security forces killed young women and boys who were standing up for their classmates.
And if you thought it couldn’t get worse: the Taliban does not even allow Afghan women to work for the United Nations to enter United Nations compounds.
That restriction has now been in place for a full year. The Secretary-General has stated, of course, we agree that it is a violation of international law, including the UN Charter, and it’s obstructing lifesaving assistance to Afghanistan, and it’s a “critical impediment” obviously to Afghanistan’s reintegration into the international community.
Colleagues, let’s just think about that contradiction. The Taliban wants a seat at the international table. They want a seat here. Yet, they’re barring women from walking through the front door of the United Nations in their own country. Again, yet they want a seat here.
So, this Council has spoken. Resolution 2822 said the erosion of the rights of women and girls and minorities is so severe that their absence makes peace, stability, and prosperity unattainable.
That same resolution extended UNAMA through June of 2027, streamlining and focusing its work. The United States welcomes that reform and expects UNAMA to demonstrate measurable value, particularly as it remains the most expensive political mission.
We also welcome the Secretary-General’s appointment in July of Rabab Fatima. I’ve had the pleasure of meeting with her, and wish her luck and health as she takes on this difficult task as a special representative. We look forward to her early engagement with this Council.
But colleagues, there is a larger question here: how many UN reports documenting abuse? How many Council resolutions demanding change? How many years of “engagement” can we pass before we see measurable results?
We will be watching closely for evidence that the revised mandate, new leadership, are translating into a leaner, more accountable mission, and focusing on the work that matters most.
The same applies for the UN-led Doha process. The comprehensive approach can provide a path forward, but only if the Taliban engages seriously and meets its commitments.
Colleagues, this Council must demand results from the Taliban. We need to see action, not words, and that will determine whether Afghanistan moves forward towards peace and legitimacy and the Afghan people.
Many soldiers from many of our countries for many years, and civilians as well, fought so valiantly so that they could have a better future. And I certainly agree with the notion of what happens in Afghanistan does not stay in Afghanistan.
Thank you, colleagues.

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Representative Sean Casten (IL-06) and Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) introduced the Environmental Health Restoration Act, legislation to restore and strengthen the Environmental Protection Agency’s core mission to protect public health, the environment, and the climate.

The lawmakers introduced the bill just days after the Trump Administration’s EPA finalized the repeal of major greenhouse gas standards for coal- and gas-fired power plants and moved to eliminate remaining federal climate pollution requirements for the power sector.

“At a time when the Trump Administration is ignoring the climate crisis and undermining Americans’ ability to breathe clean air, drink clean water, and enjoy the outdoors, it is more important than ever to restore a commitment to science-based environmental protection at the EPA,” said Rep. Casten. “The EPA was created to protect public health and our environment. I’m proud to introduce this legislation to refocus the agency on its core mission.”

“The Trump EPA has fully abandoned its decades-long duty to protect Americans’ health and safety. Its relentless attacks on science have delivered for big political donors while poisoning our air and water and speeding up the climate crisis,” said Sen. Whitehouse. “Our bill would jumpstart the long process of restoring the science, the scientists, and the original mission guiding the EPA.”

On Wednesday, September 16th, Rep. Casten and Sen. Whitehouse hosted a press conference with Protect Our Winters and Olympic athletes to highlight the bill's importance and the need to protect the great outdoors.

“As an Olympian training in the mountains all over the world, I’ve seen less and less snow, glaciers shrinking at a not-so-glacial pace, and volatile air quality,” said Tommy Ford, three-time Olympian and World Cup Champion. “This directly affects our community’s health and economy. A stronger, more durable EPA is essential for clean air, clean water and a strong, healthy community.”

“Rolling back environmental protections has real consequences for the places and experiences that define the outdoor community,” said Ben Gubits, Vice President of Campaigns at POW. “It means dirtier air, greater climate pollution, more threats to public health and accelerating damage to our winters, waterways and public lands. The Environmental Health Restoration Act draws a clear line, the EPA must follow science, enforce the law and put people ahead of polluters. This is a positive vision for the future looking well beyond the Trump years.”

The Environmental Health Restoration Act responds to recent deregulatory actions that have weakened or delayed protections governing air pollution, water quality, greenhouse gas emissions and environmental enforcement. It would reaffirm Congress’s intent that the EPA follow science, regulate harmful pollution, and protect communities from environmental harm.

The Environmental Health Restoration Act would:

Restore key protections for pollution from power plants, vehicles, and oil and gas operations that were in effect on January 19, 2025.

Require EPA decisions to be grounded in peer-reviewed science and restore independent scientific advisory bodies.

Rebuild the agency’s civil and criminal enforcement capacity and require annual accountability reporting to Congress.

Prioritize monitoring and enforcement in communities facing disproportionate pollution burdens.

Require public-health and cumulative-impact analyses for EPA actions affecting air and water quality.

Preserve states’ ability to adopt environmental standards stronger than federal requirements.

Allow people harmed by the EPA’s failure to comply with the law to seek relief in federal court.

The legislation is endorsed by Protect Our Winters and the League of Conservation Voters.

Text of the legislation can be found here.

title: Casten, Whitehouse Introduce Legislation to Restore EPA’s Core Mission

Instead, it hands President Trump the largest transfer of tariff authority Congress has ever given a president: the power to impose tariffs of up to 100% on any country, based solely on his claim they are facilitating sanctions evasion, with no Congressional oversight or legal guardrails.

Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

Families have had it with the harm of Republican leadership and the broken promises of a President who only looks out for himself. Since January of last year, House Republicans in this Committee and this Congress have surrendered their responsibility as an equal branch of government, twisting themselves into an arm of the White House and allowing President Trump to walk all over them, seize their power, and force them to advance dangerous policies that are hurting their constituents.

We just watched the price of record-high diesel climb even higher. Major retailers are being forced to ration oil sales because of how Trump is squeezing them. Inflation, fueled by Trump’s war and tariffs, continues to wipe out wage gains and send consumer sentiment to the pits. And yet, as we sit here for the last meeting of Committee business for at least seven weeks, Republicans still haven’t put anything in front of us to put a stop to the economic fallout. The cost of their inaction grows by the day.

Stunningly, Republicans have looked at this reality, yet again decided to forfeit the prerogative of the Committee, and move forward with legislation to supercharge the president’s tariff authority. Raising tariffs up to 100%! And more than $8,000 in higher costs to the average household according to analysis from the Yale Budget Lab. To my colleagues, can families in your district afford that?

text:
BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
A PROCLAMATION
During Constitution Week, we proudly commemorate the 239th anniversary of the signing of the United States Constitution, the very foundation of our Republic and an eternal reminder that all power throughout our land flows from We the People. Over two centuries later, we remain more committed than ever to protecting and cherishing the fundamental values of America and the vision of our forefathers for a just, prosperous, and free Nation.
On September 17, 1787, the Founding Fathers assembled at Independence Hall to summon the courage of the American Spirit and boldly proclaim, in a single governing document, their resolve to form a more perfect Union, establish justice, ensure domestic tranquility, provide for our national defense, ensure the welfare of all our citizens, and secure the blessings of liberty to ourselves and our posterity. The 39 patriots who signed it, many of whom had risked their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor for Independence just years before during the Revolution, immortalized the essential principles of the rule of law, the separation of powers, and federalism as the cornerstone of our Republic.
Guided by the most righteous political document ever conceived, America remains the greatest force for good in the history of the world. Americans enjoy freedom of speech, freedom of religion, equal justice under the law, and the Second Amendment — among other unalienable rights — hard won by the selfless men and women who have fought, bled, and died across the generations to preserve them for citizens of every race, religion, color, and creed. These rights come with solemn responsibilities, and since the dawn of our Republic, love of country, devotion to liberty, dedication to the rule of law, and a steadfast passion for preserving that inheritance have been the obligations of every dutiful American citizen.
These values now face a new threat: a rise in anti-American rhetoric from communists and far-left radicals, who seek to divide our communities, rob our children of their futures, and poison the minds of our citizens through slanderous fabrications of our great American story. Where our Constitution recognizes rights as gifts of Almighty God that no earthly power may take away, socialism and communism treat them as favors of the State to be rationed and revoked, demanding total submission to a movement that is only capable of bringing poverty, persecution, and ruin wherever it has been tried. These failed ideologies do not make life more affordable or prosperous — they destroy opportunity, create hardship, and leave working families with less. That same contempt for our Constitution took root at home under the previous administration, which turned its power against the very citizens it was sworn to serve and let our institutions rewrite the very story of America itself.
On my watch, the weaponization of Government has ended, and America is once again upholding its constitutional principles enshrined at the founding of our Republic. Upon returning to office, I fulfilled my vow to the American People by signing an Executive Order that harnessed the full power of the Federal Government to reverse the previous administration’s systematic campaign of fear, intimidation, and lawfare and to once again guarantee that citizens are no longer targeted for their beliefs. My Administration is rebuilding our economy around the fundamental rights of individual liberty and economic freedom. We are also restoring truth and sanity to American history, purging divisive and corrosive ideology from our institutions and national museums, saving the monuments and stories of our ancestors from a false and wicked narrative which sought to erase them, and teaching students to revere our country, honor our heroes, and respect our incredible American flag.
Under my leadership, the Constitution of the United States and the values it enshrines will always be preserved, protected, and defended as the supreme law of the land, and we will keep the Federal Government limited in its reach, honest in its conduct, and answerable only to the people it serves. I will never allow the dignity of our proud national heritage to be destroyed, and so long as I am President, America will continue to stand for freedom. Together, we will safeguard our God-given rights, our Constitution, and our glorious way of life for generations to come.
The Congress, by joint resolution of February 29, 1952 (36 U.S.C. 106), designated September 17 as “Constitution Day and Citizenship Day” and, by joint resolution of August 2, 1956 (36 U.S.C. 108), requested that the President proclaim the week beginning September 17 and ending September 23 of each year as “Constitution Week.”
NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States, do hereby proclaim the week of September 17 through September 23, 2026, as Constitution Week. Throughout this week, I call on all teachers, school administrators, and State and local leaders to educate America’s pupils on the rights and responsibilities of citizenship under our constitutional order. In doing so, we will ensure “a more perfect Union” will continue to prosper.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand this sixteenth day of September, in the year of our Lord two thousand twenty-six, and of the Independence of the United States of America the two hundred and fifty-first.
DONALD J. TRUMP
title: Constitution Day, Citizenship Day, and Constitution Week, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Steven Horsford (NV-04) today helped secure House Ways and Means Committee passage of a bipartisan digital asset tax package following months of negotiations to modernize the tax code, support innovation, and strengthen tax fairness.

“America should lead in innovation, and the opportunities it creates should reach working people and entrepreneurs,” said Rep. Air Force senior leaders discussed how the service can adapt to a contested environment, balance current readiness with future modernization and turn emerging capabilities into combat power during a panel at the Air and Space Forces Association’s 2026 Air, Space and Cyber Conference Sept. 14.
The panel featured Gen. Kevin Schneider, commander, Pacific Air Forces; Gen. Adrian L. Spain, commander, Air Combat Command; Lt. Gen. Kenyon Bell, deputy chief of staff for Logistics, Engineering and Force Protection; and Lt. Gen. Christopher Niemi, Air Force chief modernization officer.
The conversation began with lessons from recent operations and how those experiences are shaping the future force.
Schneider identified command and control, agile combat employment and resiliency as key areas for the Air Force moving forward, emphasizing the need for stronger command and control nodes, resilient data pathways and logistics capable of operating under pressure.
Spain reinforced the changing nature of the operating environment, pointing to the vulnerability of bases and the need to generate combat airpower while under attack.
“We do not operate from sanctuary any longer,” Spain emphasized. “Our bases are under attack, and we have to continue to generate air power in spite of that.”
That reality also changes how the service approaches logistics and force protection. Bell stressed that preparing for the future fight means preparing Airmen and infrastructure for conditions they cannot always predict.
“The era of uncontested logistics is over,” Bell said, highlighting the need to sustain and regenerate forces while operating in contested environments.
For Niemi, recent operations also reinforced the need to accelerate investments in point defense, a rapidly expanding mission designed to safeguard air bases against a full spectrum of airborne threats, and rethink the balance between a small number of highly capable platforms and a broader force able to generate mass.
The modernization challenge, however, is not simply determining what the Air Force needs next. Leaders must also decide how much risk the service can accept today to build that future force.
Schneider explained that each level of the Air Force operates on a different timeline, with operational commanders closest to the immediate risk.
“The operational end user, whoever has OPCON, TACON, owns the risk to mission and the risk to force to the Joint Force commander,” Schneider said. His role, he added, is to communicate that warfighter risk throughout the service so leaders can make informed decisions about the transition from current readiness to future modernization.
Spain described how ACC is balancing the immediate demands of presenting forces to combatant commanders with requirements extending decades into the future. While the force fighting within the next five years may look similar to today's force, he noted that it could look different a decade plus from now.
Niemi emphasized just how far ahead modernization decisions must look to deliver effective operational capabilities for tomorrow’s Airmen.
“We're trying to make a decision now and anticipate what the world is going to look like in 2033,” Niemi explained, noting that decisions made today may not deliver capabilities for years.
The tension in meeting today’s operational needs while shaping tomorrow’s force is an important part of the process rather than a problem to eliminate, Spain discussed.
“A healthy process here is always under tension,” Spain said. “It shouldn't be that we all agree all the time or we wouldn’t be giving the Chief and SecAF the info they need to make fully informed decisions.”
The panel then turned to how the Air Force can move emerging capabilities from development into the hands of the warfighter.
Niemi said the service should avoid trying to solve every problem at the headquarters level and instead allow operational commanders to experiment with new tools and determine what works.
“What I'm trying to focus on is to get it close enough that when it goes down to Gen. Spain or Gen. Schneider, that they have enough to be able to figure out what right actually looks like when I give them an 80% solution,” Niemi said.
Schneider similarly said that modernization cannot stop at acquiring a new platform, but must also include the sustainment of the program.
“It's more than just the equipment or the shiny thing that sits on a ramp,” Schneider said. “It's everything that enables it or allows it to be successful.”
Spain highlighted the difficulty of introducing new capabilities into established communities. New capabilities, he explained, require commanders to help operationalize them and demonstrate how they can contribute to the fight.
That challenge becomes particularly important as the service develops capabilities such as Collaborative Combat Aircraft. Niemi pointed to the cultural shift required to embrace technology that could eventually perform tasks traditionally handled by pilots.
“I can imagine a day in the future, 10 years, maybe more, where a CCA autonomous algorithm does a better job flying a fighter airplane than I did as a captain,” Niemi said. “That hurts my ego a little bit, but at the same time, I see that this trend is happening.”
The panel closed with a discussion on whether the Air Force should continue refining existing concepts or develop entirely new ones.
Spain pointed that to find the answer, start by asking what problem the service is actually trying to solve. Then look at if the current CONOP that exists sufficiently addresses the problem or could it if it was modified. If it cannot, he said, you probably need to transition to a concept that will.
“This stuff is really hard, and a lot of smart people have tried to do this the best they could under the conditions within they were working and now it is our turn,” Spain said. “We are committed to … making the best decisions that we can for the Air Force today, while also preparing our Air Force for the Future.”
Ultimately, the panelists emphasized that building the future Air Force will require more than new platforms. It will require resilient Airmen, infrastructure and logistics, risk-informed decision-making and a willingness to put emerging capabilities into the hands of warfighters to determine what works.
As the service prepares for an increasingly contested fight, the panel underscored the need to remain ready for today's fight while continually shaping the force needed for what comes next.
title: Air Force leaders chart path to future fight

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) issued the following statement after the House voted to pass H.R. 5334, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026:

“At a time when the cost of everything from gas to groceries, health care to housing, technology to toilet paper and more keeps going up, the Trump Administration keeps doubling down on the cost-of-living crisis through needless tariffs on allies and adversaries alike with no discretion. Though I support implementing sanctions against Russia, I cannot support a sanctions bill that grants the Trump Administration greater tariff authority to prolong and intensify ongoing economic uncertainty.

“Russia’s illegal war against Ukraine demands a serious response, and I stand firmly on the side of the Ukrainian people and their struggle against Putin’s invasion of their country. The U.S. must continue its role of providing support for Ukraine while holding Russia accountable. Unfortunately, rather than solely working to strengthen and enact tougher sanctions on Russia and deliver military aid to Ukraine, this bill also contains the largest transfer of tariff authority ever granted to a president by Congress, allowing the Trump Administration to launch 100% tariffs on any country it chooses without Congressional guardrails. And Trump, just off the heels of starting an unnecessary trade war with Canada, has given every indication that he would exploit this power to entrench the American people in more trade wars, which would only further drive up costs.

“In a government that hinges on checks and balances, we cannot further cede Congress’s constitutional authority to levy tariffs and allow the executive to operate with total tariff power. To address Russia’s war in Ukraine, we need substantive action that both sanctions Russia and its allies for their aggression and equips Ukraine with the tools necessary to defend itself and push back against Putin’s war machine. This is not that legislation. For that reason, I voted no.”
title: McClellan Statement on Sanctions Against Russia and Granting Trump Unilateral Tariff Authority

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06) released the following statement on his vote against H.R. 5334:

“I have a long history of standing with the Ukrainian people as they courageously defend their homeland against Vladimir Putin’s illegal invasion. I continue to support providing Ukraine with the resources, weapons, and ammunition it needs to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity.

“I oppose this bill because of its secondary tariff provisions. These provisions are overly broad and would give President Trump new, unchecked powers to impose tariffs as he sees fit.

“President Trump has repeatedly abused his tariff authorities that have been found to be illegal by the courts. I do not support giving him additional tariff powers that risk further fueling inflation, especially at a time when Sacramento County families are already struggling to make ends meet.

“The president already has robust sanctions authorities at his disposal to target Russia, its financial institutions, oligarchs, and others supporting Putin’s war, which he has insufficiently utilized since the beginning of his second term.

“I supported an amendment to remove the secondary tariff provisions in this bill while keeping the bill’s sanctions on Russia intact. Unfortunately, the Republican majority did not allow that amendment to receive a vote on the House floor. If these secondary tariff provisions were removed, I would support this legislation.

“I remain committed to standing with Ukraine and our Ukrainian diaspora community in Sacramento County. I will continue working to impose strong, targeted consequences on Putin and those enabling his illegal war.”
title: Rep. Bera Opposes Bill Granting President Trump Sweeping New Tariff Powers

Transcript of Rep. André Carson's Opening Statement from Hearing on Import Controls: Tools to Counter the CCP's Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Threats
WASHINGTON – Today, the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party held a hearing titled Import Controls: Tools to Counter the CCP's Industrial Policy and Supply Chain Threats. The hearing examined U.S. market restriction and import control policies, examples of how those policies have been used, and how they can be paired with industrial policy to strengthen U.S. manufacturing.
The following witnesses provided testimony:
- Mr. Peter Harrell, Visiting Scholar, Georgetown University Institute of International Economic Law; Senior Fellow, Council on Foreign Relations
- Mr. Craig Singleton, China Program Senior Director, Foundation for Defense of Democracies
- Mr. Oren Cass, Founder and Chief Economist, American Compass
Below is a transcript of the opening statement from Representative André Carson.
Mr. Chairman, thank you, and thank you to our witnesses for being here today.
For years, this Committee has led the debate on how to use market access policies to safeguard national security and counter the Chinese Communist Party’s dominance across critical sectors like telecommunications, drones, autos, robotics, solar, shipbuilding, batteries, and critical minerals.
These are powerful tools when used correctly. But today I want to press on a question I don't think we ask often enough: when we restrict a Chinese product or company from the U.S. market, how do we ensure American industry and workers can fill the gap?
Market restrictions on their own do not create an industry. If we restrict Chinese cranes, drones, or connected vehicles and nothing is standing behind that restriction to support American innovation, workers, and manufacturing, all we will have done is just changed our supplier—swapped Chinese firms for whichever foreign competitor is fastest to move into the gap we opened.
Take ZPMC cranes. When the Biden Administration restricted Chinese-manufactured port cranes on national security grounds, it paired that restriction with real investment in domestic crane manufacturing. That should be the model.
The goal cannot simply be "not China." It has to be building durable American and allied capacity in the sectors that matter most to our economic and national security. That means focusing on a suite of policies I like to call “economic patriotism.”
It includes smart policies like procurement preferences that give scale to firms making the leap; tax credits that de-risk capital; federal R&D that gets technology out of the lab; and maybe most importantly workforce investments that produce the welders, machinists, and engineers to actually run these plants.
I also want to make clear that restricting access to the world's largest consumer market has real consequences for businesses trying to plan, for workers whose jobs depend on supply chains we're reshaping, and for consumers who might pay the price of scarcity before American capacity catches up. This policy toolkit has real tradeoffs and should be used sparingly to address the greatest threats to the U.S., not settle political spats.
Additionally, Congress needs visibility into how these authorities are actually being used as a matter of course. That means reporting requirements with clear, public criteria for how designations get made and regular reviews of whether a restriction is actually achieving the security and economic goals it was built for.
I'll close with this. These tools — restrictions, tariffs, export controls — are not meant to be used to settle personal feuds between heads of state or as leverage in some unrelated negotiation. When they are, it doesn't just look bad. It actually undermines the credibility and effectiveness of the tools themselves, here and with our allies who we need standing beside us on this. Used well, market restrictions are one piece of a serious industrial strategy. Used carelessly, or for the wrong reasons, they're just noise that costs American businesses and workers real money.
I look forward to hearing from our witnesses on how we get this balance right. Thank you, and I yield back.
###

(Washington, DC) — Today, the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology is holding an Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee hearing titled, Balancing Biotechnology Innovation and Biosecurity: Securing U.S. Leadership in a Global Race.

Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren's (D-CA) opening statement as prepared for the record is below:

Good morning. Thank you to Chairman McCormick and Ranking Member Sykes for this hearing. Thank you to our witnesses for appearing today.

I want to start, Mr. Chairman, by asking unanimous consent to enter into the record a letter from the American Society for Microbiology, one of our country’s oldest and most respected scientific societies. I agree wholeheartedly with Ranking Member Sykes that the voices of the scientific community need to be heard in this discussion, and ASM has a valuable perspective on these issues.

One of the things that they point out in their letter is that the McKinsey Global Institute has estimated that as much as 60% of the physical imports to the global economy could in principle be produced biologically. That is a stunning possibility, and I see that one of our witnesses is connected with Dr. Endy. Visiting Dr. Endy's lab at Stanford – it is mind-blowing to see what the possibilities are.

This Committee has long and really impressive legacy of bipartisanship and oversight for biotechnology and biosecurity. Our bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act had several provisions tasking our agencies to support research on the safety and security implications of engineering biology. In this Congress, we approved H.R. 3029, a bill to support nucleic acid screening research at NIST. This bill has since passed the full House and I urge our counterparts in the Senate to take it up. We are also looking closely at the legislative ideas catalyzed by our colleagues from the National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology.

For years, this Committee has maintained a deep understanding of, and respect for, the spirit of openness that animates life science research. Republicans and Democrats alike have taken biosecurity and safety seriously, while understanding that to be the world leader in biotechnology, we must be tactful of how we legislate and perform oversight on biosecurity. Unfortunately, the term “strategic” does not adequately define the actions of the Trump Administration and how it has approached these issues. Ranking Member Sykes talked at length about many of these concerns. I will focus instead on what is at stake for us to lose.

One of the things I want to talk about, Mr. Hodges, is your work with Dr. Endy at the Hoover Institution. Dr. Endy was part of the research community that contributed to the development of one of the very first synthetic cells created entirely from scratch – a remarkable achievement for American life science. And when I texted him congratulations, he did text back saying, "We beat China."

So that was a good step forward.Dr. Endy importantly recognizes that the U.S. cannot, as he says, “ride the breaks” on biotechnology innovation and expect to remain a world leader. I remember touring the lab. There is a little sign that one of the scientists made that says, "The Wright brothers didn't need a license."

We have to keep that in mind if we are going to be successful. That doesn't mean that we don't take security seriously. We do, but we have to make sure that we don't stifle innovation in a way that is not strategic.

I just want to say a final thing on a concern that I have that's not really in the purview entirely of this Committee. And that's the fact that for years, we in the United States have benefitted from the fact that 80% of foreign-born STEM researchers have wanted to stay in the United States and become Americans with us. For a variety of reasons, hostility towards immigrants, lack of visa availability, the number of people coming from other countries to get their PhDs in STEM has dropped. And the number who want to stay after has also dropped precipitously. That is bad news for our country. A little under 50% of American Nobel Prize winners were Americans who are here by choice. Americans born in another country who decided to become one of us. Losing that will harm us and it will not only harm the research done here, but also our international partnerships and our dialogue and transparency.

So with that, Mr. Chairman, I yield back. Thank you for this hearing on this important topic.
title: Ranking Member Lofgren's Opening Statement at Hearing on Biotechnology Innovation and Biosecurity

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Stephanie Bice (OK-05), Hank Johnson (GA-04) and Lauren Boebert (CO-04) introduced the bipartisan, bicameralRenewing the Dream Actto authorize the National Parks Service to install a new plaque near the steps of the Lincoln Memorial marking where Civil Rights Movement leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his famed “I Have a Dream”speech.

“Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s moral clarity, rousing oratory and strategic nonviolent organizing propelled the Civil Rights Movement to the forefront of American consciousness,”said Rep. Raskin.“Our legislation honors the life and legacy of this Civil Rights Movement hero and his vision for a ‘Beloved Community’ by updating the dated, worn plaque marking where he delivered one of his greatest speeches. I’m grateful to this bipartisan group of my colleagues who are joining together to make sure Dr. King’s work and that moment is never forgotten.”

“Dr. Martin Luther King Jr’s ‘I Have a Dream’ speech is an iconic and critical moment in American history,”said Rep. Bice. “I’m proud to co-lead a bipartisan legislation which will replace the weathered plaque at the Lincoln Memorial, assuring that every American who visits can easily recognize this historical location for generations to come.”

“The plaque commemorating the very spot where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. delivered his iconic ‘I Have a Dream’ speech is in need of renewal, just as his dream is in need of renewal today,”said Rep. Johnson. “Dr. King dreamed that one day this nation would rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed: that all people are created equal. That dream remains as powerful and as necessary today as it was when he delivered those iconic words 63 years ago. I’m pleased to join Ranking Member Raskin and our bipartisan coalition to restore this historic marker and reaffirm the enduring power of Dr. King’s dream.”

"For over a decade, I have had a dream that one day the now deteriorated and inconspicuous stone upon which Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. stood at the Lincoln Memorial to share his ‘Dreams,’ would one day be restored to the dignity it deserves,”said Daryl Davis, Cofounder of the Prohuman Foundation. “We at the Prohuman Foundation are grateful for the blessing of the King family and thrilled with the support of Representatives Jamie Raskin, Hank Johnson, Stephanie Bice and Lauren Boebert who are championing our mission of Renewing The Dream. Every American will be proud to stand in the very spot where Dr. King stood 63 years ago this year, share his Dream and help turn it into a reality."

The Renewing the Dream Act authorizes the National Parks Service to install a new plaque near the steps of the Lincoln Memorial to honor Dr. King.Congress first authorized the plaque in October 2000. Since it was unveiled on August 22, 2003, constant exposure to the elements and countless footsteps have made the plaque nearly unreadable, as is evident in the picture below.

The new plaque includes a more durable and beautiful design, as seen below, and is completely funded by private donations.

Dr. King’s“I Have a Dream” speech was delivered during the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963. The march was part of a series of peaceful protests advocating for the civil rights and liberties of Black Americans.

Representatives Andy Barr (KY-06) and Lucy McBath (GA-06) are original cosponsors of this legislation.

The legislation is endorsed by the Prohuman Foundation and its founder, anti-racist activist and musician Daryl Davis. Daryl has advocated for the plaque’s replacement for more than ten years.

The full bill text can be foundhere.

JOHNSTOWN, Pa. – A resident of Altoona, Pennsylvania, pleaded guilty in federal court to charges of embezzlement and falsification of an annual financial report, United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced today.

On September 15, 2026, Nicole DeStefano, 52, pleaded guilty before United States District Judge Stephanie L. Haines to one count of embezzlement of labor union assets and one count of falsifying an annual financial report filed by a labor union.

In connection with the guilty plea, the Court was advised that, from 2015 through 2022, DeStefano served as the secretary-treasurer for the American Postal Workers Union Local 776 in Altoona. As the secretary-treasurer, she was responsible for maintaining all financial records, preparing annual reports, and issuing payments on behalf of Local 776. In September 2022, a member of Local 776 determined that the union’s 2021 annual financial report reflected abnormal disbursements from prior years. DeStefano had signed the financial report as both the treasurer and president, but had not provided notice either that she would be signing the report as the president or permitting union members to examine the financial records. The Blair Township Police Department opened an investigation, and law enforcement obtained a search warrant for DeStefano’s bank records.

Those bank records document that DeStefano wrote checks to herself from the union accounts—including, between December 2019 and August 2022, approximately 42 unauthorized checks totaling $30,411.68—as well as to “cash.” An audit of the union bank accounts also identified 43 unauthorized debit transactions, totaling almost $20,000. DeStefano omitted disbursing money to herself in annual financial reports that she filed with the Secretary of Labor for three consecutive years. In September 2022, DeStefano transferred $8,500 from her account into the union bank account and resigned her position with the union.

Judge Haines scheduled sentencing for January 19, 2027. The law provides for a maximum total sentence of up to five years in prison, a fine of the greater of $10 million or twice the gross pecuniary gain to DeStefano, or both. Under the federal Sentencing Guidelines, the actual sentence imposed is based upon the seriousness of the offenses and the prior criminal history, if any, of the defendant. By virtue of her felony conviction of embezzlement, DeStefano will be precluded from holding union office for a 13-year period.

Assistant United States Attorney Brendan J. McKenna is prosecuting this case on behalf of the government.

The Blair Township Police Department and the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Labor- Management Standards conducted the investigation that led to the prosecution of DeStefano.

ICE HSI Dallas investigation targets child exploitation in Oklahoma
DALLAS — ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations Dallas announced Aug. 26 that 39 defendants have been indicted or charged by complaint and several others have been identified and remain under investigation following a multiagency child exploitation enforcement operation in the Northern District of Oklahoma.
Operation Clean Sweep III was conducted in partnership with the Tornado Alley Child Exploitation and Trafficking Task Force, known as TACETT, which HSI created to bring together federal, state, local and tribal law enforcement partners to identify, investigate and prosecute child exploitation offenses. More than 25 law enforcement agencies participated in the operation.
“Operation Clean Sweep reflects HSI’s unwavering commitment to protecting children and holding predators accountable,” said HSI Dallas Deputy Special Agent in Charge Antwoine Jones. “This operation brought together law enforcement partners at every level with one mission: identify victims, remove them from harm and pursue justice against those who exploit children. HSI Dallas will continue working with our partners to ensure these investigations continue.”
From March through August 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Oklahoma received referrals from eight of the district’s 11 counties, resulting in 66 cases being opened for investigation. To date, 39 defendants have either been charged by complaint or indicted, with additional matters still under investigation.
Of the 39 defendants charged, 26 were charged with possessing child sexual abuse material, eight were charged with producing child sexual abuse material, and nine were charged with coercion and enticement for allegedly using phones and applications to target children. As a result of the operation, 21 children were identified and separated from defendants. That figure does not include children depicted in child sexual abuse material. Law enforcement agencies will continue partnering with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children to identify additional victims.
From January through August 2026, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children sent 8,621 CyberTips to the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation Internet Crimes Against Children unit. Of those tips, 2,086 cases were opened for investigation. Law enforcement partners in the Northern District of Oklahoma received 586 cases for further investigation.
As part of the operation, the U.S. Marshals Service, the Muscogee Creek Nation Lighthorse Police Department, the Cherokee Nation Marshal Service, the Pawnee County Sheriff’s Office and the Quapaw Nation Marshal Service conducted compliance checks on individuals required to register as sex offenders in the Northern District of Oklahoma. The Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act provides a comprehensive set of standards for sex offender registration and notification in the United States. In total, law enforcement checked 887 individuals in 10 of the district’s 11 counties. Investigators found that 34 individuals were not compliant with SORNA standards.
“Clean Sweep III is ending as an operation; however, the cases are not,” said U.S. Attorney Chris Nassar. “Investigations and prosecutions will continue on every open matter that has not yet been charged. The team that built this operation is not standing down. The experience, the relationships, and the enforcement effort will continue. We will keep bringing child predators to justice in the Northern District of Oklahoma.”
Participating law enforcement agencies included HSI Dallas, the FBI, the Tulsa Police Department, the U.S. Marshals Service, the Tulsa County Sheriff’s Office, the Broken Arrow Police Department, the Bixby Police Department, the Glenpool Police Department, the Mayes County Sheriff’s Office, the Rogers County Sheriff’s Office, the Ottawa County Sheriff’s Office, the Bureau of Indian Affairs, the Oologah Police Department, the Creek County Sheriff’s Office, the Skiatook Police Department, the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office, the Bristow Police Department, the Pryor Police Department, the Owasso Police Department, the Bartlesville Police Department, the Cherokee Nation Marshal Service, the Muscogee Creek Nation Lighthorse Police Department, the Pawnee County Sheriff’s Office and the Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation.
If you or someone you know is a victim of child exploitation, confidential help is available. Resources and contact information are available through the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Call 911 immediately to report a missing child and then the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children at 800-843-5678 to seek assistance.
This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by U.S. attorneys’ offices and the Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.
An indictment or complaint is merely an allegation, and each defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.
title: ICE HSI Dallas investigation targets child exploitation in Oklahoma

WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Representative Marie Gluesenkamp Perez reaffirmed her commitment to the Ukrainian community in Southwest Washington by voting for a comprehensive package of sanctions targeting Russia and anyone who facilitates sanctions evasion. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 is a critical effort to cripple funding for Russia’s War in Ukraine by penalizing countries that buy Russian oil. The bill was voted on in the Senate earlier this year, where it passed 86-11. The bill went on to pass in the House 262-159.

This package includes a number of sanctions, specifically it would:

Imposes blocking and entry (visa) sanctions on specified Russian officials, including Vladimir Putin and senior political and military leaders, oligarchs who haven’t opposed the war or continue to benefit from ties with the Russian government, executives/controlling owners of major Russian energy projects, foreign companies supporting Russia’s defense industrial base or military, and persons engaged in corruption, money laundering, or sanctions evasion for the Russian government.

Imposes sanctions on Russia’s “shadow fleet,” a network of vessels and supporting entities used to transport Russian oil and other goods while concealing ownership or transactions to circumvent sanctions.

Imposes sanctions on the Central Bank of Russia, Sberbank, VTB Bank, Gazprombank, and other covered Russian financial institutions. Foreign financial institutions engaging in significant transactions with sanctioned Russian institutions shall also be sanctioned.

Imposes sanctions on entities in which the Russian government holds a controlling/majority interest or that are otherwise government-affiliated, and restricts U.S. financial institutions from processing specified transactions involving the Russian government, government-owned entities, or Russian officials.

Restricts certain Russian securities from U.S. exchanges; prohibits new U.S. investment in Russia and its energy sector and transfer of U.S.-produced energy or energy products; prohibits purchases of Russian sovereign debt; authorizes restrictions on certain services to Russia; and sanctions certain financial-messaging providers used to circumvent sanctions.

Directs implementation of existing restrictions on Russian uranium imports under 42 U.S.C. §2297h-10a(d), including covered uranium associated with Rosatom or its subsidiaries or successors, and requires sanctions against specified officials and shareholders.

Extends the deadline of the 1996 Iran Sanctions Act from 2026 to 2031.

In addition to steep sanctions the bill would introduce aggressive secondary measures, including up to 500% duties on Russian goods and up to 100% duties on third-party countries that purchase Russian oil/gas or facilitate sanctions evasion.

“I’m proud to represent one of the largest Ukrainian communities in America–people who have lost fathers, mothers, sons and daughters in the fight to defeat fascism.,” said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “I urge the President to move quickly to implement these critical sanctions to ensure that Putin and his people know there is a steep price for their continued disregard for the sanctity of life.”

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has continuously worked to support Ukraine in its fight to end the Russian invasion and to support Ukrainian refugees displaced by the conflict. In 2024, she voted to pass HR 813, allocating over $60 billion in funding for Ukrainian defense. More recently in the FY27 Defense Appropriations markup, she spoke in support of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, a provision to strengthen domestic manufacturing capability to support Ukrainian defense. Additionally, Rep Gluesenkamp Perez supports Ukrainians living in Southwest Washington through her casework channels, helping constituents facing issues with federal agencies. To get in touch or learn about how her office can help with federal agencies, please visit her casework page or Ukrainian Language casework page.

####
title: Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez Votes to Support Ukrainian Defense and Sanction Russia

PHILADELPHIA — FEMA is proposing updates to the Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) for Morgan County, West Virginia. Community partners are invited to participate in a 90-day appeal and comment period.
The updated maps were produced in coordination with local, state and FEMA officials. Significant community review of the maps has already taken place, but before the maps become final, community partners can identify any corrections or questions about the information provided and submit appeals or comments.
The 90-day appeal period began on September 16, 2026. Residents, business owners and other community partners are encouraged to review the updated maps to learn about local flood risks and potential future flood insurance requirements. They may submit an appeal if they perceive that modeling or data used to create the map is technically or scientifically incorrect.
- An appeal must include technical information, such as hydraulic or hydrologic data, to support the claim.
- Appeals cannot be based on the effects of proposed projects or projects started after the study is in progress.
- If property owners see incorrect information that does not change the flood hazard information—such as a missing or misspelled road name in the Special Flood Hazard Area or an incorrect corporate boundary—they can submit a written comment.
The next step in the mapping process is the resolution of all comments and appeals. Once they are resolved, FEMA will notify communities of the effective date of the final maps.
Submit appeals and comments by contacting the County’s GIS and Addressing Department. The preliminary maps may be viewed online at the FEMA Flood Map Changes Viewer,
For more information about the flood maps, contact a FEMA Map Specialist by telephone; toll free, at 1-877-FEMA-MAP (1-877-336-2627) or by email at FEMA-FMIX@fema.dhs.gov.
Most homeowner’s insurance policies do not cover flooding. There are cost-saving options available for those newly mapped into a high-risk flood zone. Learn more about your flood insurance options by talking with your insurance agent and visiting https://www.floodsmart.gov.
Morgan County Flood Mapping Milestones
- May 9, 2025 — Flood Risk Review Meeting to review draft flood hazard data.
- November 21, 2025 — Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map released.
- January 15, 2026 — Community Coordination and Outreach Meeting to review Preliminary Flood Insurance Rate Map and discuss updates to local floodplain management ordinance and flood insurance.
- September 16, 2026 –Appeal Period starts.
- September 2027* — New Flood Insurance Rate Map becomes effective and flood insurance requirements take effect. (*Timeline subject to change pending completion of the appeal review process.)
If you have any questions, please contact FEMA Region 3 Office of External Affairs at (215) 931-5597 or at femar3newsdesk@fema.dhs.gov.
###
FEMA’s mission is helping people before, during and after disasters.
Follow FEMA online, on X @FEMA or @FEMAEspanol, on FEMA's Facebook page or Espanol page, on Truth Social and FEMA's YouTube account.
For preparedness information, follow the Ready Campaign on X at @Ready.gov, on Instagram @Ready.gov or on the Ready Facebook page.

This announcement came just twelve days after assuming responsibility as the Space Force’s senior uniformed leader.
Forge the Guardian Ethos
Schiess described his first line of effort as the foundational priority, rooted in the Space Force’s values of Character, Connection, Commitment and Courage. He stressed that every Guardian is a Guardian first—before specializing as an acquirer, space operator, intelligence analyst or cyber operator.
“The Space Force acts together as one Guardian team—a military force uniquely trained and equipped to deliver unparalleled space warfighting advantage,” he said.
He then pointed to the inspiration provided by Space Force Military Training Instructors who train new recruits at Basic Military Training and to the youngest Guardians already operating at what was considered science fiction just a few years ago.
Arm and Grow the Guardian Force
As his second line of effort, Schiess said he remains focused on arming and growing the Guardian Force.
Schiess echoed remarks by Department of the Air Force Secretary Troy Meink on Monday, who acknowledged the Space Force has weapons in space.
“Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the Joint Force against space-enabled attacks,” Schiess said. “We will make disciplined and responsible choices about how we build and sustain our combat advantage, which means scaling our ability to respond to threats.”
He explained Space Force growth and acquisition transformation must happen with the right organizational structures and the authorities in place to acquire and deliver capabilities to the Joint Force.
Schiess discussed a recent VICTUS HAZE mission that demonstrated the ability to launch and respond on-demand to an on-orbit threat in just 17 hours by working together with industry and across multiple acquisitions and operational Space Force units.
“Space Systems Command, our industry partners, and Combat Forces Command proved to the world that if an adversary targets the United States Space Force, we have the capability to deliver a swift response and we are going to continue working on getting faster and faster,” Schiess said.
Integrate Guardian Power at Scale
In his final line of effort, Schiess described the need for embedding Guardians on the frontlines and bringing space expertise directly into the Joint battlespace.
He highlighted one Guardian’s story, who deployed to the CENTCOM area of responsibility with the 42nd Electronic Warfare Detachment. Shortly after Operation Epic Fury began, she had to reconfigure her weapon system and conduct critical non-kinetic fires under missile attack, remaining at her console until ordered to safety.
Looking ahead, Schiess stressed the need for a sustained pipeline of trained Guardians equipped with advanced capabilities, so combatant commanders can rely on space expertise at home and abroad.
He underscored support for Guardian families, stating that he and his wife, Debbie, are committed to addressing stress points and strengthening support networks.
“We are fully committed to finding the solutions,” he said. “We want Guardians to step into the fight with absolute confidence knowing that our families are taken care of and secure.”
Schiess closed by reiterating the ultimate goal of deterring conflict.
“Deterrence is strongest when we have a credible force and the resolve to use it. That is what the Space Force brings to you…by delivering space superiority and by ensuring we get after our nation’s interests in, from and to space.”
title: Chief of Space Operations Schiess outlines priorities to strengthen Space Force combat power

(Washington, D.C.) – Today, the Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act, introduced by U.S. Representatives Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO), Sharice Davids (D-KS), and Derek Schmidt (R-KS), received a hearing in the House Committee on Natural Resources. The bipartisan legislation would designate the Quindaro Townsite in Kansas City, Kansas, as a National Historic Landmark. The site served as a critical entry point for anti-slavery settlers and a sanctuary for those escaping bondage via the Underground Railroad prior to and during the U.S. Civil War.

“The history of the Quindaro Townsite is an important piece of the story of Kansas City that must be told for generations to come,” said Congressman Cleaver. “I’m pleased that our bipartisan legislation to designate Quindaro as a National Historic Landmark was heard in the Natural Resources Committee, and following this important step in the legislative process, I look forward to continuing our push to ensure it becomes law.”

“Quindaro holds an important place in the history of Kansas and our nation. Founded during the turbulent days of Bleeding Kansas, it became a place of hope and refuge for those fighting for freedom and seeking a better future. This hearing is an important step toward ensuring Quindaro’s legacy is properly preserved and recognized for generations to come. I’m proud to lead this bipartisan effort with Representatives Cleaver and Davids, and I look forward to working with the committee to advance this legislation,” Rep. Schmidt said.

"This national landmark designation for Quindaro is long overdue. From its role on the Underground Railroad to its deep roots with the Wyandot Nation, Quindaro represents a crucial chapter of the Kansas City story. Today’s hearing gets our bill one step closer to cutting through administrative delays and making sure this history is preserved for our kids and grandkids," said Rep. Sharice Davids.

National Historic Landmarks are designated through the National Park Service System Advisory Board or an official act of Congress. Last May, the National Historic Landmarks Committee unanimously recommended Quindaro Townsite for designation as a National Historic Landmark, however the administrative process has since stalled. This bill would bypass the administrative process and designate the site by congressional action.

Representatives Cleaver and Davids submitted a letter to the House Committee on Natural Resources in support of the bipartisan legislation. The official letter is available here.

Official text of the Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act is available here.

Emanuel Cleaver, II is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth Congressional District, which includes Kansas City, Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Grandview, Sugar Creek, Greenwood, Blue Springs, North Kansas City, Gladstone, and Claycomo. He is a member of the exclusive House Financial Services Committee and Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance.
title: Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act Receives Hearing in Natural Resources Committee

CANTON, OH — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced that the Akron-Canton Regional Airport Authority will receive $175,000 in federal funding through the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) FY26 Airport Improvement Program.

The grant will fund the acquisition of 35 new vehicle movement area transponders, bringing the airport into conformity with current federal safety standards. Vehicle movement area transponders track ground vehicles operating on runways, taxiways, and other restricted airfield surfaces, giving air traffic controllers real-time visibility into airfield activity and reducing the risk of runway incursions.

The funding comes through the FAA's Airport Improvement Program, which provides federal grants to public-use airports for projects related to safety, capacity, and infrastructure. Akron-Canton Regional Airport serves as a key transportation and economic hub for Summit and Stark counties, supporting commercial passenger service, cargo operations, and general aviation.

“This federal investment in Akron-Canton Airport strengthens safety for everyone who works and travels through the airport. I'm proud to have helped secure this funding, and I'll keep working to bring resources home to Ohio's 13th District,” said Congresswoman Sykes. “Every dollar we bring home for projects like this one means a safer, stronger airport for the families and businesses that depend on it.”

“We are grateful to Congresswoman Sykes for her continued commitment to aviation and for helping secure this Airport Improvement Program grant,” said Ren Camacho, President and CEO of the Akron-Canton Airport. “This funding will allow CAK to equip our airfield vehicles with Vehicle Movement Area Transponders, adding another important layer of safety by improving visibility and situational awareness across the airfield.”

This announcement follows Congresswoman Sykes' ongoing efforts to secure federal infrastructure funding for Ohio's 13th District, including previous investments in transportation, aviation, and public safety projects across Summit, Stark, and Portage counties.

SPRINGFIELD, Mo. – R. Matthew Price, United States Attorney for the Western District of Missouri, announced today a complete defense verdict in Richardson v. United States , a wrongful death lawsuit brought against the United States of America under the Federal Tort Claims Act. The lawsuit arose after a federal agent employed deadly force to stop an imminent threat posed by an armed, aggressive individual.

On Sept. 10, 2026, judgment was entered in favor of the United States following a three-day bench trial before U.S. District Judge Roseann A. Ketchmark. The trial concluded on April 30, 2026.

The incident occurred on Nov. 2, 2020, while two Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) agents were conducting surveillance at a Springfield apartment complex. After observing behavior indicative of drug transactions, the agents followed a rented U-Haul pickup truck from the apartment complex to a residential home. The driver of the U-Haul met two other individuals at the home, including the decedent, Mr. Caleb Slay.

When one of the agents contacted Mr. Slay, Mr. Slay shouted an expletive at him while walking away. Mr. Slay then returned to engage in a brief conversation with the agent, at which point it was learned that Mr. Slay was armed with a handgun. Mr. Slay began fighting the agents upon their attempt to detain him for their safety. During the altercation, with one agent lying on his back underneath Mr. Slay, Slay reached his right hand toward his right rear waistband. One agent described the reach as a “quick gesture” to the waistband, where Slay’s hand paused. This indicated to the agent that Slay was attempting to “establish a grip on the gun.” The agent who discharged his firearm provided a warning prior to the shooting.

The court ruled that the plaintiff failed to prove the DEA agent used more force than was reasonably necessary. The court emphasized that use-of-force decisions must be evaluated from the perspective of a reasonable officer on the scene making split-second judgments in tense, uncertain situations, rather than with the benefit of hindsight.

Federal law enforcement agents place their lives on the line to enforce the laws of this nation. As such, the Department of Justice is committed to defending justified uses of force. The court’s ruling reinforces that commitment.

This case is being defended by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Wyatt R. Nelson and Christa B. Moss, Deputy Civil Chief, of the Western District of Missouri. The case was investigated by the Springfield Police Department and the Drug Enforcement Administration.
title: Defense Verdict in Use of Force, Wrongful Death Lawsuit Against the United States

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representatives Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Gabe Evans (R-CO-08) introduced bipartisan legislation to streamline and modernize how surviving spouses, children, and dependent parents apply for Social Security survivor benefits. The bill would help families avoid long phone hold times and unnecessary in-person visits during a period of intense emotional and financial strain.

"When a family loses a parent, spouse, or breadwinner, the last thing they should have to deal with is a maze of administrative red tape just to access the benefits their loved one earned through a lifetime of hard work," said Davids. "My casework team will always help Kansans recover backlogged federal benefits — including Social Security — but families shouldn’t have to turn to their representatives’ offices just to get the benefits they’ve earned. This bipartisan bill would make it easier for families to get those benefits on their own, without having to navigate unnecessary hurdles during an already difficult time."

“When families experience the loss of a loved one, the last thing they should have to deal with is red tape and complications when accessing the benefits they are owed,” said Representative Gabe Evans (R-CO-08). “I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan Survivor Benefits Applications Modernization Act to ensure grieving families have faster access to the resources and services they need during difficult times.”

Under current Social Security Act provisions, when a person passes away, their surviving family members — including young children, surviving spouses caring for children, and dependent parents — are eligible for survivor insurance benefits. However, unlike other federal programs that offer streamlined digital services, the Social Security Administration (SSA) process for survivor benefits still largely relies on manual scheduling and paper-based applications. This leads to extended processing delays, crowded field offices, and unnecessary stress for families facing sudden loss.

The bipartisan Survivor Benefits Application Modernization Act would fix that problem by requiring the Social Security Administration to:

Establish an Online Self-Scheduling Portal: Within 180 days of enactment, the SSA Commissioner must launch an online system allowing applicants for survivor benefits to independently schedule appointments.

Develop Online Application Filing: Within one year of enactment, the SSA must enable beneficiaries to complete and submit their survivor benefits applications directly through the secure online portal.

Report on Efficiency and Integrity: Requires the SSA to submit a report to Congress within three years detailing application processing trends, administrative cost savings, and fraud and identity theft instances.

“New York Life supports the Survivor Benefits Application Modernization Act, which would enable grieving families to apply for Social Security survivor benefits online,” said Heather Nesle, Senior Vice President of Corporate Responsibility, New York Life. “As the nation’s largest corporate funder of childhood bereavement causes, the New York Life Foundation has long championed efforts that help grieving families access the support they need. We thank Representatives Davids and Evans for leading the effort to help more children access the financial support they are entitled to during an incredibly difficult time.”
title: Davids, Evans Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Streamline Social Security Survivor Benefits for Families

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act would require SBA to provide consistent, current disaster loan information to small business owners

WASHINGTON, D.C. — The House Committee on Small Business today advanced legislation introduced by Representative Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) to strengthen federal disaster assistance for small businesses and ensure owners have accurate, up-to-date information when recovering from natural disasters. The legislation will advance to the House floor when scheduled for a vote.

Small businesses are increasingly on the front lines of natural disasters, facing flooding, severe storms, blizzards, and other events that can threaten their ability to stay open. The Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act would require the Small Business Administration (SBA) to establish standardized procedures to ensure disaster outreach materials are consistent, current, and accurate across its field operations centers—equipping businesses with the information to seek and receive aid in a timely manner.

“With nearly 99 percent of all businesses in my home state of New Jersey are small businesses and each one facing the threat of coastal storms and severe floods, these are over 1 million owners and potential borrowers who need all the relevant information. This is why my bill, the Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act, offers a simple solution and basic oversight to this issue,” said Congresswoman Mejia. “I urge my colleagues and members of this committee to support this legislation. In a period of time where misinformation is rampant, we must work to ensure small business owners have all the possible information they can have to make the best decision for themselves. We cannot let our federal agencies misguide, misdirect, and withhold vital information, especially when they make regulatory changes that affect Americans. The disaster loan program is one crucial step in recovery after a natural disaster.”

Small businesses make up nearly 99 percent of businesses in New Jersey, making access to reliable disaster assistance particularly important as communities across the state face increasingly severe storms and flooding.

The legislation would provide greater consistency and accountability across SBA’s disaster outreach efforts, helping ensure that the small business owners who rely on federal disaster loans receive the information they need to make informed decisions and recover more quickly.

Click here to view Rep. Mejia’s remarks.

U.S. Marshals Arrest Firearms Thief on Federal Arrest Warrant
For immediate release
Andrew Grillo, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Concord, NH – The U.S. Marshals Service (USMS) District of New Hampshire apprehended a fugitive this morning on Incline Avenue in Goffstown. The fugitive was wanted for violating supervised release conditions stemming from a prior conviction of theft of a firearm from a federal firearms licensee.
In 2020, Ryan Woods, 37, stole a firearm from Shooters Outpost in Hooksett, and he was convicted in the United States District Court for the District of New Hampshire. As part of his sentencing, Woods was placed on federal supervision. While on supervision, Woods accrued multiple violations of release conditions, and a federal arrest warrant was issued on July 27, 2026.
The U.S. Marshals worked with investigators from the Manchester, Nashua, and Goffstown Police Departments to develop information that would indicate Woods’ whereabouts.
That information led the investigators to the Incline Avenue address. Aided by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, S.W.A.T. personnel from Manchester and Nashua, the U.S. Marshals and Goffstown Police were able to safely apprehend Woods without incident. Following his arrest, Woods was transported to the U.S. District Court in Concord.
“Every arrest of a violent fugitive renders our communities safer,” said the District of New Hampshire U.S. Marshal (A), Katherine Burns. “I’m proud of the dedication shown by our investigators and grateful for the seamless coordination between our task force and local law enforcement partners that made this arrest possible.”
The USMS New Hampshire Joint Fugitive Task Force was formed in the fall of 2002 and is headquartered in Concord. The task force coordinates federal, state, county, and local resources to develop leads, gather intelligence, track and apprehend targeted fugitives. The Task Force receives vital support from Strafford, Merrimack and Rockingham Counties, as well as the cities of Manchester, Nashua and Concord.
