U.S. Marshals Arrest Cold Case Fugitive Wanted for Aggravated Vehicular Homicide
For immediate release
Josh Lowe, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Cleveland, OH - This afternoon, members of the U.S. Marshals led Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force (NOVFTF) arrested David Sawicki, 56. Sawicki was wanted by the Medina County Sheriff's Office for aggravated vehicular homicide.
On May 26, 2020, Sawicki was charged in the Medina County Court of Common Pleas with aggravated vehicular homicide and operating a vehicle under the influence of alcohol, a drug of abuse or a combination of them. The charges stemmed from an incident that occurred in Medina County in April 2020. Investigators believed Sawicki fled Ohio after the incident and had been on the run since. Information developed by the NOVFTF led them to believe Sawicki had ties to Florida and Arizona and was possibly using the alias “Anthony Horvath.”
Over the course of the investigation, task force members conducted numerous interviews and disseminated “WANTED” posters throughout the nation offering reward money to the public, which led to them vetting dozens of tips over the past 6 years. Today, members of the NOVFTF acting on a tip from the public were able to locate and arrest Sawicki at a medical facility in the 9500 block of Euclid Ave., Cleveland, Ohio where he had checked in for treatment.
Medina County Sheriff Terry Grice stated, “The family of the victim in this tragic incident is now one step closer to getting the justice they deserve. The Medina County Sheriff’s Office and the US Marshals Service will continue to work closely together to keep Medina County a safe place to live.”
U.S. Marshal Pete Elliott stated, “The arrest today was a direct result of the community and law enforcement collaborating to take another violent fugitive off the street. We couldn’t be as successful as we are at arresting fugitives without the assistance of our great citizens of northern Ohio. Today’s apprehension reflects the determination of our cold case investigators and their ability to never give up.”
Anyone with information concerning a wanted fugitive can contact the Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force at 1-866-4WANTED (1-866-492-6833), or you can submit a web tip. Reward money is available, and tipsters may remain anonymous. Follow the U.S. Marshals on Twitter @USMSCleveland.
The Northern Ohio Violent Fugitive Task Force – Cleveland Division is composed of the following federal, state and local agencies: U.S. Marshals Service, Cleveland Police Department, Cuyahoga County Sheriff’s Office, Cuyahoga Metropolitan Housing Authority Police Department, Euclid Police Department, Ohio Adult Parole Authority, Ohio State Highway Patrol, Independence Police Department, Parma Police Department, Aurora Police Department, Solon Police Department, Cleveland RTA Police Department, Westlake Police Department, Bedford Police Department, Medina County Sheriffs Office, Middleburg Heights Police Department, Newburgh Heights Police Department and the Metrohealth Police Department.
title: U.S. Marshals Arrest Cold Case Fugitive Wanted for Aggravated Vehicular Homicide | U.S. Marshals Service

text:
Ambassador Mike Waltz
U.S. Representative to the United Nations
New York, New York
AS DELIVERED
Thank you, Mr. President.
Colleagues, this is a meaningful, and frankly, somewhat surreal day for many of us here in the United States.
I’m confident, if you ask any American who was alive on September 11, who was there that day at Ground Zero—where I’m so grateful that so many of you joined us last week, and where we were this morning—that they can, you know, every American I know can tell you exactly where they were when they heard about the attack. They’ll tell you what they saw, who they were speaking to, what family members they called, and what they did next.
And in the years that followed, as we well know, and as history now looks back on, an entire generation of soldiers, firefighters, police officers, intelligence professionals, ordinary American patriots, coalitions stepped forward to serve.
One of those patriots I’d like to just take a moment to tell you about, his name was Matthew Pucino.
He was a police officer, and joined the military, joined the army because of September 11, because he could not accept the fact that these terrorists had attacked his country on his own soil.
A few years later, Matt became one of the Green Berets who served in my command and was literally one of the very best human beings I’ve ever known.
Unfortunately, where we were serving at the time, the enemy adapted. They adapted to our jammers that jammed the IEDs, and they went back to their own basics, so to speak, using trip wires and buried bombs. This was an enemy that was terrorizing the civilians that were around them, beheading local policemen.
Matt repeatedly volunteered to ride ahead of our armored convoy, but he did so on a small motorcycle, so that he could be close enough to spot any disturbances on the ground, any trip wires. And one day I confronted him and I said, “Matt, you are really pushing your luck here, brother.”
And his response, which has stayed with me ever since, he said, “Sir, if I miss one, if I miss one of these trip wires, I want to make sure it only gets me, not four or five of my brothers riding behind me in a vehicle.” One night he did miss one. He was killed by an IED in Afghanistan. I didn’t bring him home.
I wear his name with me every single day in his memory, and I share that memory and the memory that we have today of the 2,977 innocent people murdered on September 11. 2,605 Americans and citizens from more than 90 countries—I say again, 90 countries—were killed this day, citizens from 90 countries were killed this day.
Twenty-five years ago, it was the World Trade Center. It was an attack on the world. We all remember the first responders who didn’t run away. They ran towards the flames, and their families with loved ones who never came home, the nurses and doctors who waited for the injured who never came.
9/11’s death toll did not end at Ground Zero, or the Pentagon, or Shanksville, Pennsylvania.
Years later, there were heroes like U.S. Ambassador to Libya Chris Stevens, soldiers who were with him and defending him, Sean Smith, Tyrone Woods, Glen Doherty, all who died in Benghazi—murdered in cold blood by terrorists 14 years ago today, also on 9/11.
Millions around the world have since been murdered, maimed, displaced, recruited, forced to live under terrorism’s shadow because of this scourge.
Colleagues, as I look around the table, everyone in this room, all on this Council, from Latvia to Liberia, everyone has lost men and women in uniform confronting terrorism in the years since.
So, for most of you, September 11 is sadly not the only terror attack in your national memory. We should take stock of that. We should remember that.
The Bataclan in France.
7/7 in the UK.
The Beslan school attack in Russia.
The Peshawar school massacre in Pakistan.
The Mogadishu bombing in Somalia.
The El Nogal bombing in Colombia.
The Alas Chiricanas Flight 901 in Panama.
The Kunming knife attacks in China.
The Congolese church massacres.
The Copenhagen synagogue attack in Denmark.
The November 17 attacks in Greece.
The Daih bombing in Bahrain.
Each one: death, destruction, and so many innocent lives lost. And they say, “a common danger unites even the bitterest of enemies.”
And maybe this explains why, on a council that often disagrees on almost everything sometimes it seems like, but condemning terrorism remains one of those few things we all do together and do so unanimously.
And we did unanimously with France then as the president of this Council on September 11, 2001, where we unanimously adopted Resolution 1368, condemning the attacks, calling on all nations to work together to bring the perpetrators, the organizers, and the sponsors to justice.
And on behalf of the American people, I thank you for that. Seventeen days later, Resolution 1373 required states to suppress terrorist financing, to freeze terrorist assets, to deny terrorists safe haven. And with today’s Presidential Statement, this Council has spoken with one voice against the scourge of terrorism.
I saw that same unity on the battlefield. Across my career, Green Berets and I served alongside soldiers from all over the world: from Aussies and Afghans, to Emiratis, to Brits, to Poles, so many others.
Together, we hunted down bin Laden. Our coalition destroyed the ISIS’s caliphate. We killed al-Baghdadi and al-Zawahiri.
We will never fully know how many plots have been thwarted, that haven’t hit our cities, yours, colleagues, because of quiet professionals in all of our governments across our militaries.
But there is still work to do. It is not over. Our mission is not complete against extremism. Today’s threat is broader: narco-terrorism, transnational criminal organizations, resurgent political terrorism.
Evil still exists in this world, and terrorists are adapting again. They’re exploiting, as we’ve heard today, drones, AI, encrypted communications, digital finance, whatever they can invent next to spread their terrorism into our societies.
Entire regimes still fund and arm civilian killing terrorists that target civilians deliberately.
Some of their representatives come before this very Council, and after all, each of us has suffered. We cannot waste another day excusing proxies or looking away.
That goes for this institution, too. The UN has spent 25 years building a counterterrorism architecture. And now we have to deliver.
So, let’s call terrorism what it is. Let’s cut off its funding. Let’s deny safe haven. Let’s enforce this Council’s resolutions. Let’s share intelligence. Let’s hunt down those who plan these attacks, because we all must fight this scourge until it is defeated.
And we will never forget. And I thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.
###
title: Remarks at a UN Security Council Briefing Marking the 25th Anniversary of 9/11

PORTLAND, Ore.—A federal jury found Beniamin Lucescu, age 57, a Portland resident, guilty today of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, and money laundering.

According to court documents and evidence presented at trial, between April 2020 and May 2022, during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, Beniamin Lucescu and his wife, Georgeta Lucescu, conspired to steal almost $500,000 in pandemic relief funds by lying to the Small Business Administration about their intended use of the funds. Beniamin Lucescu repeatedly lied on the applications for the relief funds, claiming they would only use them for economic injuries their business, Rose City Senior Care, suffered as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. In reality, Beniamin Lucescu planned to use the pandemic relief funds for personal expenses and investments. As soon as they received the pandemic relief funds, Beniamin Lucescu used almost all of the $500,000 to pay off their old personal federal tax debt and invest in cryptocurrency.

“The pandemic was a time of unprecedented hardship, when Americans needed their government’s help most. Beniamin Lucescu chose to exploit that crisis for his own gain. His fraud stole critical taxpayer-funded resources from Americans who were counting on them. We will not tolerate those who abuse government relief programs for personal profit. Thanks to the dedicated work of the SBA-OIG and my office, Lucescu was held accountable and brought to justice,” said Scott E. Bradford, U.S. Attorney for the District of Oregon.

On September 17, 2025, a federal grand jury in Portland returned an eight-count superseding indictment charging Beniamin and Georgeta Lucescu with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to commit money laundering. Beniamin Lucescu was also charged with money laundering.

Beniamin Lucescu will be sentenced on December 14, before a U.S. District Judge.

Georgeta Lucescu is scheduled for trial on February 8, 2027. Georgeta Lucescu is charged by indictment. An indictment is only an accusation of a crime, and a defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

This case was investigated by the Small Business Administration Office of Inspector General with assistance of the Federal Bureau of Investigation and was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Meredith Bateman and Special Assistant United States Attorney Ethan Bodell.
title: Portland Man Found Guilty of Stealing Pandemic Relief Funds

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Summer Lee (PA-12), and Chris Deluzio (PA-17) wrote a letter to the Acting Director of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) exposing the lack of data transparency in current ICE records management and reporting, specifically in its partnerships with state and local law enforcement.

“According to published federal records between January 1 to August 6, 2026, of the 1,227 Pennsylvania 287(g) arrest records, only 12 of those records included the task force designation agency that was involved in arrest. ICE chose to withhold that information more than 1,000 times so far this year despite such information being a designated field included in arrest records. This discrepancy undermines transparency and leaves the public without a clear understanding of which agency or department was involved,” the lawmakers wrote.

The 287(g) program established a partnership between ICE and state or local law enforcement to authorize selected officers to carry out federal immigration enforcement or deportation. Specifically, the lawmakers are demanding training records, complaints, and oversight records about 287(g) programs in Pennsylvania to be made public.

“The public has a right to clear and complete information about the nature of the enforcement activities taking place in our neighborhoods and the departments or agencies responsible for carrying them out. Programs between federal and local law enforcement agencies must meet the highest standards of transparency,” the lawmakers continue.

Following a recent visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center in central Pennsylvania, Congresswoman Dean lead her Pennsylvania colleagues in letters to ICE and the GEO Group, the for-profit prison corporation that owns and operates MVPC, to demand answers on GEO’s failure to comply with federal standards of adequate staffing and medical care to detainees, as well as obstruction of congressional oversight.

Congresswoman Dean also recently introduced theOversight Access Act to expand congressional oversight at ICE facilities without prior notice and the No Shock Act to ban the use of electric shock gloves by ICE agents.?

Read the full text of the letter here.

Rep. Madeleine Dean is a mother, grandmother, attorney, professor, former four-term member of the Pennsylvania House of Representatives, and U.S. Representative for the Fourth District of Pennsylvania.

###
title: Dean, PA Delegation Demand Stronger Data Transparency from ICE

LAS VEGAS – A Mexican man made his initial appearance in court Thursday for allegedly smuggling two illegal aliens from Mexico into the United States.

“Human smuggling is a direct violation of our nation's laws that compromises the security of our borders and puts human lives at risk for corporate-style profit,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “This criminal complaint sends a clear message to smugglers: we will aggressively pursue, disrupt, and dismantle operations that treat human beings as cargo. Our office, alongside our dedicated federal and local law enforcement partners, remains unyielding in our mission to secure our borders and hold smugglers fully accountable under federal law.”

According to allegations in the criminal complaint, on April 14, 2025, a Border Patrol Agent initiated a traffic stop on a vehicle driven by Adrian Najera-Santos. When the vehicle came to an abrupt stop, Najera-Santos and two passengers fled into the desert. After a brief foot chase and search of the area, law enforcement apprehended Najera-Santos and the two others. During their interviews, the two passengers stated that they had paid to be smuggled into the United States and to California. They were picked up by a vehicle and taken to an unknown town where Najera-Santos picked them up to take them to Santa Maria, California. They were to pay Najera-Santos $700 for driving them.

Najera-Santos is charged with one count of transporting illegal aliens. If convicted, the maximum statutory penalty is 10 years in prison.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection is investigating the case; and the District of Nevada is prosecuting the case.

This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. Operation Take Back America streamlines efforts and resources from the Department’s Project Safe Neighborhoods (PSN).

A criminal complaint is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law.

###
title: Mexican Man Charged for Smuggling Illegal Aliens Into the United States

BOSTON – A Dominican national was sentenced yesterday in federal court in Boston for possession of child sexual abuse material (CSAM).

Jorge Junior Alvarez Rodriguez, 23, was sentenced by U.S. Senior District Court Judge Patti B. Saris to 41 months in prison. The defendant is subject to deportation upon completion of the imposed sentence. In April 2026 , Alvarez pleaded guilty to one count of possession of child pornography. Alvarez was charged in May 2025 .

On May 3, 2025, upon arrival at Boston’s Logan Airport from Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, Alvarez was flagged for secondary screening. During a review of Alvarez’s cell phone, files depicting CSAM were found. Multiple files depicting children as young as four to seven years old were discovered.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by Customs and Border Protection, Boston Division. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lauren Maynard and Julissa Walsh of the Criminal Division prosecuted the case.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse, launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the DOJ’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit https://www.justice.gov/psc .
title: Dominican National Sentenced to Over Three Years for Child Pornography Offense

ALEXANDRIA, Va. – The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia observed the 25 th anniversary of the September 11 attacks on the Pentagon and the World Trade Center with a reflective presentation hosted by First Assistant U.S. Attorney Theophani K. Stamos. The observation featured remembrances from former U.S. Attorney Chuck Rosenberg and former Assistant U.S. Attorney Robert Spencer.

Three months after the attacks, Al Qaida terrorist Zacarias Moussaoui was indicted in the Eastern District of Virginia. Moussaoui was convicted at trial of conspiracy to commit acts of terrorism transcending national boundaries, conspiracy to commit aircraft piracy, conspiracy to destroy aircraft, conspiracy to use weapons of mass destruction, conspiracy to murder employees of the United States, and conspiracy to destroy property. U.S. District Judge Leonie M. Brinkema sentenced Moussaoui to life in prison.

Moussaoui remains the only individual to date to have ever been convicted in a U.S. court in connection with the September 11 attacks.

“It is impossible to adequately describe either the responsibility of bringing a measure of justice for those lost on September 11, 2001, or the honor of having been entrusted with that responsibility,” said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Stamos. “Dedicated EDVA employees passed the Pentagon on their daily commute to this office where they tirelessly worked on the prosecution of Zacarias Moussaoui. Among the best ways we can honor those who were lost that day are vigilance against those who seek to harm America and its people and the unyielding pursuit of justice each day.”
title: Eastern District of Virginia hosts 9/11 observance on 25th anniversary of attacks

LOS ANGELES – A Compton man was sentenced today to 36 months in federal prison for assaulting and injuring a federal officer by throwing large rocks at passing government vehicles during an anti-immigration law enforcement riot last year in Paramount.

Elpidio Reyna, 42, was sentenced by United States District Judge Fernando L. Aenlle-Rocha.

Reyna pleaded guilty on February 17 to one felony count of assault on a federal officer by deadly or dangerous weapon resulting in bodily injury. He has been in federal custody since July 2025.

“Disagreeing with laws passed by Congress does not give you a right to assault federal officers,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “This defendant thought he would go unpunished for throwing large rocks at law enforcement. Instead, he’ll be serving time in federal prison, where he can reflect on his poor decision.”

According to his plea agreement, on June 7, 2025, Reyna forcibly and intentionally assaulted with a deadly and dangerous weapon a federal law enforcement officer engaged in his official duties, resulting in the infliction of bodily injury to the officer.

On that day, federal law enforcement officers were staging a joint enforcement operation in Paramount in the vicinity of a Home Depot. Protestors, including Reyna, began to throw rocks at the officers’ official vehicles, lit objects on fire, and impeded law enforcement activity.

During this time, Reyna knowingly and intentionally lit objects on fire in the middle of the street and threw rocks at a convoy of law enforcement vehicles occupied by United States Customs and Border Protection (CBP) officers, including the victim – identified in court documents as “R.T.” – all of whom were engaged in their official duties as federal officers.

Reyna threw a rock at R.T.’s government vehicle, which caused glass to shatter and injure R.T. by cutting his forehead.

“[Reyna’s] reflection on the circumstances surrounding his conduct, that his actions were ‘sudden and emotional and fueled by alcohol,’ because of his anger regarding immigration policy in the United States, is simply not an adequate excuse for his violence,” prosecutors argued in a sentencing memorandum.

The FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, and United States Border Patrol investigated this matter.

Assistant United States Attorney Brenda N. Galván of the Transnational Organized Crime Section prosecuted this case.
title: Compton Man Sentenced to 3 Years in Federal Prison for Injuring Federal Officer During Anti-Immigration Enforcement Riot Last Year

SHERMAN OAKS, CA — On September 3rd, Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32) hosted his sixth Telephone Town Hall of the year, bringing together over 3,000 constituents from across California’s 32nd Congressional District for a wide-ranging discussion on the most pressing issues facing the community and the country.

The Town Hall featured California State Senator Ben Allen, who joined Sherman to discuss issues affecting Californians at the state and local level and answer questions directly from constituents.

“These Town Halls give me an opportunity to hear directly from the people I represent, answer their questions, and make sure they know what is happening in Washington and how it affects their families and our community,” said Congressman Sherman. “I’m grateful to everyone who joined us and to Senator Ben Allen for helping provide a perspective from Sacramento. At a time of tremendous uncertainty at home and abroad, maintaining this direct dialogue with constituents is more important than ever.”

During the event, Sherman provided an update on the ongoing U.S. conflict with Iran, which has now stretched into its seventh month amid renewed hostilities in the region. Sherman discussed the continued risks to American servicemembers, the economic consequences of the conflict, including higher energy prices, and the need for Congress to exercise its constitutional responsibilities over matters of war and peace.

Sherman also discussed his concerns regarding the Trump Administration’s proposed nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia. After reviewing the agreement submitted to Congress, Sherman warned that it fails to include critical nonproliferation safeguards and could ultimately pave the way for Saudi Arabia to develop nuclear weapons. Sherman emphasized that preventing nuclear proliferation in the Middle East must remain a bipartisan national security priority.

In addition, Sherman addressed the continued economic pressures facing families throughout the San Fernando Valley and Los Angeles, including the cost of housing, groceries, gasoline, and other everyday necessities. He discussed his efforts in Congress to lower costs for consumers and protect Social Security, Medicare, and other programs relied upon by working families and seniors.

California State Senator Ben Allen provided an update on issues before the California Legislature and discussed efforts in Sacramento to address challenges facing communities throughout Southern California. Allen and Sherman also highlighted the importance of coordination between state and federal officials in delivering resources and addressing the concerns of shared constituents.

Constituents raised questions on a broad range of issues, including the war with Iran and U.S. foreign policy, the cost of living, housing affordability, immigration enforcement, health care, and protecting democratic institutions. Sherman and Allen responded directly to questions and discussed their respective efforts at the federal and state levels to address these concerns.

Participants also had the opportunity to respond to interactive survey questions and share their views on several of the major issues discussed during the Town Hall.

The results of the survey questions are as follows:

Who deserves more of the blame for America’s affordability crisis?

-President Biden and Democrats: 9%

-Trump and Congressional Republicans: 81%

-Both equally: 7%

-Unsure: 3%

Do you support Trump’s tariffs on Canada?

-Yes: 8%

-No: 90%

-Unsure: 2%

Do you believe the U.S. has a responsibility to help Ukraine defend itself from Russia’s invasion?

-Yes: 75%

-No: 25%

###
title: Over 3,000 Join Congressman Brad Sherman’s 6th Town Hall of the Year

Coast Guard Cutter Joseph Gerczak returns home following 52-day Operation Blue Pacific patrol in Oceania
Coast Guard Oceania District External Affairs - (808) 265-7748
HONOLULU – The crew of Coast Guard Cutter Joseph Gerczak (WPC-1126) returned to Honolulu, Tuesday following a 52-day patrol in support of Coast Guard Oceania District's Operation Blue Pacific.
The Joseph Gerczak crew departed Coast Guard Base Honolulu in July and traveled more than 7,500 nautical miles, making port calls in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, Fiji and American Samoa. Patrolling in support of Operation Blue Pacific, the cutter's crew worked alongside Pacific Island partners to bolster maritime security and sovereignty, counter illicit maritime activities and protect vital marine resources.
The Joseph Gerczak crew exercised partnerships with the Republic of the Marshall Islands and Fiji through bilateral maritime law enforcement agreements. In total, the Joseph Gerczak crew and their Pacific partners conducted 29 bilateral maritime law enforcement boardings and eight high-seas boardings in support of Operation Island Chief, a coordinated effort to detect and combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing in the Pacific. While in the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Joseph Gerczak crew participated in sports with local youth and students from the College of the Marshall Islands in Majuro. In American Samoa, the crew led a seamanship showcase with community leaders and National Oceanographic and Atmospheric Administration officers.
“My crew and I are very proud of this patrol,” said Lt. Andrew Loeffler, commanding officer of Coast Guard Cutter Joseph Gerczak. “The crew’s dedication to fostering these important partnerships is vital in building a more secure and prosperous Pacific. I’m extremely proud of the crew’s continued professionalism, proficiency and unrelenting courage during this patrol."
Operation Blue Pacific is an overarching multi-mission Coast Guard endeavor to promote security, safety, sovereignty and economic prosperity in Oceania. Coast Guard cutters, aircrew and personnel deploy throughout Oceania to maintain unrestricted, lawful access to the maritime domain for all nations, improve regional stability, and solidify the Coast Guard as a reliable partner for maritime safety, security and stewardship in the Pacific.
The Joseph Gerczak is a 154-foot Sentinel-class fast response cutter homeported in Honolulu. The cutter’s primary missions are maritime law enforcement, search and rescue, and national defense.
For more information Follow us on Facebook, X, and Instagram.
-USCG-
title: Coast Guard Cutter Joseph Gerczak returns home following 52-day Operation Blue Pacific patrol in Oceania

Illinois Woman Sentenced to Prison for Role in Wire Fraud Conspiracy
An Illinois woman was sentenced this week to 27 months in prison for her role in a conspiracy to fraudulently obtain tax refunds by submitting false tax returns and fictitious financial instruments to the IRS.
“Monika Skinger engaged in a wide-ranging tax fraud scheme that flooded the IRS with fictitious financial instruments, including fraudulent checks,” said Assistant Attorney General Colin M. McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. “Skinger attempted to take millions in refunds she had no right to receive. As we did in this case, the Department of Justice will continue to unmask fraudulent actors and swiftly bring them to justice.”
According to court documents and statements made in court, Monika Skinger conspired with others to submit false individual and trust tax returns that claimed millions in refunds they were not entitled to receive. To induce the IRS to accept the false refund claims, Skinger personally submitted at least 16 fictitious financial instruments — such as checks, money orders, and payment vouchers — on behalf of herself and others. She also filed at least four false individual income tax returns for herself and at least two false trust tax returns. In total, Skinger sought $4.6 million in refunds from the IRS and received more than $1.2 million in fraudulent proceeds.
Skinger pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud. In addition to the term of imprisonment, U.S. District Court Judge Amanda Brailsford for the District of Idaho ordered Skinger to serve three years of supervised release and pay $303,672.44 in restitution to the United States.
Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and U.S. Attorney Bart Davis for the District of Idaho made the announcement.
IRS Criminal Investigation is investigating the case.
Trial Attorney David F. Scollan of the National Fraud Enforcement Division’s Tax Section and Assistant U.S. Attorney Brittney Campbell for the District of Idaho are prosecuting the case.
On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Illinois Woman Sentenced to Prison for Role in Wire Fraud Conspiracy

Maurilio Lazcano-Vargas, age 40, of Mexico, who is present in the United States without authorization, pleaded guilty before U.S. Chief Judge Shelly D. Dick to sex trafficking by force, fraud, and coercion. Edyn Efrain-Arevalo, age 53, of Guatemala, and Zabdi Guzman-Diaz, age 41, of Mexico, who are also present in the United States without authorization, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit sex trafficking by force, fraud, and coercion.

According to admissions made as part of their pleas, since at least August 2024, Lazcano-Vargas operated a prostitution scheme that prostituted women, many of whom were illegal aliens in the United States, in various locations in Louisiana. He operated the prostitution venture with his co-defendants, Efrain-Arevalo and Guzman-Diaz, and would ensure that the women that he prostituted would perform commercial sex acts and provide him or others with the money that they earned from such acts.

Specifically, beginning in and after October 2025, Lazcano-Vargas placed online ads through social media mobile and computer applications for commercial sex acts featuring women in the Middle District of Louisiana. He along with others, rented apartments in the Baton Rouge, Kenner, and New Orleans areas so that women could engage in these acts.

In furtherance of the conspiracy, Lazcano-Vargas and others would take the money that the women made, tell the women the prices they were to charge and the amount of time that corresponded with the prices along with any rules for acts that were an extra charge, and communicate directly with other participants in the sex trafficking at the end of the night. Lazcano-Vargas and others also would monitor the total number of men that each women had commercial sex with and how much money was made. A single young woman would have as many as 20 “Johns” or more in one day.

U.S. Attorney Kurt Wall stated, “These defendants not only entered our country illegally, but then took advantage of these young women by trafficking them for sexual activity. These crimes check the boxes of the highest priorities of our office and this Administration.” Wall applauded the teamwork of the several agencies involved which included the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, U.S. Department of Homeland Security – Homeland Security Investigations, Social Security Administration, Office of the Inspector General, Louisiana Bureau of Investigation, and East Baton Rouge Parish Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Stephen Vick and Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Allen Ross lead the prosecution.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC .

text:
LtGen Swan, MajGen Lukeman, Pres/CEO of the Marine Corps Heritage Foundation; our other distinguished Generals, guests, speakers; and the historians, organizers, and professionals who made this necessary event possible—I’m so grateful for the opportunity to be a small part of this important occasion.
Most especially -thank you -for the gift of this anthology.
25 yrs after Sept 11th, it’d be easy to tell stories about how that day changed us-the nation and the Corps.
And, of course, it did – in so many ways.
But as I read this anthology earlier this month, something else stood out to me in a glaringly obvious way.
The Marine Corps changed Sept 11.
Not because Marines knew what was coming. No one did. As a nation, we discovered we suffered from a “failure of imagination”.
Marines altered the course of that day because when the unimagined happened, Marines fell back on something that had been engineered into them long before that morning: an ability to act amid uncertainty, to exercise initiative when orders were incomplete or nonexistent, and to adapt when the problem in front of them suddenly changed.
Those ideas resonate with all Marines. They are woven throughout our warfighting philosophy- MCDP 1.
And when you read this anthology- you’ll see that they are woven throughout it as well.
Consider the account of (then) GySgt- now retired SgtMaj and with us today- Jamie Deets.
He was a Btty Gy in 1/12 at Kaneohe Bay, Hawaii.
That AM, his mom calls from VA and tells him our nations is under attack. He watches the 2d plane strike the WTC & soon thereafter, his CO tells him to get to the barracks, wake the Marines- and stand by.
I tried to imagine ALL that he didn’t know.
He didn’t know the size or scale or objective of the attack- what the enemy’s plan was- he didn’t know whether Hawaii was next.
There was no perfect intelligence picture – and none was coming.
But he did know one important thing - his Marines still needed leadership.
And soon those Marines were drawing weapons and establishing a perimeter to protect the base.
This is exactly the picture our warfighting philosophy paints: friction, uncertainty, disorder— a space and place in time where reality refuses to behave as expected -and the imperative to act anyway.
5000 miles away, Tom Armas faced an entirely different problem.
Tom – now a Brig Gen - was a Marine Reserve officer and a Secret Service agent working in NYC.
There was no Marine unit ordered to Ground Zero -but there were Marines there.
The anthology describes Marines being drawn – even compelled to ground zero by duty and love for their fellow Americans rather than orders – You’ll see in the anthology -one Marine -headed the “wrong way” said “ As a Marine, I knew I could not go backwards- we always go forward.”
Armas began helping people escape the North Tower and made a judgment: “there must be others inside who need help”. So, he and another agent “peaked in” - as high as the 44th floor- serving others.
No HHQ could have understood his immediate situation as well as he did.
No staff could have written an order quickly enough. No PLA algorithm could predict his actions.
Yet – when it mattered – Tom saw what had to be done - And he just did it. Disciplined initiative. Decentralized action. That’s why Marines do not simply follow instructions but understand purpose—and act in accordance with it.
233 miles south of the North Tower - at the Pentagon, CMC, Gen Jones confronted still another problem.
Flight 77 had struck the Pentagon and destroyed the Navy Command Center. The normal mechanisms of C2 had been disrupted. The problem was changing.
He and ACMC decided to relocate HQMC to a Continuity of Operations location – (COOP Site) -the old Navy Annex. CMC contacted the CNO & offered the Marine Corps’ functioning facilities to the Navy.
In just a few hours, Navy and Marine Corps C2 capability had been reestablished.
He didn’t try to restore the morning’s plan - He recognized that the situation had changed—and adapted to the new one.
Friction and uncertainty. Initiative. Adaptation.
Those qualities were not “dusted off” on Sept 11th. They were already manifest in generations of Marines beforehand – present and exercised daily – before the chaos arrived.
On Sept 11th, Marines simply carried those qualities into the situation that no one had imagined.
That matters to us today b/c we don’t know the precise character of tomorrow’s uncertainty.
We don’t know exactly what the next battlefield will look like, what technology will dominate it, what communications will survive first contact or prove most resilient- or what carefully constructed plan will suddenly become irrelevant.
But we do know what kind of Marines we want to send into that uncertainty.
Marines comfortable – even compelled to acting when the picture is incomplete. Marines who understand intent well enough to exercise disciplined initiative.
Marines capable of recognizing when the problem has changed—and adapting faster/turning tighter than our enemy.
That is why this anthology matters so much to us – 25 years later - it documents more than just the story of what happened to the Corps on Sept 11th. It preserves the legacy and action-generating spirit of what Marines did on Sept 11th - & how that spirit changed the course of the day -in hundreds of ways.
Jamie Deets didn’t know what was happening. He led anyway.
Tom Armas saw what needed to be done – and did it.
CMC Jones recognized that the problem had changed – then adapted.
It is true that Sept 11th changed our nation & Corps. But this anthology reminds us that, on Sept11th, Marines changed Sept 11 too. This might be one of the most important lessons we can pass on to Marines who’ll face the next day none of us could’ve ever “imagined”.
-Semper Fidelis-

LAKEWOOD – Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (CO-07) today announced her legislation to uncover how Trump’s federal workforce cuts have impacted her constituents’ ability to resolve their federal casework issues. This effort comes after it was brought to Pettersen’s attention that there are just three federal case managers at the Department of Education processing all cases, and just five total case managers at the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), causing extraordinary delays for her constituents.

Pettersen’s Constituent Services Impacts of Federal Workforce Firings Act requires a comprehensive review of Trump’s federal workforce reduction efforts and their impact on agencies’ constituent services – including but not limited to delayed benefits at the Social Security Administration (SSA), the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and impediments to disaster relief coordination within the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

“One of the most important roles of our congressional office is helping our constituents navigate issues with federal agencies and ensure they get the help and answers they need. But we are seeing firsthand the devastating consequences of Trump and Elon Musk’s mass firings and our constituents are the ones who are paying the price - facing exponentially longer wait times or not being able to get any answers at all," said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen. “In some cases, this can be the difference between families having access to lifesaving care, seniors being able to pay their bills and keep a roof over their head, or students being able to pursue a higher education. Trump and Elon Musk took a hatchet to the critical services we depend on and the American people deserve to know the real costs to our country and a clear roadmap to recover from their disastrous policies.”

Specifically, Pettersen’s legislation would require a comprehensive study of the scope of the federal workforce reduction, including understanding impacted constituent services at regional field offices, altered response times, and delayed services and benefits, as well as how it has caused impediments to federal, state, and local disaster relief coordination.

After Donald Trump’s inauguration, in January 2025, he selected trillionaire technology CEO Elon Musk to lead the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), an unrestrained council engineered to aggressively shrink the federal government. Operating without Congressional authorization, DOGE moved to impose sweeping federal agency workforce reductions, implementing aggressive measures to dismantle the federal workforce. Widespread federal layoffs disproportionately affected probationary employees at federal agencies including the SSA, the IRS and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), among others.

Last year, Rep. Pettersen joined 50+ House Democrats in letters to the IRS and SSA, and co-led the Securing Assurance for Federal Employees (SAFE) Act to block the Trump Administration from carrying out mass federal layoffs during a government shutdown. She is a member of the House Financial Services Committee where she has been a leading voice on government effectiveness and supporting federal workers, increasing affordability, addressing the housing crisis, and expanding access to affordable and quality healthcare.

The bill is endorsed by the American Federation of Government Employees, the National Federation of Federal Employees, the National Treasury Employees Union, and the International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers.

“Federal workers deliver essential services directly to Americans every single day. The Trump Administration has dealt a body blow to the federal workforce through indiscriminate mass firings, making it much harder for government employees to do their jobs. This legislation would instruct the GAO to study the impact of federal firings on service delivery, shedding light on the harm they have caused to taxpayers and the people who rely on government programs,” said AFGE National President Everett Kelley

"The National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE-IAM) is proud to support the Constituent Services Impacts of Federal Workforce Firings Act. From day one of President Trump’s second term, this administration has led a reckless campaign to gut the federal workforce, resulting in severe reductions in the services that federal agencies provide to the American people. These are critical services that we all rely on every single day. This legislation will ensure Congress, as well as Americans across the nation, understand the true scope of the damage President Trump and his supporters have done to public services throughout the country,” said NFFE National President Randy Erwin

"NTEU is proud to endorse The Constituent Services Impacts of Federal Workforce Firings Act and applauds Representative Pettersen for her leadership on this important issue. The recent misguided efforts to gut the federal workforce are harmful to the American people and the services they rely on. If passed into law, this bill would provide valuable insight and transparency into the real and tangible damage that occurs when federal agencies and programs are underfunded and inadequately staffed. I urge the House of Representatives to swiftly pass this commonsense legislation,” said NTEU National President Doreen Greenwald

"The current Administration’s federal workforce cuts through Reductions in Force (RIFs) have lacked justification and an established process and resulted in the loss of tens of thousands of highly qualified, skilled, and dedicated federal employees. Congress needs a comprehensive assessment, and the American public deserves a full accounting of how this Administration’s RIF actions have impacted the delivery of public services, government efficiency, and accountable agency operations. We thank Congresswoman Pettersen for introducing the Constituent Services Impacts of Federal Workforce Firings Act, and we urge Members of Congress from both sides of the aisle to cosponsor this important measure,” said IFPTE International President Matt Biggs

WASHINGTON – To commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks, United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin joined President Donald J. Trump at the Pentagon, then delivered remarks at the DHS headquarters in Washington, D.C.
In the morning, Secretary Mullin joined President Trump, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, and others in a memorial ceremony at the Pentagon in Arlington County, Virginia.
Later in the morning, Secretary Mullin returned to St. Elizabeths, the DHS headquarters in Washington, D.C., to deliver remarks at the dedication of Resilience Plaza. The Plaza features several artifacts from September 11th, including an upright trident beam from the World Trade Center in New York City and several pieces of limestone from the Pentagon. Secretary Mullin was joined by Deputy Secretary Troy Edgar, Under Secretary for Management Brian J. Cavanaugh, and other DHS personnel.
The presenting of the colors in front of the World Trade Center trident beam at Resilience Plaza
Under Secretary for Management Brian J. Cavanaugh (left), Deputy Secretary Troy Edgar (center), and Secretary Mullin during the ceremony
Deputy Secretary Edgar delivers remarks
Under Secretary Cavanaugh delivers remarks
Secretary Mullin delivers remarks
The crowd in attendance, with St. Elizabeths in the background
Secretary Mullin after the ceremony
“As Secretary of Homeland Security, I serve with true patriots. 270,000 of us at the Department of Homeland Security wake up every single morning defending our homeland, every day. From the Coast Guard to Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, CISA, and Secret Service, and all the other components we have, our mission is to make sure that something like 9/11 never happens again,” said Secretary Mullin. “As a nation, we’re all Americans. Just like 25 years ago when they attacked the Pentagon, when they attacked the Twin Towers, and when all of our lives changed. Everybody’s life changed that day. We all came together. That fight isn’t done. And it never will be.”
DHS was created in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, launching on March 1, 2003 after the Homeland Security Act of 2002 was signed into law.
# # #
title: Secretary Mullin Observes 25th Anniversary of 9/11 at Pentagon, Speaks at DHS Headquarters

WASHINGTON – The United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) released the following statement commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11th terrorist attacks, which ultimately led to the founding of DHS in order to secure the homeland and protect the American people.
On that fateful Tuesday 25 years ago, 19 members of the Islamic terrorist group Al-Qaeda hijacked four commercial airliners across the United States, with the intent of crashing them into large buildings and killing thousands of Americans. American Airlines Flight 11 and United Airlines Flight 175 were crashed into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, while American Airlines Flight 77 was crashed into the Pentagon in Virginia. A fourth plane, United Airlines Flight 93, crashed in a field in Pennsylvania after the passengers fought back against the hijackers. The attacks killed 2,977 Americans and injured thousands more.
Following the attacks, the Homeland Security Act of 2002 was signed into law, ordering the creation of a new Cabinet-level agency dedicated to homeland security. As a result, DHS was created on March 1, 2003. Its mission is to defend the homeland, the American people, and our way of life.
“On this day 25 years ago, our world changed forever. 9/11 remains one of the darkest days in history. Evil came to our shores and stole the lives of nearly 3,000 Americans in a vicious attempt to bring our great nation to its knees,” said DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “But by the end of that day, even as smoke still filled the skies over New York City, Washington, D.C., and Shanksville, Pennsylvania, the American spirit endured and rose to the challenge. From the unrivaled bravery of first responders who ran into burning buildings and risked it all to save their fellow Americans, to the civilians aboard Flight 93 who fought back against their captors knowing that it would be their last acts on this earth, the best of America stood up and refused to let the worst of humanity win that day. Those Americans have all earned their place in history as some of the bravest people to have ever lived, and we should consider it an honor that we once shared a nation with them.
“When we remember 9/11, we often say ‘never forget.’ We must never forget the nearly 3,000 who lost their lives. We must never forget the potential for evil to strike again, and we must never forget how only the devotion of the good can keep all of us safe. We carry the legacy of 9/11 in our hearts, not just out of remembrance of those we lost that day, but so that we can maintain and defend a nation that they would be proud of. To forget that duty would be to forget our honored dead from that day.
“That is why, 25 years later, our mission continues. DHS was created for the specific purpose of protecting the homeland and the American people, and ensuring that something like 9/11 never happens again. It is my honor to serve as the 9th Secretary of Homeland Security, working alongside more than 260,000 of the finest that America has to offer. For more than two decades, DHS has been answering the call to keep our homeland safe. As long as there is still life in our bodies and love in our hearts, we will never forget.”
# # #
title: DHS Commemorates 25th Anniversary of 9/11

“We will continue working with our committed law enforcement partners to hold accountable those who use deception to put investors’ money at risk,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald. “As alleged, Vuk Vukovic attracted investors to his fund and lulled them into keeping their money invested by reporting high rates of return that were not real. “Vuk Vukovic allegedly used interstate commerce to carry out a deceptive scheme involving the purchase and sale of securities,” said FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. “When individuals allegedly mislead investors and defraud them, the consequences extend far beyond their immediate crimes—they threaten the economic stability and livelihoods of American citizens,” said USPIS Inspector in Charge Ketty Larco-Ward. “While investing always carries inherent risk, a breach of trust adds an unacceptable layer of deception. As alleged in the Complaint unsealed in Manhattan federal court:(1)

Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach presented the 2025 Koren Kolligian Jr. Trophy to Capt. Michael Cloninger, from the 90th Fighter Squadron, 3rd Operations Group, Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska, during a ceremony at the Pentagon, Sept. 8.
The Koren Kolligian Jr. Trophy recognizes outstanding feats of airmanship by aircrew members who by extraordinary skill, exceptional alertness, ingenuity, or proficiency, averted accidents or minimized the seriousness of the accidents in terms of injury, loss of life, aircraft damage, or property damage. This trophy memorializes 1st Lt. Koren Kolligian Jr., an Air Force pilot declared missing in the line of duty when his T-33 aircraft disappeared off the California coast on Sep. 14, 1955.
Cloninger and his flight lead discontinued the mission and maintained close proximity to the airfield to assess the situation. After rejoining, he assumed navigation and communication lead, slowed below gear speed to access the situation, lowered the gear, and his flight lead confirmed the entire right main wheel assembly was missing.
Faced with no established written procedure for this scenario, he employed crew resource management to select the “landing with gear up” checklist, precluding an asymmetric gear landing and eliminating risk of total aircraft loss and pilot injury or death. While coordinating with the tower, crash response, and operations supervisor, he flew for an hour to burn excess fuel and flew a low approach using the emergency alternate flap flight control setting. He executed a calculated on-speed shallow approach and precise centerline touchdown which prevented a post-landing fire, then immediately shut down both engines and performed a textbook emergency egress to ensure safe recovery.
His quick thinking and daring actions minimized the seriousness of the mishap, enabling the aircraft to be flown out of theater after diagnostics, an unprecedented recovery for a belly-landed F-22. His superior piloting and decision-making saved the Air Force a $156-million-dollar asset and the priceless life of an aviator.
“Wax [Capt. Michael Cloninger], today we recognize your extraordinary airmanship,” said Wilsbach. “You faced an emergency you could not see with no warning from your aircraft, while carrying a full combat load thousands of miles from home. You remained disciplined. You trusted your training, listened to your teammates, and made sound decisions. When it was time to land, you flew the aircraft all the way through the emergency. That is what we expect from American Airmen. We don’t expect them to predict every failure or control every circumstance. We expect them to be ready, know their jobs, make good decisions, trust their teammates, and adapt when the situation changes. You did all of that.”
“Without my teammates assisting with communication and walking through the checklists, I truly believe I wouldn't be standing here today,” said Cloninger. “I owe more than this award to them—this recognition is a testament to the teamwork that helped us successfully manage the emergency.”
This award is the Air Force’s most prestigious flight safety award, and the only one presented by the chief of staff.
title: 90th Fighter Squadron captain receives 2025 Koren Kolligian Jr. Trophy

Above: Gottheimer commemorates the 25th anniversary of the horrific September 11th attacks.

NEW JERSEY — Today, Friday, September 11, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) took part in the 25th anniversary of 9/11 remembrance ceremonies in Mahwah and Hackensack to honor North Jersey community members and first responders who lost their lives in the horrific attacks, commemorating those lost since, and recommitting to protecting America from extremism and terror.

Nearly 3,000 people lost their lives in the 9/11 attacks, including more than 400 firefighters, police, and other first responders. New Jersey lost nearly 750 residents, and Bergen County alone lost 147 residents. Since then, more than 9,000 first responders and others who were in and around the World Trade Center have died as a result of toxic exposure.

See Gottheimer’s full remarks here.

“Out of the worst morning in this country’s history, we decided to be loud, united, and unafraid. That’s the Jersey I know, and the America I strive for,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “A place where our memory and our pride outlast our fear. A place where every one of the neighbors we lost that day will never, ever be forgotten. We will never forget.”

Gottheimer was joined by Mayor Caseen Gaines, Deputy Mayor Agatha Toomey, Councilman Roberto Diaz, Councilwoman Sonya Clark-Collins, Councilman Philip Carroll, City Manager Thomas Freeman, Fire Chief Keith Rosazza, Police Chief Michael Antist.

Over the past year, Gottheimer served as co-chair of the bipartisan House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence review of the 9/11 Commission Report. Last week, the committee released its bipartisan 9/11 Review Task Force Report, that lays out twenty bipartisan recommendations for the Intelligence Community to protect against the new and emerging threats — including faster information sharing between agencies, adopting AI to stay ahead of our enemies, and deeper partnerships with our state, local, and private-sector partners to fight terror.

Gottheimer also introduced legislation with Rep. Stefanik to ensure that 9/11 education is taught in every classroom in America; today, just 25 states have requirements on the books. Of those who are between the ages of 18 and 24, none of whom were alive on 9/11, 60% first learned about 9/11 in class or through school assignments.

Gottheimer also recently clawed back $5 million to my district for local and state police for counterterrorism equipment to prevent tragedy and be ready in case one does happen.

And this week, he also introduced a resolution with the entire Jersey House Congressional delegation to honor the service and sacrifice of Jersey first responders on 9/11.

Last year, Gottheimer helped lead the reintroduction of the bipartisan American Victims of Terror Compensation Act, which provides funding for the United States Victims of State-Sponsored Terrorism Fund, or USVSST Fund. This legislation will help ensure the USVSST consistently provides compensation to more than 18,000 American victims of State Sponsors of Terrorism, including the families of the more than 3,000 victims of September 11th.

Gottheimer helped fight for and pass legislation like the bipartisan Never Forget the Heroes Act, to fully fund the 9/11 Victims Compensation Fund to provide long-overdue support to cover 9/11 survivors, first responders, and their families for injuries, medical expenses, and other benefits.

Gottheimer also helped pass the Saracini Enhanced Aviation Act, which requires the installation of secondary cockpit barriers on all commercial passenger aircraft to prevent terrorist attacks similar to 9/11.

Gottheimer is continuing to fight to pass the bipartisan FIRE Cancer Act to provide federal investments so that all firefighters, especially those exposed on and after 9/11, can get access to preventative tests, including multi-cancer early detection tests.

Press Release
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Tribal leaders, school administrators, language teachers and students from across Indian Country gathered at the U.S. Department of the Interior this week for the Forum on Native Languages and Education. This full-day convening on Native language revitalization was organized by the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs and the National Fund for Excellence in American Indian Education, the congressionally chartered foundation for the Bureau of Indian Education.
The forum brought together presenters from tribal nations, BIE-funded schools, tribal colleges and Native language organizations to share what is working in their communities. Sessions covered language and technology, tribal language programming, Office of Indian Economic Development Living Languages Grant Program grantees and grantees of the Native Language Program operated by the BIE in partnership with the National Fund.
“Native languages are a foundation of Native identity and communities. President Trump recognized the importance of Native language when he became the first president to meet with and honor Code Talkers in the Oval Office in 2017, noting that the preservation of Native languages supported victory in WWII. Today, this work supports the educational and personal success for Natives across the country,” said Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs Billy Kirkland. “This forum demonstrated that the knowledge and expertise to sustain and revitalize Native languages already exists within our communities. The Trump administration is supporting and working to ensure tribes have resources and flexibility to lead language revitalization efforts in their own communities.”
Through Native Language federal funding, more than $12.5 million has been made available to 17 BIE-funded schools to expand Native language programs, instruction and immersion programming. These schools also receive access to specialists in language curriculum development, instructional materials design, program evaluation and early childhood immersion methods.
"What these schools are showing us is that language is not separate from student success. It runs through it," said Heath Clayton, Lead Executive Officer of the National Fund for Excellence in American Indian Education. "Our job is to get resources into the hands of the people doing this work every day, and then get out of their way."
Several schools presented early results at the Forum. Turtle Mountain Community High School in Belcourt, North Dakota, reported that Anishinaabemowin, the Ojibwe language, is now taught across five class periods daily, with an after-school language club open to any student.
"We are seeing students show up differently when their language is part of their school day," said Cindy Keplin, Assistant Principal at Turtle Mountain Community High School. "That is what this funding made possible."
In a survey of language program participants, 67% showed improved daily attendance, with some gains as high as 8.6% points, and 58% improved their grade point average, with gains ranging from 0.04 to 0.62 points. Turtle Mountain also reported that 511 language-eligible students took part in Anishinaabemowin activities during the January through March 2026 quarter.
Santa Fe Indian School described a program serving students from more than 23 Native language communities across six languages, built around Pueblo language teachers and a shared Native Language Philosophy developed with participants from seven Pueblos.
The Forum also previewed the National Native Language Summit, which the National Fund and the National Indian Education Association will convene October 6 in Buffalo, New York, bringing together educators, students, researchers and language advocates from across Indian Country.
The Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs advises the Secretary of the Interior on Indian Affairs policy issues; communicates policy to and oversees the programs of the Bureau of Indian Affairs, the Bureau of Indian Education, and the Bureau of Trust Funds Administration; provides leadership in consultations with tribes; and serves as the DOI official for intra- and inter-departmental coordination and liaison within the Executive Branch on matters concerning American Indians and Alaska Natives and the federally recognized Tribes in the United States.
The Bureau of Indian Affairs directly administers and funds tribally operated infrastructure, law enforcement and justice, social services, tribal governance and trust land and natural and energy resources management programs for the Nation’s federally recognized American Indian and Alaska Native Tribes through four offices: Indian Services, Justice Services, Trust Services and Field Operations. The BIA Office of Indian Services Division of Human Services administers the bureau’s Indian Child Welfare Act program.
The National Fund for Excellence in American Indian Education (The National Fund) is the Congressionally chartered foundation for the Bureau of Indian Education and its 185+ BIE-funded schools. As a 501(c)(3) organization, The National Fund garners resources and partnerships that support community-led efforts to create educational environments where Native students thrive, grounded in their language, culture, and holistic well-being. Learn more at www.nfeaie.org or contact info@nfeaie.org.
####
title: Department of the Interior hosts Forum on Native Languages and Education

CHICAGO — A Chicago trader has been sentenced to more than 16 years in federal prison for engaging in unauthorized speculative bond trading that cost his employer and others more than $30 million in losses and also caused his employer to become insolvent, which in turn led to more than 200 people losing their jobs.

KEITH WAKEFIELD worked as the head of fixed income trading for IFS Securities, Inc., a broker-dealer in Chicago. In 2019, Wakefield knowingly and fraudulently engaged in unauthorized speculative trading in U.S. Treasury bonds using his employer’s trading accounts, exposing his trading to approximately $250 million in losses and actually causing more than $30 million in losses to the employer and its counterparties. Wakefield attempted to conceal the unauthorized trades and losses by entering fake off-setting trades into a clearing broker’s order system, creating the false impression that he had profitably traded through a different clearing broker.

In addition to the fraudulent trading scheme, Wakefield from 2017 to 2019 embezzled hundreds of thousands of dollars from IFS Securities by falsifying the company’s books and records to create fake commissions that Wakefield knew were not actually owed to him.

A jury in U.S. District Court in Chicago in 2024 convicted Wakefield, 52, of Chicago, of securities fraud and wire fraud. On Wednesday, U.S. District Judge Steven C. Seeger sentenced Wakefield to 16 years and eight months in federal prison.

The sentence was announced by Andrew S. Boutros, United States Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, and Ryan Whalen, Special Agent-in-Charge of the Chicago Field Office of the FBI. The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission provided valuable assistance.

“This crime was driven by pure greed,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Jared Hasten argued in the government’s sentencing memorandum. “Defendant’s fraud had a ripple effect causing multiple financial institutions to lose money and causing IFS to go out of business.”
title: Chicago Trader Sentenced to More Than 16 Years in Federal Prison for Engaging in Unauthorized Trading That Caused $30 Million in Losses

SALEM, OR — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) Ranking Member of the House Agriculture Subcommittee on Forestry and Horticulture, celebrated the U.S. Forest Service’s decision to extend the public comment period on the Trump Administration’s proposal to rescind the Roadless Rule.

The Forest Service announced that it will extend the comment deadline by 15 days, from September 21 to October 6, giving Americans additional time to weigh in on a proposal that would eliminate longstanding protections for 44 million acres of National Forest System lands.

The extension comes just days after Rep. Salinas led a bipartisan coalition of 164 Members of Congress in calling on the U.S. Department of Agriculture and U.S. Forest Service to provide the public with more time to comment on the proposed rollback. In their September 3 letter, Salinas and her colleagues urged the Forest Service to extend the comment period from 30 days to 120 days, hold in-person public meetings, and conduct full Tribal consultation to allow Americans to have their voices heard.

“When the Roadless Rule was first adopted 25 years ago, more than 1.6 million comments were submitted in favor of the rule. That’s more than any other rule in our nation’s history at the time it was adopted,” said Rep. Salinas. “Oregonians deserve a real opportunity to make their voices heard before the Trump Administration makes a decision that could fundamentally change 44 million acres of our public lands. I’m glad the agency listened to our demands to extend the comment period, and I urge them to listen to every American who demands that we protect our wilderness.

“While 15 additional days still falls well short of the 120-day comment period we requested, this extension gives Oregonians and communities across the country more time to speak up for our forests, clean drinking water, wildlife habitat, and outdoor recreation economy. I will continue pushing the Administration to provide the robust and transparent public process that a decision of this magnitude demands.”

The Roadless Rule has protected undeveloped areas of the National Forest System from most road construction and logging for more than 25 years. The original rule was developed following an extensive public process that included more than 600 public meetings and approximately 1.6 million public comments.

By contrast, the Trump Administration initially provided only 30 days for the public to comment on its proposed rescission of the Roadless Rule and associated Draft Environmental Impact Statement. Rep. Salinas and her colleagues argued that such a short window was inadequate given the scope of the proposal and the significant consequences it could have for communities, drinking water, wildlife habitat, outdoor recreation, and forest management across the country.

The new deadline for public comments is October 6, 2026.
title: Rep. Salinas Secures Extension of Public Comment Period on Trump Administration’s Roadless Rule Repeal

PITTSBURGH, Pa. - A resident of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, has been sentenced in federal court to 37 months of imprisonment on his conviction of possessing firearms and ammunition as a convicted felon, United States Attorney Troy Rivetti announced today.

United States District Judge Mark R. Hornak imposed the sentence on Aquay Mitchell, 26, on September 10, 2026.

According to information presented to the Court, on September 24, 2024, Pittsburgh Bureau of Police detectives observed and attempted to stop Mitchell, suspecting that he possessed a firearm. Mitchell fled and was ultimately located hiding in a stairwell, with officers also finding a firearm, keys, and a cell phone along Mitchell’s flight path. The firearm was a loaded semi-automatic pistol with an obliterated serial number that had been reported stolen, and the cellular telephone and keys belonged to Mitchell, who has multiple felony convictions. Federal law prohibits possession of a firearm or ammunition by a convicted felon. Mitchell was indicted in connection with the incident and a warrant issued for his arrest.

On February 4, 2026, Pittsburgh Bureau of Police officers were conducting a proactive patrol of Pittsburgh’s Knoxville neighborhood when they observed Mitchell at a convenience store and took Mitchell into custody on the federal arrest warrant. In a search incident to arrest, officers recovered from Mitchell’s person a loaded semi-automatic pistol that also had been reported stolen, a knotted plastic baggie containing 11 grams of crack cocaine, a digital scale, and a cellular telephone.

Assistant United States Attorney Brendan T. Conway prosecuted this case on behalf of the government.

United States Attorney Rivetti commended the Pittsburgh Bureau of Police and Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives for the investigation leading to the successful prosecution of Mitchell.
title: Pittsburgh Felon Sentenced to More Than Three Years in Prison for Unlawful Possession of Firearms

The FVEY A4 Collaboration Forum stood at the center of allied strategic partnership July 28–31, 2026, as logisticians from five partner nations converged at Scott Air Force Base, Illinois, to discuss the air forces’ most critical operational challenges and solutions. This yearly forum brought together senior leaders and logistics experts from the United States Air Force, Royal Air Force, Royal Australian Air Force, Royal New Zealand Air Force and Royal Canadian Air Force in an effort to synchronize global logistics capabilities.
While initially established as an intelligence-sharing alliance, contemporary geopolitical tensions and global sustainment challenges have driven FVEY air forces to expand their focus to maintenance and interoperability, munitions loading, base response and recovery, additive manufacturing, force protection and other enterprise challenges. Today, the alliance has transformed to include active collaboration on military logistics, formalized through initiatives like the annual FVEY A4 Collaboration Forum, established in 2022. The joint charter, updated in late 2024, provides a platform to synchronize shared partner basing, infrastructure and interoperable sustainment logistics across the globe.
As the designated “heartbeat” of global military movement, Scott Air Force Base is the premier venue for leaders to discuss Air Force logistics. The base serves as the joint headquarters for the U.S. Transportation Command, which orchestrates global logistics solutions across all branches of the U.S. military, as well as the Air Mobility Command, which directly oversees the U.S. Air Force’s massive airlift, aeromedical evacuation and aerial refueling operations.
This year’s theme, “Time on Target,” takes a classic military concept and directly applies it to how we keep our forces agile and effective. Just like coordinating different weapon systems to strike a target at the exact same moment, the FVEY A4 Collaboration Forum is focused on synchronizing our applied logistics capabilities. It comes down to ensuring that critical gear, fuel and munitions from five different nations arrive at the tactical edge at the precise moment they’re needed. By aligning our logistics networks and sharing real-time data, we’re ensuring our forces can keep up a relentless operational tempo without missing a beat.
“From a logistics standpoint, we understand that the tyranny of distance is always a challenge. As partners, we come from various parts of the globe; our ability to exercise together ensures that we’ll have common knowledge, meaning that if we ever need to come together in order to solve challenges in a conflict, we’re going to be that much stronger,” said Lt. Gen. Kenyon K. Bell, U.S. Air Force Deputy Chief of Staff for Logistics, Engineering and Force Protection.
To project allied power, unified collaboration is non-negotiable. A pivotal discussion at the forum focused on the critical distinction between being interoperable and being interchangeable. Interoperable forces can load weapons, move munitions and fly together. However, interchangeable forces can sustain one another, meaning a U.S. aircraft can touch down at an allied base and utilize the host nation’s fuel, parts and munitions for a rapid turnaround, eliminating the need for specialized equipment.
“Working with our partners, we can combine our resources to mitigate some of those vulnerabilities that we otherwise might have. In doing this, we’re improving the resilience of our logistics capabilities which ultimately underpins deterrence and builds stability in the region,” said Air Commodore Natasia Pulford, Royal Australian Air Force Director General Airbase and Logistics Capability.
Attendees engaged in targeted briefings spanning national updates, current conflict intelligence and working group milestones. A key highlight included site visits to USTRANSCOM and the 618th Air Operations Center—the Tanker Airlift Control Center. As the U.S. Air Force’s premier air operations hub, the 618 AOC provides 24/7 command and control support for a massive global fleet of nearly 1,100 mobility assets
Now in its fifth year, the FVEY A4 Collaboration Forum continues to mature as a vital platform for addressing shared operational vulnerabilities and opportunities. Whether through tactical field training where allied Airmen train like they fight, or executive forums aligning logistics policies and resources, the mission remains unified: we are stronger together, and we must integrate our capabilities to secure a decisive, collective strategic advantage.
“The collaboration at this forum and the mindset that comes with it is really important,” said Air Commodore Craig Watson, Royal Air Force Head of Engineering and Logistics, HQ Air Command. “It helps us understand common challenges, share the learning in response to those challenges, and identify opportunities to work together. That’s a real advantage across allies.”
title: FVEY A4 Collaboration Forum synchronizes global allied logistics at Scott AFB
