Dompé U.S. Agrees to Pay $32M to Resolve False Claims Act Liability Relating to Self-Disclosure of Patient Kickbacks
Dompé U.S. Inc. (Dompé), based in California, has agreed to pay $32 million to resolve allegations that, between 2018 and 2021, it paid Medicare beneficiary co-pays through two patient assistance foundations to induce the purchase of its drug, Oxervate, in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute and the False Claims Act.
“This settlement demonstrates the United States’ commitment to enforcing the Anti-Kickback Statute and ensuring that pharmaceutical manufacturers do not use unlawful inducements,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The Department encourages companies that uncover improper kickbacks to self-disclose such conduct.”
“Kickbacks to beneficiaries undermine the purpose of the Medicare co-pay system and drive up the cost of drugs,” said U.S. Attorney Leah B. Foley for the District of Massachusetts. “My Office has recovered over $1.4 billion for taxpayers through settlements and enforcement actions concerning drug company kickbacks to purported charities, and we will continue to pursue these matters to ensure that all drug companies play by the rules and to protect federal taxpayer funded healthcare programs.”
“Pharmaceutical manufacturers that attempt to disguise kickbacks as charitable patient assistance are engaging in blatant misconduct which corrupts medical decision‑making and drains federal health care programs,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “Dompé’s actions undermined critical safeguards Congress put in place to protect Medicare, driving up costs for taxpayers while exploiting patients. HHS-OIG does not tolerate such conduct and will continue to work tirelessly for justice and accountability.”
When a Medicare beneficiary obtains a prescription drug covered by Medicare, the beneficiary may be required to make a partial payment, which may take the form of a co-payment, co-insurance, or deductible (collectively “co-pays”). Congress included co-pay requirements in these programs, in part, to encourage market forces to serve as a check on health care costs, including the prices that pharmaceutical manufacturers can demand for their drugs.
Under the Anti-Kickback Statute, a pharmaceutical manufacturer is prohibited from offering or paying, directly or indirectly, any remuneration – which includes money or any other thing of value – to induce Medicare patients to purchase the company’s drugs. This prohibition extends to the payment of patients’ co-pay obligations.
As part of the settlement, Dompé admitted that, around the time of Oxervate’s 2018 launch in the United States, Dompé U.S. employees expressed reservations about launching the drug before making a payment to a patient assistance foundation that paid the co-pays for Oxervate. After conversations with Dompé employees, two foundations opened funds that, among other things, paid co-pays for Oxervate, and Dompé made contributions to those foundations. Dompé also solicited patient assistance foundation data directly from the foundations, and from the specialty pharmacy that provided hub services to Dompé U.S. patients. This data was provided, directly or indirectly, to certain individuals involved in the patient assistance foundation budgeting process.
Dompé is the U.S. subsidiary of Dompé farmaceutici S.p.A., a pharmaceutical company incorporated in Italy. Dompé farmaceutici self-disclosed this conduct to the United States. Following the disclosure, both Dompé farmaceutici and Dompé U.S. cooperated with the government in this matter and received credit under the Department’s guidelines for taking self-disclosure, cooperation, and remediation into account in False Claims Act cases.
The resolution obtained in this matter was the result of a coordinated effort between the Justice Department’s Civil Division, Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts, and the Department of Health and Human Services’ Office of Inspector General.
The investigation and resolution of this matter illustrates the government’s emphasis on combating healthcare fraud. One of the most powerful tools in this effort is the False Claims Act. Tips and complaints from all sources about potential fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement, can be reported to the Department of Health and Human Services at 800-HHS-TIPS (800-447-8477).
This year the Administration launched the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division to enhance the Administration’s war on fraud, waste, and abuse in federal programs. When unscrupulous actors exploit these programs for their own financial gain, they defraud the government, harm the people these programs are designed to aid and protect, and undermine American businesses that play by the rules. The Civil Division’s FCA enforcement plays a critical role in combatting such fraudulent schemes, recovering billions of dollars for the American taxpayers, and holding wrongdoers accountable. FCA matters will continue to be on the forefront of the battle against fraud, and the Civil Division’s FCA work will support and advance the mission of the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud and the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
The matter was handled by Senior Trial Counsel Sarah Arni of the Civil Division and Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lindsey Ross and Brian LaMacchia for the District of Massachusetts.
The claims resolved by the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.
title: Dompé U.S. Agrees to Pay $32M to Resolve False Claims Act Liability Relating to Self-Disclosure of Patient Kickbacks

Beyond Labor Day, Coast Guard East District targets illegal charters as Operation Safe Voyage enforcement push continues year-round
Editor's Note: Click images to download high-resolution version
For B-Roll video of Operation Safe Voyage in Washington D.C. click here
PORTSMOUTH, Va. — Following an intensive enforcement surge across mid-Atlantic waterways over the Labor Day weekend, U.S. Coast Guard East District law enforcement crews conducted 114 safety boardings, terminated seven voyages including two active illegal passenger-for-hire operations.
As part of Operation Safe Voyage, mobilizing across the Chesapeake Bay, Hampton Roads, and coastal North Carolina, boarding teams integrated dozens of underway patrol hours with dockside outreach and joint-agency enforcement. Operations spanned from the National Capital Region, where crews completed 90 boardings and handed out roughly 150 educational safety flyers, to North Carolina waters in which boat crews logged 22 active patrol hours. In Virginia, boardings across bustling coastal hubs confirmed full compliance among vetted recreational and legitimate bareboat vessels, demonstrating how targeted boardings, shared intelligence, and interagency ride-alongs work in tandem to distinguish lawful operators from high-risk ventures.
While Labor Day traditionally marks the end of the recreational boating season in our waters, Coast Guard officials emphasize that passenger-for-hire activity remains vibrant throughout the fall and winter across the East District. Coast Guard crews will maintain active monitoring, boarding patrols, and intelligence-led investigations year-round to ensure commercial operators comply with federal safety regulations.
Since 2021, the Coast Guard has initiated more than 414 enforcement actions nationwide, proposing nearly $10.6 million in initial civil penalties against unlawful operators.
"Holiday surges allow our teams to focus boarding resources during peak boating traffic, but our obligation to protecting passengers doesn't expire when summer ends," said Rear Adm. Zeita Merchant, commander of the Coast Guard East District. "In waterways around Hampton Roads, the Outer Banks, and coastal Carolina, boating runs well into autumn and beyond. If an operator is charging passengers without proper credentials and inspections, our crews will find them and terminate their operations,” she said.
It is important for prospective passengers to understand the practical and financial reality of what happens when an illegal trip is terminated. When Coast Guard boarding officers discover an uninspected vessel carrying paying passengers or an uncredentialed operator, the voyage is immediately halted. Passengers are escorted back to the nearest public boat ramp or marina under Coast Guard watch, regardless of how much time or money was invested in the trip. Illegal operators rarely provide refunds, and third-party booking apps frequently dispute chargebacks once a trip has technically departed the slip. Passengers regularly lose hundreds or thousands of dollars for excursions that in some cases lasted less than an hour.
A significant factor driving unlawful charters is the rapid growth of peer-to-peer boat rental applications and social media classifieds. While these platforms have made booking private boat excursions as effortless as ordering a rideshare, they also present an illusion of safety that can mislead even the most cautious consumer.
"Online booking apps, polished social media profiles, and positive customer reviews do not equal legal and safe," said Merchant. "Many digital platforms take a transaction fee while disclaiming all maritime safety responsibility in the fine print. Just because a boat appears on an app does not mean the captain is licensed or the vessel has undergone mandatory safety inspections," she said.
The Coast Guard’s ongoing enforcement campaign also safeguards local maritime economies. Compliant passenger-for-hire businesses invest substantial capital annually to maintain Coast Guard Certificates of Inspection and safety equipment, carry commercial maritime insurance, subject their vessels to regular mechanical checks, and enroll crews in mandatory random drug and alcohol testing pools. Unlawful operators bypass these required investments, allowing them to undercut legitimate businesses while subjecting passengers and uncredentialed crews to unregulated and unsafe environments.
Coast Guard East District urges anyone planning a paid excursion on the water to ask three straightforward questions before handing over payment or stepping onto a dock.
- "Can I see your Merchant Mariner Credential?" Licensed captains are legally required to carry their physical credential. Ask to see it. If they refuse or cannot produce it, do not board.
- "Does this vessel carry a Certificate of Inspection?" Any commercial charter carrying more than six passengers for hire must display a Coast Guard Certificate of Inspection (COI) detailing safe passenger capacity and required safety gear.
- "Do I have absolute freedom to choose my own captain?" If renting a boat under a bareboat charter, the owner cannot require or steer you to a designated crew member. If they dictate the captain, the voyage must adhere to strict, inspected passenger-for-hire regulations.
If an operator evades safety questions or refuses to present proof of credentialing, passengers should walk away and report the incident to Coast Guard authorities.
Anyone with information concerning suspected illegal charter activity is encouraged to contact their local Coast Guard Sector Command Center or submit an anonymous report to the Coast Guard Investigative Service (CGIS) via the CGIS Tips mobile application or the National Response Center hotline at 1-877-24WATCH (1-877-249-2824).
For further updates on regional maritime safety and ongoing operations, follow Coast Guard East District on official social media channels.
-USCG-
title: Beyond Labor Day, Coast Guard East District targets illegal charters as Operation Safe Voyage enforcement push continues year-round

COLUMBIA, S.C. — Ricardo Gonzalez Bahena, 43, an illegal alien residing in Graniteville, has been sentenced to two years in federal prison for identity theft and passport fraud. Gonzalez Bahena, a Mexican national, will be deported after serving his sentence. Evidence obtained in the investigation revealed that Gonzalez Bahena was working at the Savannah River Nuclear Site under a false identity. During his employment, he attempted to obtain an increased security clearance, but investigators discovered inconsistencies during the background investigation. Thereafter, they uncovered his scheme. On two separate occasions, he also attempted to apply for a U.S. passport in Augusta, Georgia using the same false identity. The stolen identity belonged to a vulnerable adult and American citizen in Puerto Rico who has never left Puerto Rico. United States District Judge Sherri A. Lydon sentenced Gozalez Bahena to 24 months’ imprisonment, to be followed by a three-year term of court-ordered supervision. There is no parole in the federal system. Bahena was also ordered to pay $35,695 in restitution to the victim. This case was investigated by the Department of Energy and the U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service (DSS). Assistant U.S. Attorney Scott Matthews is prosecuting the case.

MONTGOMERY, Ala. — An Auburn, Alabama man has pleaded guilty to federal charges stemming from a scheme to fraudulently obtain federal COVID relief funds and to unlawfully employ aliens who were not authorized to work in the United States.

On September 9, 2026, Cesar Campos-Reyes, 52, pleaded guilty to an Information charging him with wire fraud, money laundering, and unlawful employment of aliens.

United States Attorney Thomas Govan, Special Agent in Charge Christopher R. Flowers with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Mobile Division, and Acting Special Agent in Charge Ellen Johnson for Homeland Security Investigations in Georgia and Alabama made the announcement.

“Federal COVID relief funds were intended to help legitimate businesses and their employees, not to be diverted for personal gain or used to support an unlawful workforce,” said U.S. Attorney Govan. “This defendant defrauded programs designed to assist American businesses, misused taxpayer-funded assistance, and knowingly employed individuals who were not authorized to work in the United States. We will continue to hold accountable those who abuse federal programs and violate federal law.”

“Campos Reyes’s actions diverted critical pandemic relief funds away from the small businesses they were meant to support,” said FBI Special Agent in Charge Flowers. “This guilty plea underscores the FBI’s commitment to protecting taxpayer resources, safeguarding victims, and rebuilding public trust by holding accountable those who exploit federal programs and violate the law.”

“Fraudulently obtaining pandemic relief funds and knowingly employing unauthorized workers undermines both the integrity of federal programs and the rule of law,” said HSI Acting Special Agent in Charge Johnson. “HSI will continue to work with our federal, state, and local partners to investigate individuals who exploit taxpayer-funded programs and violate our nation’s employment laws for personal gain.”

According to court documents and admissions made as part of his guilty plea, in May 2020, Campos-Reyes fraudulently applied for and received approximately $866,500 in funds through the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program. The PPP and EIDL programs were established under the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act to provide financial assistance to eligible small businesses affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Campos‑Reyes admitted that he did not use the relief funds for their intended purposes. Instead, in June 2020, he used $262,145.20 to purchase real property located in Opelika, Alabama.

Campos‑Reyes further admitted that, up to July 15, 2025, he knowingly hired and employed unauthorized aliens at multiple restaurants he owned or operated, fully aware that they were not permitted to work in the United States.

A sentencing hearing for Campos-Reyes will be scheduled in the coming months. At that hearing, he faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in federal prison for wire fraud, up to 10 years for money laundering, and up to six months in prison for unlawful employment of aliens. Campos-Reyes also faces substantial fines and the forfeiture of proceeds seized during the investigation. A federal district judge will determine Campos-Reyes’s sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. There is no parole in the federal system.

The investigation and resulting charges in this case are the culmination of a coordinated investigation led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), and the Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA). Additional assistance was provided by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Alabama Department of Corrections, Auburn Police Department, Opelika Police Department, Prattville Police Department, Wetumpka Police Department, the Elmore County Sheriff’s Office, the Lee County Sheriff’s Office, and the United States Marshals Service.

This operation received significant assistance from the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children.

The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Mobile comprises agents and officers from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Drug Enforcement Administration, Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and other federal and local agencies. The prosecution is being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Middle District of Alabama.
title: Auburn Man Pleads Guilty to Wire Fraud, Money Laundering, and Unlawful Employment of Aliens

EPA Proposes to Approve Wisconsin's Coal Combustion Residuals Permit Program
WASHINGTON — U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) today proposed the approval of the state of Wisconsin’s coal combustion residuals (CCR) permit program application. If finalized, the action would shift authority for permitting CCR disposal in landfills from the federal government to the state. This proposal advances EPA’s broader effort to Unleash American Energy Dominance and strengthens cooperative federalism while maintaining strong human health and environmental protections.
“Today’s proposed approval represents a significant step in the Trump EPA’s efforts to provide clarity and certainty for the vital CCR facilities that Wisconsinites depend on for reliable energy,” said EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin. “This is powering the Great American Comeback in practice, allowing Wisconsin experts to oversee the CCR landfills in their state under one central set of regulations and protect public health and the environment.”
“EPA’s proposed approval of Wisconsin’s CCR program reflects cooperative federalism in action—empowering state experts to oversee CCR disposal while supporting reliable, affordable energy,” said EPA Region 5 Administrator Anne Vogel. “This approach strengthens American energy independence and ensures that strong protections for human health and the environment remain firmly in place.”
After reviewing the application from the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, EPA is proposing that the program meets all standards for approval.
If finalized, EPA will continue to regulate surface impoundments, as Wisconsin is only seeking approval for permitting CCR disposal in landfills. If finalized, Wisconsin would become the eighth state to receive CCR program approval under the Trump EPA.
Under the Trump Administration, EPA has made significant progress working with states as they seek to manage their own CCR programs. EPA will continue working with state partners to prioritize timely action and empower those with local expertise to oversee more effective CCR disposal operations. The agency anticipates proposing CCR permit program decisions for at least three additional states soon.
EPA will hold a 60-day public comment period, which will include a virtual hearing on November 9, 2026. For more information, visit the Wisconsin CCR permit program webpage.
Background
EPA has recently proposed to approve CCR permit applications from Virginia, Louisiana and Alabama. On March 12, 2025, EPA committed to taking swift action on CCR, including state permit program reviews and updates to the CCR regulations. Since then, EPA has approved permit programs for North Dakota and Wyoming. Approved states cannot have CCR regulations and policies that are less protective of human health and the environment than the federal regulations.
On July 13, 2026, EPA announced an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to gather input on a potential general permit option for coal combustion residuals facilities. This effort builds on EPA’s February 20, 2020, proposal to create a federal CCR permitting program and the April 13, 2026, proposal to allow permit authorities to set certain site-specific alternative requirements.
On April 9, 2026, EPA proposed several revisions to the federal regulations governing the disposal of CCR and the beneficial use of CCR. This proposal would promote resource recovery, allow for site-specific considerations in permitting, provide regulatory relief while continuing to protect human health and the environment, and ensure continued transparency. Earlier in 2026, EPA announced a final rule that extends the compliance deadlines for CCRMU requirements. This action provides additional time to meet facility evaluation requirements and to comply with groundwater monitoring provisions.
Additionally, in November 2025, EPA proposed to extend an alternative closure requirement deadline. would promote electric grid reliability by allowing a subset of coal-fired power producers to continue to operate.
On February 20, 2020, EPA proposed a streamlined federal permitting program for disposing of CCR in surface impoundments and landfills, including an electronic permitting option. EPA proposed clear requirements for applications, permit content and modifications, and procedural steps. EPA would implement the CCR permitting program directly in Indian Country and for CCR units in states that have not sought approval for their own state CCR permit programs. In a separate action, EPA reopened the public comment period for 60 days to accept additional feedback on this rule, given the time elapsed since the 2020 rule was proposed, subsequent changes made and proposed to other CCR regulations.

San Diego, CA — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) released the following statement after San Diego Unified School District (SDUSD) and San Diego City College both informed the Congressman's office of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) arrest activity outside their schools within the past week:

"I am deeply troubled by reports that students and parents were detained without warning while trying to attend classes or bring kids to school. Schools are supposed to be a safe place for young people to learn. Yet this Administration exploits the places we trust most—schools, childcare facilities, hospitals, courthouses, and places of worship. President Trump has turned these places into hunting grounds.

“ICE isn’t going after the 'worst of the worst,' as President Trump promised. We saw this at Buona Forchetta, when ICE agents threw the owner against a wall, handcuffed employees, and used flash-bang grenades on bystanders. These people weren't drug lords or violent criminals; they were workers trying to make a living.

“Parents and children should not have to worry about ICE agents waiting outside a classroom or a doctor's office. That's why I led introduction of the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act, which would bar immigration enforcement within 1,000 feet of schools, hospitals, and churches except in true emergencies. I will also continue working with SDUSD and City College to make sure San Diegans have the resources they need to stay informed and protected.

"Until ICE operates responsibly and reasonably to target dangerous criminals instead of hardworking families, I will push for real reforms from ICE and hold them accountable for the fear they have inflicted on my constituents and communities across the country. I urge all state and local elected officials to express their support for the Protecting Sensitive Locations Act and my Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act so we can deliver commonsense reforms that keep our communities safe."

Background:

Last year, Rep. Peters led the Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act, a bill to make our communities safer by establishing a stronger standard for Federal immigration agents' use of force. The bill would also restrict use of crowd munitions like tear gas and create greater transparency in enforcement by requiring the use of body cameras and strictly limiting the use of masks. Rep. Peters has pushed Congress to pass these common sense reforms, but they have been blocked by the Republican majority.

title: Peters Statement on Reported ICE Activity Near San Diego Schools

SEC Charges Founder and His Two New Jersey-Based Companies in Alleged $16 Million Ponzi Scheme
Washington D.C., Sept. 10, 2026 —
The Securities and Exchange Commission today charged Ernest Ossei Boateng and two New Jersey-based companies he controls, Intercontinental Wealth Network LLC and I Wealth Network LP, for allegedly raising approximately $16 million from more than 200 inexperienced investors through a Ponzi scheme he operated from at least January 2020 until at least March 2026.
According to the SEC’s complaint, Boateng, acting through his two companies, solicited, recommended, and sold interests in an alleged investment fund, primarily targeting Christians of Ghanaian heritage in New York and New Jersey, many of whom had no prior investing experience. The complaint alleges that Boateng told investors that their investments would generate guaranteed fixed returns and that the investment fund would pursue a low-risk investment strategy. Rather than investing the money as promised, however, Boateng allegedly misappropriated more than $5.8 million for his personal expenses, including the purchase, renovation, and furnishing of his home. Boateng also allegedly used approximately $6.6 million to make Ponzi-like payments to earlier investors. The complaint further alleges that, to the limited extent Boateng did invest the money, he failed to do so in low-risk investments with fixed returns. Instead, according to the complaint, Boateng used investor money to engage in high-risk, speculative day trading, leading to more than $750,000 in trading losses.
“We allege that the defendants’ investors included retirees, taxi drivers, home health care providers, students, an ailing widow with young children, and at least two churches and one prayer group,” said Thomas P. Smith, Jr., Associate Director of the SEC’s New York Regional Office. “The defendants’ sales pitch to victims included assuring them that their investments were safe and without risk—telling many their money was protected by so-called ‘financial, investment insurance.’ That’s as big of a red flag as we see in these types of scams.”
The SEC’s complaint, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, charges Boateng, Intercontinental, and I Wealth with violating the antifraud provisions of the Securities Act of 1933 and Securities Exchange Act of 1934, and Boateng and Intercontinental with violating the antifraud provisions of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940. The complaint seeks permanent injunctive relief, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains with pre-judgment interest, and civil penalties against all of the defendants, as well as conduct-based injunctions against Boateng and Intercontinental.
###

Several new sidewalk areas are planned in the Heights after the Memorial Heights Redevelopment Authority secured an $850,000 federal grant to improve mobility and pedestrian safety. 
The gist
MHRA was approved for the grant secured through U.S. Rep. Lizzie Fletcher’s office, with the funding going toward sidewalk improvements, safer connections and improved access for students and children. 
The grant was part of a Community Project Funding request during fiscal year 2023-2024, according to a news release on MHRA’s website. The grant will provide the funding needed to improve sections of sidewalk that are missing, in poor condition or undersized, organization officials said. 
The grant funds will specifically be allocated to the construction portion of the project. The associated design, survey, environmental and grant management work will be funded locally by MHRA.
Some background
In a sidewalk evaluation, MHRA found that almost 25% of sidewalks within the district boundaries were in poor condition or non-existent, and over 40% of sidewalks did not meet current standards for width.
“We are very grateful for the Congresswoman’s efforts in delivering these funds,” said MHRA Board Chair Ann Lents in a previous statement. “The initiative to provide safe and continuous sidewalk access in the area will improve quality of life in the community and have mobility, health and economic benefits.”
The project will also improve access to transit, as Metropolitan Transit Authority of Harris County (METRO) bus routes in the area connect to areas like downtown and Uptown. 
Also of note
Work is already underway, with the project team finalizing sidewalk routes and coordinating with the city of Houston on design plans, according to a post on MHRA’s Facebook page. 
Construction is set to begin in the third quarter of 2027.

A man who received and possessed child pornography was sentenced today to more than 27 years in federal prison.

Matthew Jason Manos, age 42, from Coggon, Iowa, received the prison term after a March 11, 2026, jury verdict finding him guilty of receipt of child pornography and possession of child pornography, including a depiction of a prepubescent minor or a minor who had not attained 12 years of age.

The evidence at trial and sentencing showed that in February 2023, law enforcement officers searched Manos’s residence in Coggon and took his cell phone. Between December 2022 and February 2023, Manos had downloaded images of child pornography. He viewed the images on his cell phone multiple times. Manos then fled Iowa, abandoning his pets in his home where the pets were later rescued by law enforcement. Manos ultimately moved to Illinois, where he was arrested in August 2023. During his arrest, law enforcement officers took his new cell phone. Evidence showed that Manos had used that new phone to access child pornography as well. Manos was previously convicted of continuous sexual abuse of a child, lascivious acts with a child, lascivious conduct with a child, dissemination and exhibition of obscene material to minors, and indecent exposure.

This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse. Led by the United States Attorneys’ Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to locate, apprehend, and prosecute individuals who sexually exploit children, and to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc . For more information about Internet safety education, please visit www.usdoj.gov/psc and click on the tab “resources.”

Manos was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Chief Judge C.J. Williams. Manos was sentenced to 327 months’ imprisonment and was ordered to make $3,000 in restitution to a victim in the case. He must also serve a five-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in the federal system.

Manos is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison.

The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorneys Devra T. Hake and Ashley Corkery and was investigated by the Linn County Sheriff’s Office and the Cedar Rapids Police Department, with assistance by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file number is 25-CR-14.

Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.
title: Coggon Man Sentenced to Decades in Prison for Child Pornography Offenses

Oxford, MS – A Batesville woman was sentenced today to more than six years in federal prison for possessing one or more homemade bombs on separate occasions.

According to court documents, Christina Willis, 29, previously pled guilty to possession of the bombs, or destructive devices, one of which Willis placed on the vehicle of her ex-boyfriend in June 2025. Senior U.S. District Court Judge Michael P. Mills sentenced Willis to 78 months in prison followed by 3 years of supervised release. Willis was remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals following sentencing.

U.S. Attorney Scott Leary made the announcement and stated, “We live in a wonderful country but it’s still a dangerous world, as confirmed by this case. When bombs are being produced an all-hands-on-deck response is required, which is what happened in this case. Federal, state and local law enforcement worked closely together in this coordinated investigation. The ATF and FBI working with the Lafayette County Sheriff’s Office, the Panola County Sheriff’s Office, the Yalobusha County Sheriff’s Office, the Mississippi Bureau of Narcotics and the Tupelo Police Department-this is what a successful investigation looks like. Well done.”

“ATF is dedicated to preventing and reducing violent crime involving the criminal use of explosives,” said ATF New Orleans Special Agent in Charge Joshua Jackson. “The collaborative effort of federal and local law enforcement, led by the U.S. Attorney’s Office, secured a sentence today that sends a message that ATF will continue to investigate and perfect charges against those who use explosives. ATF will continue to work tirelessly to protect our communities and neighborhoods and hold accountable those who threaten our safety.”

Assistant United States Attorney Robert Mims prosecuted this case.

BOSTON – Dompé U.S., Inc. (Dompé), based in California, has agreed to pay $32 million to resolve allegations that, between 2018 and 2021, it paid Medicare beneficiary co-payments through two patient assistance foundations to induce the purchase of its drug, Oxervate, in violation of the Anti-Kickback Statute and the False Claims Act.

When a Medicare beneficiary obtains a prescription drug covered by Medicare Part B or Part D, the beneficiary is often required to make a partial payment, which may take the form of a co-payment, co-insurance, or deductible (collectively “co-pays”). These co-pay obligations may be substantial for expensive medications. Congress included co-pay requirements in these programs, in part, to encourage market forces to serve as a check on health care costs, including the prices that pharmaceutical manufacturers can demand for their drugs. The Anti-Kickback Statute prohibits pharmaceutical companies from offering or paying, directly or indirectly, any remuneration – which includes money or any other thing of value – to induce Medicare patients to purchase the companies’ drugs.

Dompé admitted that, around the time of Oxervate’s 2018 launch in the United States, Dompé U.S. employees expressed reservations about launching the drug before making a payment to a patient assistance foundation that paid the co-pays for Oxervate. After conversations with Dompé employees, two foundations opened funds that, among other things, paid co-pays for Oxervate, and Dompé made contributions to those foundations. Between 2019 and 2021, despite having an annual budgeting process for contributions, Dompé sometimes approved mid-year increases to those foundations or held certain amounts in “reserve” so that it could determine mid-year which of the foundations were running low on funding and allocate the “reserve” accordingly. Dompé also solicited patient assistance foundation data directly from the foundations, and from the specialty pharmacy that provided hub services to Dompé U.S. patients. Certain Dompé employees involved in the patient assistance foundation budgeting process received this data through either direct or indirect means.

“Kickbacks to beneficiaries undermine the purpose of the Medicare co-pay system and drive up the cost of drugs,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “My Office has recovered over $1.4 billion for taxpayers through settlements and enforcement actions concerning drug company kickbacks to purported charities, and we will continue to pursue these matters to ensure that all drug companies play by the rules and to protect federal taxpayer funded healthcare programs.”

“Kickbacks to beneficiaries undermine the purpose of the Medicare co-pay system and drive up the cost of drugs,” said United States Attorney Leah B. Foley. “My Office has recovered over $1.4 billion for taxpayers through settlements and enforcement actions concerning drug company kickbacks to purported charities, and we will continue to pursue these matters to ensure that all drug companies play by the rules and to protect federal taxpayer funded healthcare programs.”

“This settlement demonstrates the United States’ commitment to enforcing the Anti-Kickback Statute and ensuring that pharmaceutical manufacturers do not use unlawful inducements,” said Assistant Attorney General Brett A. Shumate of the Justice Department’s Civil Division. “The Department encourages companies that uncover improper kickbacks to self-disclose such conduct.”

“Pharmaceutical manufacturers that attempt to disguise kickbacks as charitable patient assistance are engaging in blatant misconduct which corrupts medical decision‑making and drains federal health care programs,” said Acting Deputy Inspector General for Investigations Miranda L. Bennett of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS-OIG). “Dompé’s actions undermined critical safeguards Congress put in place to protect Medicare, driving up costs for taxpayers while exploiting patients. HHS-OIG does not tolerate such conduct and will continue to work tirelessly for justice and accountability.”

Dompé is the U.S. subsidiary of Dompé farmaceutici S.p.A., a pharmaceutical company incorporated in Italy. Dompé farmaceutici voluntarily self-disclosed this conduct to the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Massachusetts, which Dompé U.S. discovered following an internal compliance review. Following the voluntary disclosure, both Dompé farmaceutici and Dompé U.S. fully cooperated with the government in this matter. By 2022, Dompé implemented changes to its patient assistance foundation contribution practices.

U.S. Attorney Foley, AAG Shumate and HHS-OIG Acting DIGI Bennett made the announcement today. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Lindsey Ross and Brian LaMacchia, Chief of the Affirmative Litigation Unit, handled the matter along with Senior Trial Counsel Sarah Arni of the Civil Division’s Commercial Litigation Branch, Fraud Section.
title: Dompé U.S. Agrees to Pay $32 Million to Resolve False Claims Act Liability Relating to Self-Disclosure of Patient Kickbacks

New York, NY - U.S. Representative Dan Goldman (NY-10) presented the Kings County District Attorney’s Office with a $354,000 Community Project funding award. The award will be used to bolster the Outreach and Assistance Response (SOAR) program. The program is designed to conduct immediate outreach to violent crime victims and their families.

Rep. Goldman requested and secured funding for the project, which was included in a package of bills to fund the federal government. Goldman secured $13,756,000 for 15 community projects in NY-10 in the FY 2026 appropriations process.

Rep. Goldman presented the award to Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez.

“Violent crime often leaves lasting trauma for victims and their families, who benefit greatly from immediate assistance,” said Congressman Dan Goldman. “I am proud to have secured $354,000 to fund the Kings County District Attorney’s Office’s program that does just that – from financial help to mental health assistance.. Thank you to District Attorney Gonzalez for his leadership on this issue to provide Brooklyn families with the respect and care they deserve."

Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez said, “While Brooklyn is experiencing a public safety renaissance with historic lows in homicides and shootings, there are still too many families dealing with the trauma of a shooting, an assault or the loss of a loved one. And even when there has not yet been an arrest or a criminal case, victims and families may need immediate support. The new SOAR program will offer just that and fill gaps that traditional compensation programs cannot always cover, allowing our counselors to assist and stand with every victim of serious violence and their families. I am grateful for Congressman Dan Goldman who secured the grant that will allow us to launch this important initiative.”

Kings County District Attorney’s SOAR (Support Outreach and Assistance Response) conducts outreach and provides support to victims of violent assaults and homicides regardless of whether anyone has been arrested for the crime. Typically the victim’s services staff in a DA’s office only comes into contact with a victim once an arrest has been made and a case generated. The SOAR team responds to violent crimes even when there is no case in the DA’s office. The response team provides assistance with victim compensation, counseling, and relevant case related information. The SOAR team also engages in community outreach to inform the public of KCDA’s services and commitment to public safety.

Immediately following a violent incident or homicide, usually within the first 24 to 48 hours, SOAR counselors work with the NYC Police Department to obtain contact information of survivors or surviving family members. In cases where other agencies or organizations, such as the offices of elected officials or community-based organizations, have already had contact with the victim or family, SOAR counselors work with those agencies to ensure a warm handoff from those organizations to our experts in trauma, crime victim’s rights, and criminal justice.

The funds will assist with building the SOAR team by covering the salary for a program coordinator and four new staff members dedicated to the program.

###
title: Congressman Dan Goldman Presents $354,000 Grant Award to Kings County District Attorney’s Office

text:
Remarks

Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Keiko Fujimori, Peruvian President

Presidential Palace

Lima, Peru

September 10, 2026

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) Welcome to the Túpac Amaru Hall of the Government Palace. Next, we will hear the remarks of the President of the Republic Keiko Sofía Fujimori Higuchi and the Secretary of State, His Excellency Marco Rubio. They will give their remarks after the meeting they held in the framework of the official meeting.

Next, we’ll listen to the remarks by the President of the Republic, Ms. Keiko Sofía Fujimori.

PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) Good morning, Secretary of State Mr. Marco Rubio, ministers, high officers, journalists. Your presence in Peru, Secretary Rubio, represents much more than an official visit. It symbolizes the meeting of two nations which for 200 years share the same view about freedom, independence, and sovereignty.

Two hundred years ago Peru started to build its republic. The United States were already consolidating it. We were two young nations but with a very strong aspiration, that America could decide about its own destiny. Two hundred years have gone by and that vision is still in force, with different nuances, aspects, and new challenges, but with the same aim: that no external force takes away from us the possibility of living in freedom.

For that reason, the first topic of our meeting has been how to face transnational organized crime, and we have talked about citizenship and security. As president of the Republic of Peru, I am happy to inform our nation that Peru will become part of the Shield of the Americas – (applause) – a multilateral coalition that includes more than 15 countries and which is led by the United States.

Thank you, Secretary Rubio, for this opportunity because we have had to face terrorism and we know how difficult it is to face these criminal organizations that do not respect any borders. And for this reason, we need to join efforts with other countries. Being part of the Shield of the Americas will enable us, as we have already proved, to obtain faster information and act more firmly. And from Peru, we will act with all the powers granted by the law and the constitution.

We have also had the chance to talk about the challenge posed by the El Niño phenomenon. We were sharing with Secretary Rubio that this phenomenon will begin, it was announced, in February; however, the previous government did not take pertinent actions. In the first days of August, as the press already knows, we began with the cleaning of the riverbeds and prepare ourselves for the emergency. And we would like to take the opportunity to thank the United States for the support that is being provided thanks to the coordinations of Ambassador Navarro.

And we are thankful because in February 2027, the Comfort American ship will arrive to the coast of Peru. This is one of the largest hospital vessels of the world, with more than 1,000 beds and highly equipped technology. This will help the population of the northern part of our country. We thank for the assistance that could be given by the Southern Command and the support that we are already receiving from the DEA and the FBI and other federal agencies. We’ve been able to talk about many subjects – education, infrastructure investment, our trade exchange.

But we salute today the political decision of President Trump to look at Latin America that Secretary Rubio is here in Peru because it shows the true value you’re giving to this bilateral relations. We’re talking about 200 years of friendship. Welcome, Secretary Rubio. (Applause.)

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We thank the words of President of the Republic. Now we have the remarks from the Secretary of State, our Excellency Marco Rubio.

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you very much, dear President, for having a meeting. The cooperation that exists through the first 40 days of your administration has meant a lot. We’ve done a lot, but we will do more. I think that I come and I leave with a lot of confidence that the relations between our countries will start a very special era and will benefit both countries in a very important way.

It’s important to have, like you’ve said, the relation for more than 200 years between our countries. We are a very, very young republic. You were starting as a republic; and we’ve done a lot during these 200 years, but we still have a lot to do. We are facing the modern threats, which are different from a decade ago, those new (inaudible) threats.

Our obligation, the most important thing, is to achieve peace, to achieve security of the people. And when that is threatened, it’s impossible. It’s impossible to have economy growth, prosperity. It’s impossible to achieve other things if peace, calm, and order are not present. These are important things and are very necessary for economic growth and prosperity, which is all – what we want.

Which is the biggest threat? The threat nowadays are transnational organized crime. Bear in mind that we had these groups operating within national territories only, but nowadays it is a network, it’s a terrorist network, a criminal network, which is very dangerous, operating through borders and multiple countries with liaisons. It’s a criminal infrastructure with banking, finance, and they’re trying to take this hemisphere. We cannot let this happen. The only way we can confront them is to be strong and confront them.

This is why we’re very happy and – well, that you have been elected. People elected you because you promised to confront this, and we will provide the support. Why? Not only because of the friendship, because it’s only of our national interest. To have operating criminals operating in this hemisphere – it’s a direct threat not only for the Peruvian people, but as well for the United States.

I’m very, very happy to listen to the announcement that you will be partner of the Shield of the Americas. A shield against what, people may wonder? A shield against these criminal bands, criminal groups, terrorist groups that are a direct threat to the sovereignty to our countries. When we are encountering criminal bands that have more money and best military equipment than the military themselves, that is not acceptable. And against that is the shield. This is why we have 14 countries working together – hopefully we will add more countries – to confront and defeat forever these elements.

What can we do at the same time for security, prosperity? And this is why we will always seek trade opportunities to work together with your government and your country, to seek trade agreements that will benefit directly our people, and as well, the United States economy. And we have multiple possibilities. We have spoken about that today and we still have a lot to do. And we’re starting to work on those topics.

So for us, it is an honor to be here with you today and to start this new era in the relations between Peru and the United States. I think we have the possibility in our hands to start a very important time, historical era, in terms of what we can achieve together.

If I may please switch to English because I do have U.S. press covering this.

(In English) (Inaudible) President Fujimori for receiving us here today. I truly believe that we are entering a new era in U.S.-Peru relations, a golden era in many ways, because her administration has the right ideas. In her first 40 days in office, we’ve already done many things together, and there’s so much more for us to do together.

I remind everybody that the most important obligation of any government to its people is the security and the stability and the order in that country. And when that is threatened, nothing else is possible – not economic growth, not prosperity, not upward mobility. And in fact, we look at the criminality that exists and the terrorism that exists in this region today – and the people most victimized by it are working people, common people, who cannot defend themselves against these criminal elements.

This is – this has always been a threat in this region. But it has become a new threat because these are now transnational threats. These are transnational terrorist organizations that do not respect sovereign borders and operate in multiple countries with the same aim and the same goal of exploiting countries and exploiting their people and harming them.

And I’m very pleased to hear the announcement that Peru will be joining the Shield of the Americas. What is it a shield against? It is a shield against these threats to the sovereignty of these independent nations. It is a shield against these transnational criminal groups that, in many cases, have more money and better military equipment than the states. That is unacceptable, and the only way to defeat it is to confront it forcefully. And it’s the reason why President Fujimori was elected because she told the people of this country she would confront this threat and she would defeat it, and we will help her. We are going to help as we possibly can because it is in our national interest as well.

Beyond that, there is extraordinary commercial opportunities. We’ve talked about some of those today. There are real opportunities to us to work together on commercial deals and commercial projects that are extraordinarily beneficial to Peru, to the people of Peru, but also beneficial to the people of the United States. That will be a core of our relationship as well.

So it’s an honor to be here. It’s an honor to be with you. And I thank you and I thank your team for receiving us. I can’t wait to see the exciting things we’ll do together. Thank you. (Applause.)

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We thank our Secretary of State for his remarks. Now we will take two questions per country for each authority. Please we’d like to invite the press. Start with the name of your organization.

QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Good afternoon, President and Secretary of State. My first question is for you. What is the importance of this meeting that you have sustained with the Secretary of State, considering that this first official encounter with the United States of America? And number two, what is the importance that Peru becomes part of the Shield of the Americas, and how this will strengthen the security policy in favor of Peruvians? Thank you.

PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) For Peru, it is of the essence – it is of the essence for Peru to know that the United States has now a political view of Latin America. We were speaking with Secretary Rubio that in previous administrations that importance was not given to the region. And his presence marks this difference – President Trump’s view.

Entering the Shield of the Americas is of the essence for Peru. First of all, because it relaunches the joint work of both countries (inaudible) during the ‘90s. Let’s remember that the USA helped us in the fight against drug trafficking, and we were able to reduce the coca leaf production. In 1990 we had 120,000 hectares; that went down to 20,000 hectares. This reduction was possible with the work done with alternative crops, directly working with the farmers themselves. We have already shown results when two countries have a political decision, can work jointly shoulder to shoulder.

Entering the Shield of the Americas will help us to obtain information. Peru confronted Shining Path and the MRTA, two terrorist groups, and was able to defeat them. And these two groups worked within Peruvian territory. Now criminal organizations know no borders. Some weeks ago it was possible to capture a criminal from the Los Pulpos criminal organization, and he was in Bolivia. This information was handed over to us through the FBI, and the Peruvian and Bolivian police were able to work jointly.

For this reason it is of the essence to be part of the Shield of the Americas, because we will be able to act directly on our own behalf and on behalf of the cabinet of ministers led by Mr. Galarreta. We have the will to confront them, and with information from all countries we will be able to act faster and obtain specific and tangible results.

QUESTION: Vera Bergengruen with The Wall Street Journal . Mr. Secretary, you have stressed that the members of the Shield of the Americas are sovereign partners. But if one of these governments refuses to act against one of these groups that Washington deems a terrorist threat, does the U.S. reserve the right to act unilaterally, including here in Peru?

And President Fujimori: (Via interpreter) The question wanted more information about the partner of the Shield of the Americas. This will include to collaborate with the United States here in the country.

SECRETARY RUBIO: I’ll answer that question in English to Spanish. I don’t know if you guys heard it. Basically, the gist of the question is, if you’re a member of the Shield and refuse to act, does the United States – will the United States act unilaterally?

Well, if we were going to act unilaterally, why would we need the Shield? We’re not – if we were interested in acting unilaterally, we have the capacity to act unilaterally. The reason why we’re not doing it is because we want to do it with our partners. It’s the most effective way to do it. For us to confront transnational criminal groups, we need to do it inside the sovereign territory of countries, and we want to partner with those countries. It’s in their interest to do it. That is why we have the Shield. That is why the Shield exists.

People make up these problems that don’t exist. They’re getting ahead of themselves with these – these ridiculous sort of things that no one’s even contemplating. The bottom line is the reason why we have a Shield is because we choose to act in partnership with our partners. So it’s very simple. This is not very complicated; let me explain this to you. It’s a very, very simple equation. We have a country that says we want to defeat these criminals, these terrorists, these evil, despicable human beings; we want to defeat them. We want to work with America to defeat them. And so we say, of course we want to work – what should we say to them? No, we don’t want to work with you? No, we’d like you not to do anything about these groups?

We have a president here who has said very clearly – not to us, to the people of her country; it’s why they elected her – I am going to defeat these groups that extort you, I am going to defeat these groups that kill you, I am going to defeat these groups that terrorize your children in our communities. And the United States has said we’re so happy you’re doing that, it’s important for us as well, and we’re going to partner with you. That is the purpose of the Shield, to shield the region against this threat to the sovereignty of every one of our nations.

(Via interpreter) The question was if the United States will act unilaterally if the member country of the Shield will not act. It’s a ridiculous question because if we’re going to do it unilaterally, then why would we have the Shield? The reason why we have the Shield is because we don’t want to act unilaterally. We want to act together. We want to act jointly.

Why do we want it? It’s very simple. These are terrorist groups. Please be clear, these are not criminals stealing a bank. These are terrorist groups extorting people, extorting and doing a lot of – committing multiple crimes, things that you cannot even think about. They’re evil. So these – we need to defeat them, and we need to work together. When we see that there is a leader, a president that was elected with that promise to the people – and she is compliant with this; she will defeat and confront these groups – we will support her. Because it’s of our interest as well to work with you, of course, to your country or a sovereign country.

And this is an enormous responsibility to confront these groups, and we will do our best to support to be able so she can comply with that promise. She will help us, but we will help them as well. This is how the partnerships work, this is how allies work, and this is what is the Shield. It is a powerful partnership against these diabolic groups that have terrorized the region for many, many years and through multiple leaders, and many, many, many political leaders from multiple countries don’t have the courage to confront them, or at many times they were involved. And this impunity will no longer be accepted, and this is what we are seeing, and in other countries as well that are a member of the Shield of the Americans.

PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) I want to reflect on a question. When we requested powers, this request was filed with congress by the prime minister. We requested to declare these criminal groups as hostile and terrorist groups. This mechanism will be fundamental.

Second of all, we want to coordinate and strengthen the justice administration system to face decisively these criminal organizations. All of these mechanisms will help us obtain information through the Shield of the Americas and the different government agencies.

(In English) So we are extremely happy, and we are thankful for Peru to be part now of the Shield of the Americas.

QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Ayrton Luera from ATV Noticias . My question was with this incorporation of Peru into Shield of Americas, Mr. Rubio, would be – will we expect military operations or emergency operations in Peruvian territory?

And if so, Madam President, could you tell us about the conversations that have taken place, if these interventions respect Peruvian sovereignty? And Mr. Rubio, what would be your answer to this public response of the Chinese embassy after your column in the press?

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) I don’t know what the Chinese embassy said. I’m not here to talk about what the Chinese embassy said. So, but the first question that you asked, we’re going to be – this is a sovereign country. You have your laws, you have a process. It’s a democratic country. You have a system, government system, a legal system; you will comply to that. We’re willing to do all what we can to assist you. This is going to be based on the cooperation that you request. We don’t want to be less, offer less, but not offer more than what you’re requesting. We’ll work together with this government that has an interest in defeating and have an obligation it’s committed to confront and defeat these criminal groups. So we’re not going to do anything that is outside the legal framework of your country or outside what the government will request.

(In English) The question was would we do anything in the country, military activities and the like – we’re not going do anything that our partners don’t ask us to do. This is a democracy. This is a republic. They have laws, they have a system of government, they have regulations, they have a process they have to go through. We are not – we don’t want to do less than what you ask of us, but we’re not going to do more than what you ask of us. We are partners and we are allies. That’s how partnerships and alliances work.

PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) I wanted to mention that even before we entered the Shield of the Americas our police force was being trained by the FBI. Even Great Britain was assisting us in this training and in the strengthening of our police force. And with our entry into the Shield of Americas we will have a more solid position.

With regard to the entry of troops, there is a special provision in the constitution. Every time there is this kind of entry, a special authorization is requested to the congress of the republic. Of course, we will uphold this rule. Peru’s sovereignty is intact. We will recover order, tranquility, and peace for all of the Peruvian people. For this reason, we thank Secretary Rubio for his presence and to be here to be able to announce that Peru will be part of the Shield of the Americas. Thank you so much.

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We will now listen to the last question of this conference.

QUESTION: Eric Martin with Bloomberg News. Secretary Rubio, as you get ready to conclude this three-day visit to Peru, Colombia, and Ecuador, what is your message to the people of the region about the benefits of partnering with the U.S. and to voters in neighboring Brazil as they face elections in one month from now in some of the same security and other challenges of countries in the region?

And President Fujimori – Presidente Fujimori: (Via interpreter) After the visit of Secretary Rubio —

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Oh, he spoke Spanish. You’re tricky.

(In English) I didn’t know he spoke Spanish.

(Via interpreter) I can no longer speak Spanish because he’ll know.

(In English) I’m sorry.

QUESTION: (Via interpreter) Thank you, Secretary. President Fujimori, after the visit of Secretary Rubio, after today, and after being six weeks in office, are you prepared to take more steps to associate and work with the United States despite the massive investment of China in Peru during the last years, including the Port of Chancay? Thank you.

SECRETARY RUBIO: (Via interpreter) Thank you. He speaks Spanish. I mean, I was – I’m no longer going to be able to speak Spanish in front of you. It’s a joke, obviously.

First, what’s our message? Let’s be clear on this. I’ve said for more than 20 years, unfortunately, administrations of both political parties, they’ve ignored the region. The focus was on different parts of the world. If you study – because I have two jobs: Secretary of State and also I am a consultant to the national security for President Trump at the Security Council. So our National Security Strategy speaks very openly about we will give priority to this side of the hemisphere. Why? Because we’re part of it, because geography is real, and the problems of the hemisphere impacts directly. It doesn’t mean that other problems outside this hemisphere are not important, but what really happens here in South America, Central America, and the Caribbean has a direct impact to the United States.

Number two, we have a lot of people in common. How many U.S. Americans come visit, have businesses here, are tourists, live here, and vice versa? We have very – a very strong bond we cannot ignore, so we’ll give the priority. And not rhetorically – because there has been other administrations, oh, no, yes, we are focused on the side of the hemisphere, but they are not doing things, they haven’t done things. We are going to be focusing. First, it’s important for us, Peru as a country, as part of our national interest.

So this visit is not unexpected. I’ve done this visit as a senator, I’m doing this as the Secretary of State, and we will continue doing this type of visits, and we will have concrete efforts. It’s not just simply the Shield of the Americas. We’ll have other efforts jointly to confront the interests that we have in common with our friends and our allies. And we want all the time – this is the most important. This is very, very important in democracy. When a president is elected and the president decides to cooperate and work with the United States, it’s super important that we can show the people that there are benefits for the people to get a partnership with the United States and work together, not only at the security level but as well trade and economically speaking.

And we need to try to do that, and we want to make sure that the countries that cooperate with us are going to be able to respond to their voters: This is the consequence, the result of our cooperation with the United States.

(In English) Very briefly, the question was in English: What is our message? Our message is what we’ve been saying all along. We have a National Security Strategy. I helped write it. And it talks about how the Western Hemisphere is a priority for this administration – not a rhetorical priority, not a symbolic priority, not a ceremonial priority – a real priority. That’s why I’ve traveled extensively in the region, that’s why we’ve received visitors from the region, and that’s why we’re here today. Because geography is real. The things that happen in this hemisphere directly impact us. We’re not doing anybody a favor here. Us getting involved in the region is not a favor; it is essential to our own security, to our own prosperity, to our own well-being in the United States of America.

And this administration is committed to this. And there’ll be more if – people talk about the Shield of the Americas. I’m very proud of it. There’s going to be more initiatives like that in multiple realms where we can work together. But for this administration, this hemisphere is a priority, and you will continue to see it demonstrated over and over and over again.

PRESIDENT FUJIMORI: (Via interpreter) Peru is part of APEC, the Asian Pacific economic forum; the United States too. And Peru has a significant production of minerals, fish products, agricultural products, and we will continue with this effort of having trade exchanges with different countries from Asia, from the Pacific, and from Europe of course. But today, with the presence of Secretary Rubio and the agreement signed in recent days, and with this direct collaboration that will be reciprocal, we begin a new era of relations between Peru and the United States. And these relations will surely strengthen both countries.

So thank you, Secretary Rubio, for your presence. We hope you can visit us again. And we have already talked about other dates where we will be able to exchange more ideas and re-establish this cooperation, bridges between both countries. Thank you. (Applause.)

MODERATOR: (Via interpreter) We would like to thank the press for their questions, and we would like to invite President Fujimori and Secretary Rubio to step up for an official photograph. We hope that you can move forward to be able to capture this photo. This act has ended. Thank you for your presence. We wish you a good afternoon, and we will now like to request the Peruvian press to remain in your places while we wait for the other part of the press to leave. Thank you.

Asset threshold increased from $3 billion to $6 billion in total assets for qualifying banks eligible for less onerous 18-month exam cycle

Approximately 50 additional OCC-regulated institutions eligible for longer exam cycle

WASHINGTON—The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency today published an interim final rule that raises the asset threshold for certain supervised institutions with less than $6 billion in total assets to qualify for an 18-month on-site examination cycle, pursuant to the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act.

Under the interim final rule, approximately 50 additional OCC-regulated institutions will be eligible to extend their exam cycles from once every 12 months to once every 18 months. The longer exam cycle will yield cost savings for these financial institutions and enable them to reallocate resources to other activities to better serve their customers.

“The OCC is proud to support President Trump’s and Secretary Scott Bessent’s vision of parallel prosperity and a strong community banking system that thrives and drives economic growth,” said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan V. Gould. “The community bank comeback is underway, and today’s action supports that effort by reducing burden for these banks that are vital to the strength of local economies across America, so they can focus more of their time and energy on serving their customers.”

The OCC remains committed to addressing the challenges for community banks and has taken a series of actions to rightsize regulatory burden and tailor supervisory activities so these institutions may grow and continue to meet the needs of the customers and small businesses they serve. These actions include:

Creating a distinct line of supervision focused on community banks and the issues that affect them most.

Removing OCC examination activities that were previously required by OCC policy and instead tailoring examination scope and frequency in a manner that is consistent with risk-based supervision.

Increasing the upper asset range of the community bank supervision portfolio to give them room to grow organically or through acquisition, without facing the increased supervision scrutiny that comes with being a larger bank assigned to other supervision portfolios.

Updating the OCC’s model risk management guidance to clarify that model risk management should be risk-based, tailored, and commensurate with a bank’s size, complexity, and extent of model use, excluding community banks from unnecessary requirements.

Simplifying licensing requirements and alleviating unnecessary compliance burdens by expanding community banks’ access to expedited or reduced filing procedures.

Establishing Community Bank Minimum Bank Secrecy Act and Anti-Money Laundering examination procedures to tailor supervisory activities to community banks’ generally low money laundering/terrorist financing risk levels and eliminating Money Laundering Risk System data collection requirements.

Reducing complexity by clarifying that the OCC will not use expanded procedures—generally unsuitable to community banks—when examining community banks’ retail nondeposit investment product offerings.

Eliminating duplicative data collection requirements , further alleviating regulatory reporting burden for community banks.

Proposing guidance for a simplified Community Reinvestment Act strategic plan process to help community banks better focus their resources on local credit needs and clarify measurable goals and other requirements.

Issuing a revised compliance guide for the community bank leverage ratio framework as part of its ongoing work to provide regulatory relief for community banks.

Tampa, Florida – United States Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe announces the unsealing of an indictment charging Brandon “Dutch” Mendenhall (47, Brandon, Florida) and Amy Marie Smith Vaughn (48, New Port Richey, Florida) with 10 counts of theft or embezzlement from employee benefit plans and five counts of theft or embezzlement in connection with health care. If convicted, Mendenhall and Vaughn each face a maximum penalty of 10 years in federal prison. The indictment also notifies Mendenhall and Vaughn that the United States intends to forfeit the proceeds traceable to the offenses.

According to the indictment, Mendenhall and Vaughn were the founders, registered agents, or officers of several entities, including RAD Diversified REIT, RADD Capital, The Seminar Solution, and DHI Holdings. The employees of these entities could participate in the companies’ 401(k) retirement plan and health insurance plan by having funds directly withheld from their paychecks. Beginning in the spring of 2024, Mendenhall and Vaughn stopped contributing the funds that were being withheld from their employees’ paychecks to the 401(k) plan. Then beginning in September of 2024, Mendenhall and Vaughn stopped contributing the funds being withheld from their employee’s paychecks to the company’s health insurance plan.

An indictment is merely a formal charge that a defendant has committed one or more violations of federal criminal law, and every defendant is presumed innocent unless, and until, proven guilty.

This case was investigated by the Department of Labor – Employee Benefits Security Administration, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Internal Revenue Service – Criminal Investigation, and the Florida Office of Financial Regulation – Bureau of Financial Investigations. It will be prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Merrilyn Hoenemeyer.
title: RAD Diversified REIT Co-Founders Indicted for Stealing Funds from Their Employees’ Benefit Plans
