USITC Makes Determinations In Five-Year (Sunset) Reviews Concerning Oil Country Tubular Goods From India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam
The U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) today determined that revocation of the antidumping and countervailing duty orders on imports of oil country tubular goods (OCTG) from India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam would likely lead to continuation or recurrence of material injury within a reasonably foreseeable time.
As a result of the USITC’s affirmative determinations, the existing antidumping duty orders on imports of this product from India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam and the existing countervailing duty orders of this product from India and Turkey will remain in place.
Chairman Brett W. Doyle and Commissioners Peter-Anthony Pappas, Bart Thanhauser, and David Foley Jr. voted in the affirmative with respect to the existing antidumping orders on imports of OCTG from India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam and the existing countervailing duty orders on OCTG from India and Turkey. Commissioner Jason E. Kearns voted in the affirmative with respect to the antidumping duty orders on imports of OCTG from India, South Korea, Turkey, and Vietnam and the countervailing duty orders on OCTG from India and Turkey and voted in the negative with respect to the antidumping duty order on OCTG from Ukraine.
Today’s action comes under the five-year (sunset) review process required by the Uruguay Round Agreements Act. See the attached page for background on these five-year (sunset) reviews.
The USITC’s public report, Oil Country Tubular Goods from India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam (Inv. Nos. 701-TA- 499-500 and 731-TA-1215-1216 and 1221-1223 (Second Review), USITC Publication 5790, September 2026), will contain the views of the USITC and information developed during the reviews.
The report will be available on the USITC website by October 22, 2026.
BACKGROUND
The Uruguay Round Agreements Act requires the Department of Commerce to revoke an antidumping or countervailing duty order, or terminate a suspension agreement, after five years unless the Department of Commerce and the USITC determine that revoking the order or terminating the suspension agreement would be likely to lead to continuation or recurrence of dumping or subsidies (Commerce) and of material injury (USITC) within a reasonably foreseeable time.
The USITC’s institution notice in five-year reviews requests that interested parties file responses with the USITC concerning the likely effects of revoking the order under review as well as other information. Generally, within 95 days from institution, the USITC will determine whether the responses it has received reflect an adequate or inadequate level of interest in a full review. If responses to the USITC’s notice of institution are adequate, or if other circumstances warrant a full review, the USITC conducts a full review, which includes a public hearing and issuance of questionnaires.
The five-year (sunset) reviews concerning Oil Country Tubular Goods from India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam were instituted on July 1, 2025.
On November 24, 2025, the USITC determined to conduct full five-year reviews. For Ukraine, Commissioners David S. Johanson, Jason E. Kearns, and Amy A. Karpel concluded that the domestic interested party group response and the respondent interested party group response were adequate, and voted for a full five-year review for Ukraine. For India, South Korea, Turkey and Vietnam, Commissioners David S. Johanson, Jason E. Kearns, and Amy A. Karpel concluded that the domestic interested party group response were adequate and the respondent interested party group responses were inadequate, and voted for full five-year reviews for those countries to promote administrative efficiency.
Chairman Brett W. Doyle and Commissioners Peter-Anthony Pappas, Bart Thanhauser, and David Foley Jr. did not participate in the adequacy votes as they were not members of the USITC at the time.
A record of the USITC’s vote to conduct expedited reviews is available on the investigations page for Oil Country Tubular Goods from India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam; Inv. No. 701-TA-499-500 and 731-TA-1215-1216 and 1221-1223 (Second Review).
title: USITC Makes Determinations In Five-Year (Sunset) Reviews Concerning Oil Country Tubular Goods From India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Wednesday, September 9, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) introduced the bipartisan Stop Rogue AI Act to ensure businesses and federal agencies have the ability to see rogue and dangerous AI agents operating inside their own networks, and stop them before they cause real damage.

Right now, most organizations have no reliable way to know how many unauthorized AI agents are running in their systems, who built them, or what they have access to. AI agents can be activated by employees, embedded in third-party software, or deployed by vendors — often with little to no visibility for the organization whose networks they’re operating on to know that they are there. That blind spot is becoming more dangerous by the day. The recent Hugging Face incident and other autonomous cyberattacks have shown AI systems are being used to hack organizations at scale, without a person ever watching or stepping in.

“Right now, AI agents are running loose in our networks, and nobody can see them or verify who built them — making it increasingly hard to stop them,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “That’s a five-alarm security risk. We’ve already seen AI systems hack organizations on autopilot, with no person at the wheel. My bipartisan bill with Congressman Lawler puts humans back in the driver’s seat so we can find agents and know exactly who’s behind them so that organizations can effectively protect their systems.”

“AI agents are becoming more capable and more deeply integrated into our government and economy. We need to make sure we know what these systems are, what they can access, and who is responsible for them. We can harness the benefits of AI while making sure these systems don’t operate in the shadows of the networks they have access to,” said Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17).

The Stop Rogue AI Act would direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), to develop national standards, guidelines, and best practices for discovering, verifying, and controlling AI agents.

Under the bill, those standards will provide guidance to organizations on how to:

Find and track every AI agent operating on their systems, in a continuous, easily readable inventory;

Verify who built and operates each agent, using verifiable identity and provenance — not just a vendor’s word;

Monitor agents in real time, including detecting prompt injection, data theft, and agents behaving outside their approved limits; and

Allow, deny, or revoke an agent’s access, actions, and interactions at any time – so people have the final say over what it can access or do.

The bill also requires federal contractors and agencies to build these safeguards into how they buy and deploy AI agents, and directs NIST and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to fold the standards into existing federal cybersecurity guidance.

The bipartisan legislation has already earned support from a broad coalition spanning network security, internet infrastructure, and AI governance, including:

Palo Alto Networks

GoDaddy

Infoblox

AI Policy Network

Alliance for Secure AI

“As AI agents become more capable of acting and transacting on our behalf, identity and accountability are foundational. We need open, interoperable standards that make it possible to know which agent is acting, who stands behind it, and whether its credentials are valid. Representatives Gottheimer and Lawler’s bipartisan effort is an important step toward establishing those standards and putting them to work through federal adoption. GoDaddy is pleased to support an approach that can strengthen security while keeping the agentic web open to businesses and innovators of every size,” said Jared Sine, Chief Strategy & Legal Officer, GoDaddy.

“Securing AI agents starts with knowing they exist and being able to trust who they are. This bill rightly treats agent discovery as foundational cybersecurity, giving agencies the ability to continuously find, verify, and control the AI agents interacting with their systems. We’re especially encouraged that this legislation promotes open, vendor-agnostic, and interoperable discovery standards built on existing internet infrastructure like the domain name system, rather than locking agencies into proprietary platforms. That approach is scalable, resilient, and the right foundation for agent security. Reps. Gottheimer and Lawler are doing commendable work, and we look forward to supporting the bill’s advancement,” said Wei Chen, Chief Legal Officer and EVP, Regulatory Strategy, Infoblox

“As AI agents rapidly scale across government and enterprise systems, security and governance must evolve to address the novel risks of agentic decision-making. Palo Alto Networks applauds Representatives Josh Gottheimer and Mike Lawler for their bipartisan leadership in introducing the AI Agent Standardization and Security Act. This legislation provides a strong foundation for organizations to safely adopt agentic AI while maintaining continuous visibility, runtime monitoring, identity verification and control,” said Daniel Kroese, Vice President, Public Policy and Government Affairs, Palo Alto Networks

The Stop Rogue AI Act builds on Gottheimer’s work as Co-Chair of the House AI Commission and his bipartisan track record on AI safety and consumer protections. It comes as Congress and federal regulators face growing pressure to keep pace with the rapid development and deployment of autonomous AI systems.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Stop Rogue AI Agents and Keep People in Control

PHILADELPHIA – United States Attorney David Metcalf announced that DeWhite Dawkins, aka Dwight Dawkins, “Twin White,” and Kaleem Fraites, 42, a Jamaican national who has been unlawfully residing in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was sentenced this afternoon to 115 months in prison by United States District Judge Timothy J. Savage for illegally reentering the U.S. after the defendant’s 2023 deportation.

At a separate sentencing hearing this morning, Dawkins was sentenced to 92 months in prison by United States District Judge Kai N. Scott for bribing a postal carrier to deliver packages of marijuana.

The sentences will run concurrently, and after completing them, Dawkins will be removed from the U.S. once again.

As detailed in court filings and statements, for more than a year, Dawkins, a marijuana dealer, paid a United States Postal Service carrier substantial bribes to deliver Priority Mail packages that contained marijuana to him and an associate. He admitted that, in exchange for the bribes, the carrier delivered some 15 parcels containing approximately 237 pounds of marijuana in total, which were shipped from California to addresses on the postal carrier’s route in Levittown, Pennsylvania. The marijuana in the 15 parcels was valued at approximately $450,000.

The illegal reentry case was investigated by Immigration and Customs Enforcement and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Josh Davison.

The bribery case was investigated by the U.S. Postal Service Office of Inspector General, with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations and the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General, and prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Terri A. Marinari.
title: Jamaican National Sentenced to Over 9½ Years in Prison for Illegally Reentering the U.S.

U.S. Marshals, WV State Police Arrest 59 in Operation Coal Country
For immediate release
Mark Waggamon, Deputy U.S. Marshal
Charleston, WV - The U.S. Marshals Southern District of West Virginia CUFFED Task Force, in partnership with the West Virginia State Police (WVSP), have completed Operation Coal Country, a multi-week enforcement initiative targeting noncompliant sex offenders, individuals wanted for sex crimes, violent fugitives, and other wanted individuals throughout southern West Virginia.
Operation Coal Country began August 13 and concluded September 1. During the operation, law enforcement officers made 59 arrests. Of those arrested, 16 were registered sex offenders, while 10 additional individuals were arrested on warrants related to sex crimes. One missing child was also recovered during the operation.
The operation brought together federal, state, and local law enforcement resources in a coordinated effort to locate and apprehend fugitives while also conducting enforcement activities involving registered sex offenders.
Operation Coal Country focused heavily on sex offender compliance and fugitive apprehension throughout the West Virginia State Police Troop 5 area and surrounding communities. Investigators worked to identify registered sex offenders who were not complying with state and federal registration requirements and to locate individuals wanted for crimes involving sexual offenses.
During the operation, the West Virginia State Police conducted 383 sex offender compliance checks, finding 51 to be out of compliance of sex offender registration requirements. The West Virginia State Police also obtained 72 arrest warrants during the operation. Two sex offenders were also indicted in the Southern District of West Virginia for violations of the Adam Walsh Act from U.S. Marshals-led investigations.
In addition to sex offender and sex crime arrests, participating law enforcement agencies apprehended fugitives wanted for a variety of other felony offenses to include, murder, attempted murder, wanton endangerment, malicious wounding, strangulation, felon in possession of firearm, child neglect and various drug related felonies.
“The success of Operation Coal Country demonstrates what can be accomplished when federal, state, and local law enforcement agencies combine their resources toward a common mission,” said Marshal Jack Chambers, U.S. Marshal for the Southern District of West Virginia. “Fifty-nine arrests over the course of this operation means 59 wanted individuals were located and taken into custody. More importantly, this operation placed a significant emphasis on protecting our communities from individuals who have committed sex offenses or failed to comply with their registration requirements. The U.S. Marshals Service and West Virginia State Police will continue working together to investigate noncompliant sex offenders and apprehend dangerous fugitives throughout southern West Virginia.”
“Each arrest resulting from these targeted enforcement operations protects our communities and makes them safer,” said United States Attorney Moore Capito. “The success of this operation continues the momentum we’ve created through dedicated, collaborative, and aggressive efforts with our law enforcement partners.”
“When law enforcement works together, criminals have fewer places to hide,” said Colonel James Mitchell, superintendent of the West Virginia State Police. “Operation Coal Country shows the power of a coordinated, proactive approach to protecting our communities and holding offenders accountable. The West Virginia State Police is proud to stand with the U.S. Marshals Service and our law enforcement partners in doing everything we can to keep the people of West Virginia safe.”
Significant arrest includes:
Matthew Allen Waggle, 33, of Indian River County, FL was taken into custody on Aug. 19 in Dunbar, W.Va. Waggle was wanted for 1st Degree Murder by the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office in the shooting death of 52-year-old Dawn Kriskewic. Waggle was considered armed and dangerous.
Jonathan Gregory Bowersock, 35, of Cottonwood, Arizona, was taken into custody in Sedona, Arizona. Bowersock was wanted by the Parkersburg Police department. Between 2014-2020, Bowersock is alleged to have sexually abused a female juvenile family member.
Law Enforcement also made the following seizures:
•    74.1 grams Fentanyl 
•    3.4 pounds Methamphetamine 
•    33.3 grams Cocaine 
•    $6,000 in U.S. currency 
•    1 Firearm and assorted ammunition
The U.S. Marshals Service sex offender investigations mission is to protect the public from sex offenders through the coordinated enforcement of sex offender registration laws.
With the passage of the Adam Walsh Child Protection and Safety Act of 2006, the U.S. Marshals Service was designated as the lead federal agency to investigate violations of federal sex offender registration laws and to assist state, local, tribal and territorial jurisdictions in locating and apprehending sex offenders who fail to comply with their sex offender registration requirements. The Marshals collaborate with those partner agencies to aggressively investigate and pursue non-compliant offenders, placing the highest priority on those who have committed violent acts and crimes against children.
If anyone has information regarding the whereabouts of a wanted or noncompliant sex offender, tips can be submitted anonymously through the USMS Tips application or by calling 1-877-WANTED-2. Information may also be provided to the West Virginia State Police. Tips are kept confidential.
Members of the public can also access sex offender registry information through the National Sex Offender Public Website (NSOPW) at https://www.nsopw.gov and the West Virginia State Police Sex Offender Registry https://apps.wv.gov/StatePolice/SexOffender.

WORCESTER – Yesterday, Congressman Jim McGovern (MA-02), Ranking Member of the House Rules Committee and Co-Chair of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, alongside Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) visited the Worcester YMCA to discuss the historic 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act and how the new law will make it easier to build new housing, lower housing costs, and—for the first time ever—counter private equity from buying single-family homes.

The lawmakers also discussed the development of Grandfamily Villages, an effort by Senior Connection to provide affordable housing for seniors and their families in Worcester. They heard from families and community leaders about what more can be done to address the housing crisis in Massachusetts.

“The ROAD to Housing Act is a big deal for communities across the country,” said Congressman McGovern. “Everywhere I go, I hear from families struggling to find housing they can afford. I’m grateful to Senator Warren for her leadership in getting this important legislation passed. This is going to make a real difference for people across the Commonwealth and throughout the country. I’m also proud to be working alongside amazing partners like Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley on our Grandfamily Housing Act to make sure grandparents raising grandchildren have the support they need. These grandparents stepped up for their families, and we need to step up for them, too. That’s what the Grandfamily Village is all about, and I’ll keep fighting to get projects like this across the finish line.”

“America is in a housing crisis, and it’s hitting families hard here in Massachusetts. I’m proud to have worked with Congresswoman Pressley and Congressman McGovern to pass the biggest housing bill in decades into law,” said Senator Warren. “This new law will help lower housing costs and for the first time ever stop private equity from buying up single family homes. Thanks to the leadership of Congresswoman Pressley, the new law also includes an Innovation Fund which will help our state build more housing and upgrade our infrastructure. This is one step forward. We have much more work to do to lower costs for Massachusetts families.”

“I’m proud to work with Senator Warren and Ranking Member Waters to deliver this historic housing package to support safe, stable, and accessible housing for families in Massachusetts and throughout the country,” said Congresswoman Pressley. “The ROAD to Housing Act and my four bills within it will bring essential relief to Americans struggling amid Trump’s housing and affordability crises—and I’ll keep pushing to pass our Grandfamily Housing Act without delay. Every individual, family, and grandfamily deserves a place of refuge, rest, and peace. It’s time that we treat housing like human right that it is.”

Other participants of the roundtable included: State Senator Robyn Kennedy, State Representative David LeBoeuf, Worcester City Manager Eric Batista, Moses Dixon, President & CEO, Senior Connection, Joanne Calista, CEO, Center for Health Impact, and several grandparents raising their grandchildren.

McGovern has worked for years to support grandparents raising grandchildren and address the unique housing challenges facing grandfamilies.

He recently secured $1.2 million in federal funding for a Grandparents Raising Grandkids Resource Center in Worcester to help connect grandparent-led households throughout central Massachusetts with housing, transportation, health, food, education and other services.

In 2018, his bipartisan Supporting Grandparents Raising Grandchildren Act was signed into law, creating a federal advisory council to identify and share resources for grandparents and other relatives raising children.

In 2019, after McGovern and Pressley held a roundtable in Worcester to hear directly from grandparents about the challenges they face, the lawmakers introduced the Grandfamily Housing Act, which would help grandfamilies access safe, affordable and age-appropriate housing and supportive services. They reintroduced the legislation in 2021, and it passed the House in 2022.

McGovern and Pressley introduced the latest version, H.R. 5916, the Grandfamily Housing Act of 2025, in November 2025.

###
title: McGovern, Warren, Pressley Tout Historic New Law to Combat High Cost of Housing in America

BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Martino Carter, 39, of Sloan, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District judge Lawrence J. Davis, II.

The group includes both Democratic and Republican lawmakers from the House and Senate

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Pat Ryan joined current and former Members of Congress in challenging the legality of President Donald Trump’s Executive Order seeking to exert control over mail-in ballots ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

The group, made up of a bipartisan, bicameral coalition of 261 lawmakers, filed an amicus brief to the Supreme Court of the United States in the matter of United States Postal Service, et al., v. State of California, et al., a lawsuit brought by a coalition of State Attorneys General against the U.S. Postal Service. The court case challenges a Final Rule issued by the USPS pursuant to Trump’s directive that imposes unconstitutional and unworkable restrictions on mail-in voting, including requiring states to provide a “citizenship verification list” and attempting to give USPS control over who can vote by mail.

“Trump’s second term has been defined by crushing cost increases, a war in Iran – which has cost us billions in taxpayer dollars and the lives of 18 brave Patriots – and slashing critical programs our community relies on like SNAP and Medicaid,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “That’s not a winning message, and Trump knows it. Instead of lowering costs and ending the war, Trump – who consistently votes by mail!– is trying to silence the American people ahead of the midterm elections. It’s a pathetic, illegal move – and it won’t work. The Supreme Court must block this disastrous, un-American, unconstitutional order. Your voice is your vote, and we won’t let anyone take it away.”

One-third of Americans are expected to vote by mail in the upcoming midterm elections—a voting practice Donald Trump himself used as recently as August 2026, when the president voted in Florida’s Republican primary.

In the court filing, the amici curiae argue that Trump’s Executive Order 14399, “Ensuring Citizenship Verification and Integrity in Federal Elections,” violates the separation of powers and usurps congressional authorities outlined in Article I of the U.S. Constitution, which gives the states and Congress exclusive authority over election administration.

“As current and former legislators, amici took an oath to uphold and defend the Constitution of the United States—including its guarantee of the separation of powers. Amici have a particular interest in defending the institutional role of the Legislative Branch under Article I of the Constitution and in vindicating the long-settled principle that the Constitution commits ultimate regulatory authority over federal elections to Congress. The Constitution does not contemplate the Executive Branch acting unilaterally to assert power over federal elections. Yet that is what the Order and Final Rule do,” wrote the lawmakers.

The amici also pointed to a recent federal court ruling blocking the USPS from implementing its newly finalized mail ballot rule for the midterm elections, saying the agency lacked the authority to implement the rule and that its actions are “substantively unconstitutional and contrary to law.”

“The district court correctly concluded that Appellees are likely to succeed on the merits of their claims that USPS lacked authority to issue the Final Rule, that the Final Rule unconstitutionally imposes mail-ballot requirements on the States, and that the Final Rule unconstitutionally bars non-compliant State and local election officials from using the USPS to mail ballots at all.”

The group concluded by asserting States’ power to administer elections and Congress’s power to make or alter rules regulating elections, which the Supreme Court itself has described as an “override” authority. The president’s illegal incursion on this authority is an attempt to disenfranchise people who depend on mail-in ballots to vote.

The lawmakers concluded: “The integrity of our constitutional system depends on each branch keeping to its assigned role. The Framers set up a two-part system that gave the States default authority to regulate federal elections subject to Congress’s authority to override the States. The Framers did not provide the President with any authority to interfere in that system, nor has Congress imbued the Executive Branch with any such authority by statute.”

Click HERE to view the full brief.

The effort was led by House Administration Ranking Member Joe Morelle; Assistant House Minority Leader Joe Neguse, who leads the House Democrats’ Litigation Task Force; and Task Force Co-Chairs Oversight Ranking Member Robert Garcia and Judiciary Ranking Member Jamie Raskin. In the Senate, the brief was championed by Rules Committee Ranking Member Alex Padilla; Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer; Senate Judiciary Committee Ranking Member Dick Durbin; and Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee Ranking Member Gary Peters.

“Presidents do not control our elections—the American people do. Today, in a bipartisan agreement, Members defended the constitutional authority of Congress and deliberately chose to protect our elections from executive overreach. Our elections are safe and secure, and we intend to keep them that way. We will not allow USPS to put Americans’ ballots at risk,” said Ranking Member Joe Morelle.

“The law is clear: states and Congress have authority over our elections — not the President and certainly not the Postal Service. Protecting the right to vote-by-mail is critical to ensure every eligible voter can make their voices heard in the November midterm elections and in future elections,” said Senator Alex Padilla. “Despite the Trump Administration’s attempts to eliminate vote by mail and suppress voter participation, voting by mail remains one of the most safe and secure ways to vote, especially for service members, rural voters, and Americans living abroad. I urge the courts to uphold our Constitution and reject Trump’s attacks on our fundamental right to vote."

“Donald Trump is trying to unconstitutionally rig the midterm elections because he knows that's the only way he can hold on to power. This scheme could potentially stop millions of American citizens from receiving their ballots and having their vote counted. We are fighting this in court and defending the Constitution,” said Ranking Member Robert Garcia.

“Donald Trump’s attacks on mail-in voting are in direct contravention of the U.S. Constitution. His executive order and the USPS actions to implement it would disenfranchise millions of Americans, silencing an untold number of citizens that rely on mail ballots to make their voices heard. But the right to vote is sacrosanct, and we’ll do whatever it takes to protect it,” said House Assistant Minority Leader Joe Neguse. “I’m proud to see the outpouring of support from current and former Members of Congress—across the political spectrum—to assert the rule of law in this matter and to stand up for the right of every eligible voter to fairly cast their ballot.”

“The Constitution is clear that the states and Congress make the rules for federal elections, not the President. Yet, in utter defiance of the Constitution, President Trump is attempting to use the Postal Service to decide who can and cannot receive a ballot just days before mail-in voting begins in some of the states. This is a naked power grab by a historically unpopular President—who himself regularly votes by mail—to inject confusion and chaos into our elections in a last-ditch effort to keep his party in power. It will not work. I’m proud to stand with a strong bipartisan, bicameral group of current and former colleagues in urging the court to continue rejecting this lawless election interference,” said Ranking Member Jamie Raskin.

“Donald Trump is once again asking the highest court in the land to silence voters and destroy the precious integrity of the American electoral process,” said Leader Schumer. “Mail-in voting is proven safe and secure, and Trump’s continued efforts to obstruct America’s free and fair elections are blatant, unconstitutional attempts at interfering with the November midterms. Trump’s message to the American people is clear: he isn’t worried about voter fraud, he’s afraid of voter accountability. I urge the court to uphold the Constitution and reject Trump’s baseless attempt at poisoning our democracy.”

###
title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN, OVER 250 CURRENT & FORMER MEMBERS OF CONGRESS URGE SUPREME COURT TO BLOCK TRUMP’S EXECUTIVE ORDER LIMITING MAIL VOTING

The Federal Trade Commission rescinded the 2021 Policy Statement on Breaches by Health Apps and Other Connected Devices.
This controversial policy statement purported to apply the FTC’s Health Breach Notification Rule to health apps and connected devices that collect consumer health information. In 2024, however, the Commission updated the Health Breach Notification Rule to cover health apps and connected devices like fitness trackers, rendering the policy statement unnecessary.
In an executive order, President Donald J. Trump directed agencies to eliminate not just unnecessary rules, but also obsolete guidance documents and policy statements because they contribute to the “ever-expanding morass of complicated Federal regulation” without providing any benefit to American consumers.
The Federal Trade Commission works to promote competition and protect and educate consumers. The FTC will never demand money, make threats, tell you to transfer money, or promise you a prize. Learn more about consumer topics at consumer.ftc.gov, or report fraud, scams, and bad business practices at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Follow the FTC on social media, read consumer alerts and the business blog, and sign up to get the latest FTC news and alerts.

CHICAGO — Today, Congressmembers Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05), and Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), joined by a coalition of local elected officials including State Senator Celina Villanueva, State Representative Edgar Gonzalez Jr, Cook County Commissioner Alma Anaya, Alderperson Michael Rodriguez, Alderperson Jessie Fuentes, and immigration advocacy organizations, including Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) and The Resurrection Project (TRP), held a press conference to mark one year of resistance to Operation Midway Blitz.

The coalition called for action on immigration reform, including by forcing a vote on the Dream and Promise Act, and demanded full accountability from local and federal authorities, including the Cook County State’s Attorney, for the brutality and terror inflicted by the federal government’s immigration enforcement actions on communities throughout the region.

“A year ago, the Trump administration tried to break us and take away our dignity by sending masked federal agents into our city through Operation Midway Blitz. They failed, and instead our community came together, stood up and challenged their abuse of power,” said Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García. “One year later, we are more united than ever. But the fight is not over. Masked federal agents continue to operate in our neighborhoods, and we will keep demanding that they leave and that those responsible for their crimes be held accountable. Most importantly, we will continue fighting for meaningful immigration reform so that no community has to endure the failures of our broken immigration system again.”

"We are commemorating the one-year anniversary of Midway Blitz, when the Department of Homeland Security began a campaign of terror in Chicago. Those of us who lived through its terror are clear: DHS REMAINS the biggest threat to our collective safety," said Congresswoman Delia Ramirez. "As we regain the majority next year, our grief, our anger, and our calls for justice must move us to action that honors all those stolen from us by DHS, by holding EVERY fascist who has permitted and profited from DHS’s violence accountable, by abolishing ICE, and by dismantling DHS."

"Donald Trump's Operation Midway Blitz had one goal and one goal only: to terrorize Chicago. ICE and CBP agents didn't go after the worst of the worst, they kidnapped people off the streets, tear gassed elementary schools, and killed a father of two," said Congressman Mike Quigley. "Unfortunately, the horror of Trump's immigration policies didn't end with Operation Midway Blitz. Just last month, I attended a deportation hearing where I saw children in court without their parents, facing a language barrier, and being asked to explain why they deserve to stay in this country. This cruelty must be stopped. I'm more committed than ever to working with my colleagues and advocates to protect our immigrant neighbors and stop Trump’s DHS in its tracks before they can do any more harm."

“One year after Operation Midway Blitz, we remember the harm caused by this authoritarian operation, but we also honor the faith leaders, community organizers, attorneys, educators, and ordinary Chicagoans who stepped up to protect their neighbors and defend the values that make our city strong,” said Congressman Jonathan Jackson. “I will continue to demand accountability for the abuses inflicted on immigrants and our communities. I stand with my Congressional colleagues in renewing our call for comprehensive immigration reform rooted in the fundamental belief that every person deserves dignity, equity, and due process.”

“This week marks the one-year anniversary of Operation Midway Blitz, and Chicago residents are still reeling from the horrors our communities have been forced to face, as masked officers continue to wreak havoc across our city by taking countless residents into custody and dismantling families left and right,” said State Senator Celina Villanueva. “Since the operation was launched last September, Latino communities, especially those I represent, have lived in constant fear – afraid of leaving their homes and sending their children to school. After a year of brutalizing protestors, patrolling city streets, raiding our neighborhoods and harming our residents, it is far beyond time to demand accountability and justice from this administration, not only for Latino Illinoisans but also for everyone who has been impacted by these senseless acts of hate.”

“Operation Midway Blitz did not break our community, it strengthened our resolve. For a year, our immigrant families, neighbors, and community organizations have stood together against fear and intimidation. We will continue to defend every family and protect the welcoming spirit that defines our community,” said 22 Ward Alderperson Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Whether it be the apartment raids in South Shore, the shooting of Marimar Martinez in Brighton Park, or the murder of Silverio Villegas González, it’s been proven that ICE does NOT keep us safe - they are designed to intimidate communities of color and deport as many people as possible…Local leaders and politicians must stand with immigrants and enforce the laws and policies our communities fought for to make Illinois a welcoming place for all, said Lawrence Benitio, Executive Director, ICIRR.

“Operation Midway Blitz isn’t over - we’re still reeling from the impact of thousands of neighbors being stripped from our community. Families separated. Jobs lost. Communities destabilized. Yet, through it all, our community keeps showing up and fighting back. We refuse to let this terror be normalized,” said Any Huamami, Director of Organizing, Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“On this day, last year our communities were being terrorized by masked agents, kidnapped without explanation, and families have been forcibly broken by this federal administration’s immigration enforcement campaign. Last year showed us we were all at risk of being detained only based on what we look like. Unlawful arrests became the norm, but we are still here exposing those actions and reminding people that ICE is still in our communities. It is our duty to continue to be vigilant and protect each other,” said Antonio Gutierrez, Co-Founder and Strategic Coordinator, Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“Chicago's Northwest Side was one of the concentration points for Operation Midway Blitz. Local community members came together to fight back against this attack on our community as part of the statewide network of rapid responders anchored by ICIRR. Our work did not end when Midway Blitz concluded. We continue to see daily ICE abductions and assaults in our neighborhoods to this day. Community members will continue doing their part to keep us safe. It is now long overdue for police departments locally to do their job, and investigate the actions of these agents, so we can hold them to account. It's the least that our community members and neighbors who were tear gassed, pepper sprayed and faced assault and aggression from the federal government deserve,” said Pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, Board President, PLSNA.

“The fear that swept through our communities is real, but this year wasn’t defined by fear, but by the beauty and resilience of our community. The Trump administration set out to make an example of Chicago. Instead, we led by example—building a statewide coordinated response that has connected tens of thousands of community members to legal support, and a rapid response network that shows that immigrants across Illinois never stand alone, said Eréndira Rendón, Vice President of Immigrant Justice, The Resurrection Project.

Read an op-ed by Congressman García about Operation Midway Blitz, HERE.

The Institute of Museum and Library Services is Accepting Fiscal Year 2027 Grant Applications to Strengthen America’s Cultural Heritage
Institutions across America are encouraged to apply by November 13.
WASHINGTON, DC — The Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS), the leading source of federal funding for America’s museums and libraries, is now accepting applications for its Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 discretionary grant programs.
After supporting many projects related to the 250th anniversary of American independence in 2026, the agency looks forward to building on the renewed appreciation for American history, culture, and innovation. To accomplish this goal, IMLS is investing in eligible institutions that serve communities of all sizes because America’s story is worth knowing, its history is worth preserving, and its communities are worth supporting.
Museums, libraries, historical societies, and other cultural institutions preserve the stories of American communities by safeguarding the objects and knowledge that open the doors of discovery to every generation.
To further this important work, IMLS is offering 13 funding opportunities to organizations across the United States to ensure America’s extraordinary cultural, historical, and natural heritage remains celebrated and accessible to the American people.
Eligible institutions in all 50 states, Washington, D.C., U.S. territories, and freely associated states are encouraged to apply. Applications are due on November 13, 2026. To receive updates and reminders, subscribe to IMLS grant newsletters.
Library Grant Programs:
Libraries are among America’s great institutions of learning and civic life. They open doors to knowledge, preserve the written record of our civilization, and give Americans opportunities to learn, discover, and participate fully in their communities.
- Laura Bush 21st Century Librarian Program invests in the professionals who keep America’s libraries and archives strong by equipping the next generation of librarians and the library workforce with the knowledge, skills, and training meet the needs of their communities and steward our nation’s intellectual heritage.
- National Leadership Grants for Libraries support innovative ideas and proven model programs that enhance the quality of library and archive services nationwide, expand library users’ access to knowledge, and ensure that Americans have the tools they need to learn, discover, and thrive.
- Native American Library Services: Basic Grants help Native communities build and sustain strong library services that preserve and share local knowledge and connect tribes with the resources they need.
- Native American Library Services: Enhancement Grants support Native communities in strengthening library services that reflect their unique histories, knowledge, and traditions.
- Native Hawaiian Library Services Grants strengthen Native Hawaiian organizations as centers of knowledge, learning, and community life.
Museum Grant Programs:
America’s museums and cultural institutions preserve the knowledge, achievements, relics, objects, works of art, and natural beauty that allow every generation of Americans to celebrate their history and understand the world around them.
- 21st Century Museum Professionals Program invests in the professionals entrusted with America’s museums by building career pathways and developing the museum workforce to enable them to meet identified needs of their communities.
- Inspire Grants for Small Museums support small museums of all disciplines, including small rural institutions and small museums that have not previously received federal funding, through project-based efforts to serve their communities through educational programs and exhibits, community partnerships, and collections stewardship.
- Museum Grants for African American History and Culture strengthen museums that share the history, achievements, experiences, and enduring contributions of African Americans to the American story.
- Museum Grants for American Latino History and Culture support the capacity of museums that share American Latino history and strengthen the institutions that connect these stories to communities across the nation.
- Museums Empowered equips museum professionals with the knowledge and training to strengthen their institutions, cultivate excellence, and better serve the public.
- Museums for America invests in museums of every size and discipline so they can preserve their collections, educate the public, strengthen their communities, and make America’s rich cultural heritage accessible to all.
- National Leadership Grants for Museums support projects that address the most important challenges facing America’s museums, strengthen the museum profession, and ensure that museums remain trusted places of learning, stewardship, and public service.
- Native American/Native Hawaiian Museum Services support Native American Tribes, Alaska Native Villages, and organizations that primarily serve and represent Native Hawaiians in preserving and sharing their heritage, culture, knowledge, and traditions for generations to come.
title: The Institute of Museum and Library Services is Accepting Fiscal Year 2027 Grant Applications to Strengthen America’s Cultural Heritage

MEDIA ADVISORY: Coast Guard to honor 9/11 hero with commissioning of Fast Response Cutter Jeffrey Palazzo in New York
            
            NEW YORK — The Coast Guard is scheduled to hold a commissioning ceremony for Coast Guard Cutter Jeffrey Palazzo, Sept. 12, 2026.
WHO: Adm. Kevin Lunday, commandant of the Coast Guard, presiding official
WHAT: Commissioning ceremony for the Coast Guard’s 63rd Fast Response Cutter, Jeffrey Palazzo.
WHEN: Saturday, Sept. 12, 2026 at 12:00 PM - 2:00 PM
WHERE: Intrepid Museum and Pier 86 located in Hudson River Park at 46th Street and 12th Avenue in Manhattan, New York and streamed online @uscgnortheast Facebook page.

Each Fast Response Cutter is named after an enlisted U.S. Coast Guard hero who performed extraordinary service in the line of duty. Jeffrey Palazzo of Rescue Company 5 was a New York City firefighter and U.S. Coast Guard reservist who made the ultimate sacrifice on Sept. 11, 2001, while responding to the attacks on the World Trade Center. Palazzo served in the Coast Guard Reserves as a Machinery Technician 1st Class aboard Coast Guard Cutter Cape Horn out of Station Rockaway, responding to many high-profile incidents and large-scale emergencies.

WASHINGTON, DC — Como parte de su agenda para priorizar lo básico y atender la crisis de agua en Puerto Rico, el Comisionado Residente, Pablo José Hernández, solicitó al Senado que mantenga en la versión final de la legislación federal de infraestructura de agua varios proyectos y prioridades para Puerto Rico que ya fueron aprobados por la Cámara de Representantes.

Las prioridades ya están incluidas en la versión de la Ley de Desarrollo de Recursos Hídricos, conocida como el Water Resources Development Act (WRDA) de 2026 de la Cámara de Representantes, que avanzó en comité, y Hernández está trabajando para que se mantengan durante las negociaciones con el Senado y lleguen a la versión final.

“Mi agenda de priorizar lo básico se trata de conseguir resultados en los problemas que afectan a nuestra gente todos los días. Puerto Rico necesita mejor infraestructura de agua, comunidades más protegidas de las inundaciones y acción para nuestras costas. Ya estamos avanzando estas prioridades en la Cámara y ahora estoy trabajando para asegurar que lleguen a la meta,” expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Entre las medidas que el Comisionado Residente busca asegurar se encuentran hasta $75 millones para proyectos de infraestructura de agua y ambiental en Puerto Rico, $10 millones para agua y alcantarillado en Corozal y nuevos estudios de impacto para el proyecto de control de inundaciones del Río Puerto Nuevo en San Juan, de manera que se puedan atender las preocupaciones de las comunidades aledañas.

También está defendiendo nuevos estudios para proyectos de control de inundaciones, protección costera y daños por tormentas en Ceiba, Fajardo, Loíza, Naguabo, Humacao, Vega Baja y Yabucoa.

###

Rep. Hernández Pushes Water Projects for Puerto Rico

Resident Commissioner seeks to secure projects for Corozal, San Juan, and seven municipalities as part of his agenda to prioritize the basics

WASHINGTON, DC — As part of his agenda to prioritize the basics and address the water crisis in Puerto Rico, Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández asked the Senate to maintain, in the final version of federal water infrastructure legislation, several projects and priorities for Puerto Rico that have already been approved by the House of Representatives.

The priorities are already included in the House version of the Water Resources Development Act, known as the 2026 Water Resources Development Act (WRDA), which advanced in committee, and Hernández is working to ensure they remain during negotiations with the Senate and make it into the final version.

“My agenda to prioritize the basics is about delivering results on the problems that affect our people every day. Puerto Rico needs better water infrastructure, communities better protected from flooding, and action for our coasts. We are already advancing these priorities in the House, and now I am working to make sure they reach the finish line,” said the Resident Commissioner.

Among the measures the Resident Commissioner seeks to secure are up to $75 million for water and environmental infrastructure projects in Puerto Rico, $10 million for water and sewer infrastructure in Corozal, and new impact studies for the Río Puerto Nuevo flood control project in San Juan, so that the concerns of neighboring communities can be addressed.

He is also advocating for new studies for flood control, coastal protection, and storm damage projects in Ceiba, Fajardo, Loíza, Naguabo, Humacao, Vega Baja, and Yabucoa.
title: Comisionado Impulsa Proyectos de Agua para Puerto Rico.

On September 3, 2026, members of the Robertson County Sheriff’s Office, ATF, Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), and United States Marshals Service conducted a coordinated operation to execute federal arrest warrants. Six of the indicted defendants were arrested during the operation. An additional defendant was located in Ohio the following day and remains in custody there on state warrants. Five defendants were already in custody on other charges and are expected to make appearances in federal court later this month.

“Cocaine and crack cocaine poison neighborhoods, and the firearms that travel with them turn drug deals into shootings,” said United States Attorney Braden H. Boucek. “For more than two years, the Robertson County Sheriff’s Office and ATF built this case one transaction at a time, and today a dozen alleged traffickers are facing federal charges because of that work. This office will use every tool the law gives us to dismantle drug networks in Middle Tennessee, and we are grateful to our partners at every level of law enforcement who made this operation possible.”

Washington D.C. - New Dem Members hosted a roundtable with housing policy experts and industry representatives to solicit ideas on what Congress’s next steps should be to address the affordable housing crisis. New Dem Housing, Infrastructure, & Transportation Working Group Chair Norma Torres (CA-35), New Dem Vice Chair for Outreach Salud Carbajal (CA-24) and Housing Task Force Chair Emilia Sykes (OH-13) hosted the roundtable. They were joined by 14 additional New Dem Members and eight stakeholders for the discussion.

“Getting the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into law was an important step forward, but the lasting impact of this law will depend on how effectively we put it into practice," said Rep. Norma Torres. "It's also critical that we look at what's next, which is why we put together this roundtable to hear from experts, stakeholders, and Coalition Members to kickstart work on further policy changes we need to make homes more affordable for our constituents."

“New Dems are leading the charge to address our nationwide housing crisis. In the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, roughly half of the provisions were sponsored by New Dems or priorities from our Housing Affordability Agenda. While this law represents significant progress, our work is far from complete,” said Rep. Salud Carbajal, New Dem Vice Chair for Outreach. This week’s roundtable gave us an opportunity to engage with housing stakeholders and map out the next steps needed to build on the momentum we’ve created.”

"As Chair of the Housing Task Force, I've seen firsthand how the affordable housing crisis touches every part of our country," saidRep. Emilia Sykes. "We achieved great wins in the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, including provisions from my HOMES Act to rein in corporate investors who are pricing working families out of their own neighborhoods. But there's more to do. This roundtable was about listening to the people building, financing, and studying housing every day, so we can turn their expertise into the next set of solutions Congress delivers."

This roundtable continues the discussion around affordable housing solutions following successful passage of the 21st Century Road to Housing Act earlier this year. This landmark housing package contained provisions from 22 New Dem Member-led bills and two New Dem proposals and delivered on many of the key objectives laid out in the New Democrat Coalition’s Housing Affordability Agenda.

New Dem Members’ work to address the affordable housing crisis has become a cornerstone of our efforts this Congress. This roundtable expanded these efforts and was an opportunity for Members and guests to discuss what Congress needs to do next to build more homes quickly, expand access to affordable housing, make it easier for families to finance their homes, and more.

NEW ORLEANS - On August 21, 2026, United States District Judge Darrel James Papillion entered a Final Order of Forfeiture in United States v. Jamie P. McNamara (“ MCNAMARA ”), Criminal Docket No. 22-151, requiring the forfeiture of over $7 million dollars in criminally derived funds, and 3 luxury vehicles, announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle.

MCNAMARA plead guilty on May 29, 2026, to conspiracy to commit health care fraud, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 1349 and 1347, and was sentenced to ten years in prison on October 23, 2025.

According to court documents, MCNAMARA operated several laboratories in Louisiana and Texas, which obtained fraudulent doctors’ orders for genetic testing from telemarketers and call centers that used aggressive telemarketing campaigns to induce Medicare beneficiaries to agree to receive genetic testing. Orders for genetic testing were signed by purported telemedicine doctors who were not the beneficiaries’ treating physicians, did not perform consultations with the beneficiaries, and did not follow up with the beneficiaries after the testing was performed. To obtain the orders, MCNAMARA paid illegal kickbacks and bribes, which he disguised through sham contracts. In furtherance of the scheme, he also shifted the billing between his laboratories to evade scrutiny from Medicare and law enforcement and concealed his ownership and control of the laboratories by falsely listing the names of his family members as owners and company representatives on Medicare and other documents. In approximately one and a half years, the laboratories operated by MCNAMARA submitted over $174 million in claims to Medicare for genetic testing and received over $55 million in reimbursements.

Before MCNAMARA was indicted, law enforcement officers seized several of his assets that had been purchased with the proceeds of his scheme. In its recent order, the Court ordered the forfeiture of the contents of an investment account and a bank account held in the name of a company controlled by MCNAMARA , along with three vehicles purchased with proceeds of the offense, namely, a Land Rover Range Rover, a BMW, and a Ford F-150. In total, the forfeited accounts contained a value totaling approximately $7,051,089.08.

Asset forfeiture is a law enforcement tool that allows the United States to take property derived from, or used to commit, federal crimes. It is designed to strip criminals of the proceeds of their offenses, remove the instruments used to carry them out, and- where victims can be identified- return recovered funds to the people who were harmed.

U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle praised the work of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services – Office of Inspector General and the Federal Bureau of Investigation. Assistant United States Attorney, Alexandra Giavotella, Asset Forfeiture Coordinator, handled the forfeiture component. Assistant Chief Justin M. Woodard and Trial Attorney Kelly Z. Walters of the Criminal Division’s Fraud Division and Assistant U.S. Attorney Nicholas Moses for the Eastern District of Louisiana prosecuted the case.

On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”). The Fraud Division is laser-focused on investigating and prosecuting those who commit fraud against the American people. The Department’s work to combat fraud supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government effort chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance to eliminate fraud, waste, and abuse within Federal benefit programs.
title: Federal Court Orders Forfeiture of Approximately $7 Million and Three Vehicles Following Conviction of Jamie P. McNamara

CNO, MCPON Visit Sailors in Mayport, Kings Bay
09 September 2026
                            MAYPORT, Fla. – Chief of Naval Operations Adm. Daryl Caudle and Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy John Perryman visited Sailors and commands in Mayport, Florida, and Kings Bay, Georgia, Sept. 9, reinforcing the Navy’s focus on warfighting readiness, Sailors and the forces charged with defending the nation at sea.
Caudle and Perryman began the day at the headquarters of U.S. Naval Forces Southern Command/U.S. 4th Fleet, where they met with command leadership and spoke with more than 400 Sailors during an all-hands call.
The visit provided the Navy’s senior uniformed and enlisted leaders an opportunity to hear directly from Sailors while discussing the Navy’s role in defending the homeland, strengthening partnerships and maintaining combat-ready forces capable of responding wherever and whenever the nation requires.
“Every Sailor in this room contributes to the combat power of our Navy,” Caudle said. “Our nation depends on us to be ready to fight and win at sea, and that readiness starts with disciplined, well-trained Sailors who understand the importance of their mission. What you do every day matters to the security of our nation.”
U.S. Naval Forces Southern Command/U.S. 4th Fleet conducts maritime operations in support of U.S. Southern Command and works with regional maritime partners throughout the Caribbean, Central America and South America to strengthen security and interoperability.
While in Mayport, Caudle and Perryman also visited the crew of the Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS Thomas Hudner (DDG 116), which recently returned to its homeport following an almost nine-month deployment spanning three numbered fleet areas of operation.
During the deployment, Thomas Hudner operated in the U.S. 4th, 5th and 6th Fleet areas of operation, taking the ship and crew from the Caribbean to the Mediterranean and Red seas. The demanding deployment demonstrated the ability of Navy ships and Sailors to move rapidly between theaters and provide combatant commanders with ready, flexible naval forces.
Caudle and Perryman thanked the crew for their service and recognized the sacrifices made by the ship’s Sailors and their families during the extended deployment.
“What this crew accomplished is exactly why our Navy remains the finest fighting force in the world,” Caudle said. “You took this ship across three fleets, operated in some of the world’s most consequential waters and answered every task the nation gave you. That is what readiness looks like, and America is proud of you.”
Perryman emphasized the people behind the ship’s operational accomplishments.
“A warship is steel, weapons and technology, but Sailors are what make it a fighting force,”
Perryman said. “You spent months away from your families, stood the watch day after day and represented our Navy and our nation around the world. That kind of service deserves our utmost gratitude and respect.”
Following their engagements in Mayport, Caudle and Perryman traveled to Naval Submarine Base Kings Bay, Georgia, home to the Navy’s East Coast sea-based strategic deterrent force.
There, they met with leadership and Sailors assigned to Commander, Submarine Group 10 and held their second all-hands call of the day.
Submarine Group 10 leads and synchronizes the efforts of “Team Kings Bay,” ensuring submarines and their crews are properly manned, trained, equipped and certified to conduct operations around the world. The mission is central to one of the Navy’s most consequential responsibilities: maintaining the nation’s survivable sea-based nuclear deterrent.
“Strategic deterrence is a no-fail mission, and the Sailors of Team Kings Bay carry an extraordinary responsibility on behalf of our nation,” Caudle said. “Every time one of our ballistic-missile submarines goes to sea, it reminds our allies, our partners and anyone who might threaten us that the United States is ready, capable and resolute. You stand a silent watch, but the message you send is unmistakable.”
During the Kings Bay visit, Caudle and Perryman also toured modification to the waterfront and training facilities in preparations for the arrival of the Columbia-class ballistic-missile submarine program. The Columbia class will replace the Navy’s Ohio-class ballistic-missile submarines and serve as the sea-based leg of the nation’s nuclear triad well into the second half of the century.
Kings Bay is simultaneously sustaining the Ohio-class force while preparing the installation, workforce and support infrastructure for the arrival of the Columbia class — a transition critical to maintaining uninterrupted strategic deterrence.
“The Columbia class represents an investment not just in a new submarine, but in the security of generations of Americans who will follow us,” Caudle said. “We have an obligation to get this transition right, because credible sea-based strategic deterrence has helped keep our nation safe for decades, and it must continue to do so for decades to come.”
Perryman said the transition also highlights the enduring importance of the Navy’s people.
“We can build the most advanced submarine in the world, but it will still take talented, dedicated American Sailors to take her to sea,” Perryman said. “Technology changes. Platforms change. But our greatest advantage has always been our people — Sailors who raise their right hand, serve something bigger than themselves and stand the watch so their fellow Americans can sleep safely at night.”
The Mayport and Kings Bay stops continued a series of fleet engagements by Caudle and Perryman focused on connecting senior Navy leadership directly with Sailors and assessing the people, training, infrastructure and operational forces that generate Navy readiness.
For Caudle, the visits also underscored the connection between the Sailors serving at sea today and the Navy being built for tomorrow — from a destroyer recently returned from operations across three fleets to the submarine force preparing for the next generation of strategic deterrence.
“For 250 years, American Sailors have stood the watch, defended our freedom and carried our flag across the world’s oceans,” Caudle said. “Today that watch belongs to us. We owe the American people a Navy that is ready when called, lethal when challenged and worthy of the trust they place in us. Looking at the Sailors I met today, I know that watch is in good hands.”
Built in the Foundry – Tempered in the Fleet – Forged to Fight.
title: CNO, MCPON Visit Sailors in Mayport, Kings Bay

BLM Welcomes Community Perspectives on Proposed Colorado Parcels for March 2027 Oil and Gas Lease Sale
Organization:
Media Contact:
LAKEWOOD, Colo. – The Bureau of Land Management is proposing to offer 38 oil and gas parcels in Colorado, totaling about 66,221 acres, in a March 2027 federal lease sale. The public is invited to provide initial input on this proposal during a 30-day scoping period that closes Oct. 9.
This effort is part of the BLM’s commitment to managing federal energy resources in a transparent and balanced way that considers community needs, national energy priorities, and protection of natural and cultural resources.
Federal oil and gas leasing helps strengthen U.S. energy security, supports jobs and local economies, and generates revenue that is shared with states and counties to fund schools, roads, and other essential public services.
Partnership with the public is central to how the BLM manages public lands. Community perspectives help shape how potential lease areas are evaluated and ensure that future development—if pursued—supports national energy needs while protecting wildlife habitat, water resources, cultural sites, and recreation areas that Coloradans and visitors value.
Leasing is the first step in the process to develop federal oil and gas resources. Before development operations can begin, an operator must submit an application for permit to drill detailing development plans. The BLM reviews applications for permits to drill, posts them for public review, conducts an environmental analysis and coordinates with state partners and stakeholders.
All parcels that are included in a federal oil and gas lease sale include appropriate stipulations to protect important natural resources. Maps, parcel details, and instructions for providing comments are available on the BLM National NEPA Register.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: BLM Welcomes Community Perspectives on Proposed Colorado Parcels for March 2027 Oil and Gas Lease Sale

CHICAGO — Hoy, los miembros del Congreso Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Mike Quigley (IL-05) y Jonathan Jackson (IL-01) —acompañados por una coalición de funcionarios electos locales, entre ellos la senadora estatal Celina Villanueva, el representante estatal Edgar Gonzalez Jr., la comisionada del condado de Cook Alma Anaya y los concejales Michael Rodriguez y Jessie Fuentes, así como organizaciones defensoras de los inmigrantes como Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights (ICIRR), Brighton Park Neighborhood Council (BPNC), Organized Communities Against Deportations (OCAD) y The Resurrection Project (TRP) — ofrecieron una conferencia de prensa para marcar un año de resistencia frente a la Operación Midway Blitz.

La coalición instó a tomar medidas en materia de reforma migratoria, incluyendo la exigencia de una votación sobre la Ley Sueño y Promesa (Dream and Promise Act), y reclamó plena rendición de cuentas por parte de las autoridades locales y federales —incluida la Fiscal Estatal del condado de Cook— ante la brutalidad y el terror que las acciones de control migratorio del gobierno federal han infligido a las comunidades de toda la región.

“Hace un año, la administración Trump intentó quebrantarnos y arrebatarnos la dignidad enviando a agentes federales enmascarados a nuestra ciudad mediante la Operación Midway Blitz. Fracasaron; en su lugar, nuestra comunidad se unió, alzó la voz y desafió su abuso de poder”, declaró el Congresista Jesús “Chuy” García. “Un año después, estamos más unidos que nunca. Pero la lucha no ha terminado. Los agentes federales enmascarados siguen operando en nuestros vecindarios, y continuaremos exigiendo que se marchen y que los responsables de sus crímenes rindan cuentas. Y lo que es más importante: seguiremos luchando por una reforma migratoria significativa para que ninguna comunidad tenga que volver a sufrir las consecuencias de nuestro sistema migratorio fallido”.

“Conmemoramos el primer aniversario de Midway Blitz, cuando el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) inició una campaña de terror en Chicago. Quienes vivimos ese terror lo tenemos claro: el DHS SIGUE SIENDO la mayor amenaza para nuestra seguridad colectiva”, afirmó la Congresista Delia Ramirez. “Al recuperar la mayoría en el Congreso el próximo año, nuestro dolor, nuestra indignación y nuestras exigencias de justicia deben impulsarnos a una acción que honre a todos aquellos que el DHS nos arrebató; debemos hacer rendir cuentas a CADA fascista que haya permitido la violencia del DHS y se haya beneficiado de ella, así como abolir el ICE y desmantelar el DHS”.

"La 'Operación Midway Blitz' de Donald Trump tenía un único objetivo: aterrorizar a Chicago. Los agentes del ICE y la CBP no fueron tras los peores delincuentes; secuestraron a personas en plena calle, lanzaron gases lacrimógenos contra escuelas primarias y mataron a un padre de dos hijos", declaró el Congresista Mike Quigley. "Lamentablemente, el horror de las políticas migratorias de Trump no terminó con la Operación Midway Blitz. Apenas el mes pasado, asistí a una audiencia de deportación donde vi a niños ante la corte sin sus padres, enfrentándose a una barrera idiomática y teniendo que explicar por qué merecen quedarse en este país. Hay que poner fin a esta crueldad. Estoy más comprometido que nunca a trabajar con mis colegas y con los defensores de derechos para proteger a nuestros vecinos inmigrantes y poner un alto al Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) de Trump antes de que causen más daño".

"Un año después de la Operación Midway Blitz, recordamos el daño causado por esta operación autoritaria, pero también honramos a los líderes religiosos, organizadores comunitarios, abogados, educadores y ciudadanos de Chicago que dieron un paso al frente para proteger a sus vecinos y defender los valores que fortalecen a nuestra ciudad", afirmó el Congresista Jonathan Jackson. "Seguiré exigiendo que se rindan cuentas por los abusos cometidos contra los inmigrantes y nuestras comunidades. Me uno a mis colegas del Congreso para reiterar nuestra exigencia de una reforma migratoria integral, basada en la convicción fundamental de que toda persona merece dignidad, equidad y el debido proceso".

“Esta semana se cumple el primer aniversario de la Operación Midway Blitz, y los residentes de Chicago aún se encuentran conmocionados por los horrores que nuestras comunidades se han visto obligadas a enfrentar, mientras agentes enmascarados continúan sembrando el caos en toda la ciudad, deteniendo a innumerables residentes y desmantelando familias sin miramientos”, declaró la Senadora Estatal Celina Villanueva. “Desde que se lanzó la operación el pasado mes de septiembre, las comunidades latinas —especialmente aquellas a las que yo represento— han vivido con miedo constante: temor a salir de sus hogares y a enviar a sus hijos a la escuela. Tras un año de agresiones brutales contra manifestantes, patrullajes en las calles, redadas en nuestros vecindarios y daños a nuestros residentes, ya es hora de exigir rendición de cuentas y justicia a esta administración, no solo para los latinos de Illinois, sino también para todos aquellos afectados por estos actos de odio sin sentido”.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no quebrantó a nuestra comunidad; fortaleció nuestra determinación. Durante un año, nuestras familias inmigrantes, vecinos y organizaciones comunitarias se han mantenido unidos frente al miedo y la intimidación. Seguiremos defendiendo a cada familia y protegiendo el espíritu acogedor que define a nuestra comunidad”, afirmó el Concejal del Distrito 22, Michael D. Rodriguez.

“Ya sean las redadas en apartamentos de South Shore, el tiroteo contra Marimar Martínez en Brighton Park o el asesinato de Silverio Villegas González, ha quedado demostrado que ICE NO nos protege; su función es intimidar a las comunidades de color y deportar a tantas personas como sea posible. Los líderes locales y los políticos deben apoyar a los inmigrantes y hacer cumplir las leyes y políticas por las que nuestras comunidades lucharon para convertir a Illinois en un lugar que dé la bienvenida a todos”, afirmó Lawrence Benitio, director ejecutivo del ICIRR.

“La Operación Midway Blitz no ha terminado; todavía sufrimos las consecuencias de ver cómo miles de vecinos fueron arrancados de nuestra comunidad. Familias separadas. Empleos perdidos. Comunidades desestabilizadas. Sin embargo, a pesar de todo, nuestra comunidad sigue dando la cara y luchando. Nos negamos a permitir que se normalice este terror”, declaró Any Huamami, directora de organización del Brighton Park Neighborhood Council.

“Hace un año, por estas fechas, nuestras comunidades sufrían el terror provocado por agentes enmascarados; hubo personas secuestradas sin explicación y familias separadas a la fuerza debido a la campaña de control migratorio de esta administración federal. El año pasado nos demostró que todos corríamos el riesgo de ser detenidos simplemente por nuestra apariencia. Las detenciones ilegales se convirtieron en la norma, pero seguimos aquí denunciando esas acciones y recordando a la gente que ICE continúa operando en nuestras comunidades. Es nuestro deber mantenernos alerta y protegernos mutuamente”, afirmó Antonio Gutiérrez, cofundador y coordinador estratégico de Organized Communities Against Deportations.

“El noroeste de Chicago fue uno de los puntos clave de la Operación Midway Blitz. Los miembros de la comunidad local se unieron para resistir este ataque, formando parte de la red estatal de respuesta rápida coordinada por ICIRR. Nuestra labor no terminó cuando concluyó la Operación Midway Blitz; a la fecha, seguimos presenciando secuestros y agresiones por parte del ICE en nuestros vecindarios. Los miembros de la comunidad seguirán haciendo su parte para mantenernos a salvo. Ya es hora de que los departamentos de policía locales cumplan con su deber e investiguen las acciones de estos agentes para que podamos exigirles responsabilidades. Es lo mínimo que merecen los miembros de nuestra comunidad y los vecinos que sufrieron ataques con gases lacrimógenos y gas pimienta, además de agresiones y violencia por parte del gobierno federal”, declaró el pastor Juan Pablo Herrera, presidente de la junta directiva de PLSNA.

“El miedo que recorrió nuestras comunidades es real, pero este año no estuvo definido por el miedo, sino por la belleza y la resiliencia de nuestra comunidad. La administración Trump se propuso dar un ejemplo con Chicago. En cambio, nosotros dimos el ejemplo: construimos una respuesta coordinada a nivel estatal que ha conectado a decenas de miles de miembros de la comunidad con asistencia legal, así como una red de respuesta rápida que demuestra que los inmigrantes de todo Illinois nunca están solos”, afirmó Eréndira Rendón, vicepresidenta de Justicia para Inmigrantes de The Resurrection Project.

CORRECTION 2: UPDATE: Coast Guard locates missing boaters near St. Lawrence Island, Alaska
Editor's note: The previous version incorrectly stated that a Coast Guard HC-130 Hercules aircrew from Air Station Kodiak located the survivor clinging on the capsized vessel at approximately 3 p.m. This version has been corrected to reflect that he was located sitting on top of the vessel at approximately 10:30 a.m.
JUNEAU, Alaska — The Coast Guard concluded its search efforts for three missing boaters following the rescue of one survivor and the recovery of two deceased from the water approximately 4 miles east of St. Lawrence Island, Monday.
A Coast Guard HC-130 Hercules aircrew from Air Station Kodiak located the survivor sitting on top of the capsized vessel at approximately 10:30 a.m. and deployed a raft along with survival equipment.
Watchstanders at the Coast Guard Arctic District command center coordinated the rescue of the survivor with the Northwest Explorer, a nearby good Samaritan vessel.
Before departing the scene to refuel, the HC-130 aircrew deployed a line of flares to guide the Northwest Explorer to the overturned vessel.
The 15-year-old survivor was rescued from the overturned skiff experiencing symptoms of hypothermia.
The two deceased were also recovered from the water unresponsive, taken aboard the good Samaritan vessel, and transported to Nome with the survivor.
The Coast Guard Arctic District coordinated search efforts with the Alaska Rescue Coordination Center, the Alaska Air National Guard's 176th Wing units 211th Rescue Squadron and 212th Rescue Squadron from Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska State Troopers, and local authorities in Savoonga.
In total, two HC-130s, two MH‑60 Jayhawk helicopters from Air Station Kodiak, and a 211th RQS HC-130 with 212th RQS Guardian Angels were also launched to assist.
“Our hearts go out to the families, friends, and communities affected by the tragic loss of these two mariners," said Rear Adm. Bob Little, the commander of the Arctic District. “We are grateful for the incredible efforts of the motor vessel Northwest Explorer, Federal, State, Village first responders and mission partners who assisted in the effort that resulted in a life saved.”
For any questions, reach out to the Arctic District public affairs office at uscgalaska@uscg.mil.
title: CORRECTION 2: UPDATE: Coast Guard locates missing boaters near St. Lawrence Island, Alaska

TYLER, Texas – A Longview man has been charged with federal violations related to falsified tax returns in the Eastern District of Texas, announced U.S. Attorney Jay R. Combs.

Jason Elias Briley, 42, was named in a 19-count indictment returned by a federal grand jury in August 2026, charging him with aiding or assisting in tax fraud. Briley appeared in federal court before U.S. Magistrate Judge K. Nicole Mitchell on September 9, 2026.

According to information presented in court, Briley owned a tax preparation business in Longview and is alleged to have prepared federal tax returns on behalf of his clients that included false information in an attempt to increase the refund amounts. The documented tax loss is alleged to be approximately $370,000.

If convicted, Briley faces up to three years in federal prison. It is important to note that an indictment or arrest should not be considered as evidence of guilt and that all persons charged with a crime are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

This case is being investigated by the Internal Revenue Service-Criminal Investigation and prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Alan Jackson.
