Devonte Skinner, age 34, of Albany, Louisiana, was sentenced to 92 months in federal prison following his conviction for distribution of fentanyl, announced United States Attorney Kurt L. Wall. U.S. Chief Judge Shelly D. Dick further sentenced Skinner to serve five years of supervised release following his term of imprisonment.

According to admissions made as part of his guilty plea, on February 21, 2024, the Department of Homeland Security – Homeland Security Investigations and the United States Drug Enforcement Administration conducted a controlled purchase of 3,792 pills pressed to resemble 30 mg oxycodone and containing 539.2 grams of fentanyl from Skinner and another individual using a confidential source (CS). The CS met Skinner in a restaurant parking lot on O’Neal Lane in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. Skinner was in the front passenger seat of a vehicle and exchanged the pills and money with the CS.

U.S. Attorney Kurt L. Wall praised the work of the Department of Homeland Security – Homeland Security Investigations, Drug Enforcement Administration, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and Livingston Parish Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Paul L. Pugliese led the prosecution.

“I am very pleased with the dedicated work of our prosecutors and our law enforcement partners,” said U.S. Attorney Wall. “Fentanyl continues to pose a grave threat to communities throughout Louisiana and distributing this substance in such quantities risks devastating harm. The Federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account the criminal act and the defendant’s prior criminal history, called for a sentencing range of 262 to 327 months. Although we respect the Court’s role in sentencing, we have concerns that a sentence far below the guidelines range sends a harmful message. Unfortunately, our district has experienced hundreds of fentanyl overdoses over the past few years. Recently, we are beginning to see a reduction in those numbers, which gives us some optimism that the message of the dangerousness of fentanyl is finally gaining traction. The defendant’s conduct has to be viewed in the same light as if he had fired 3,972 rounds of ammunition on our public streets. A 92-month sentence is insufficient, and our office is reviewing the judgment closely and considering all options, including appeal.”

“Fentanyl traffickers endanger our communities with every pill they put on the street,” said HSI New Orleans Acting Special Agent in Charge Matt Wright. “This investigation and conviction reflect HSI’s continued commitment to working with our federal, state, and local partners to identify, investigate, and hold accountable those who distribute deadly narcotics in Louisiana. Through the Homeland Security Task Force, we will continue using every lawful tool available to disrupt criminal networks and protect the public from the devastation caused by fentanyl.”

This prosecution was part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Orleans comprises agents and officers from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives (ATF), and the United States Marshals Service (USMS), U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), the United States Postal Inspection Service (USPIS), the U.S. Coast Guard, Investigative Service (CGIS), U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Office of Field Operations (CBP OFO), U.S. Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol (CBP BP) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney's Office for Middle District of Louisiana.

U.S. Marshals Capture Escaped Federal Inmate in Tucson
For immediate release
Colleen Grayman, Supervisory Deputy U.S. Marshal
Tucson, AZ — The U.S. Marshals Service apprehended escaped federal inmate James Casady Cangro on September 2, 2026, the same day he escaped from the Federal Prison Camp in Tucson.
At approximately 8:10 a.m., prison staff observed Cangro near the visitor parking lot of the Federal Correctional Complex at 8901 South Wilmot Road. When approached by staff, Cangro fled on foot toward Wilmot Road and was last seen entering the surrounding desert.
The U.S. Marshals Service immediately initiated a coordinated fugitive investigation and deployed all available resources and appropriate investigative tactics to locate Cangro. Working alongside federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, including the Federal Bureau of Prisons, the Tucson Police Department, Pima County Sheriffs Office, and U.S. Border Patrol, Deputy U.S. Marshals safely took Cangro into custody later that day not far from the prison facility. The personnel, equipment, intelligence, and specialized capabilities provided by these partners were instrumental in swiftly locating Cangro and safely returning him to federal custody.
No injuries were reported during the apprehension. Cangro will remain in federal custody and face additional judicial proceedings related to his escape.
“The safe apprehension of this dangerous escapee on the same day he fled demonstrates the determination of our deputy U.S. marshals and the strength of our law enforcement partnerships,” said United States Marshal Van Bayless for the District of Arizona. “I want to specifically thank the Tucson Police Department and U.S. Border Patrol for their immediate response, valuable assistance, and commitment throughout this operation. Their personnel and resources, along with the efforts of our other federal, state, and local partners, were instrumental in bringing this search to a swift and safe conclusion.”
Cangro is a validated member of the Soldiers of Aryan Culture, also known as SAC, a violent prison gang that originated in Utah. His criminal history includes prior convictions for robbery in Utah, aggravated assault in Utah and Oklahoma, and firearms-related offenses. He also has a prior federal conviction for using a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime.
In 2025, Cangro was sentenced in the District of New Mexico to 132 months in federal prison following convictions for violent felon in possession of body armor, felon in possession of a firearm and ammunition, possession of an unregistered firearm, possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, and possession with intent to distribute 50 grams or more of a mixture or substance containing methamphetamine.
The Arizona WANTED Violent Offender Task Force is a U.S. Marshals Service led multi-jurisdictional fugitive apprehension unit responsible for more than 1748 arrests in the last year. The task force is comprised of 22 agencies bringing together the resources of federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to locate and arrest the community’s most violent offenders and sexual predators.

Wild Horses in Peril: Emergency Operations Start Next Week on Riddle Mountain
Organization:
Media Contact:
BURNS, Ore.—The Bureau of Land Management plans to begin a second emergency operation next week to rescue wild horses from another southeast Oregon herd whose health is under immediate threat from severe food and water shortages. The animals' survival is compromised by a lack of resources due to an especially dry winter and recent wildfires.
Last month, the Bald Mountain Fire burned through the Riddle Mountain Herd Management Area, which was already showing a lack of forage due to ongoing drought.
“We can’t leave these horses out on the burned landscape,” said Don Rotell, Burns District Manager. “Two-thirds of their food was lost to wildfire.”
The BLM will transport the rescued horses to off-range holding facilities, where they will receive veterinary evaluations, appropriate care, high-quality feed, and continuous access to fresh water. The facilities provide ample space that meets established agency standards. Once they have been evaluated and are ready, some of the horses may be available for adoption through the BLM Online Corral.
The rescue operation is planned to start September 9. Media and the public can view the first two days of operations (September 9 and 10), provided that doing so does not disrupt operations or jeopardize the safety of the animals or staff. BLM staff will escort the public to gather observation sites located on public lands. Observation is available by reservation only and is limited to 10-15 people per viewing day. Reservations will be accepted by email only at blm_or_wa_press@blm.gov and must be submitted no later than 4 p.m. on the prior business day. Phone and voicemail reservations will not be accepted.
Reservations are accepted on a first-come, first-served basis, based on the email date and time received. Participants will receive confirmation by 9 p.m., including meeting times, locations, and additional instructions. Media and public participants should generally plan to meet near Burns, between 4:30 and 6 a.m. for caravanning to the site. Participants must receive confirmation before attending. Viewing opportunities may change or be canceled on short notice because of weather, changing gather locations, safety concerns, or other operational needs.
The BLM will provide updates on the operation’s progress, details about public viewing opportunities, and information on adoption opportunities online.
Public safety and animal welfare remain top priorities. The Wild Horse and Burro Program is committed to the humane and sustainable management of wild horse populations and their habitats. These drive-trap gather operations are guided by the Comprehensive Animal Welfare Program, which sets handling standards that prioritize the care and well-being of the animals.
The BLM manages about 245 million acres of public land located primarily in 12 western states, including Alaska, on behalf of the American people. The BLM also administers 700 million acres of sub-surface mineral estate throughout the nation. Our mission is to sustain the health, diversity, and productivity of America’s public lands for the use and enjoyment of present and future generations.
title: Wild Horses in Peril: Emergency Operations Start Next Week on Riddle Mountain

Ocala, Florida – Samantha Calvente (44, Winter Haven) has pleaded guilty to possession of 5 grams or more of methamphetamine with the intent to distribute it. She faces a minimum penalty of 5 years, up to 40 years, in federal prison. A sentencing date has not yet been set. U.S. Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe made the announcement.

According to the court records, on August 21, 2022, Calvente went to the Coleman Federal Correctional Complex (“FCC Coleman”) in Sumter Countyto visit her husband, R.C, who was an inmate at the facility. As Calvente entered the prison, she told correctional officers that she did not have any prohibited items on her person, including narcotics. When Calvente entered the visitation room, however, staff observed her retrieving an unknown object from her waistband and placing it between her legs. Correctional officers promptly escorted Calvente out of the visitation room. Before a search could take place, Calvente handed the officers an object wrapped in a black latex material that contained over 24 grams of methamphetamine. Calvente then admitted that she had introduced contraband into prison facilities for her husband on prior occasions.

This case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the Federal Bureau of Prisons. It is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Hannah Watson and Anthony C. Marek.
title: Polk County Woman Admits to Smuggling Methamphetamine into Federal Prison for Her Inmate Husband

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32), senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, issued the following statement after reviewing the proposed U.S.-Saudi Arabia Section 123 Agreement for peaceful nuclear cooperation submitted to Congress by the Trump Administration:

“I have read the proposed 123 Agreement that the Trump Administration has sent to Congress, both the unclassified and classified portions. The classified portion of the Agreement includes a blank page labeled “to be filled in later.” Clearly the Trump Administration has not submitted the Agreement for review as required by the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, which requires that Congress see the whole agreement.

I am profoundly disturbed by the path this agreement creates for a nuclear-armed Saudi Arabia.

This deal claims to facilitate peaceful nuclear technology for Saudi Arabia but intentionally excludes the very safeguards that determine whether or not a country with nuclear technology can use it to build nuclear weapons: the Gold Standard and Additional Protocol. Not only that, but this agreement explicitly allows uranium enrichment on Saudi soil under certain conditions. And only President Trump, not the Congress, will determine if those vague conditions have been met.

Crown Prince Mohammad Bin Salman has been clear about his intentions to pursue a nuclear weapon, and Saudi Arabia has already shown a willingness to advance down that path covertly by standing up an undeclared, Chinese-backed yellowcake-extraction facility just a few years ago.

Saudi Arabia is in a volatile region that has seen the collapse of many dictatorships that were thought to be stable. It was the United States that provided preliminary nuclear technology to Iran through the Atoms for Peace program when it was ruled by a friendly, pro-Western monarch – and all of the technology in the hands of the Shah in 1978 fell into the hands of the Ayatollah in 1979.

Today, we are fighting a war designed to prevent Iran from having an uncontrolled nuclear program. Now, the Trump Administration is green-lighting an uncontrolled nuclear program for Saudi Arabia. While the current Saudi government is far less problematic than the one in Tehran, no one knows who will be in power in Riyadh ten years from now. This region has seen the collapse of many dictatorships that were thought to be stable, and this deal gambles the nuclear security of the United States and the world on the very weak assumption that pro-Western leaders will continue to head Saudi Arabia in the decades to come.

A Saudi nuclear bomb would shred the nonproliferation regime of the last half century. Once Saudi Arabia has an uncontrolled nuclear program with America’s blessing, Egypt, Turkey, and perhaps South Korea and Brazil will not be far behind.

This should not be a Democratic or Republican issue – this is about American national security, and the United States’ longstanding bipartisan commitments to non-proliferation. It was the policy of the first Trump Administration that a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia needed to include the Gold Standard and Additional Protocol provisions. Secretary of State Marco Rubio recognized the need for these safeguards years ago when he joined me in introducing the Saudi Nuclear Nonproliferation Act in 2016, and I applaud Senator Kennedy (R-LA) for registering his opposition to this no-safeguards Saudi nuclear deal last month. Members of Congress – Republican and Democrat alike – must reject this deal with a Joint Resolution of Disapproval until the necessary safeguards are included.”

###
title: Congressman Brad Sherman Statement on Trump Administration Deal Opening the Door to a Nuclear-Armed Saudi Arabia

LAREDO, Texas – A 40-year-old Laredo resident has been sentenced for conspiring to distribute fentanyl.

Rolando Soliz pleaded guilty Sept. 16, 2025.

U.S. District Judge John A. Kazen has now ordered Soliz to serve 110 months in federal prison to be immediately followed by four years of supervised release. At the hearing Sept. 1, the court heard additional evidence to include details about Soliz’s extensive criminal history as well as his possession of large amounts of cash and 10 different firearms, one of which was a short-barreled rifle converted to operate as a machine gun. In handing down the sentence, Judge Kazen noted his conviction was for distributing fentanyl during a time when it was killing more and more people in the community. He also noted his extensive criminal history including four prior felony convictions.

The investigation, which began July 11, 2024, indicated Soliz had been engaged in multiple transactions involving fentanyl in the Laredo area.

Law enforcement set up surveillance at Soliz’s apartment and witnessed multiple hand-to-hand drug transactions. A subsequent traffic stop resulted in the discovery of fentanyl that had been obtained from Soliz at his residence.

On July 31, 2024, authorities executed a search warrant at Soliz’s apartment and discovered 24.8 grams of fentanyl inside a toilet bowl. They had also searched his mother’s residence. As a result of the warrants at both locations, law enforcement seized the drugs, over $16,000 in cash, and multiple firearms.

Soliz has been and will remain in custody pending transfer to a Federal Bureau of Prisons facility to be determined in the near future.

The Drug Enforcement Administration conducted the investigation with the assistance of Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives; Webb County District Attorney’s Office; and Webb County Constables Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Andrew P. Hakala-Finch prosecuted the case.
title: Firearm-wielding fentanyl dealer sentenced to over 100 months

text:
Ranking Member Johnson’s Opening Statement At Hearing On Protecting America’s Patent System And Innovation Economy
Washington, D.C. (September 2, 2026)—Today, Rep. Hank Johnson, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet, delivered opening remarks at a subcommittee hearing on renewing the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s (USPTO) fee-setting authority and protecting a fair, accessible patent system that rewards American innovation and ingenuity.
Below are Ranking Member Johnson’s remarks, as prepared for delivery, at today’s hearing.
WATCH Subcommittee Ranking Member Johnson’s opening statement.
Ranking Member Hank Johnson
Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet
Hearing on “Renewal of USPTO Fee Setting Authority: Giving Full Effect to the America Invents Act”
September 2, 2026
Thank you, Chairman Issa.
The USPTO’s fee-setting authority has given it the flexibility to move its workers remote, plan its budgets ahead, and tailor fees for small and micro entities. Originally, it was set to expire in just a few days on September the 16th. Yesterday, however, House and Senate Republicans were generous enough to kick the can down the road until after they are reelected. The authority is now set to expire on December 12th, 2026. Failing to reauthorize the USPTO’s fee setting authority risks transforming a traditionally nonpartisan agency into one that serves political ideology over merit.
Ensuring that USPTO remains a beacon of American innovation means not just reauthorizing the fee setting authority but ensuring USPTO advisory committees can continue to advise the USPTO without interference by this administration. Two months after he was inaugurated, Trump’s Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick fired every member of PPAC and TPAC. A year and a half later, they finally swore in the first few new members.
When Congress originally authorized fee setting authority under the America Invents Act, we built in several oversight measures to ensure that this power could not be exercised without transparency but rather with public input and independent expert review. PPAC and TPAC remain a critical part of those guardrails. Their full and independent participation is essential to ensuring that fee-setting remains accountable to all who rely on our patent and trademark systems, the big and the small. That is why these committees must be fully constituted as they are a necessary safeguard for independence.
And that independence matters. If we do not give USPTO the flexibility it needs to set fees, access to our patent system will be taken over by special interests. This will make it even harder for small, independent inventors to protect their inventions and easier for those who can pay-to-play to infringe on those rights.
How do we know? Because we are already seeing this happen in the rest of the executive branch. Every day we learn again how easy it’s become for oligarchs and powerful companies to buy a seat at Donald Trump’s table. Millions of dark money in campaign contributions. Lavish gifts like private jets, and business deals. Rampant insider trading on predictive markets. Access to the Trump White House has transformed into a currency that only the rich and famous can afford.
And while the wealthy are busy buying a seat at the table, Americans across the country are left paying the price. Constituents of Georgia’s 4th Congressional district are struggling to afford rent or pay their mortgage, and the cost of groceries continue to skyrocket. Hardworking families should not struggle to afford healthcare while Elon Musk becomes a trillionaire, and while Donald Trump lines his own pockets through unabashed greed built on the backs of American taxpayers.
Conflicts of interest and self-dealing have become routine features in Trump’s Washington, blurring the line between public service and private financial gain. This was a man who campaigned on draining the swamp, and yet all Trump has done is put it behind a velvet rope and began charging an admissions fee. Because in Trump’s America money buys access. Access buys influence. And influence too often becomes the law for everyone else. Innovation should not be a luxury that only the wealthy can afford. So, I, for one, am determined to not allow USPTO to be sucked in to that swamp.
Reauthorizing this fee setting authority with the transparency, public participation, and independent oversight that Congress intended is essential to keeping our patent system working for all—not just for those with the closest connection to big tech, the aspiring oligarch class, or the Trump White House. We have just a few months to get this done. This is not time for Members or big money special interests to advocate for changes to the way the USPTO operates because they’re not happy with Director Squires’ Patent Trial and Appeals Board actions. I think we are overdue to examine proposals like Rep. Ross’s PREVAIL, which would reform PTAB abuses. I’m sure some of my colleagues on both sides of the aisle agree with me, just as others disagree. But I’m not trying to make those changes right now. We have a program that everyone agrees has been successful; inserting our own USTPO agendas into the debate will only serve to make this reauthorization controversial.
I want to thank the witnesses for being here today. While I think this hearing is unnecessary and a distraction from the disastrous policies of the Trump Administration, I do believe it is vital that Americans truly understand the importance of allowing this agency the independence and discretion it needs to keep America at the top of our global innovation economy. Because if we want to continue to lead the world in the technological advancements of tomorrow, then we must ensure today that the institution most responsible for protecting those innovations is independent and built to last.
I yield back the balance of my time.
title: Ranking Member Johnson’s Opening Statement At Hearing On Protecting America’s Patent System And Innovation Economy

WASHINGTON — Congressman Glenn Ivey (MD-04) led a bipartisan delegation of Members of Congress to Cape Canaveral, Florida, from Saturday, August 29 through Monday, August 31, in partnership with the U.S. Space Force and NASA, to witness the successful launch of NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

The Roman Space Telescope lifted off aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Sunday, August 30, from Launch Complex 39A at NASA's Kennedy Space Center, and reached orbit roughly 10 minutes later. The delegation observed the launch in person and met with Space Force and NASA leadership to discuss the future of the U.S. space and space science enterprise.

“The successful launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is a tremendous achievement for NASA and a proud moment for Maryland. I congratulate the exceptional NASA Goddard workforce and every partner whose expertise and dedication made this mission possible—especially nine months ahead of schedule and under budget. This observatory will reveal to us distant worlds, helping us understand dark matter and dark energy, and inspire the imagination of the next generation. Goddard’s critical scientific missions continue to reaffirm America’s global leadership in space science and will now advance discovery for years to come,” said Congressman Ivey, representative of Maryland’s Fourth District.

The delegation included Representatives George Whitesides (D-CA), Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA), and Mike Haridopolos (R-FL). Science communicator Bill Nye the Science Guy also joined the delegation for part of the trip.

ABOUT THE MISSION

Named for NASA's first chief astronomer, known as the “mother of Hubble,” the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is NASA's next flagship observatory and its most significant astrophysics mission since the James Webb Space Telescope. Roman carries a primary mirror with a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble's, enabling it to survey wide swaths of the sky to study dark energy and dark matter, search for exoplanets, and advance infrared astrophysics. The observatory launched roughly nine months ahead of its required launch readiness date and is now on a three-month journey to join Webb at the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2), where it will operate collaboratively with Hubble and Webb to give humanity an unprecedented view of the universe, paving the way for future observatories in the search for signs of life beyond our solar system.

PARTNERS

Roman is a worldwide collaborative effort, featuring a network of 85 national partners across 17 states and 13 international partners across 9 countries. More information about the global network of partners contributing to this mission can be found at: https://science.nasa.gov/mission/roman-space-telescope/partners/

ABOUT CONGRESSMAN IVEY
title: REP. IVEY LEADS BIPARTISAN CODEL TO WITNESS SUCCESSFUL LAUNCH OF NANCY GRACE ROMAN SPACE TELESCOPE

Deputy U.S. Marshals Arrest Two Dangerous Fugitives Wanted for Separate Murders in Less Than Eight Hours
For immediate release
Eastern District of Missouri
St. Louis, MO - On Aug. 27, members of the U.S. Marshals Fugitive Task Force made up of Task Force Officers and Deputy U.S. Marshals from the Eastern District of Missouri were alerted to a suspect wanted for his part in a murder which occurred in Independence on Aug. 24. Information was received that the suspect was possibly in the St. Louis area and the deputies immediately began their search. The subject was found to be in the city of Moline Acres and was taken into custody without injuries to the suspect or deputies.
Almost immediately following this arrest, the U.S. Marshals Service was made aware that an unrelated dangerous murder suspect, wanted in an Aug. 23 murder of a woman was believed to be at his residence in Moberly. Without hesitation the team responded to Moberly. With the assistance of local law enforcement, the Deputy U.S. Marshals effectuated another arrest after a short standoff.
Both dangerous murder suspects were preparing to flee the areas they were in to avoid arrest and prosecution. Two murderers brought to justice - all in a day’s work for the men and women of the U.S. Marshals Service in the Eastern District of Missouri.
“Our Deputy Marshals with the assistance of state and local partners, are ever vigilant in their pursuit of the most dangerous fugitives in society and make a difference every day,” said U.S. Marshal Steven Lewis, of the Eastern District of Missouri.
The task forces organized by the U.S. Marshals Service are composed of Deputy United States Marshals and officers from the Missouri State Highway Patrol, St. Louis Metropolitan, St. Louis County and St. Charles County Police departments and multiple municipal officers with the sole purpose of finding and stopping violent offenders with active warrants before they offend again.

BOSTON – A Sudbury man, formerly of Hudson (Mass.), was sentenced on Aug. 27, 2026 in federal court in Worcester for carrying out a scheme to steal money from his two former employers, both medical practices.

Adam Gentile, 40, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Margaret R. Guzman to four years in prison, to be followed by four years of supervised release. Gentile was also ordered to pay restitution to the two victims in the amounts of $3.8 million and $3.3 million, respectively, and was ordered to pay forfeiture in the amount of $7.8 million. In March 2026 , Gentile pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud after being charged in December 2025.

In or around 2014, Gentile was hired as an administrative assistant for a medical practice near Boston. He was promoted to the role of office manager shortly thereafter. In his capacity as office manager, Gentile processed payroll and oversaw other recordkeeping and administrative responsibilities for the practice. Beginning in or around 2015 and continuing through November 2020, Gentile embezzled more than $4.5 million from his employer by issuing himself extra paychecks, sometimes labeling the payments as “bonuses.” Gentile also paid off personal credit cards with the practice’s bank account.

In 2021, Gentile was hired as an officer manager for a second medical practice, for which he similarly had sole responsibility for processing payroll. From in or around April 2021 through May 2024, Gentile executed a similar scheme in which he caused extra payroll payments to be issued to himself – sometimes recording these payments as “bonuses.” Gentile used the employer’s bank account to pay off his personal credit cards; purchase and upgrade his home in Hudson; and put toward a side business he ran while employed by the medical practice. Gentile embezzled more than $3.3 million from his second employer.

United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Ted E. Docks Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Boston Division made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Leominster Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Kaitlin J. Brown prosecuted the case.
title: Sudbury Man Sentenced to Four Years in Prison for $7.8 Million Embezzlement Scheme

AUSTIN, Texas – An Armenian national was sentenced in a federal court in Austin on Tuesday to 26 months in prison for his participation in a criminal conspiracy to export goods from the United States to the Russian Federation through the Republic of Armenia without the requisite license or authorization from the U.S. government, announced U.S. Attorney Justin R. Simmons for the Western District of Texas.

According to court documents, from February 2022 until at least August 2024, Kamo Kirakosyan knowingly and willfully combined, conspired, and agreed with others to export and reexport goods subject to the Export Administration Regulations without having first obtained the required licenses from the U.S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of Industry & Security. The exported goods included items that could be used for semiconductor manufacturing.

Kirakosyan became the straw or substitute purchaser of the U.S.-origin goods for his co-conspirators shortly after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, and the imposition of additional sanctions and export restrictions on Russia. As part of the scheme, Kirakosyan sent a co-conspirator instructions on opening a bank account in Armenia for the purpose of evading sanctions. While arranging the transshipment of goods to Russia, Kirakosyan represented himself to U.S. companies as the Armenian buyer of goods and did not provide truthful information about the end users, despite the U.S. companies’ requests for end user statements, and despite Kirakosyan’s knowledge that the unauthorized export or reexport to Russia of certain shipments was prohibited without a license. On Feb. 23, 2023, the company Kirakosyan conspired with was designated by Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control and added to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, subjecting the Russian company to U.S. blocking sanctions and a general prohibition on transacting with U.S. persons or entities.

Kirakosyan was initially charged in a criminal complaint on or about July 31, 2024. He was extradited from Germany to the U.S. on Aug. 29, 2025, and, in April of this year, pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to violate federal law.

The FBI San Antonio Counterintelligence Task Force, comprised of the Bureau of Industry and Security of the U.S. Department of Commerce, and other partners, led the investigation. The FBI’s Legal Attaché office in Berlin provided significant assistance. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs also played a key role in securing Kirakosyan’s extradition to the United States.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Mark Roomberg and Keith Henneke prosecuted the case with assistance from the National Security Division’s Counterintelligence and Export Control Section.

###
title: Armenian Man Sentenced to Federal Prison for Smuggling Controlled Goods to Russia

WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today blasted President Trump for denying New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill’s appeal for $84.4 million in federal disaster aid following February’s deadly blizzard.

“Donald Trump is stiffing New Jersey taxpayers out of $84 million in disaster aid that his own government determined we qualified for. Twelve people died. New Jersey communities were buried under record snowfall. But apparently if you live in a state Trump doesn’t like, you’re on your own,” said Pallone.

“And where are the Republicans in Congress? I asked the committee chairs responsible for overseeing FEMA to investigate this weeks ago. Not one of them even bothered to respond. Trump is treating federal disaster aid like his personal political slush fund, and Republicans in Congress are too afraid to lift a finger to stop him,” Pallone continued.

In August, Pallone called on the Republican chairs of the congressional committees with jurisdiction over FEMA to investigate Trump’s initial denial of New Jersey’s disaster declaration after reports that regional FEMA and NOAA officials determined New Jersey and other affected states met federal thresholds for assistance. The Republican chairs have not responded. Governor Sherrill appealed the denial on July 20, seeking Public Assistance, including snow assistance for 19 counties, and statewide Hazard Mitigation assistance. Today the Trump Administration denied that appeal.

###
title: Pallone: Trump Stiffs New Jersey Again on Disaster Aid

A man who was previously convicted for a bank robbery was sentenced today to more than five years in federal prison.

Tony Spies, age 56, from Wyoming, Iowa, received the prison term after an April 29, 2026, guilty plea to two counts of distribution of a controlled substance.

Evidence at the plea and sentencing hearing showed that in November 2025, Spies sold methamphetamine to an individual cooperating with law enforcement on two separate occasions. On November 24, 2025, law enforcement officers stopped Spies car. Officers found methamphetamine and marijuana in the car.

Spies was sentenced in Cedar Rapids by United States District Court Judge Leonard T. Strand. Spies was sentenced to 66 months’ imprisonment. He must also serve a four-year term of supervised release after the prison term. There is no parole in the federal system.

Spies is being held in the United States Marshal’s custody until he can be transported to a federal prison.

The case was prosecuted by Special Assistant United States Attorney Michael S.A. Hudson and investigated by the Iowa Division of Narcotics Enforcement, the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigations Laboratory, the Iowa State Patrol, and the Muscatine County Drug Task Force, consisting of the Muscatine Police Department, Muscatine Conty Sheriff’s Office, and Cedar County Sheriff’s Office.

Court file information at https://ecf.iand.uscourts.gov/cgi-bin/login.pl .

The case file number is 26-CR-00024.

Follow us on X @USAO_NDIA.
title: Convicted Bank Robber Sentenced for Distributing Methamphetamine

ARLINGTON, VA — Yesterday, Tuesday, September 1, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) attended a wreath-laying ceremony at the Pentagon Memorial to honor the victims of the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, in advance of the 25th anniversary. The Congressman joined fellow Members of Congress to pay tribute to the 184 lives lost at the Pentagon and the nearly 3,000 Americans killed on 9/11.

“Twenty-five years later, we still carry the memory of the nearly 3,000 innocent lives lost on September 11th, 750 of which were from New Jersey. We will never forget,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “We honor those we lost, the families who carry that grief every day, and the first responders and service members who ran toward danger. As we mark this solemn anniversary, we recommit ourselves to their memory and to keeping our nation safe.”

Gottheimer serves as the Co-Chair of the bipartisan House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence review of the 9/11 Commission Report. The review evaluates the progress made on the intelligence-related recommendations produced by the 9/11 Commission Report, released in July 2004, and identifies areas of improvement to protect against the next generation of threats.

Gottheimer has helped lead and pass legislation like the bipartisan Never Forget the Heroes Act, to fully fund the 9/11 Victims Compensation Fund to provide long-overdue support to cover 9/11 survivors, first responders, and their families for injuries, medical expenses, and other benefits.

Gottheimer is continuing to fight to pass the bipartisan FIRE Cancer Act to provide federal investments so that all firefighters can get access to preventative tests, including multi-cancer early detection tests.

Below: Gottheimer attends a wreath-laying ceremony at the Pentagon Memorial with other House Intelligence members.

###
title: PHOTO RELEASE: Gottheimer Attends Wreath-Laying Ceremony at the Pentagon 9/11 Memorial Ahead of 25th Anniversary of September 11th

Today, NOAA announced priorities for advancing reforms within NOAA Fisheries to move towards regulations grounded in science that support American seafood dominance. These agency-level actions follow the Regional Priorities guidance that was released on July 2, 2026, to apply the same standard of accountability to NOAA’s own operations, regulatory frameworks, and scientific pipelines. This priority list serves as an operational roadmap of NOAA Fisheries’ direct support of the President's Executive order on Restoring American Seafood Competitiveness and will lead to the broader interagency America First Seafood Strategy that will be released in the coming months.
“Through these priorities, the agency is taking actionable steps to fulfill the president's vision of making the United States the world's dominant seafood leader,” said Neil Jacobs, Ph.D., NOAA administrator. “NOAA is proud to deliver real-world results to the American public through innovative solutions that streamline regulations.”
“These priorities represent NOAA Fisheries’ commitment to ensuring that federal fisheries management boosts domestic harvesters,” said Eugenio Piñeiro Soler, assistant administrator for NOAA Fisheries. “We are proud to empower hard-working American fishermen to produce more seafood for American plates.”
After considering input from more than 700 individuals and organizations, including from councils, the fishing industry, and the public, NOAA Fisheries is advancing a science-based approach to fisheries management that supports sustainable fishing opportunities while ensuring responsible conservation practices and improving regulatory efficiency. These efforts touch on all aspects of the agency’s mission from protected resources and science to national policies and improving fishing opportunities.
While this announcement outlines the immediate internal priorities for the agency, it also serves as a bridge towards a broader, interagency transformation of federal seafood policy. In the coming months, the agency will unveil future actions towards this goal to strengthen national seafood markets, rebuild U.S. fisheries infrastructure and processing capacity, and tackle IUU fishing issues to ensure American seafood dominance.
title: NOAA announces priorities to promote science-based American seafood dominance

Milton Daniel Lopez-Bonilla is charged with one-count of deported alien found in the United States. A preliminary hearing is scheduled for September 16, 2026, before United States Magistrate Judge Elayna J. Youchah.

Trump’s tariffs have cost Minnesotans $4.8 billion
WASHINGTON, DC – On the House floor, U.S. Representative Kelly Morrison (MN-03) called for an end to President Trump’s costly and dangerous trade war with Canada – Minnesota’s closest trading partner, and to restore the diplomatic relationship between the United States and Canada.
According to new data, Trump’s tariffs have cost Minnesotans $4.8 billion (equaling about $2,000 per household) since January 2025 — and this number will only go up if Trump continues this trade war. Minnesota has also lost more than 6,000 manufacturing jobs as a result of Trump’s tariffs.
Trump’s attacks on Canada, including putting up to 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, are threatening to disintegrate the previously strong bonds between the United States and Canada – which poses a unique threat to Minnesota. In Minnesota, which exports more than $5 billion a year to Canada and imports more than $14 billion from Canada each year, this trade war could pose an existential threat to small business owners who rely on a strong partnership with Canada.
This week, Representative Morrison joined almost 90 of her colleagues in a letter urging President Trumpto repair his relationship with Canada for the sake of the American people.
Representative Morrison spoke on the House floor to urge Trump to end his trade war with Canada and highlighted the importance of Minnesota’s trade with Canada.
Read Representative Morrison’s full remarks below:
Mr. Speaker, 
Today I rise on behalf of Minnesotans who continue to be forced to pay for the President’s failing economic policies. 
President Trump’s tariffs have cost Minnesotans 4.8 billion dollars. 
And for what?! 
For a debunked policy that is raising costs, damaging our economy, and alienating our allies?
For taking the American people’s money during a cost of living crisis to bankroll his corrupt, inexplicable war?
And now he’s escalating with Canada of all places – one of our nation’s strongest allies and Minnesota’s number one trade partner. 
Why would we ever pick a fight with them?!
This will be a disaster for our small businesses, farmers, and every Minnesotan who is going to have to pay higher prices because of tariffs on everything from steel, to kitchen appliances, to hockey sticks.
But we are not powerless — and it begs the question yet again: when will the Republican majority stand up to this President and represent the American people?
If Trump won’t end this trade war, then Congress has to.
###
title: U.S. Rep. Kelly Morrison Calls to End Trade War with Canada, Minnesota’s Closest Ally

Washington, DC -- Marking one year since the Trump administration’s first boat strike, U.S. Representatives Gregory W. Meeks (D-N.Y.), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee; Jim Himes (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence; and Bennie G. Thompson (D-Miss.), Ranking Member of the House Homeland Security Committee, introduced a War Powers Resolution today to block the administration from continuing to use U.S. Armed Forces to conduct strikes in the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific.
“One year ago today, the Trump administration launched a campaign of extrajudicial killings, using the U.S. military and taxpayer dollars to execute at least 227 individuals without due process or a credible national-security justification. The administration calls this counternarcotics. However, it remains unclear whether these operations have made any real difference in stemming the flow of illegal drugs into the United States, and they were never authorized by Congress. A year later, the administration has little to show for this lawless campaign except a mounting body count, a massive price tag, and a stain on the American conscience.
“The lack of transparency on behalf of this administration and DoD to not meaningfully inform Congress of the use of lethal military force is staggering. It is especially troubling given the strong bipartisan agreement that the flow of illegal narcotics into the U.S. poses a serious risk to the health and well-being of Americans that demands government action. But that action should be taken legally with law enforcement in the lead.
“Time and again, this administration has refused to use the military responsibly or consult with Congress, even though the American people have made clear they do not want their tax dollars being spent on more endless military campaigns. It’s time for this failed campaign to end. The War Powers Resolution we’ve introduced today would end the Trump administration’s unauthorized military campaign, check the president’s overreach, and reclaim Congress’s constitutional authority over the use of military force.” 
###
title: Ranking Members Meeks, Smith, Himes, and Thompson Introduce War Powers Resolution to End Trump’s Illegal Boat Strikes

CONCORD –Felina Pimental, 24, of Hyde Park, Massachusetts, pleaded guilty today in federal court to one count of Conspiracy to Distribute and Possess with Intent to Distribute a Controlled Substance, United States Attorney Erin Creegan announces.

According to court documents and statements, in late 2023, law enforcement agencies began investigating a drug-trafficking organization (DTO) operating in New Hampshire and Massachusetts. Investigators utilized cooperating witnesses and an undercover officer to conduct controlled purchases of narcotics from various DTO members. Typically, the transactions would be arranged through the DTO’s customer telephone, which was usually operated by the DTO leader, co-defendant Alexander Aguasvivas-Pena, or by someone at his direction, namely Pimental, where a customer would contact a DTO phone number to arrange a drug deal. Pimental was involved in multiple transactions. During the course of the conspiracy, the DTO trafficked over 10 kilograms of methamphetamine and other drugs.

The charging statute provides for a sentence of not less than 10 years and up to life in federal prison, at least 5 years of supervised release, and a maximum fine of $10,000,000. U.S. District Court Judge Joseph N. Laplante scheduled sentencing for December 16, 2026.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation Major Offender Task Force led the investigation with valuable assistance from the Drug Enforcement Administration, New Hampshire State Police, Strafford County Sheriff’s Office, and Boston Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Yasir Sadat is prosecuting the case.

This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF New Hampshire comprises agents and officers from FBI, HSI, IRS, DEA, ATF, USMS, and DSS with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of New Hampshire.

Physician-scientist and informatics leader Dr. Peter Embí to helm NIH’s National Library of Medicine
Wednesday, September 2, 2026
Physician-scientist and informatics leader Dr. Peter Embí to helm NIH’s National Library of Medicine
National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director Jay Bhattacharya, M.D., Ph.D., today announced the selection of Peter Joseph Embí, M.D., M.S., as director of NIH’s National Library of Medicine (NLM). Dr. Embí, an internationally recognized leader in biomedical informatics and health system innovation, brings nearly three decades of clinical, research, academic, and executive leadership experience to the position. He currently serves as a tenured professor of biomedical informatics and internal medicine and the Endowed Director of Biomedical Informatics at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, where he has also served as chair of the Department of Biomedical Informatics, Senior Vice-President for Research and Innovation, and, most recently, founding director of the ADVANCE AI Center. He is anticipated to begin his role on Sept. 10, 2026.
“Dr. Embí is a pioneer at the intersection of biomedical informatics, research, and clinical care, with a proven track record of turning data into better health outcomes,” said Dr. Bhattacharya. “As NLM enters an era defined by AI and data-driven discovery, his leadership will be essential to ensuring the library continues to serve as a trusted, cutting-edge resource for researchers, clinicians, and the public.”
As the NLM’s fifth director since it became the National Library of Medicine in 1956, Dr. Embí will oversee the world’s largest biomedical library and shepherd the investment of its approximately $495 million annual budget. He will lead a workforce of nearly 1,400 who support NLM as a global leader in biomedical informatics and computational health data science research. NLM has a multifaceted role as an information hub, learning center, and innovation incubator and plays a central role in advancing science through the effective use of data and analytics for discovery and health care. NLM makes the world’s biomedical data and information available, accessible, and understandable to all. NLM also conducts and funds research, development, and training in biomedical informatics and health information technology, hosts the world’s largest and most heavily accessed genomic data repositories, and coordinates the Network of the National Library of Medicine, which actively engages with more than 2,000 member organizations to provide training opportunities, resources, and health information in communities across the United States.
Dr. Embí previously served as President and CEO of the Regenstrief Institute, Vice-President for Learning Health Systems at IU Health, and professor and associate dean at Indiana University School of Medicine in Indianapolis. Earlier, at The Ohio State University, he served as professor and vice-chair of biomedical informatics and as the nation’s first chief research information officer.
Throughout his career, Dr. Embí has advanced the use of health data, evidence, and emerging technologies to improve care, accelerate research, championed the safe and effective adoption of artificial intelligence in medicine, and trained generations of physicians and scientists in biomedical informatics. He is credited as a founder of the field of clinical research informatics and originated the concept of algorithmovigilance, the systematic evaluation and monitoring of AI in health care.
Dr. Embí earned his bachelor’s degree from the University of Florida, in Gainesville, and his medical doctorate from the University of South Florida, in Tampa. He completed his internal medicine residency at Oregon Health & Science University in Portland, followed by a fellowship in biomedical informatics there, during which he earned a Master of Science in medical informatics and clinical epidemiology. He subsequently completed fellowship training in rheumatology and immunology at the Cleveland Clinic.
Dr. Embí is president of the American College of Medical Informatics (ACMI) and a past president and board chair of the American Medical Informatics Association (AMIA). His honors include election to the National Academy of Medicine and to fellowships in the American College of Physicians, ACMI, and the International Academy of Health Sciences Informatics. In recognition of his leadership and contributions to the field, Dr. Embí received the William W. Stead Award for Thought Leadership from AMIA.
“I would also like to extend my appreciation to Stephen Sherry, Ph.D., who has led NLM as its Acting Director since October 2023. We appreciate the dedicated leadership he has provided,” said Dr. Bhattacharya.
The National Library of Medicine (NLM) is a leader in research in biomedical informatics and data science and the world’s largest biomedical library. NLM conducts and supports research in methods for recording, storing, retrieving, preserving, and communicating health information. NLM creates resources and tools that are used billions of times each year by millions of people to access and analyze molecular biology, biotechnology, toxicology, environmental health, and health services information. Additional information is available at https://www.nlm.nih.gov.
About the National Institutes of Health (NIH): NIH, the nation's medical research agency, includes 27 Institutes and Centers and is a component of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. NIH is the primary federal agency conducting and supporting basic, clinical, and translational medical research, and is investigating the causes, treatments, and cures for both common and rare diseases. For more information about NIH and its programs, visit www.nih.gov.
NIH…Turning Discovery Into Health®
title: Physician-scientist and informatics leader Dr. Peter Embí to helm NIH’s National Library of Medicine September 2, 2026 — He is anticipated to begin his role on Sept. 10, 2026.

Today, G20 member ministers concluded a two-day Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina. The Ministerial was hosted by the Department of Commerce and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP).
At the conclusion of the Ministerial, G20 Ministers released a consensus statement recognizing that “emerging technologies have the potential to unlock prosperity, enhance productivity, and expand opportunity for all our peoples.”
The Innovation Ministerial Statement articulates shared principles across six pillars: pro-innovation policy frameworks; technology for opportunity and prosperity; skilled technical workforce development; intellectual property policies for artificial intelligence; AI for standards and standards for AI; and industrial innovation and investment in supply chains. Ministers also reached consensus on the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, which call on countries to invest in foundational research, strengthen commercialization pathways, and enable trusted technology adoption and deployment.
The full G20 Innovation Ministerial Statement can be accessed here.
“Achieving consensus in the G20 is no small feat, but the topic of innovation as a driver of growth brought us together for a historic moment of unity,” said Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick. “The statement released by the G20 members ministers today gives entrepreneurs the confidence to invest in their ideas, promotes domestic manufacturing, and ensures intellectual property frameworks foster and protect innovation.”
“In Chapel Hill, G20 countries realized an optimistic vision for the future of emerging technologies, recognizing that flexible policy frameworks crafted to promote innovation will drive economic growth and prosperity. That is the spirit of the Carolina Principles, and that is how we will expand opportunity for Americans and people around the world,” said OSTP Director Michael Kratsios.
At the Innovation Ministerial, OSTP Director Kratsios hosted fireside chats with Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX; David Sacks, Co-Chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology; Bob Mumgaard, CEO of Commonwealth Fusion Systems; Demis Hassabis, Co-Founder and Chair of Google DeepMind; Mark Zuckerberg, Chairman and CEO of Meta; and Michael Crow, President of Arizona State University.
Secretary Lutnick hosted fireside chats with Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA; Tom Brown, Co-Founder of Anthropic; Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI; and Alex Karp, CEO of Palantir.
Other deliverables of the Ministerial included the AI Prosperity Objectives and the AI Prosperity Compact which will further technical workforce development across G20 nations and expand opportunities for private sector partnership.
Representatives from the following nations and unions were present at the two-day Ministerial: the African Union, the Argentine Republic, the Commonwealth of Australia, the Federative Republic of Brazil, Canada, the People’s Republic of China, the European Union, the French Republic, the Federal Republic of Germany, the Republic of India, the Republic of Indonesia, the Italian Republic, Japan, the United Mexican States, the Republic of Poland, the Russian Federation, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Republic of Korea, the Republic of Türkiye, and the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
title: G20 Innovation Ministerial Concludes with Consensus Statement

WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Linda T. Sánchez (D-Calif.), a senior member of the Ways and Means Committee, today introduced the Protecting Our Widows and Widowers in Retirement (POWR) Act, a bill to improve financial security for widows and widowers by adjusting the way the Social Security Administration calculates insurance benefits for surviving spouses in two-income households.

“The grief of losing a loved one shouldn’t be compounded by the stress of financial hardship,” said Congresswoman Sánchez. “Sadly, that’s the reality for too many surviving spouses, who can lose half their household income overnight. The POWR Act moves to fix that. After decades of hard work and paying into the system, widows and widowers deserve to keep the benefits they earned together.”

“The nonpartisan Elder Justice Coalition is proud to support the POWR Act,” said Bob Blancato, national coordinator of the Elder Justice Coalition. “Social Security is about promoting economic security. The two provisions of the POWR Act aim to remedy shortcomings that prevent widows, widowers and those on SSI from achieving that. We commend Rep. Sánchez for leading this important reform effort.”

According to the National Academy of Social Insurance, women are more likely to suffer a greater financial hit following the loss of a spouse. Despite higher workforce participation rates, women continue to rely more heavily on Social Security than men. The average widow sees a 33% to 50% drop in her benefits after the death of a spouse.

However, surviving spouses typically need 79% of the couple’s prior combined income just to maintain their standard of living. The POWR Act closes that gap, creating an alternative benefit equal to 75% of a couple’s combined Social Security benefits.

The POWR Act is cosponsored by Representatives Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), Steve Cohen (D-Tenn.), Jan Schakowsky (D-Ill.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Shri Thanedar (D-Mich.) and Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.).

It is endorsed by the Elder Justice Coalition, Alliance for Retired Americans and National Committee to Preserve Social Security and Medicare.

The full text of the bill is available HERE.

###
title: Sánchez introduces bill to strengthen Social Security benefits for widows, widowers

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) called on the House Financial Services Committee to hold a hearing on institutional investors’ impact on Manufactured Housing Communities (MHCs) across the country. Congressman Vasquez led a letter to Chairman French Hill (R-AR) and Ranking Member Maxine Waters (D-CA) — along with five other Members — urging the Committee to hold a hearing to address reports from MHC residents across the country who have said they have experienced price jacking, utilities neglect, and abuse in these communities after private equity firms purchased their communities.

“Congress recently passed a landmark housing bill with overwhelmingly bipartisan support to help Americans purchase homes and specifically targeted institutional investors' role in purchasing single family homes. But the bill did not include equitable protections to address private equity’s role in purchasing hundreds of thousands of lots across several manufactured housing communities,” wrote Vasquez. “There is still more work to be done.”

“The Land of Enchantment Manufactured Home Owners Alliance strongly endorses Representative Vasquez’s call for a House Financial Services Committee hearing on institutional investment and protections for manufactured homeowners,” said Joanne DeMichele, President, Land of Enchantment Manufactured Home Owners Alliance (LEMHOA). “Congress has recognized the damage institutional investors can cause in the single-family housing market through the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Manufactured home communities deserve the same scrutiny. Homeowners in these communities own their homes but not the land beneath them, making them captive tenants when investors acquire that land and rapidly raise rents or neglect essential infrastructure. In Silver City, New Mexico, residents recently saw lot rents increase by 70% virtually overnight after investors purchased the land beneath their homes. This is exactly why Congress must examine private equity’s growing role in manufactured housing and ensure that affordable homeownership is protected, not exploited.”

Last year, local leaders and constituents in various communities across New Mexico raised alarm bells to Rep. Vasquez regarding an uptick in predatory pricing practices and property maintenance neglect in mobile and manufactured home communities owned by corporate landlords and private equity companies. They cited severe examples of landlord utility neglect for mobile home communities resulting in instances of elderly residents being forced to go without natural gas and hot water for months on end.

Unfortunately, these cases are not anomalies, and the scale of this problem nationwide is astounding. One in six homes in New Mexico are mobile homes. In 2020 and 2021, institutional investors accounted for 23 percent of all manufactured home purchases, up from 13 percent between 2017-2019.

“Manufactured housing is a critical pathway to stable, affordable housing for New Mexicans but private equity has continued to threaten this by failing to keep up their end of the deal in our communities,”said Vasquez. “Manufactured Housing Communities are often forgotten in the conversation to preserve affordable housing which is why Congress must look for every opportunity to fix this problem.”

Read the full letter HERE. This letter has been endorsed by the Land of Enchantment Manufactured Home Owner's Alliance and Private Equity Stakeholder Project.

“Congress must act with urgency to protect the dignity, safety, and security of the millions of Americans living in manufactured housing owned by private equity and other institutional investors,” said Chris Noble, Policy Director at the Private Equity Stakeholder Project. “Across the country, manufactured housing residents living in investor-owned communities are contending with extreme rent hikes, aggressive evictions, and cascading junk fees. In some communities, residents can't even count on having access to clean water. That is unacceptable and exactly why the Private Equity Stakeholder Project applauds Representative Vasquez’s efforts to uplift and center this issue as part of Congress’ housing affordability agenda.”

Rep. Vasquez has repeatedly led efforts to stop greedy, corporate landlords from jacking up New Mexicans’ rents and continues his long track record of championing solutions to make housing more affordable for every hardworking New Mexican.

Some of his most recent actions on this front include:

Hosting a Town Hall in Carlsbad focused on enacting solutions to address the housing affordability crisis in New Mexico.

Introducing the Keep Mobile Homes Affordable Act, a bill to ensure investors who purchase over 2,500 mobile homes or pads are not engaging in price gouging or failing to provide basic utilities to residents. This legislation was inspired by the Congressman’s conversations with mobile home residents in places like Alamogordo and Albuquerque who raised serious concerns about mobile home affordability.

Voting in favor of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, an overwhelmingly bipartisan bill that marked the most sweeping win for housing affordability in a generation and became law in July 2026.

Co-sponsoring the Bipartisan Families First Housing Act and the Stop Wall Street Landlords Act to crack down on greedy, corporate landlords and ensure hardworking New Mexicans have a fair shot at homeownership.

###
title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Calls for Hearing to Protect Manufactured Housing Communities from Private Equity

Washington, DC – U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) today sent a letter to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and National Park Service Comptroller Jessica Bowron demanding transparency and answers over the Trump Administration’s alleged proposal to parcel off part of Yosemite National Park to a private real estate developer.

“I write in strong opposition to recent reports that the National Park Service (NPS) is working to parcel off part of Yosemite National Park in California to give to a private real-estate developer. Under the alleged proposal, land within Yosemite National Park would be ceded to the developer to construct a road that connects private property to the park,” Correa said.

“I am outraged by this alleged action that threatens Yosemite’s natural resources at the expense of private real-estate developers. Yosemite National Park was created in 1890 and since then our nation has worked together to protect its precious ecosystem and natural wonders, including Half Dome and the giant sequoia trees,” Correa continued. “This agency proposal runs counter to over 135 years of protecting this land in California for both wildlife and the public.”

“The NPS was created in 1916 to protect our precious natural resources and to promote and regulate national parks, monuments, and reservations to “conserve the scenery and the natural and historic objects and the wildlife therein and to provide for the enjoyment of the same in such manner and by such means as will leave them unimpaired for the enjoyment of future generations,” Correa concluded. “This proposed land exchange is contrary to the NPS’s 150 years of work to protect our national parks and Congress’s intent when it created the agency.”

Read the full text of the letter HERE.

Washington, D.C. (September 2, 2026)—Today, Rep. Hank Johnson, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet, delivered opening remarks at a subcommittee hearing on renewing the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office’s (USPTO) fee-setting authority and protecting a fair, accessible patent system that rewards American innovation and ingenuity.

Thank you, Chairman Issa.

The USPTO’s fee-setting authority has given it the flexibility to move its workers remote, plan its budgets ahead, and tailor fees for small and micro entities. Originally, it was set to expire in just a few days on September the 16th. Yesterday, however, House and Senate Republicans were generous enough to kick the can down the road until after they are reelected. The authority is now set to expire on December 12th, 2026. Failing to reauthorize the USPTO’s fee setting authority risks transforming a traditionally nonpartisan agency into one that serves political ideology over merit.

Ensuring that USPTO remains a beacon of American innovation means not just reauthorizing the fee setting authority but ensuring USPTO advisory committees can continue to advise the USPTO without interference by this administration. Two months after he was inaugurated, Trump’s Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick fired every member of PPAC and TPAC. A year and a half later, they finally swore in the first few new members.

When Congress originally authorized fee setting authority under the America Invents Act, we built in several oversight measures to ensure that this power could not be exercised without transparency but rather with public input and independent expert review. PPAC and TPAC remain a critical part of those guardrails. Their full and independent participation is essential to ensuring that fee-setting remains accountable to all who rely on our patent and trademark systems, the big and the small. That is why these committees must be fully constituted as they are a necessary safeguard for independence.

And that independence matters. If we do not give USPTO the flexibility it needs to set fees, access to our patent system will be taken over by special interests. This will make it even harder for small, independent inventors to protect their inventions and easier for those who can pay-to-play to infringe on those rights.

How do we know? Because we are already seeing this happen in the rest of the executive branch. Every day we learn again how easy it’s become for oligarchs and powerful companies to buy a seat at Donald Trump’s table. Millions of dark money in campaign contributions. Lavish gifts like private jets, and business deals. Rampant insider trading on predictive markets. Access to the Trump White House has transformed into a currency that only the rich and famous can afford.

And while the wealthy are busy buying a seat at the table, Americans across the country are left paying the price. Constituents of Georgia’s 4th Congressional district are struggling to afford rent or pay their mortgage, and the cost of groceries continue to skyrocket. Hardworking families should not struggle to afford healthcare while Elon Musk becomes a trillionaire, and while Donald Trump lines his own pockets through unabashed greed built on the backs of American taxpayers.

Conflicts of interest and self-dealing have become routine features in Trump’s Washington, blurring the line between public service and private financial gain. This was a man who campaigned on draining the swamp, and yet all Trump has done is put it behind a velvet rope and began charging an admissions fee. Because in Trump’s America money buys access. Access buys influence. And influence too often becomes the law for everyone else. Innovation should not be a luxury that only the wealthy can afford. So, I, for one, am determined to not allow USPTO to be sucked in to that swamp.

Reauthorizing this fee setting authority with the transparency, public participation, and independent oversight that Congress intended is essential to keeping our patent system working for all—not just for those with the closest connection to big tech, the aspiring oligarch class, or the Trump White House. We have just a few months to get this done. This is not time for Members or big money special interests to advocate for changes to the way the USPTO operates because they’re not happy with Director Squires’ Patent Trial and Appeals Board actions. I think we are overdue to examine proposals like Rep. Ross’s PREVAIL, which would reform PTAB abuses. I’m sure some of my colleagues on both sides of the aisle agree with me, just as others disagree. But I’m not trying to make those changes right now. We have a program that everyone agrees has been successful; inserting our own USTPO agendas into the debate will only serve to make this reauthorization controversial.

I want to thank the witnesses for being here today. While I think this hearing is unnecessary and a distraction from the disastrous policies of the Trump Administration, I do believe it is vital that Americans truly understand the importance of allowing this agency the independence and discretion it needs to keep America at the top of our global innovation economy. Because if we want to continue to lead the world in the technological advancements of tomorrow, then we must ensure today that the institution most responsible for protecting those innovations is independent and built to last.

I yield back the balance of my time.
title: Ranking Member Johnson’s Opening Statement At Hearing On Protecting America’s Patent System And Innovation Economy
